title: 3 Statements From Rookie Coordinator Declan Doyle Reveal Why Ravens Run Game Stinks
full_text:
The Ravens’ run game is in crisis mode.
Schematic and personnel changes are in order, including less Derrick Henry and more of a speed approach on the perimeter. The offensive line is a mess and, if this team was a meritocracy, there would be at least three changes being made on that five-man unit as well (like these ). And rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has made plenty of mistakes trying to figure out life without MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, taking his lumps in the football world about having string-bean rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane trying to crack on bulldozing edge rusher Khalil Mack on the first play of the game Monday night for a predictable loss for Henry (it was a major talking point when he met the media Thursday .
There is a lot to clean up in a lost season if the Ravens (4-6) are going to break a five-game slide and restore any semblance of balance and promise to this campaign. Doyle seems far removed from the heady days of August when he was being proclaimed a “genius” by players and a lot has been asked of him with constantly shuffling quarterbacks and an ever-changing offensive line. Carolina is 27th in run defense Expected Points Added, so another poor showing Sunday and it’s further proof that the problems rest within the Ravens roster.
Three of Doyle’s responses Thursday seemed quite revealing and telling about where his head is as the season slips away and it becomes tougher and tougher to create positive plays and winning scripts, and as his ability to position the team to succeed in the second-half of games gets called into greater question , along with rookie head coach Jesse Minter on the defensive side of the ball.
Here’s what he said, and here’s what it means:
“We're going to hang the sign that says 'physical, detailed, explosive' and physical's No. 1 there,” Doyle said. “And that's us playing fundamentally sound with pad level and coming off the ball with cadence and all those things. I felt like they beat us up physically, and that was just the bottom line.
“There's no sugarcoating that. That's what showed up on tape, and the tape is the truth. So, we have to play better. This will always be a fundamental game. It will always go back to pad level, get off, being able to utilize technique, being able to communicate, utilize double teams and things like that. That really is what we're working toward, and that's the emphasis.”
What It Mean s: He was scared to run the ball. He could have either adopted an uber-jumbo philosophy and gone with multiple tight ends and an extra offensive lineman, and tried to operate that way on the ground or through the air, and instead he thought it was a better idea to have a brand-new quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, drop back 50 times in his debut. Problem is his tackles were getting obliterated. Doyle has some of the wrong defaults and better right them, quickly.
“When you look at that kind of defense, the best avenue is generally to go outside of it – at least to start the game – and try to soften those edges,” Doyle said. “Soften it up, and then you start to create a little more space on the inside. So, that was one where Jak is our most physical blocker in that crack scheme. That's a play that we ran against Atlanta a few weeks back, and it was a successful play.
“So, really, you're trying to attack the defense. You're trying to start the game off with a run and trying to get Derrick [Henry] out in space, which is something that – as you watch the self-scout – that's something that he does really well. And it just so happens, like Khalil plays out; it gets strung out, and it ends up being a negative play. And anytime that happens, you go back to the drawing board, and you say, 'I failed as a play-caller on that play, because I didn't put him in position to have success.
What It Means: He is entirely too cute here. The Ravens are a terrible team running the ball with RBs out of 11 personnel, Brissett wants to be surrounded by TEs and this OL needs all the help it can get in every aspect of play. Watching this five times, it looks like a show-off way to open the game. It’s awfully naïve. How about "softening it up" with a tight end who has more of a fighting chance?
Henry has run 51 times for just 197 yards out of 11 personnel (3.9 yards/carry) and averaged just 0.86 yards before contact when doing do. As a team their backs average 3.9/carry doing this (23rd in the NFL). It’s not a strength and with Brissett airdropped into this offense in the middle of the season, with plenty of tight ends available, this is a stretch he can’t be making.
“That is something that every week during the planning, you're trying to find ways to five-man release it,” Doyle said, “and trying to find ways to make sure the quarterback knows where he's protected. Yet at the same point in time, it's a double-edged sword, because if you release somebody and they bring a pressure, they can dictate where you throw that ball. So, it's kind of that risk-reward balance that you go through every week."
What It Means : Dude just doesn’t understand the assignment and what he is up against here. His line is garbage. Neither tackle was any good in this game, his center is getting shoved around. Doyle told you bad they were outmuscled in the run game; you think they were holding up being walked back into the quarterback. People around the league were befuddled by 50 dropbacks, period, trying to do so with incorporating as few max-protect concepts as possible in a tight, must-win game under these circumstances shows he doesn’t grasp the hand he’s been dealt.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens' Secondary Is Failing Like Never Before. Jesse Minter's New Reality Is Bleak
full_text:
The Ravens were hopeful of having a record setting defense in their first season under wunderkind defensive mind Jesse Minter.
And they are indeed doing some truly unique things on that side of the ball with the overmatched rookie head coach in place , just not the likes of which anyone could have reasonably expected. Minter was hailed as the closest thing out there to Seattle’s Super Bowl winning coach Mike Macdonald (one of the many coaches who got away from Baltimore in recent years) and anointed as a schematic savant with a particular genius for the secondary.
And his defensive backs are among the biggest disappointments in the NFL, his defense is bottom eight in the league overall and arguably the worst in the clutch among all 32 teams. It is devoid of playmakers , yet again (you mean it wasn’t all Zach Orr’s fault?)– and Kyle Hamilton, rather than ascend to Defensive Player Of The Year heights has been largely pedestrian. Hamilton’s greatest impact has been in calling out this joke of a defense week in and week out going back to Week 2’s horrible home loss to the Saints.
Looking for unprecedented performances from the Ravens secondary? How about $19M failure Marlon Humphrey finally getting deactivated after Mayor Brandon Scott issued a public statement rebuking the cornerback’s regrettable podcast remarks? Yeah, heady times indeed in Owings Mills, where it turns out Orr could coached circles around anything Minter has mustered to this point.
But let’s quantify some of these failings, and put them in their proper perspective. Because after making creating interceptions a hallmark in two seasons running he Chargers defense, top three in interception percentage, Minter cannot get one of his defensive backs in Baltimore to get their hands on a football to save their lives (or, if this was serious organization, his job).
The Ravens are the only team in the NFL that does not have a defensive back create an interception this season ( Hamilton plays more linebacker than anything else and was playing linebacker when broken back-up quarterback Tua Tagovailoa threw a ball to him rushed into duty in overtime in Atlanta).
The Ravens and Colts – arguably the worst team in football right now – are the only teams in the NFL that do not have an interception from a cornerback.
Mind you, everyone playing the most in the Ravens’ secondary is either at the top of the pay-scale at their position, or a former first-round pick of failure GM Eric DeCosta … or both. There are supposed to be no weak links, yet instead there is no discernable strength from a playmaker standpoint (same on virtually every defense DeCosta ever built ).
Their slot coverage remains the dregs of the NFL, allowing a 123.4 passer rating (30th) as we have been documenting all season. They are the only team in the NFL without an interception on a pass to the slot. And these aren’t just layups; Baltimore is allowing 9.2 yards/attempt in the slot, 25th in the NFL.
The Ravens are allowing an opposing passer rating of 116.4 in the second half of games, second worst in the NFL (despite facing mostly bad passing offenses). They have allowed 1278 passing yards in the second half of games (30th), with 10 touchdown passes to no interceptions (worst ratio in the NFL). They paid aging designated pass rusher Trey Hendrickson’s $60M guaranteed for two years to be their “closer” but he has five pressures in the fourth quarter all season and has been ineffective all around since finger surgery in early October.
Only eight teams in the NFL have allowed more completions of 25+ yards than the Ravens, despite Minter selling out to take that away above and beyond everything else. He plays all that dime coverage and zones everything up and has resorted to doubling his use of Cover-3 during this five-game slump, but even that isn’t working. The pre-snap subterfuge is out the window and even rudimentary looks can’t get stops.
The Ravens are giving up an average of two passes of 25+ per game over the last sex weeks. That’s failure by any standard, and given Minter’s philosophy, it’s begging questions about his ability to perform either of the jobs he was hired to do .
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Finally Discipline Struggling CB Marlon Humphrey For Podcast Remarks
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter has been talking about standards and accountability throughout a miserably lost season, and he finally backed it up Thursday.
The rookie coach, overmatched to this point 10 games into his job, announced that $19M corner Marlon Humphrey (who carries the highest cap hit at his position in the NFL despite a credible case to be released or dealt after a terrible 2026 season ) was sent home, will not practice with the team and will not play Sunday at Carolina. Humphrey, overpaid and propped up as a “leader” on this team, has been rankling players and coaches for years with his podcasting and social-media proclivities, and his remarks on his podcast caught up to him this week.
Mayor Brandon Scott released a statement Wednesday condemning Humphrey’s comments after he asserted Baltimore is "best at making criminals ” on his podcast. Humphrey was allowed to practice and meet the media Wednesday after releasing the pod, but on Thursday Minter announced there would actually be some discipline attached.
Minter said of his communications with the former Pro Bowl player – who was a bottom 10 corner in the NFL last season – “the conversations are very, very personal and private, and to me need to remain that.”
There was every reasonable football reason to be made to pay Humphrey $4M to leave in the offseason (given his bonus structure), but he is a favorite of general manager Eric DeCosta, who rose to his defense before the season began and proclaimed him to be a “$19M corner.” And Humphrey has been picked on by bad quarterbacks and exposed by blocking tight ends in coverage. A legion of former coaches, players and execs have come on “The Daily Flock Show” including Wink Martindale, Marty Hurney, Ryan Clark, Bucky Brooks pointing out Humphrey needed a limited role in the slot, but players making $19M with a powerful font office and a rookie head coach don’t end up benched or “relegated” to the slot.
Instead, Humphrey was repeatedly allowed to take on top receivers all season and he remains as targeted as any corner in the NFL. The Ravens front office has been pushing a narrative about young corner TJ Tampa for years but he’s barely seen the field even with Humphrey struggling, though he and veteran Chidobe Awuzie will see more action Sunday now
Defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver – who vowed Humphrey and linebacker Roquan Smith would have huge bounce-back seasons and prove people wrong this spring – said on Thursday, “we love him,” about Humphrey, while pointing out how regrettable his remarks were, even in gest.
Weaver pointed to “technique and fundamentals” as key issues in Humphrey’s poor season and also noted it’s hardy been limited to him. “Defensively, we haven’t lived up to our standard,” Weaver said. This is another new low in a lost season full of them.
The Ravens have a bottom-eight defense in the NFL despite Minter being hailed as a genius on that side of the ball, and they have allowed the fifth-most points in the NFL. Minter began publicly expressing the need for locker room leadership by October, and Humphrey has been called into question in that regard for years.
The Ravens are the worst second-half team in the NFL, Baltimore does not have a second-half interception and they do not have an interception from a corner or safety in coverage all season (Kyle Hamilton’s came as a linebacker), despite Minter’s zone coverages being hailed as exemplary in that regard. Minter is being viewed around the NFL as a potential one-and-done head coach if he cannot quickly stop this rot after five straight defeats, all embarrassing in their own way.
DeCosta has said not addressed the media since telling Ravens fans why Humphrey was worth $19M a season and how optimistic he was about signing Lamar Jackson back before this brutal season began.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Should Jesse Minter Relinquish Play-Calling Duties? NFL Analyst Ryan Clark Believes So
full_text:
Struggling Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter was dismissive when questioned last week about relinquishing defensive play-calling duties amid his team’s collective failures. He should not have been.
There is a certain ego and hubris involved in performing that task for him – and ego and hubris have got the franchise into an ugly mess in all aspects of the organization – but Minter, soon enough, is going to see that the big picture of him trying to establish himself as anything close to an NFL head coach may require divesting himself of some duties. Longtime Raiders team president Amy Trask believes it must be on the table, and longtime NFL safety and NFL analyst Ryan Clark thinks the same thing.
Baltimore’s defense is a shell of what it was supposed to be.
The coverage is terrible, the pass rush is barely-pedestrian, they produce no turnovers or big plays and they have been the worst in the NFL in the second half. They blew double-digit leads with regularity back when the offense was good enough to build them (before Lamar Jackson got hurt) and lately they have been getting torn up in the first quarter of games to fall too far behind for the back-up QBs to have a chance.
Minter has not found the ability to motivate these players or make anything close to sage in-game adjustments in any aspect of play, bringing up questions of this being a potential one-and-done scenario should a five-game losing streak spill into December. Yes, calling plays on defense got him this job, but he’s become one of the worst coordinators in the NFL trying to wear both hats, and something has to give as players continue to say and do ridiculous things on their podcasts on the field of play with no accountability to this point.
It’s a dichotomy Minter better get his head around, fast.
Clark, who joined “The Daily Flock Show”’ this week, believes Minter needs to rely more on coordinator Anthony Weaver on game-day; Weaver is a former NFL player with a long coaching history on the defensive line and calling defenses himself.
“You say to yourself, this was the thing I was really good at,” Clark said of Minter calling plays. “And because I was really good at that thing, I want to continue doing that because that gives me something on game day I can control outside of delegation.
“So, I don't know if he should pull it back. What I do know is when I watched Miami play under Anthony Weaver defensively, Miami knew they sucked, right? No, they did … There was no secret. They were terrible. But their defense played hard as hell … They ran and they hit and they pressured ... Maybe, maybe giving Anthony Weaver that sort of control over the defense would help.
“Because no matter what, even though I see Anthony Weaver in the room every week, I know he's not the guy, right? Like, we got a different relationship cuz this is the guy. And so maybe him relinquishing that to (Weaver) would probably feel like I failed as a defensive coordinator here and I'm removing myself because I failed. Hopefully he would be able to see it as I'm not failing. I'm giving someone who I trust the power to make a difference on game day so I can now fully focus on this job I've earned.”
Clark, like many others, believes Minter has watered down his approach and shunned pre-snap masking just hoping to sit in a shell and take away big plays. Even that isn’t working. The standard has fallen so low, that just getting guts to run to the football and wrap up as tacklers has been too tall a task at times. Instead of Kyle Hamilton moving all over in a role where no one knows what he’s doing, Clark sees him just standing around at the line of scrimmage “90% of the time.”
It’s not bringing out the best in anyone (except linebacker Trenton Simpson ), and other teams are picking on the weak links with abandon.
“I see it on film; other teams see it on film,” Clark said. “What adjustment is Anthony Weaver and Jesse Mentor making to get it right? And, yes, players got to make plays, but I also schematically I earned this job because of my success as a defensive coach. Where are the adjustments?
“We saw Mike Macdonald make those adjustments and become a head coach in Seattle, right? When are they going to make that adjustment with this iteration of the Baltimore Ravens?"
My best guess is - not this season.
Clark described it as a simplistic defense at this point. That might be kind. Teams attack corner Marlon Humphrey from the jump every week, there isn’t enough pressure on opposing quarterbacks, and Minter should be feeling the heat.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Three Changes Ravens Rookie Offensive Coordinator Declan Doyle Must Make Now
full_text:
The Ravens' season has slipped away, Lamar Jackson may have thrown his last pass for the franchise and the team’s young coordinators have much to prove in games that won’t matter much come January.
All the talk about 30-year-old offensive coordinator Declan Doyle being a “genius” from this summer has subsided, he cannot figure out a way to run the ball whatsoever right now to the point where overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter seems more frustrated about that than anything else, and general manager Eric DeCosta handed him an offensive line that is truly atrocious and is the kind of thing that would get people fired in an organization in which the owner was engaged and cunning.
Evaluating Doyle is more difficult given how jaundiced this prism has become – no Jackson (and maybe no Jackson ever again , as Ryan Clark explained), no pass protection, no holes in the run game, only one receiver who wins downfield. Honestly, what Minter has been unable to do on the defensive side should be giving massive pause to everyone in The Castle beyond some of these offensive struggles, but it’s fair to wonder if Jackson is the only thing close to a genius in that building and this is a four-win team , at best, without him, with or without Doyle calling the plays.
Still, there is pressure on this young staff and Doyle must take some tangible and obvious measures to try to derive a modicum of balance and some element of surprise from an offense that is woefully lacking in that regard. As always, we have some cogent suggestions for him:
My buddy Marty Hurney, longtime general manager and admittedly old-school, was going to pull his hair out talking to me about Baltimore’s offense this week and the decision to drop back 50 times with Jacoby Brissett in his first game with the team in Monday’s loss to the previously-winless Chargers.
“You have to be willing to stick with the run and give it a chance to work,” he intoned. “It’s the whole league, man! It’s not just the Ravens.”
One way to help that cause is to dedicate to personnel groupings that can help a terrible line have a fighting chance. We’ve documented the woes of the run game – and the case for more Justice Hill ( at length here ) – but Baltimore is averaging a gaudy 5.4 yards/rush when it utilizes an extra offensive lineman. Doesn’t matter if the other team knows it’s a run; Doyle has to commit to it.
The Ravens also got out of their 13 personnel (three tight end) looks when blocker Durham Smythe was lost for the season but it needs to come back. Doyle has no wide receivers who win on the outside anyway and rookie Ja’Kobi Lane is getting funneled and is struggling right now and the tight ends are more trustworthy and Jacoby Brissett threw a higher percentage of passes to TE in two years in Arizona than anyone in the NFL; and the Cardinals are second in the NFL in usage of 13 this season, so the QB is accustomed to it.
The Ravens went from using 13 over 16% of the time in the first six weeks to just 9.7% since Week 7. Doyle needs to ramp it up. Keep Josh Cuevas involved and get Matthew Hibner going and Nick Vannett is a blocking option and they have a fullback to use more, too.
What’s the point of having Elijah Sarratt inactive every week as fourth-round receiver on a bad football team going nowhere? Even cutting back on the 11 personnel as I am calling for,  we seriously prefer Chris Moore to him (even with Moore on special teams?). We can’t coach Sarratt up on teams and get him at least blocking?
Hibner needs a run on seam routes. We documented how poorly many individuals are on this offensive line are performing , and want to see Carson Vinson at tackle. Doyle had the temerity to fall back on “player development” for not playing Smythe as much he should have back in Week 2, so let’s see the kid TEs now.
Remember when Doyle said he was going to dabble with calling games from the sidelines and the press box and then make up his mind? Then he had a great game against the Eagles fourth stringers in a preseason game upstairs and never came down. Might be time for a rethink.
Yeah, let’s mix it up, rook.
Doyle seems too disconnected from the action to me and part of why these QBs are getting hung out to dry by weird play calling behind a bad line might be because he isn’t seeing things at ground level like he should. He has a lot of new parts and a new offensive line every week and wants to script the entire game from the jump. That's not how it works.
He gave this a run, it’s been a disaster without Jackson, and he needs to take a different tact.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: NFL Analyst Ryan Clark Explains Why Lamar Jackson Could Leave Ravens, And Why GM Eric DeCosta's Time May Be Up
full_text:
The window for the Baltimore Ravens to win with anything of note with the core that legendary general manager Ozzie Newsome imparted when he handed over day-to-day duties running the organization is over.
At 4-6, with five straight losses and one of the worst sustained stretches in the history of the franchise, with a first-year head coach who is making the case to be a potential one-and-done , and with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson holding the future of the franchise in his hands in 2027 based on whether he wants to stay in Baltimore or go somewhere else , these are perilous times indeed. Newsome’s group peaked in 2023, failing general manager Eric DeCosta took over in 2019 and was more empowered than ever this season with legendary coach John Harbaugh fired ... and this franchise looks lost.
And add longtime NFL analyst and former Steelers safety Ryan Clark, who battled the Ravens at the height of that rivalry and has studied them closely ever since, to the legion of guests who have come on “The Daily Flock Show” lately to express their belief that Minter’s coaching tenure absolutely should be in the balance, that the Ravens face an inevitable reboot regardless, that DeCosta should probably be cast aside , and Jackson quite likely and reasonably will want to play elsewhere in 2027.
It’s been getting heavy in Owings Mills and with each mounting defeat, with the Ravens’ remarkably slim playoff offs growing slimmer, the overarching questions about their roster and payroll and cap situation and future become more pressing. Clark expressed a belief similar to what longtime Raiders team president Amy Trask recently conveyed about Minter and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle effectively coaching for the jobs , and he believes years of serious missteps in how DeCosta and owner Steve Bisciotti have handled Jackson’s unique brilliance have painted the franchise into a dark corner they might not be able to get out of.
Clark pointed out severe limitations in Baltimore offensive line, outside receivers, and run game, and Jackson’s absence has exposed this roster as being one of the worst in football – too old and far too bloated in ket spots. Getting Jackson to reup on a long-term deal after he has amassed unprecedented leverage feels more and more like a longshot to many around the football world.
“Ozzie Newsome gave the Baltimore Ravens the greatest parting gift of all time,” Clark noted. “You kidding me? He said, ‘Look, I'm not going to leave you stranded. I'm going to do something that nobody else is willing to do and I'm gonna move up in the first round (in 2018) and draft this kid because I know he's special.
“Here: You're welcome. Build around him. And they haven't done that in the way that I think makes Lamar Jackson likely to in any way take any shorts to be with this program or to feel that he's been treated in a way that he's a fabric of everything they want to do going forward.”
Indeed, Jackson’s’ path with this franchise has been nothing like what Josh Allen has experienced with the Bills or what Patrick Mahomes has experienced with the Chiefs . He played out his entire rookie contract without the Ravens added a penny in additional incentives, was placed on a non-exclusive franchise tag, was a part of a collusion claim and issues a public trade demand before finally getting his last deal done and has rebuffed all of Baltimore’s offers (however robust or not; who knows) since.
It’s super smart on his part, and seems like perfect timing, too, with this franchise falling to pieces the moment he misses a game, to be able to call his own shot.
“If I'm Lamar Jackson and regardless of what you say about playoff struggles, my level of play has been what it was here,” Clark said. “Yet, I haven't been treated that way in so many different terms. What am I staying for? Why do I want to be here?
“Like, what loyalty do I need to show and in that, what are you going to tell me about our plans for next year - for moving forward for next year - that make me want to stay, right? Those are the conversations we have to have.”
Clark illuminates the player perspective in a way few can, and also exposes just how rudimentary and searching Minter’s scheme and approach has become on the defensive side of the ball, where he was supposed to be an immediate home-run hire. The Ravens future looks as bleak as it ever has, and there will be more humbling losses still to come.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Claimed Trey Hendrickson's Surgery Would Save His Season. It May Have Ended It
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens trumpeted the signing of aging pass-rusher Trey Hendrickson in numerous ways, none of which has come close to holding up amid what’s already a lost season.
At first, he was part of an alleged master plan to bookend with Raiders super star Maxx Crosby (general manager Eric DeCosta reneged on a trade for “medical” concerns). Hendrickson was anointed as an absolute game-changer, despite being older and more injury-prone than Crosby. They heralded Hendrickson, about to turn 32, as the “closer” who would eliminate this defense’s second-half choking gene with fourth-quarter dominance upon making a rare massive free-agent swing on him in March..
Then, when he had a middling stretch and was dealing with a finger injury, the team declared that getting a procedure early in the season would propel him to his CLOSER status when he returned. Except, well, instead of trading him at the deadline for anything they could get for him in a salary dump, they now have a very expensive player who is not good against the run or pass.
They have a player who has not made an impact play in the fourth quarter all season – while the defense hits new second-half lows under alleged defensive genius head coach Jesse Minter – and might not ever do so in 2026. They have a young player in Mike Green, making no money, who is vastly outperforming him. They have a version of Hendrickson, post-surgery, that is a shell of even what he was before missing several weeks with the procedure.
They have a $60M problem on their hands - at a time when Baltimore has the worst salary cap situation in the NFL with Lamar Jackson counting $84M against the 2027 cap – and it’s not getting better. And with Hendrickson missing time with injuries and hold-outs and hold-ins with Cincinnati, availability alone is a question (Crosby is playing as much as defensive lineman in the NFL). But compare all of that to what was being said about about the free-agent splash last month when he come back from surgery:
“I think he's feeling a lot better than even the couple games he played with the finger, so I'm really excited for him,” Minter said when Hendrickson returned in mid-October. “You come into a new place and you get hurt in that first game, what he's dealt with, he's been a great, great teammate, I would say. I'm excited for him to be feeling better. I think we'll get a chance to see what he can bring to our defense.”
Hendrickson said at the time of his return : “I needed (the surgery) Week 1. I've had two healthy quarters here. It's not what I planned for the offseason, but God has a plan. It's one of the things that is very humbling, but [I was] pushing through it through Week 2 and Week 3, but the best decision for everybody was getting it fixed for [the] long-term and short-term … Significantly less painful, believe it or not. So, it's actually great."
So how’s that working out?
Turns out, Hendrickson was far more impactful early in the season, even in the more acute pain playing through the finger injury, than he’s been since he came back. Now, maybe we will have some “revelation” about him later in the season like there just was about Mark Andrews (broken hand eh, with nothing on injury report and no cast?), but this has been ugly and it’s getting worse.
Even his big “revenge” game against the Bengals was a total bust, he has just five pressures in the fourth quarter all season and two total sacks as a Raven. He’s yet to pass long-injured run-stuffer Tavius Robinson for second on the team in sacks (3.5) and he has been increasingly invisible as the team had to fight for its season in Cleveland and at Buffalo and against Jacksonville.
Hendrickson First 3 Games : 1 sack     14 Pressures               3 QBH              10 Hurries
17.5% Pressure Rate               15.9% 2nd Half Pressure Rate
Hendrickson Last 5 Games: 1 sack     15 Pressures               4 QBH              10 Hurries
12.5% Pressure Rate               11.8% 2nd Half Pressure Rate
Minter has resorted to trying to talk up Hendrickson’s impact against the run – which is comical (Wink Martindale called him out for the liability he is watching his tape this season). That’s a bad sign, folks. He hasn’t made other people better, he’s been an Opener and nothing like a Closer, and after the Chargers ripped Baltimore on the ground Monday night watch the volume of run plays increase against this defense as the weather turns.
The Ravens need much more Zion Young and Mike Green on early downs, and they need to extend Robinson's contract and be willing to start him next year and accept Hendrickson is “a designated pass rusher” as Martindale explained. At this age, less is more, even in that role. That’s reality, but this franchise has been incapable of accepting its realities for quite some time.
Just like DeCosta has been incapable of finding consistent playmakers on his defense no matter how much spends or who he drafts . That’s only been getting worse. Like Hendrickson after his surgery.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Three Vital Changes The Ravens Must Make To The Run Game, Including Less Derrick Henry
full_text:
The Ravens’ run game is beyond broken.
And it’s probably unfixable. The loss of historically mobile, two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has sunk their ability to win the numbers game at the line of scrimmage and create holes and math that works in their favor; and Jackson isn’t coming back to this sinking ship. Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has become very predictable in his run concepts, with multiple execs from other teams pointing out to me that teams are keying on when the under-center and outside zone runs are coming.
And, well, the offensive line that failing general manager Eric DeCosta has concocted is the worst by far of all the suspect units he’s constructed, one that seems hellbent on getting quarterbacks maimed, and quickly-aging 32-year-old running back Derrick Henry swarmed behind the line of scrimmage. It’s so bad that one could rightfully make the case that four of the five starting spots should be shuffled so that someone perhaps less prone to crushing mistakes could get a shot.
It’s a fairly dire circumstance and the fact that no QB on this roster is going to shift that math in Doyle’s favor is damning. If he is in fact the genius he was purported to be this summer, well, now would be the perfect time to show it. More likely, Doyle will be hard-pressed to change things even on the margins, but he absolutely must lean into these three fundamental changes to his approach after henry ran 10 times for 10 yards against a middling Chargers defense Monday night and the team ran 15 times for 16 yards.
“There's to me just a combination of a lot of factors that we need to figure out how to be able to run the football,” struggling rookie head coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “There's been spurts of it, but the last few games, it's obviously not where it needs to be.
“It starts with me, starts with the coaches, goes down to the players. Unacceptable, honestly, that we're not able to. The first half, to have no yards rushing, it's embarrassing. And so, we'll keep trying to find a better way to do it."
We have a few suggestions:
Nothing lasts forever, there was always a good reason to suspect a decline at this age (all the data pointed to it ), and that Doyle was not going to be able to get the 300 carries he badly wanted from him with the effectiveness he would expect. That’s out the window now. (Henry has never run 300 times for three straight years).
With failing center Cam Jurgens now anchoring this line, under center runs are impossible and running between the tackles, period, is out. That’s Henry’s bread-and-butter, along with outside zone rushes, but teams are shooting the gap with linebackers and defensive backs and blowing that up in the backfield. Monday night – on the feels of five weeks of stagnation (at best) – should be the end of thinking this can be based around Henry with this line and personnel.
Henry: 110 – 358 – 3 TD        3.3 yards/carry           0.36 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 23 – 187 – 1                8.8 yards/carry           3.78 Yds Before Contact
Henry: 60 – 194 – 4                3.21 yards/carry         0.53 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 19 – 144 – 0                  7.60 yards/carry         4.63 Yds Before Contact
Henry: 28 – 84 – 1                  3.00 yards/carry         0.54 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 8 – 85 – 1                      10.6 yards/carry         8.63 Yds Before Contact
So, yeah, it's time for more spread formations and less I-formation and more sprint plays with speed out of the gun.
The Ravens cannot get as caught up in outside zone and trying to do something they thought would be a calling hard. They have had a new line almost every week and Doyle isn’t fooling anyone. It’s time to incorporate more power and duo blocking and see if that can unlock Henry and save the perimeter stuff for others.
And that goes way beyond just Hill.
The team seems reluctant to get fifth-round pick Adam Randall into a football game this season as he sits on Injured Reserve. But they need to see what he can do as a “Joker” in this offense who can run wide receiver routes as an inside player and also carry the football and serve as an H-back and fullback. They are desperate for some new looks and traits.
And Zay Flowers needs to get back into the flow of the run game and used like he was early in the season with Jackson. They need to think about pony packages with Hill and Flowers in the backfield and Henry and Flowers and, shoot, Henry and Randall.
Anybody see what Sean McVay did last week due to injuries, basically just leaning on 13 personnel and pony packages to destroy the Cardinals on Sunday? Get that film to Doyle.
Feel like we say this all the time, but in light of what we just noted with McVay, and given the limitations of this roster, Doyle needs to be willing to throw more manpower at the problem and get the tackle eligible involved and let Jacoby Brissett take some play-action shots out of that heavy stuff.
They should think about having a fullback be much more a part of this offense (paging Pat Ricard).If Carson Vinson replaces Ronnie Stanley at left tackle, as I would espouse, then find another swing tackle.
The Ravens have gone with six offensive linemen 31 times, which is fourth-most in the NFL, but given the depths the traditional run game has hit, that’s not enough. They average a hefty 5.4 yards/carry when they do it, which is also fourth in the NFL. Doyle is using two or more tight ends 44% of the time, which is top 10 in the NFL, but the head coach Doyle worked for last year in Chicago – Ben Johnson, a true savant – is using them over half the time and running the ball with vigor and getting plenty of people involved.
Baltimore could badly use more of that.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Had Superior Options To Jesse Minter On Recent Coaching Staffs. We Rank Them 1-5
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are facing an existential crisis.
Their front office has made it clear – after surviving the firing of potential Hall of Fame coach John Harbaugh – that it’s actually by far the biggest issue in the organization. Both through its systematic roster and contract failures under GM Eric DeCosta and through hiring a rudimentary and inexperienced coaching staff that has been thoroughly overmatched to this point. Which begs questions about the future of the coordinators if not the outright potential for Jesse Minter to be a one-and-done as his losing streak hits five games after being by the winless Chargers, his former team.
If it feels like a lot just 10 games in, well, that’s because it is. And, yeah, that hot seat should be getting a little toasty. You sell Lombardi Trophy contention and can’t beat the worst team in the NFL – by far – at home on MNF, welcome to reality. Life comes at you fast in the NFL .
It also begs massive questions about how coaches were being evaluated for years inside The Castle and how the once-proud franchise finds itself among the dregs of the NFL facing a roster crisis and a salary-cap crisis and an unprecedented contractual situation with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, having to recruit him to stick around Baltimore at a time when those in charge are lacking leadership, solutions and with little to bank on inside that locker room moving forward.
Since reaching the AFC title game in 2023, it’s been all downhill, and in reality there are at least five coaches who have been in Baltimore since then that could make the case as superior head coaching options to what Minter and this novice staff are providing right now. Personally, any of the names listed below would carry a stronger profile and pedigree to what the Ravens are getting from their current head coach – who was sold at the solution right now, in the present, for a team in Super Bowl-or-bust mode, not some lengthy rebuild.
He is the unicorn. He is the chosen one on the defensive side of the ball in the way Sean McVay is on offense and of course the Super Bowl went through those two last year. Left after two years as Ravens defensive coordinator, went 10-7 and nearly made the playoffs his first year making no big moves and running it back with Pete Carroll’s players.
Lombardi Trophy in Year Two. No way Steve Bisciotti was going to replace Harbaugh with him after giving away that Championship Game to the Chiefs … but he was The Special One. The fact that Minter hung out with him as young assistants in Baltimore means nothing, and Macdonald would never be associated with the $160M disaster that is the Ravens’ 2026 defense (which is markedly worse than the 2025 version that got Zach Orr fired ).
He might win NFL Coach Of The Year with the Browns. That young team plays with more fire and passion and will than Minter’s veteran’s ever will. Cleveland in the best fourth-quarter team in the NFL; Baltimore remain the biggest chokers in the NFL. Monken helped Jackson to his two best seasons by far and blended his passing concepts with the vestiges of the Greg Roman run game.
He has verve and he can motivate players and no one is shattering expectations more than he is with a team that might mess around and make the playoffs. Damn near pulled off a comeback road win with Shedeur Sanders at QB against a Saints team that pulled off a double-digit comeback against Minter in Baltimore.
This ain’t even close to being a discussion. Minter had a nice run as a college head coach. Jets should have hired him as HC when they hired Adam Gase. Ravens could have promoted him to the big chair in Baltimore. Already kicked Minter's ass once and De Costa-ed the Ravens in the process, overcoming a 10-point deficit in the second half.
Amazing run as a head coach with the Colts. Overcame cancer, hired a tremendous staff. Players ran through walls for him. You wanted to keep this team together and try to get over the top real quick in a few years? Coulda hired Pagano.
There would be standards and guardrails coming in. He already knew what he was up against with DeCosta and Sashi Brown in charge and could thread that needle. He understands their quirks and was part of better defenses from the past in Baltimore than Minter ever was and could have helped them discover young coordinators to take over for him.
It would have been better than this, people .
He brought the secret sauce to this coaching staff when he got together with Macdonald for that epic 2023 run. He added his flair to the Wink Martindale installed packages Macdonald was operating with and helped that defense win the triple crown for the first time in NFL history – led the NFL in sacks, takeaways and points allowed.
Former standout at Maryland, and a native Marylander, he played the game at a high level and can relate to players in a way Minter never could -  a star for Terps who got a cup of coffee with Washington in the NFL. Deep personnel background trained to scout with the Bears and extensive coaching experience and now doing a tremendous job with the Giants as their defensive coordinator.
The Ravens foolishly let him leave as DC for the Titans in 2024 – the front office viewed Zach Orr, a former Ravens player , as more one of them and Wilson was an outsider. Harbaugh thought enough of his work to hire him in NY. The Terps should hire him as their head coach and he’s going to be getting head coaching interviews soon enough.
Has far more presence and heft than Minter in terms of getting up in front of an entire 53-man roster. Has a far more diverse background too, while Minter is merely an extension of the Harbaugh brothers for the most part.
Yeah, the message was stale, and he had to go and I am not going to pretend that wasn’t the case … But imagine Bisciotti flipped the script - blew up the personnel side and kept Harbaugh with Monken and maybe a new defensive coordinator, you can’t tell me that wouldn’t be better than this.
They wouldn’t have given up 33 or more in three-straight games, while failing to score 14 in four straight in losing five straight. Not with this cupcake schedule.
They wouldn’t lead the NFL in offensive penalties and pre-snap penalties. Yeah, maybe they would still choke game away, because that was part of the brand, but this has been adject failure since Minter’s first home game in charge. Say what you want about Harbaugh’s many faults, but he had a doghouse and wasn’t afraid to shake things up, while Minter has offered nothing but empty rhetoric in that regard.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Six Bills Coaches Considered 'Rising NFL Names to Watch' for Future Head Coach Jobs
full_text:
Each and every year, NFL insider Tom Pelissero lists off several coaches around the league who could garner interest for head coaching vacancies down the road and this year's list has six Buffalo Bills coaches on it.
Pelissero's list is divided into two sections , with one naming all of the coaches who could receive interest in 2027, and another listing potential candidates in 2028 and beyond.
All six of the Bills coaches who were listed by Pelissero fell into the second category and were headlined by first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard .
Here's a look at the other five:
Of all of the coaches listed, Leonhard should be considered the favorite to land a head coaching gig first, simply because he is already a defensive coordinator.
While past performance isn't the only factor teams consider when hiring a new head coach, it's definitely an important part of the equation and Leonhard doesn't have a great resume as a play-caller yet given Buffalo's struggles defensively in 2026 .
But he's still very early in the process and if he can turn things around from now through next season, it's possible teams will come calling in 2028.
Given their experience, we would peg Hardegree and Egorugwu as the Bills assistants who are most likely to get a look from teams as coordinators, which is the best path to eventually landing a head coaching gig.
Hardegree is the only coach on the list who has actually served as an offensive or defensive coordinator when he was the interim offensive coordinator for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2023.
Egorugwu is in his second stint with the Bills after he served as the team's defensive quality control coach in 2017 and then as the assistant linebackers coach from 2018-20.
Egorugwu's NFL coaching experience dates back to 2015 and only Hardegree (2014) has been coaching in the league longer.
Terrell's NFL coaching career dates back to 2018, and on top of being a wide receivers coach, he was a passing-game coordinator in Arizona, which is a step above from just being a position coach.
The son of former NFL head coach Pat Shurmur, Kyle spent stints with Washington, the Kansas City Chiefs and Cincinnati Bengals during his playing career before moving into coaching. His NFL coaching career began in 2022 with the Bills , when he was a defensive quality control coach.
Valai's pro coaching career goes back to 2018, when the Chiefs hired him as a defensive quality control coach. He went back to college in 2019 and only re-emerged in the NFL this year.
While it remains to be seen if any of these assistants will ever get a better gig, it's at least good to see the Bills have a lot of promising coaches on their staff.

title: Bills' Training Camp Fan Favorite Earns Second Pro Opportunity, Chosen in UFL Draft
full_text:
He had a cup of coffee with the Buffalo Bills this past summer, but this rookie offensive tackle apparently isn't satisfied.
Duke product Bruno Fina, who signed an undrafted free agent contract with the Bills back in May, was amongst those players selected in the United Football League's 15-round draft that unfolded this week in St. Louis.
The UFL's Colorado Stampede picked Fina at No. 91 overall (Round 12) on Thursday.
Bruno Fina is Colorado bound 💪 pic.twitter.com/j5YT5kKyiA
This past spring, Fina instantly became a Bills Mafia fan favorite as a result of his surname. His father, John, played 10 seasons for the Bills after being chosen No. 27 overall in the 1992 NFL Draft .
Fina Sr. displayed his excitement over the news by sharing the Stampede's draft post on X. The Bills' former first-round pick knows the joys of professional football firsthand after making 160 career appearances, including 12 playoff games, for the organization that drafted him.
The 24-year-old Bills' legacy, a true roster long shot, moved inside to offensive guard during training camp. Fina appeared in all three preseason games before being waived on cutdown day .
In the exhibition opener in Orchard Park, Fina saw four snaps on offense to go along with five special teams reps against the Carolina Panthers. His snap count increased  the following week on the road against the Cleveland Browns. He logged 24 offensive reps plus five more on specials.
Fina, who spent the past two seasons as Duke's starting left tackle, did the Bills a solid in the preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
With the Bills attempting to preserve veteran backup Lloyd Cushenberry , and starter Connor McGovern on the shelf, Fina stepped up to start at center against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Fina logged 65 snaps on offense in the 28-27 win.
Defensive back MJ Devonshire was selected by the Dallas Renegades at No. 83 overall (Round 11).
Devonshire, a 2024 seventh-round pick by the Las Vegas Raiders, signed with the Bills' practice squad last December after the team lost Ja'Marcus Ingram to the Houston Texans. Buffalo gave him a futures contract in January, but subsequently waived him in May.
Punter Jack Stonehouse was selected one pick prior to Fina, going to the Renegades at No. 90 overall.
Stonehouse, a Syracuse product, met with the Bills at the NFL Combine. He subsequently interviewed with Buffalo at their local pro day in April. The Bills, however, opted to draft Florida's Tommy Doman to compete for primary punting duties .

title: Three Keys to Bills Avoiding Trap-Game Letdown vs. Dolphins
full_text:
With a win against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, the Buffalo Bills will improve to 9-1 for the first time since 1991.
Thirty-five years, three additional gut-wrenching losses in the Super Bowl, and countless other heartbreakers have since occurred between when Buffalo last achieved that regular-season mark following a game against the Green Bay Packers on November 10, 1991, and now, but that doesn’t change the fact that fans and media members are drinking the Kool-Aid , so to speak, when it comes to first-year head coach Joe Brady’s chances of leading his team on a deep postseason run later on in January.
And, it’s hard to blame anyone for doing so.
Following the recent trade for veteran playmaking safety Amani Hooker, the right recipe appears to be in place for quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills to finally get over the proverbial playoff wall in a mere matter of months.
However, before anyone can really start focusing on anything past the regular season, the Western New York franchise still has plenty of business to attend to as the calendar creeps toward December.
The team’s remaining schedule is anything but easy—and very well may be the toughest slate of the whole year for Brady’s crew—so it’ll be important for Allen and Co. to stockpile as many more wins as possible against opponents like the Dolphins, which is a team still searching for its second win of the 2026 campaign under fellow rookie head coach Jeff Haffley.
With that in mind, considering that Buffalo has a primetime matchup versus the Kansas City Chiefs on tap for Thanksgiving night in Orchard Park on Thursday, is there a possibility of the Bills falling victim to the classic “trap game” on Sunday afternoon against Miami?
But, if the team wants any chance at obtaining the No. 1 seed in the AFC entering the playoffs down the road, then it’ll be crucial to avoid any such event from unfolding this weekend.
So, keeping that in mind, here are three keys to the Bills avoiding letdown against their divisional counterpart.
For the fourth consecutive game since the team’s much-needed bye week last month, Buffalo’s defense is being gifted the opportunity to face a backup quarterback instead of the opponents’ preferred option at gunslinger.
So, while it’s true that Bills’ defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s youthful unit is putting up some historically impressive numbers in recent weeks, there’s no denying that the statistics have been somewhat skewed.
However, the team can only play who’s in front of them, and so far the defensive players have been handling business in November.
That must continue on Sunday versus Dolphins’ rookie quarterback Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL start on the road last week at Lucas Oil Stadium against the Indianapolis Colts that ended in a 24-22 loss.
Regardless of the opponent, narrowly missing out on a road win in your first NFL start is impressive for any player.
And, McCord (17-of-32 for 209 yards ) did so while falling just 11 passing yards shy of breaking former Dolphins’ quarterback Ryan Tannehill’s debut passing record ( 219 yards ), which he set in 2012. He also rushed for one touchdown.
So, needless to say, while the young former Syracuse University star won’t be shell-shocked in Western New York this weekend with one road start already under his belt, it’ll be crucial that Leonhard’s cast of players make him feel unwelcomed and uncomfortable for four quarters.
Pass-rushers like Gregory Rousseau, rookie T.J. Parker, and captain Bradley Chubb, who is a former Dolphins’ defender, will need to help make sure that’s the case.
Although the Bills convincingly came out on top against the New York Jets last week with a 31-12 road victory, the team actually only possessed a four-point lead at halftime on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in case any Bills Mafia members may have forgotten.
And, despite the game never seeming to be truly in question against the Jets, Buffalo must avoid having a similar sluggish start on offense against Miami head coach Jeff Hafley and coordinator Sean Duggan’s defense this week at home.
The Dolphins recently held the Detroit Lions’ high-powered offense, which ranks fifth in the NFL in points per game this season heading into Week 11, to just 19 points back on November 8, so they’re certainly a capable unit on defense despite some inconsistencies at times.
Overall, the team is ranked 10th in total yards allowed at just 320.6 per game according to FOX Sports ' database, as well as seventh in passing yards allowed at 202.1 yards per game, so it might be more of a struggle for Allen and his group of playmakers versus Miami than some might think.
Buffalo can’t afford to let anything wonky happen this weekend, which could certainly happen if the offense can’t start the game out quickly and smoothly.
With that in mind, Allen must take what the defense gives him and not force the issue.
After recently placing veteran defensive lineman Zach Sieler on injured reserve nearly two weeks ago, as well as fellow interior defenders Zeke Biggers and Jordan Phillips on the list just on Tuesday, there’s no denying that the Dolphins are hurting up front on the defensive line entering Sunday’s matchup in the AFC East.
And, pairing that with the fact that the team is only ranked 18th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game to the opposition at a rate of 118.4 yards per contest on the ground, it would appear that the Bills might be hard-pressed to find a better avenue to take to exploit their divisional foe’s defense this weekend.
So, while it’s true that veteran running back James Cook’s high-usage rate might be a bit of a concern to some heading toward the latter part of the regular season, it’ll be critical that Buffalo maintain a healthy ground attack this weekend at Highmark Stadium.
Effectively keeping the clock rolling versus Miami and trying to quickly move on to Thanksgiving’s showdown with Kansas City isn’t a bad plan of attack.

title: Bills' Updated Week 11 Injury Report: Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid Remain Out
full_text:
Six starters are amongst those affected.
In all, five Buffalo Bills ' defensive backs, one linebacker and two tight ends have been noticeably limited by injury during the practice week as preparations for a November 22 home game take shape.
With the Miami Dolphins set to visit Orchard Park for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday, the Bills held their second Week 11 practice on Thursday.
For the second day in a row , starting cornerback Christian Benford, inside linebacker Dorian Williams, safety Damar Hamlin and tight end Dalton Kincaid were all non-participants.
New safety Amani Hooker and third tight end Jackson Hawes practiced on a limited basis again. Hooker's status is much less worrisome being that his knee did not cause him to miss a single snap in his Bills' debut .
Meanwhile, starting safety Cole Bishop and slot cornerback Dee Alford both saw their status upgraded on Thursday.
Additionally, backup running back Ray Davis, a new addition to the injury report in Week 11 , was limited by a hamstring.
Alford is moving through the concussion protocol after being ruled out due to a head injury early in the fourth quarter to this past Sunday.
After missing Wednesday's walkthrough , Alford returned to the practice field on Thursday in a limited capacity. He was wearing a red non-contact jersey.
Bishop, who was sidelined for only three plays against the Jets, had his shoulder examined on the sideline. He appeared to aggravate it late in the fourth quarter while diving towards Jets' running back Braelon Allen on a screen play.
The Bills listed Bishop as limited for Wednesday before upgrading the starting safety to full participation on Thursday.
Benford and Williams left the Week 10 road game early, and neither returned.
"There's always concern whenever guys are nicked up or aren't able to finish a game," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady.
The Bills ruled out Benford with a groin injury early in the fourth quarter. The starting boundary cornerback missed the game's final 18 snaps. Now, he's missed back-to-back practices.
Even if the severity proves to be mild, it may be overly optimistic to expect a player to recover from a groin injury in only six days. Still, it's not impossible for Benford to be ready by Sunday.
"You guys saw it with Spencer Brown last week. Christian's always gonna do everything he can to get ready to go. If he can't, I feel confident with the guys on our depth [chart] to be able to step in like they have," said Brady.
Williams played deep into the third quarter before leaving with a calf injury. He was ruled questionable to return in the fourth quarter, but the Bills rolled with fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr the rest of the way.
As for Hamlin, Buffalo initially listed the safety as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough. That status has since been adjusted to match the DNP he posted on Thursday.
Dealing with a toe injury, Hamlin was seen wearing a boot on his right foot while using a mobility scooter following Wednesday's practice.
Already on the injury report last week for an ankle, Kincaid injured his thumb against the Jets. It appeared to occur on a third-quarter red zone play when the tight end engaged with a defender down field. He saw only two more snaps the remainder of the game.
Kincaid has played through injuries in the past, but a thumb injury can obviously prove tricky for a pass-catcher. It wouldn't be surprising if Buffalo holds him out against the Dolphins.
Meanwhile, Jackson Hawes was added to Wednesday's injury report after the fact with a shoulder issue. He participated in both practices thus far, albeit in a limited capacity.

title: Buffalo Bills' Legend Andre Reed Receives Ultimate Honor from Organization
full_text:
Andre Reed spent 16 seasons in the NFL, 15 of which were with the Buffalo Bills. A fourth-round pick out of Kutztown in 1985, Reed developed into one of the most trustworthy wide receivers on a dominant offense that made four consecutive trips to the Super Bowl.
Reed, who was the No. 1 target for the legendary Jim Kelly, recorded 941 receptions for 13,095 yards, and 86 touchdowns . He's currently the franchise leader in all three of those categories and no one has even come close to threatening his numbers. He was also a stud in the postseason with 85 receptions for 1,229 yards and nine touchdowns in 21 playoff appearances.
The Bills have always appreciated the hard work Reed gave them throughout his career, but now, they're going to show it. Buffalo announced that Reed's No. 83 will be retired and hung in the rafters . Reed will be honored during a home game at some point in 2027, which is when his number will be officially retired. He will be the first player to have his number retired at the New Highmark Stadium.
With so many players on an NFL roster, it's not often teams decide to retire numbers. Some might not hand out numbers that belonged to former stars out of respect, but the official retiring of a jersey number is rare. That's why the Bills, despite their long history, have retired just three numbers. All of those were players who played alongside Reed during their stretch in the 1990s.
Jim Kelly and Thurman Thomas were on hand for the announcement, and Kelly said Reed is a huge reason he had the success he did during his career. He also felt Reed should have been honored before now, but is just happy to see his former teammate join the elite club.
"He's one of the main reasons I'm up on that wall," Kelly said via Mike Maynard of the Bills' official website . "He's one of the main reasons I'm in the Pro Football Hall of Fame; it takes both of us. When your quarterback goes in, usually you're probably going to have a receiver or two go in… To have Andre for my whole career was just totally awesome."
"I thought it should have been done a few years ago, but I'm glad that it's getting done, and I'm glad I'm able to be here and celebrate his going on the wall to join me, Bruce and Thurman."
Thomas was also complimentary of his former teammate, saying he had a toughness that you don't see every day.
"You saw his work ethic when we were in training camp together for 12 years, like, yeah, that guy is special, and he was a big part of our run to try to win a Super Bowl here. There aren't too many people today that go over the middle as much as Andre Reed did back in the day. He took a lot of punishment, but he was always there for us," Thomas said.

title: Three Bold Predictions for Bills' Divisional Test vs. One-Win Dolphins in Week 11
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills (8-1) will play the Miami Dolphins (1-8) for the first time in 2026 this Sunday, and it's an opportunity for them to make a few tweaks.
The Bills will face Kyle McCord , a quarterback making his second career start.
Such a situation presents an opportunity to make some bold predictions as Buffalo must take care of businees against a divisional foe before embarking on its most difficult stretch of the season.
The 2024 NFL MVP posted these conditions in Week 10 against the New York Jets, going 11-for-21 for 196 yards , a touchdown and an interception as Buffalo let the Jets hang with them for most of the game.
The Dolphins defense has also been playing well as of late, coming off back-to-back performances in which they allowed just 19 points to the Detroit Lions and pick-sixed Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10.
Buffalo will also want to run the ball with James Cook early and often against a Dolphins defense that has the sixth-worst EPA per run play in the league, meaning Allen won't have to do much if the running game is effective.
Indianapolis, which has the sixth-worst pressure rate in the NFL, sacked the new Miami quarterback six times in his NFL debut. Buffalo, meanwhile, has the fifth-highest pressure rate in the league , which means that even more sacks are likely to come.
Miami, meanwhile, has set up McCord to fail with running back De'Von Achane, their receptions leader in 2025, out with a torn ACL, and it allows pressures at the second-highest rate in the league.
The Bills picked up four sacks of Geno Smith and Cade Klubnik while facing a quality Jets offensive line, and if Buffalo controls the pace of the game, the defense will earn the right to rush the passer and continue its strong run of form .
Playing off of the Bills likely getting pressure on McCord, one of Indy's sacks was a strip-sack that was recovered in the end zone to start the second half, and if similar pressure comes, a defensive score could follow.
Another area where Buffalo could get in the end zone is from the return game. While last year's All-Pro, Ray Davis, isn't being used often, with just 12 kickoff returns, Greg Dortch also poses a threat to go the distance.
Dortch is averaging 27.2 yards per kickoff return this season, good for seventh among players with at least 15 returns, and his 9.2 yards per punt return gives him the same mark.
Miami has also allowed 31.2 yards per kick return this season, the most in the league by 3.3 yards, and their 10.1 yards per punt return allowed is also bottom-10.

title: Josh Allen's Expectations Facing One-Win Dolphins Don't Include 'Cakewalk' for Bills
full_text:
If anyone has a reason to take the Miami Dolphins for granted, it's Buffalo Bills ' quarterback Josh Allen.
Since his rookie season in 2018, Allen has practically owned Miami.
The Bills' ultimate dual threat has consistently registered gaudy stats, highlighted by a 14-3 win-loss record, over 17 games, including a 2022 playoff victory.
Allen has accounted for 45 passing touchdowns and five rushing touchdowns over that sample, which is equivalent to a full regular season.
On November 22, the Bills (8-1) will host the one-win Dolphins (1-8) for the first time in the new Highmark Stadium, but Allen doesn't foresee a proverbial cakewalk in Week 11.
"If you were looking at strictly records, one win compared to eight. You turn on the tape of that defense, they're doing some fantastic things. I'm not just saying that," said Allen during his practice week press briefing.
Allen sounded similarily to Bills' head coach Joe Brady when he addressed the notion of winnable games .
Although he didn't reference it in his comments, there's no doubt that Allen vividly remembers last year's 30-13 loss to the Dolphins in November.
Furthermore, despite the brutal win-loss record, Miami has been rather plucky this season. Since Week 5, they covered the point spread against the Minnesota Vikings, New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts while pushing against the Cincinnati Bengals.
"They are very sticky. That scheme is freakin awesome. Their head coach has them playing extremely hard. They're very in sync," said Allen, a five-time NFL MVP finalist. "They've played a few good offenses, some of the top offenses in the league, this year, and they've done a really good job with them."
Residing amongst the top one-third of the league, the Dolphins rank 10th overall in total defense (320.6). Their pass defense (202.1) is seventh overall.
"This isn't just a cakewalk. It's a team that's hungry. They're looking to upset, but the way their defense is playing gives them a shot in every game that they're in," said Allen.
Bills' veteran wide receiver Khalil Shakir appears to wholeheartedly agree with his quarterback.
“This is not a walk in the park by any means. It's a team, like you said, they're young, they're hungry, they play hard. They want to be successful," said Shakir. "They're going to do everything that they can to make plays. We just have to make sure that we're focused and detailed and dialed in like every other game."

title: Why Buffalo Bills Should Rest Three Key Injured Defensive Backs vs. Dolphins
full_text:
Heading into the Buffalo Bills ' Week 10 game against the Miami Dolphins, the Bills' injury report is full of key contributors , but no other area is struggling with this more than the secondary.
Among those injured are cornerbacks Dee Alford and Christian Benford and safety Damar Hamlin. Despite there being a bunch of ailments in the defense's backfield , there may be little concern for Sunday's game against Buffalo's AFC East rival.
There are multiple reasons as to why Buffalo should exercise caution with them for Sunday's game, and it is likely in its best interest that the team should do so.
Benford suffered a groin injury on Sunday against the New York Jets. He did not return to the game and has not practiced on Wednesday or Thursday. This season, he and rookie Davison Igbinosun lead Bills corners with 33 tackles and Benford is second on the team with eight passes defended.
Alford also got banged up against the Jets, suffering a concussion and is currently in the league's protocol, as he made it to the practice field on Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. Earlier in the year, he also missed two games with an ankle injury .
Hamlin, meanwhile, is dealing with a toe injury, and his run defense is vital to the team's success. However, behind Cole Bishop and trade acquisition Amani Hooker, Hamlin's defensive snap count dropped from 44 in Week 9 to 17 in Week 10 (92% to 24%).
While these wounds may be troublesome on paper, when one sees the circumstances, people can breathe easy.
The Dolphins will start quarterback Kyle McCord in his second career start, which has to be music to the ears of Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, who has Buffalo's defense on an outstanding pace since the bye week.
McCord went 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, and on Sunday, the biggest mismatch will be up front. Miami's offense allows the second-highest pressure rate in the NFL, while the Bills' defense pressures opposing passers at the fifth-highest rate.
If Buffalo's front can rattle McCord, the secondary won't be tested against a Miami receiving core that features three rookies, and it'll help the injured defensive backs and youngsters like Igbinosun and 2025 first-rounder Maxwell Hairston prepare for what is to come.
The Bills' schedule cranks up to 11 starting on Thanksgiving, as in a five-game stretch, they play the Kansas City Chiefs, the New England Patriots, the Green Bay Packers, the Chicago Bears and the Denver Broncos.
The game against the Patriots may be a freebie with quarterback Drake Maye out long-term with an ankle injury, but the other opponents have either dynamic passing attacks or a knack for coming up big in the clutch. That spells trouble for a secondary that has not been tested since the bye.
Kansas City and Denver will be the biggest games against Buffalo in the race for the AFC's No. 1 seed, and the Bills would do well to ensure everyone is rested and ready to go on Thanksgiving to get a good start.
Miami is not a good opponent, as many say they are trying to "ethically tank" for the first overall pick, so Buffalo should not worry about resting their injured defensive backs for the gauntlet awaiting them.

title: Bills' Practice Update Creates Concern for Dalton Kincaid, Three Others vs. Dolphins
full_text:
They're not trending in the right direction as the Buffalo Bills prepare for a Week 11 home game.
The Bills appear in danger of being without three starters and one key backup when they host the Miami Dolphins for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff in November 22.
For the second day in a row, tight end Dalton Kincaid, cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams were absent from Bills' practice .
Additionally, safety Damar Hamlin, who was seen using a scooter while wearing a boot following Wednesday's walkthrough, was not present during the media-viewing portion of Thursday's practice in Orchard Park (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
Although Kincaid and Benford are holdovers from last week's official injury report , both are dealing with new injuries in Week 11. Meanwhile, Williams and Hamlin are new additions coming out of the November 15 win over the New York Jets.
In a positive development, starting slot cornerback Dee Alford was present after missing Wednesday's practice. He wore a red non-contact jersey as he moves through the concussion protocol.
Here's what we know about each of the four key contributors who were not spotted at Thursday's practice.
No longer listed with the wrist injury that originated in Week 9, Benford is now hampered by a groin issue.
He left the Week 10 win over the Jets, and the Bills officially ruled him out for the remainder of the way early in the fourth quarter. While the severity of the growing injury is not publicly known, it seems over optimistic to expect Benford to heal in time for Sunday's game against Miami.
"You guys saw it with Spencer Brown last week. Christian's always gonna do everything he can to get ready to go. If he can't, I feel confident with the guys on our depth [chart] to be able to step in like they have," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady on Wednesday .
It's not known when, or how, Hamlin sustained the toe injury that landed him on the Week 11 injury report.
Hamlin, who played 17 defensive snaps against the Jets, was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough. While the limited status suggests the issue could've popped up during practice, it's unusual to happen in a walkthrough setting.
There is speculation that Hamlin is dealing with turf toe on his right foot, but regardless of what the official issue is, it's discouraging to see him in a walking boot.
Already on the injury report after his ankle got twisted up against the Minnesota Vikings on November 9, Kincaid now has a thumb injury to deal with, too.
Kincaid, who made a momentum-building 54-yard catch early in the third quarter against the Jets, played only 45 percent of offensive snaps in Week 10. He has a history of playing through injuries, but missing back-to-back practices does not bode well for his Week 11 availability.
It's unknown exactly when Williams was injured, but he was in the game late in the third quarter. The Bills officially tabbed the starter as questionable to return early in the fourth quarter.
After exiting, however, Williams, who tallied 32 defensive snaps, remained sidelined the rest of the way. Fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr replaced him for the remainder of the 31-12 win.

title: Joe Brady Claps Back at 'Winnable Game' Notion After Bills Reporter's Question
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills will host the one-win Miami Dolphins on November 22 with the seven-win Kansas City Chiefs on deck for a Thanksgiving night meeting.
Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady, however, isn't looking ahead, and he's not planning to hold anything back against the Dolphins.
"The only game is this week. If we ever approach it differently, then we're not doing everything we can to win this football game. We'll worry about next week, next week," said Brady when asked if he'd consider possibly resting an injured player against Miami.
"I think it's always been disrespectful to the players and the profession when people think one game is less important or is gonna be easier," said Brady.
While the Bills (8-1) are currently a 16.5-point home favorite on the betting line ( per DraftKings ), and own a 14-3 straight-up record against the Dolphins (1-8) when Josh Allen starts at quarterback, Brady expects nothing less than a dog fight.
"I never focus on the records. It's all about what the tape shows. You watch a lot of the [Miami] games, you watch in the fourth quarter and it's seven-point games. It's them having leads," said Brady.
In back-to-back weeks before their bye, the Dolphins lost by five points on the road against the Minnesota Vikings before a 31-24 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals .
In Week 8, the Dolphins squandered a second-half lead in a five-point setback to the New England Patriots. Last time out, they dropped a two-point decision on the road to the Indianapolis Colts.
As an underdog, Miami covered the point spread in three of those four losses and pushed against the Bengals.
"You can never just wake up and think you can just roll out of bed and be able to go out and execute. It's too hard," said Brady. "Credit to the guys in that we have in that locker room for not approaching it any differently."
The Bills experienced a letdown at the hands of the Dolphins a little more than one year ago in Miami.
In what was billed as a highly winnable game for Buffalo, the Dolphins posted a 30-13 outright victory as 7.5-point home favorites. Brady, who is in his first season as head coach, was the Bills' offensive coordinator that day.
"It's always drove me crazy whenever people were like 'hey, that week, or this week, is a winnable game.' I don't know what the hell that means," said Brady on Wednesday in Orchard Park when asked about the challenges of being a favorite.
Brady, who has the Bills off to their best start since 1991, is focused sorely on Miami right now.
"There's never been a week that I've coached that I've worked any less or I felt like it was any easier, I didn't come out of the game absolutely exhausted from the chess match of it," said Brady.
Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday at Highmark Stadium.
