title: 3 Traps the Panthers Must Avoid vs. Scuffling Ravens
full_text:
Following a much-needed win against the New Orleans Saints, the Carolina Panthers return to Bank of America Stadium. Carolina has struggled at home, currently sitting at 1-3 when playing in Charlotte, with their lone win coming against the Detroit Lions in Week 4.
Now looking for their second home win of the season, the Panthers welcome the Baltimore Ravens . What was supposed to be an AFC favorite has turned into an injury-riddled roster that's started three different QBs this season.
Baltimore enters Carolina as low as ever, losing at home, on Monday Night Football to the Los Angeles Chargers, who were 0-8 going in.
That said, Baltimore will come in with a strong sense of urgency and desperation. Entering Week 11, Carolina and Baltimore both have four wins, but Baltimore has one more loss and doesn't have its bye week until Week 13.
The game will be close; even without Lamar Jackson, Baltimore can beat the Panthers. Here are three traps Carolina can't fall into against the Ravens on Sunday.
Brissett hasn't been effective this season, posting 2059 passing yards, 10 touchdowns, 8 interceptions, and a 48.9 QBR. That QBR ranks 23rd in the league.
Brissett was benched in the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys, who have the NFL's worst defense. However, Brissett has shown throughout his long career that he can be productive, even last season with the Cardinals.
Carolina can't play too aggressively or try to force turnovers; Brissett is still competent enough to take what defenses give him. Carolina's defense ranks 8th in passing yards allowed per game, so on paper this should be a good matchup, but nothing is guaranteed.
Time of possession will be the leading factor in this game and Baltimore's best path to victory. The offense starts and ends with Derrick Henry, and if he's able to get downhill and continue to gash Carolina with 7- to 12-yard runs, then this game could go south quickly.
The best part of Baltimore's offense attacks the weak point of Carolina's defense. The Panthers rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed per game. Henry hasn't ripped off too many explosive runs this season, but Carolina will be doomed if he dictates the pace and leads Baltimore to 7- to 10-minute scoring drives.
Carolina has continued to shoot itself in the foot all season with self-inflicted penalties. In fact, it's only gotten worse, as the Panthers set a franchise record in Week 10 against the Saints, committing 17 accepted penalties for 152 yards.
The Panthers lead the NFL in penalties, sitting at 87 for 787 yards. Derrick Henry is enough of a problem as is, but letting the Ravens stay on the field because of penalties will ensure long drives and likely a loss against a very beatable Baltimore squad.

title: Panthers Send Clear Message About Chuba Hubbard as Jonathon Brooks Nears Return
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are getting closer to having Jonathon Brooks return to the backfield, but that doesn't mean Chuba Hubbard is going to lose his featured role on the team.
Hubbard has become a star offensive player for Carolina, and as head coach Dave Canales recently said, the team is comfortable with him being the featured running back. In fact, Canales compared Hubbard's workload to that of Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit, which can give us some insight into how the team views the veteran running back.
Josh Norris posted on X about the comments from Panthers head coach Dave Canales on the workload of running back Chuba Hubbard. Norris said fantasy managers shouldn't worry about Brooks' return just yet, pointing to Canales' comparison of Hubbard's workload to that of Gibbs in Detroit.
Dave Canales comparing Chuba Hubbard's workload to Jahmyr Gibbs fantasy folks, I would not sweat Jonathon Brooks returning https://t.co/vIGsoRn9WL
This is what Canales had to say on Panther Talk about the workload of Chuba Hubbard this season compared to that of Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit.
Canales then said: "I'm not comparing him to Jahmyr Gibbs. I'm just saying the Lions really give Jahmyr a lot of touches. In the pass game, in the run game. That's their guy. And we have our guy."
Canales was not stating that Hubbard and Gibbs are identical players. He was trying to get across the point that the Panthers have a lot of confidence in Hubbard and feel that he can handle a lot of different roles on offense.
Hubbard had a career-high 172 scrimmage yards against the Saints in Week 10, including 92 rushing yards, 80 receiving yards and two touchdowns. His 32 touches in the game were also a career high. Hubbard's big performance helped Carolina get back in the win column.
His production this season is a big reason why the Panthers are viewing him as a key piece of their offense.
While it's great to have former second-round pick Jonathon Brooks on the road to recovery from multiple injuries throughout his NFL career, the Panthers are likely to keep utilizing Hubbard as the featured back in Carolina even after Brooks returns to the backfield.
Brooks is working his way back from a groin injury that landed him on injured reserve after Week 2. He was a full participant in practice this week and appears to be getting close to returning for the Panthers against the Ravens. Brooks' potential return has already become a major fantasy football storyline.
Just because Jonathon Brooks is returning to the Panthers' backfield doesn't mean that Chuba Hubbard's role will be reduced. Canales also mentioned that the team is very aware of Hubbard's workload throughout the week and makes sure that other running backs are being used so Hubbard stays fresh.
Having Brooks in the mix is certainly a positive for the Panthers, as it gives the team another talented back to bring in for a change of pace, but it doesn't have to take away from Hubbard's featured role. Carolina has previously discussed how it plans to use both running backs.
What Canales did say, however, was that the team believes Hubbard can handle a lot of responsibility on offense. He compared Hubbard's workload to that of Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. This does not mean that Canales believes Hubbard is the same player as Gibbs, but rather that the Panthers have a lot of trust in their running back.
Of course, Brooks could eventually take on a larger role once he gets comfortable on the field, but that doesn't mean the team is going to move away from Hubbard. He's the running back that the coaching staff has the most trust in, and that's not going to change anytime soon.
For now, Hubbard looks like he will remain the running back to watch for the Panthers, even with Brooks' return to the backfield. Canales' comments make it clear that the Panthers are very confident in the veteran running back and trust him to continue handling a significant workload.

title: Panthers QB Bryce Young Still Deserves to Be in MVP Conversation
full_text:
MVP never truly goes to the player who represents the most value to their team. That is semantically part of the debate, but it is ultimately an award designed for the best quarterback. Matthew Stafford undoubtedly wasn't more valuable to his team than Drake Maye was to his last year.
If that were the case, Bryce Young would have a strong argument. Sunday's win was the first in ages where it felt like the offensive load wasn't entirely on Young's shoulders. The Carolina Panthers aren't a truly good team, but their success is almost always tied directly to Young's play.
It's a shortcoming of the roster building, but it also showcases how valuable Young really is. And when you analyze the stats behind his value, it's clear that Young isn't just really valuable to the Panthers.
He is one of the most valuable quarterbacks in the entire NFL for their teams.
Early on in the season, Bryce Young's stats made him a legitimate MVP candidate. He was never the favorite, but his odds consistently rose, and he found himself on MVP ladders pretty frequently .
That level of play tapered off, though it has way more to do with an offensive line and rookie play-caller that have regressed than anything Young has done. Most QBs wouldn't survive with an inconsistent OC and a line yielding a 50% pressure rate.
But even still, as the numbers have dipped to good but not elite , Young quietly deserves to be in the conversation even still. If we're talking about how much heavy lifting a quarterback is actually doing, few are doing more than Young.
Which QB is carrying their offense? Here's the gap between QB WAR and the rest of the offenses WAR. Jordan Love is carrying his team the most this year, and should absolutely be in the MVP conversation. https://t.co/NjT3UGYGDj pic.twitter.com/dH0OIoA3pE
That's right. According to this WAR graph, Jordan Love and C.J. Stroud have been the only QBs doing more for their offense than Young, and it's an offense ranking 10th in yards per game and 12th in points per game.
Young's QB WAR is sitting at a very solid 1.58, but unlike those with similar or better numbers (excluding Love and Stroud), Young's teammates are providing 0.94 WAR, giving him the third-largest gap there.
Last Sunday's game was an outlier. Overall, Young is carrying this offense more than most QBs are carrying theirs. That should make him an MVP candidate, and it should put to rest the questions over whether an extension is warranted. It is, and it's probably just fine that it's in the $50 million range.

title: Panthers' Midseason MVP Surprisingly Isn't Bryce Young
full_text:
This season, Bryce Young has shown flashes of brilliance for the Carolina Panthers during the first half of the 2026 NFL season. However, Bleacher Report doesn’t see him as being the most valuable player for the team so far this season. In their midseason MVP selections for each NFL team, the website Bleacher Report named linebacker Devin Lloyd as the most valuable player for the Carolina Panthers so far this season. This is an interesting choice considering the Panthers offense is largely built around the team’s young quarterback Bryce Young.
According to Bleacher Report's midseason MVP selections , Lloyd has recorded 63 tackles, two sacks and three interceptions. One of those interceptions was returned for a touchdown. Derrick Brown, Jaelan Phillips and rookie safety Zakee Wheatley have also had strong seasons, but Lloyd's production has made him difficult to overlook.
The Panthers have needed players on defense to step up, particularly during games when the offense has struggled to score. Lloyd has been one of those players. He has contributed against the run and in pass coverage, giving defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero another dependable option in the middle of the field.
Three interceptions from a linebacker is an impressive accomplishment. According to the Panthers' official breakdown of the Week 10 win over New Orleans , Lloyd became the first Carolina linebacker to record at least three interceptions in a season since Luke Kuechly in 2017.
Lloyd also earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors in Week 2. His performance has helped give Carolina a playmaker who can impact games in more ways than simply stopping the run.
The first half of the season has included some really good games from Bryce Young. He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns against the Chicago Bears. He also passed for 329 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's win over the Detroit Lions. Against Denver in Week 9, Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns.
Those performances show what Young can do when the offense is clicking. He remains a huge part of the team's success, and the Panthers need him to continue improving as the season moves forward.
However, his performance against New Orleans in Week 10 was much quieter. Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or an interception. He helped lead the team on the final drive, setting up the game-winning field goal, but the defense had to carry the offense for much of that game.
The Panthers have several players who deserve consideration when discussing the team's most valuable contributors. Young has had some strong performances on offense, but Lloyd's production on the other side of the ball is difficult to ignore.
Brown and Phillips have also been important pieces of the Carolina defense. Phillips, in particular, had a big performance against New Orleans in Week 10. He recorded five tackles, three tackles for loss, a sack and a fumble recovery in the Panthers' 20-17 victory. His performance earned him NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors.
Bleacher Report's decision to select Lloyd over Young may surprise some Panthers fans. However, the linebacker has made an impact throughout the season and has given Carolina a consistent presence on defense. If he keeps producing during the second half of the season, he will have a strong case to remain the team's most valuable player.

title: Why Derrick Henry Doesn’t Pose a Major Threat to New-Look Panthers D
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are coming to town , and they're bringing Derrick Henry with them. Ordinarily, that might pose a huge threat to the Carolina Panthers this week.
The Panthers give up the 10th-most rushing yards per game, and they're prone to letting people run all over them. They have two games surrendering 250 rushing yards or more. The Chicago Bears nearly had 300 in Week 1.
That doesn't inspire confidence for the Panthers, but there are a few reasons no one should be overly concerned about this week's matchup.
Are the Panthers worried about Jacoby Brissett? That is highly unlikely, which means that they can stack the box against Derrick Henry more often than not. The Panthers have a strategic advantage there.
The winless Los Angeles Chargers just held the Henry-led rushing attack to 16 yards. It is the third-fewest in a game in NFL history, and the Panthers are a much better team than the Chargers.
CBS Sports' John Breech pointed out that without Lamar Jackson, Henry has 81 touches for 246 yards. His 3.0 average per touch in five games is the lowest for any player in a five-game span. Ever.
Without Jackson, Henry looks very human. And the Panthers likely aren't worried about human running backs. Despite getting Trevor Etienne back and having Alvin Kamara, the New Orleans Saints ran for 49 yards.
Under Todd Wash , the Panthers have a much stronger run defense. In the two games since Ejiro Evero's firing, the Panthers have allowed 136 yards combined on the ground. Opponents are averaging 2.72 yards per attempt against this new-look defense.
Jaelan Phillips is back, too. That would normally be bad news for Jacoby Brissett, and it is. But it's also bad news for Derrick Henry. Phillips was the second-highest graded run defender in the NFL in Week 10.
He sets the edge better than most Panthers OLBs, and he forces running backs to either get past him (which they're not) or cut back inside to Derrick Brown, Lee Hunter, and others. It's a winning formula. So far, it's worked out impossibly well.
If you look at fantasy, Henry has a strong projection, and the Panthers are marked as a green matchup. That is skewed, and it's misleading. The Panthers probably have the advantage here, and Henry shouldn't strike fear into their hearts like he once did.

title: Fantasy Football Advice: To Keep or Trade Panthers WR Jalen Coker
full_text:
It's been an up-and-down season for the Carolina Panthers , both in real life and in fantasy football as well. Bryce Young started the year as a top-10 QB; Tetairoa McMillan had the best Week 4 performance of any receiver, and Jalen Coker was the WR1 after Week 1.
The highs have come in short spurts; the rest of the season has been mediocre or just bad from a fantasy perspective. Focusing on Coker, he's avaeraging 10.8 points in PPR, and is a top 40 fantasy receiver entering Week 11.
Coker is coming off his worst game of the season, posting just 0.3 fantasy points against the New Orleans Saints. The only Panther who was actually productive against the Saints was Chuba Hubbard, posting 34.2 points.
Coker hasn't scored over 10 fantasy points since Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Since then, his highest point total was against the Packers, posting 9.6 points.
On a good team, just under 10 points is passable at flex spot, assuming the receiving core is good around Coker. The question around Coker and the Panthers as a whole, when it comes to fantasy, is if there's any reliability for the rest of the season.
Coker has been far from reliable, which means his trade value isn't high.
If Coker was going to be traded off a roster, it should've been done after Week 1, or after Week 6. The only scenarios where trading Coker makes sense are if a team needs a running back more than receivers, or if someone in a league has multiple players on bye, and is willing to give up a solid player in return who isn't playing this week.
There's no real value on Coker right now, realistically, he's not starting in a 10-man league this week, and would be a flex in a 12-man league. Now four weeks removed from his last double-digit performance, the best thing to do with Coker is to keep him on the bench, especially this week against a good Ravens defense.
Potential trade targets if a team needs a running back include Broncos RB Jonah Coleman, Washington RB Rachaad White, 49ers receiver Keenan Allen, or Vikings RB Aaron Jones Sr.
Trading Coker would require specific circumstances, but entering Week 11 , it's smarter to wait and see if he can string together a few good games or even one great performance, making him a sell-high candidate.

title: Two Stunning Stats Show Jeffery Simmons' Massive Impact on Bears
full_text:
There is no doubt that the addition of defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons has made a huge impact on the Chicago Bears.
Simmons was acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans before the deadline that saw the Bears give up a historic package that included two first-round picks.
That's a lot, no doubt, but if things keep heading in the direction they are now in terms of what Simmons is bringing to the table, that deal might end up looking like a steal .
ESPN's Courtney Cronin recently provided two eye-opening stats during an appearance on "Good Morning Football" that perfectly spell out just how much Simmons is making a difference on the football field.
When Simmons is on the field, the Bears are giving up just 4.5 yards per play. When he's on the sideline, Chicago's defense is permitting 11.4 yards per play.
The good news is, Simmons doesn't get off the field much. Over his first two games with the Bears, the four-time Pro Bowler has played 87.3% and 97.1% of the snaps.
Then, there's Simmons' impact on the Bears' blitz rate, which has dropped a whopping 20% since he was added, Cronin noted.
The reason for the drop in blitz rate has to do with the fact that the defensive line is getting more push and pressure with Simmons included, so defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can drop extra players into coverage, which helps out the back end.
Simmons does more than just that, though. He also commands so much extra attention upfront that he frees his fellow line mates up for more one-on-one matchups and opens up holes for blitzing defenders to wreck plays in the backfield.
Over his first two games, Simmons has tallied five pressures and two sacks. The latter mark is one more than Bears interior defenders had combined before Simmons' arrival.
If Simmons gets another sack in Week 11 versus the New Orleans Saints, it will be the first time in his career he has recorded a sack in three consecutive games.
We knew Simmons was going to be a game-changer for the Bears with his elite talent, but the veteran defensive lineman has proven to be quite the leader , also.
"One player told me it feels like they got a captain at midseason for the way Simmons has commanded respect in that locker room and the way that the defense just rallies around him," Cronin reported.
For Simmons, he says being a leader pretty much comes naturally to him and it's something he doesn't think a lot about.
“It’s one of those things where I don’t, I’m not going to say I don’t think about it, but I don’t think about it. I think about just how can I continue to be the best version of me, and that’s on the football field and off the football field," Simmons explained, per Bears Insider's Michal Dwojak .
It's pretty rare for a player to meet the kinds of expectations that Simmons had after how much the Bears gave up for him, but it's clear he's well on his way to doing just that.

title: Bears' Defense Dealt Tough Blow After Kyler Gordon Injury Update From Ben Johnson
full_text:
We've been monitoring Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon all week since the team emerged from the bye.
When the Bears hit the practice field on Monday and Tuesday, Gordon was not spotted for either session, and head coach Ben Johnson revealed Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury that had the team labeling him as day-to-day.
Then, on Wednesday, Gordon was listed as an estimated non-participant in practice and he didn't take part on Thursday .
Now, it looks like Gordon isn't going to play in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints.
On Friday before practice, Johnson revealed that Gordon would sit out yet again, and he does not expect the slot cornerback to suit up on Sunday at Soldier Field.
"Ben Johnson said that he does not expect Kyler Gordon (shoulder) to play against the Saints. He will not practice today," ESPN's Courtney Cronin relayed.
Gordon appears to have suffered his injury in the first half of the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9, when he briefly exited to get checked out before returning.
The fact that he was given the day-to-day label suggests it isn't anything serious, so hopefully his absence won't extend beyond this week.
But any time Gordon is injured, it's an ominous sign, as the veteran defensive back has had issues staying on the field during his career.
Gordon has never played in 17 games in his career and he missed all but three games last season and has only played in four of the team's nine (and soon to be 10) contests.
With Malik Muhammad having practiced fully this week, it looks like he is going to make his return after a two-game absence, which is especially huge considering the circumstances.
With Muhammad back, the Bears could opt to deploy him in the slot, where he had a ton of success earlier in the season before Gordon returned from injury. From there, the Bears would likely put Tyrique Stevenson on the boundary in place of the rookie.
The preferred approach would be to shift Cam Lewis from safety to the slot, where he has also played well this season, and move Elijah Hicks into a starting role next to Dillon Thieneman.
That's the preferred approach because then the Bears can keep Muhammad opposite Jaylon Johnson and they would be less reliant on the struggling Stevenson.

title: The One Penalty Refs Never Call Against Bears Opponents and Why
full_text:
When the Bears take the field Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, it will mark one full calendar year since a particular positive happened for their offense .
It might seem surprising a specific positive hasn't happened for this long considering h ow deadly a Ben Johnson offense can be. However, this isn't a catch or a run or a touchdown. There are other people and circumstances involved.
The Bears have not benefited from a defensive pass interference penalty since Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson was detected interfering with tight end Cole Kmet for a whopping 6-yard flag on Nov. 23, 2025.
The Bears have not received the benefit of a DPI walk-off this year and they are the only team not to have received one. Bears opponents have had the far less punitive holding or illegal contact calls but never pass interference in that period.
Bears offense on third down: 45.3% overall (4th) 3rd and medium: 2nd 3rd and long: 7th 3rd and short: 26th Red zone: 55.3% (18th), 70.6% since Caleb returned (7th) Kyle Monangai is the short yardage answer. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/RQlNcp6kLG
In fact, since Johnson became head coach they have benefited from only two such calls. The other besides the one on Wilson was a 19-yarder against Giants cornerback Deonte Banks last year. That's it, just two DPI walk-offs against Bears opponents in the Johnson era.
If this was a penalty rarely called in the NFL it would be understandable how a team could have no DPI calls and only two the previous season is almost beyond explanation.  Denver has benefited this year from 13 DPI calls, Dallas and Arizona 11 each. Teams had eight DPI calls this year when playing the Packers, four in games with the Lions and two with the Vikings.
Going into Week 11, there had been 173 DPI penalties called in this NFL season and not one got walked off against a Bears opponent.
Pass Interference Penalties Drawn - CHI hasn't drawn a SINGLE DPI all season - SF has drawn just 10 yards on 3 DPIs - DEN leads the league with 169 yards on 12 DPIs pic.twitter.com/GdnlEboSxi
Last year Bears fans on social media caught wind of how few flags and penalty yards were being assessed against the team's opponents. They set the internet on fire complaining. Eventually the trend did turn somewhat. Bears opponents had the ninth fewest total penalty flags, but only the two DPI calls.
Is it the officials' dislike for the Bears? It seems rather unlikely.
Are Johnson's pass plays not putting receivers in situations where the defense must commit a penalty to prevent yardage? That's a possibility.
Bears vs. Officials…AGAIN 😡 New episode out now: https://t.co/RHZqDz89HB pic.twitter.com/9dpgH4GN9f
Considering the Lions  offense in 2024 benefited from only one 24-yard DPI call while Johnson was offensive coordinator, this theory appears to carry weight. However, it wasn't that way the previous two seasons for the Lions, as they benefited from seven and eight DPI calls and finished with the 10th most called on opponents both seasons. Johnson was coordinator then, too.
Are the Bears not getting the type of play from their wide receivers to challenge defenders enough?
That's always a possibility, but they are 12th in passing despite Caleb Williams missing three full games, and they finished 10th last year in passing yards. They've been doing something right.
The Bears Big 3 in Explosive plays (20+ yard receptions) 1. Rome 15 2. Luther 14 3. Colston... 2
They have four receivers in the top 100 at average separation distance per reception, but this isn't an unusual amount. At least it's not like they're all running wild and free behind and away from defenders so that no flags could be thrown. Kalif Raymond is No. 9 in the league at 3.96 yards of separation, Luther Burden 34th at 3.37 yards, Colston Loveland 47th at 3.14 and Rome Odunze 98th at 2.61. These distances are per NFL Next Gen Stats.
Williams has often been criticized by critics with being too conservative with the ball, and then running with it too much. Yet, anyone who saw last season down the stretch could not seriously consider this the primary reason.
Williams' season was a thrill ride as much as it was football. There could be a little truth to this, though, and that is evident in the fact he is No. 1 in NFL history for fewest interceptions per his first 1,325 pass attempts. Then again, before Johnson came to Chicago Williams was quarterback for all of 2024 and the Bears benefited from nine pass interference with him starting every game at quarterback.
The NFL’s most explosive deep threat WRs. I compared deep target % with explosive reception % to see who consistently creates big plays vs. who just gets a ton of deep looks. The top right are receivers that turn a high share of their catches into explosive plays. pic.twitter.com/U7W7Oxr0ru
Johnson and Williams both have said they don't like 50-50 balls. Many DPI calls come on those type of plays, but it's not as if those type of passes never occur with the Chicago offense.
Then there are the officials.
It is true that the Bears have had a negative differential in yards walked off for penalties every single season since 2021.
It's also true that from 2021 through last week they have a penalty yardage differential of minus-972, worst in the NFL for that time period. This year's total of minus-109 doesn't seem like it's going to rectify the — shall we call it — discrepancy.
After 15 straight games without a DPI call and one full calendar year, maybe Johnson or players need to start getting on Brad Rogers' officiating crew right away from the sidelines on Sunday and point out what Saints defensive backs are doing illegally, whether they actually are doing anything wrong or not.
🎤 Bryce Young discusses one of the most bizarre officiating moments of the Panthers’ 26-21 loss to the Broncos. Officials allowed Carolina to run an entire play without blowing the whistle before going back to review Denver’s challenge of the previous play, ultimately… pic.twitter.com/sMaqGunKEQ
It's worth trying the old squeaky wheel theory when this type of one-sided trend is working against them. The Broncos fans and organization whined incessantly last year about how they were at minus-306 yards, the worst differential in the NFL. The Bears were second-worst at minus-292. This year the Broncos are plus-169 in differential after all of their complaining, the fifth-best penalty yardage differential in the league. Meanwhile, the Bears remain in the negative, like every other year since 2020. They're 25th in yardage differential this time. Sunday's opponent, the Saints, have been flagged eight times for pass interference, tied for 16th most. So, it's not like the Saints are getting flagged every other play for this penalty but it's sure a lot more times than Bears opponents have drawn this flag over the past two seasons. So maybe Soldier Field fans will be treated to the rare occasion on Sunday.
Fans will continue to believe the “NFL is rigged” as long as the league continues to allow game changing, objectively WRONG calls from officials In no world is this play defensive pass interference, if anything, it’s offensive PI All flags should be reviewable under 2 mins NFL…
With numbers like these, it's no wonder there are always Bears fans on the internet complaining about how the team keeps getting the short end of the stick when it comes to penalty calls. It's not paranoia  when it happens over and over and over and over.
It's hard to see how a team as strong as the Bears have been under Johnson — 18-8 overall and 18-6 since Week 3 of the 2025 season — can continue the same trend bad Bears teams have had for negative penalty yardage.
It really defies logic when a powerful offense can't benefit from officials walking off a single pass interference call in a full year, considering how that penalty itself has become virtually a total guess in terms of what's legal and what isn't based on how it gets called week to week across the NFL.
2026: -109 (25th)…

title: Bears Suggested as Landing Spot for 2-Time Super Bowl Champ Who is Set to Be Waived
full_text:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson recently admitted that even though the trade deadline has passed, the team is will continue looking for ways to improve the roster.
Nothing earth-shattering in Johnson's statement, as every team is always keeping tabs on things throughout the year for opportunities to improve the roster.
"(Looking for talent) continues still, it's just different now that it's not a trade deadline, it's more the waiver wire and how can we continue to improve our roster. It's continuous," he explained .
Well, it just so happens that a two-time Super Bowl champ is about to hit the waiver wire and "Up and Adams" host Kay Adams thinks the Bears are a possible landing spot.
On Thursday, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that not only has Reid requested his release, but the New Orleans Saints are going to oblige the veteran safety's request.
"The  Saints are planning to grant the release requested by safety Justin Reid, as both sides agreed this would be mutually beneficial," Schultz reported.
The release has not been made official yet, but once it happens, Reid will be subject to waivers, as all players are after the trade deadline.
The problem for the Bears if they're interested is that their 7-2 record puts them pretty far down in the waiver order, so their chances of getting Reid aren't great.
The Bears certainly don't have a dire need at safety, especially if Coby Bryant can get back from his knee injury this season, but it certainly wouldn't hurt to add more depth.
We still don't know for sure if Bryant will be back this season , and we know that Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury currently, isn't exactly reliable from a health standpoint.
No, Gordon doesn't play safety, but one of the Bears' options to replace him if he does miss time is Cam Lewis, who has played snaps both at safety and in the slot when needed this season.
Reid, who has proven to be an asset in coverage, against the run, and when asked to blitz, is a great fit for Chicago because he can offer depth at both spots thanks to having played snaps at box and free safety and slot cornerback during his career.
Then, there's the experience factor. Not only does Reid have nine seasons under his belt, he has also appeared in 13 playoff games and owns a pair of Super Bowl rings from his time with the Kansas City Chiefs.
Having the opportunity to add a player of Reid's caliber at this stage of the offseason is rare, so the Bears would be wise to consider it as they make a push to a Super Bowl in 2026.

title: How Press Taylor Knew Caleb Williams Would Shrug Off Four Picks
full_text:
The Bears have looked Caleb Williams over after his four interceptions in the last game and are not expecting some sort of confidence crisis from their quarterback, who turned 25 years old on Wednesday.
Offensive coordinator Press Taylor admitted they needed to see in the game if the picks had some sort of effect on Williams' play, but they saw nothing.
"One of the things you always ask for as a play caller is what's the look in his eyes," Taylor said. "Is he gonna be shaken by this? That's not something we've seen from Caleb. So, we're going to keep firing.
"If it was a re-occurring issue over it, you know, we're missing this coverage, we're missing the coverage-tell whatever it is, we're being tricked by things, that would be a different discussion."
#Bears QB Caleb Williams is on pace to finish 2026 with these stats in 14 games: • 3,607 passing yards • 257.7 passing yards per game (would be team record) • 68.7% completion rate • 19 passing TDs • 12 interceptions • 95.4 passer rating pic.twitter.com/inBnMrVpQ5
Williams insisted on Tuesday the picks would not drag him down, mainly because of how they occurred.
"Two of them were funky," Williams said. "One was a bad decision and the other one, the ball popped up in the air."
🚨 CALEB WILLIAMS IS THE NFL'S MOST BLITZED QUARTERBACK! 🐻⬇️ According to multiple analytics providers, opposing defenses are blitzing Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams more frequently than any other QB in the NFL! 📊 StatRankings: 41.4% blitz rate 📊 PFF reported… pic.twitter.com/xvTCrzakVZ
Two of the passes occurred on attempts to throw the ball away but instead of having it strike the ground, defenders got to it beforehand. They were a matter of improperly executing the throwaway rather than a pass.
"The ball just didn't hit the ground in those situations, which it has in the past," Williams said. "But obviously it's frustrating. You don't want to go out there and throw four picks. That's never what you want to do. That's never what the plan is, obviously.
The Saints defense generates pressure on 33% of QB dropbacks, per @statyxio . Caleb Williams leads the entire NFL in clean-pocket completion percentage at 80.6%. If the Saints can’t get pressure on Caleb, they’ll be in for a long day. pic.twitter.com/QICV7MF1h9
"The biggest thing in the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me personally, I don't want to let my teammates down. That's always big for me. In those situations, I feel like I did. So that's the frustrating part that lingers. I think that's what lingers. But the other half of it is, like I said, I've thrown three picks before in big games. I've thrown picks before, picks that seal the game and things like that. So I'll move on from it, I've moved on from it."
Undaunted, WIlliams made a key 38-yard pass to wide-open Colston Loveland to set up the winning field goal.
Williams has 18 career interceptions. It's the fewest in NFL history for any quarterback with at least 1,325 pass attempts.
Every quarterback will say he's put interceptions in the rear-view mirror, but Taylor said coaches found it easier to accept Williams had moved on based on his past.
"Like, that's something that's been his thing," Taylor said. "You think of the late-game plays he's able to make, things like that, he's demonstrated that over and over.
Dear Caleb Williams, You threw 4 picks and your defense gave up 3 points and 62 yards combined between each of those 4 drives. Dak throws one pick and his defense instantly gives up 7 points and 90 yards on one drive. How? pic.twitter.com/MMK2Gg7fIa
"So as you see it over and over and it continues to reveal itself, then you're going to trust him more and more with that type of situation. And every game is really a learning opportunity for all of us to learn how everybody responds to certain situations as a unit, as an individual, whatever that may be."
The wildness was in direct contrast to the drastic improvement in Williams' completion percentage this year, from 58.1% to 68.7%. A more tangible confirmation than words would be in how Williams comes out Sunday against New Orleans when he is making throws into tighter coverage.
Williams went 15-of-26 for 172 yards with an interception in last year's 26-14 win over New Orleans, one in which Chicago ran for 222 yards.
Dawg... TJ Ward really doesnt like Caleb Williams for some reason... 🤔 #DaBears pic.twitter.com/c7esOPS373

title: Caleb Williams' Popularity Reaches New Heights Based on Latest Jersey Sales Figures
full_text:
It appears that Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is reaching a new level of popularity in his third NFL season.
Jersey sales are a pretty good way to determine just how popular a player is because, typically, the more popular a player is, the more jerseys they sell.
Well, it would appear that Williams is reaching new heights in 2026. According to Fanatics, via ESPN's Adam Schefter , Williams' jersey was the top-selling one among NFL players in the first half of this season.
Williams finished ahead of the Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (No. 2), Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (No. 3), Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (No. 4) and San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner (No. 5).
The Bears went into the 2026 season hoping that Williams would take the next step after two uneven seasons to begin his career.
Well, Williams is in the process of doing that just. The former No. 1 overall pick has played like one of the best signal-callers in the NFL this season.
Williams has made a big jump with his accuracy , which was a major point of emphasis during the offseason. After completing 58.1% of his passes last season, Williams sports a completion rate of 68.7% in 2026.
If not for his missing three games due to injury , Williams would be on pace to top his yardage output from last season and become the first 4,000-yard passer in franchise history.
As a result of Williams' top-notch play, the Bears are sitting pretty with a 7-2 record and look like a true Super Bowl contender .
And, Williams' ascension has almost certainly contributed to the rise in sales of his jersey.
Barring a total collapse, Williams is well on his way to securing a monster extension in the near future. He will be eligible for one after this season.
Before the season, general manager Ryan Poles said he wanted Williams to give the franchise the green light to ink him to a lucrative, long-term deal.
‘‘It’s good to almost feel like you’ve got it,’’ he said. ‘‘If you go with a traffic light, it went red as a rookie to yellow. You can creep forward a little bit and start having some of these conversations to anticipate it. But we need him to give us a green light.
‘‘I think we’ll find out this year about his progress.’’
Contract extensions for top players usually reset the market and that could happen with Williams. At the very least, he's going to come very close.
The current high-water mark belongs to Kansas City Chiefs superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes, whose historic deal is worth a whopping $448 million and $64 million per year, per Over The Cap .
Allen comes in second in total value at $330 million, and Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott ranks second in annual average at $60 million per.
Williams should land somewhere in between Mahomes and Allen in total value, and Mahomes and Prescott in annual average.

title: Bears' Thursday Injury Report: Updates on Monangai, Burden, Simmons, Gordon & Muhammad
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have put out their second injury report of the week ahead of the contest against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.
The Bears' first injury report of the week on Wednesday was an estimation, as Chicago did not practice yesterday after holding sessions on Monday and Tuesday.
Five players were included on the initial injury report, including two cornerbacks, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon, running back Kyle Monangai, wide receiver Luther Burden and defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons.
Let's see where all five players stand on Thursday.
It's status quo for everyone on the injury report this week, as Gordon, Monangai, Burden, Simmons and Muhammad saw no change from their participation levels on Wednesday.
Earlier in the day, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen gave some good news on Simmons, who he expects to play despite being limited thus far.
"I don't anticipate any issues with him," Allen said of Simmons, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
It's now officially time to be concerned about Gordon's status for Sunday after another day of no participation in practice . Gordon didn't suit up for the sessions on Monday and Tuesday, either, before he was an estimated non-participant on Wednesday.
Earlier in the week, head coach Ben Johnson characterized Gordon as day-to-day. Johnson added that "we'll see" about Gordon's status for Sunday, so he's truly up in the air.
As of right now, Gordon is likely headed for a quesitonable tag, at best.
As for Muhammad, Burden and Monangai, they remain on track to play in Week 11.
Burden suffered a concussion in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but Johnson told reporters he cleared the concussion protocol, so Burden is good to go.
Muhammad has missed each of the last two games with his toe injury, and Monangai missed the last five with his. Both of their returns will be huge for the Bears.
Muhammad has been the Bears' best cornerback this season amid the struggles of his position mates, Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, and he was someone we nomiated as a candidate for the team's non-QB MVP as a result.
Like Muhammad, Monangai has been the best at his position on the team, also. Monangai has more yards per carry and yards per game than D'Andre Swift, and he has just 252 less yards on the ground despite playing in five less games.

title: Bears Get Clarity on Jeffery Simmons' Knee Ahead of Sunday's Game vs. Saints
full_text:
Chicago Bears fans got a little bit of a scare after the Bears' Wednesday injury report was released. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was listed as a limited participant with a knee injury. It must be said that this injury report was an estimation as the Bears held a walkthrough instead of a full practice, but fans never want to see their superstar defender on an injury report for any reason, least of all for a knee issue.
Luckily for those fans, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen came in with a dose of good news during his media availability on Thursday. According to a tweet from Bears insider Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune , Allen said that he "does not anticipate any issues with Simmons' availability."
Even though Chicago's defense had overachieved relative to their low expectations at the start of the season, their formula was clearly not sustainable. They only got consistent pressure by sending blitzers at the quarterback, and for just about any defense that isn't schemed up by Brian Flores, that's going to eventually lead to giving up big plays in bunches.
But ever since the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons , Dennis Allen has been able to open up his entire playbook. Now that he can finally get consistent pressure with just his front four, Allen can keep his linebackers and defensive backs in coverage more often, muddying up the picture for opposing quarterbacks and creating more opportunities for takeaways.
Simmons' presence also creates a ripple effect on the rest of the defensive line. In the two games since trading for him, both Montez Sweat and Austin Booker have looked significantly more disruptive. Additionally, one recent poll of NFL analysts showed a consensus of the Bears being the NFC's Super Bowl team this year, and a big part of that is due to Simmons' presence.
It could be argued that only one player is more integral to the Bears' Super Bowl aspirations than Simmons, and that's quarterback Caleb Williams. High praise indeed for a defensive tackle, but that's just how good big No. 99 is. He's a consistent force on the field and a strong candidate to be the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year.
So Bears fans can breathe a sigh of relief. His appearance on Wednesday's injury report appears to be nothing serious, and he should be good to go to wreck the New Orleans Saints' game plan on Sunday.

title: Are 7-2 Bears Built Like an NFC Champion? How They Compare to Last Five Winners
full_text:
Few teams came into the 2026 NFL season under more pressure than the Chicago Bears. Their breakout season in 2025, which culminated in a triumphant Wild Card victory over the Green Bay Packers before falling in the Divisional round, was great, but the Bears had to prove that they weren't a one-hit-wonder. Sustained success was the goal, and that meant, at minumum, another playoff appearance in 2026.
After 10 weeks of football, that bar already feels far too low. The Bears are 7-2 and Caleb Williams has played like a Top 5 quarterback. A playoff berth is virtually assured, and now the fans and media are sizing the Bears up to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl.
With that in mind, let's take a look at the last five NFC champions (Seattle Seahawks, Philadelphia Eagles, San Francisco 49ers, Eagles, and Los Angeles Rams) and see how this Bears team stacks up by the numbers. One point to remember is that some of the Bears' stats will be based on a 17-game pace since the season is only halfway over.
Total yards allowed per game
Passing yards allowed per game
Rushing yards allowed per game
At first blush, the offensive numbers don't look great for the Bears. While their total yards per game is better than three of the previous five NFC champions, their points-per-game average is the lowest of the group. Yards are great, but they don't win games if they don't get you into the endzone.
They're also on pace for 32 turnovers, which would be four more than the next most of recent NFC champions, the 2025 Seahawks. While not a terribly large gap, it's concerning when you consider that the Seahawks last year were defined by an elite defense that carried a so-so offense. The 2026 Bears were supposed to be the opposite of that.
On the other side of the ball, things don't look much better for Chicago, but that's more understandable given the expectations for this unit at the start of the season. Additionally, the Bears' trade for Jeffery Simmons seems to have them moving in the right direction.
Their 20.4 points per game and 310.9 yards per allowed are both only better than the 2021 Rams, but their 91.1 rushing yards allowed per game is the best of the bunch. They're on pace for only 25 takeaways, which would tie with the Rams and Seahawks for fewest, but their 49-sack pace would rank third.
Give Dennis Allen some credit. His defense has been overachieving for most of the season, and he did that without a bona fide start on the defensive line for the first seven games. He's also dealt with a revolving door of starting defensive backs due to injuries, and he still hasn't been able to use his star safety Coby Bryant, who continues to make progress on his injury recovery , albeit slowly.
The numbers don't look great for the Bears when comparing them to the previous NFC champions. In the most important stats, they're lagging behind at least four teams. However, there's important context for fans to consider before writing the Bears off as a hopeless cause.
For one thing, Caleb Williams' Week 2 injury robbed the Bears of their superstar quarterback for three games. Sure, the Bears beat two bad teams without him, but a pathetic performance in their 31-7 loss to the Packers in Week 5 hurts their averages. Even that Week 2 game can be waved away given the torrential downpour that severely limited the offense. And adding insult to injury, Williams' injury came on a play in which he had a clear lane to waltz into the endzone for the go-ahead score.
Williams' absence hasn't been the only problem for the Bears. Kyle Monangai has missed the last five games with a turf toe injury, and Chicago's ground game has suffered quite a bit. D'Andre Swift is a good player, but he isn't built to carry an entire rushing attack by himself. Monangai's return in Week 11 should see the Bears' ground game get back into form.
Last of all, as I already mentioned, the Bears have only played two games with superstar Jeffery Simmons. His presence immediately changed how opponents have to plan for the Bears and is opening up the field for his teammates.
While comparing teams across seasons is never an apples-to-apples affair, it has to be admitted that the Bears' numbers don't look great compared to the last five NFC champions. However, none of those five teams lost their starting quarterback for three games, nor did their best defensive player not arrive until Week 8.
I'm confident that, when we revisit these numbers at the end of the season, that the 2026 Bears will stack up much better with these other teams. Whether that leads to a Super Bowl berth, however, remains to be seen.

title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow's 9-Game Pace is Better Than Most Recent MVP Winners
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is a torrid pace rarely seen in the NFL. Before the clock strikes midnight Monday evening, he could be on one never witnessed at all.
Burrow has had four total touchdowns in five consecutive games, a streak matched only by Peyton Manning during the Hall of Famer’s MVP season in 2004.
Matching – and exceeding – MVP-level performances is something Burrow has been doing all season.
And by playing back-to-back island games with the 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid in Week 9 and a 38-18 dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, Burrow has surged to the betting favorite to win the MVP.
"Joe Shiesty better be in your MVP conversations," left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. posted on X after the Atlanta win. "Just tore up the dirty birds in Madrid!!"
While Burrow was reserved after throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the win against the Steelers, there was a level of chest pounding after the Atlanta win in which he threw for three touchdowns and ran for another while throwing for 271 yards against Atlanta.
"I wanted to come out and put on a show for everybody, and show what the excitement of the NFL can be," Burrow said. "And the NFL is really all about the stars and players making big time plays. And so you saw Ja'Marr Chase, you saw me, you saw Tee Higgins, you saw a lot of great players out there doing great things, and hopefully people took notice."
The show has multiple acts.
His stats through nine games are among the best by MVP-winning quarterbacks in recent history.
Since running back Adrian Peterson won the MVP in 2012, the last 13 awards have all gone to quarterbacks who, in most cases, had smaller numbers through nine games than what Burrow has done in leading the Bengals to a 7-2 record.
Burrow’s 74.7 completion percentage leads the group. Only Lamar Jackson in 2023 (71.5) and Manning in 2013 (71.0) topped 70 percent.
Burrow’s 27 touchdowns through nine games are third most on the list. Manning had 33 in 2013, and Patrick Mahomes had 29 in 2018.
The current numbers posted by Burrow also rank in the top five in passer rating, yards per attempt and rushing touchdowns.
His 117.4 passer rating is fourth best, trailing only Manning 2013 (121.0), Aaron Rodgers in 2014 (120.1), and Matt Ryan in 2016 (119.0).
His three rushing touchdowns are tied for fourth behind Cam Newton in 2015 (six), Jackson in 2019 (six) and Jackson in 2023 (five).
And his 8.2 yards per attempt are fifth, ranking behind Ryan in 2016 (9.5), Mahomes in 2018 (9.2), Manning 2013 (8.8) and Rodgers in 2014 (8.7).

title: Analyst Predicts Bengals-49ers Super Bowl Rematch, Praises Offensive Line
full_text:
The Bengals dominated the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in front of the world and solidified themselves as legitimate Super Bowl contenders this season. Rich Eisen went so far as to predict that the Bengals would make the Super Bowl and face off against a familiar foe for their third matchup in the big game.
Eisen initially predicted that the Rams would face off against the Bills at the start of the season. However, he annually gives himself a chance to change his pick at Thanksgiving based on the current standings of the league.
"I'm going to be given a chance at a mulligan for my preseason Super Bowl choices of at the time Bills versus the Rams, if my fingers on that mulligan chess piece right now, I'm going to say Bengals versus the 49ers," Eisen predicted.
Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins were obvious reasons for Eisen's pick, but he said the performance of the offensive line and defense was why he changed his pick from the Bills to the Bengals.
"The reason why I am choosing the Bengals over an 8-1 Bills team quarterbacked by Josh Allen is because yes obviously Joe Burrow is the MVP frontrunner, and sure Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are playing out of their skulls," Eisen said. "But two things you could not say about the Joe Burrow Bengals together, they're protecting Joe Burrow who against the Steelers looked like he was having a ham sandwich before he chose which wide open receiver to throw to, and their defense has been 1,000% improved."
Burrow, meanwhile, has maintained that it is far too early to celebrate given that they are only midway through the season.
While the Bengals currently lead the AFC North with a record of 7-2, he stated that seven wins are still not enough and that the team has a long way to go.
"As big a win as we've had here in a while, but we got a lot of football to be played," Burrow said after the game. "We're clicking right now, but seven wins certainly isn't gonna do anything for you and nobodies winning championships in week 9, so it's a big win but we got a long way to go."

title: 'I'll Be Lying if I Say There Wasn't Any Hard Feelings' - Bengals Jonathan Allen Eyes Return to D.C.
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Jonathan Allen began his career in Washington as a first-round pick in 2017 and played eight seasons for the franchise before it all came to a turbulent end.
The rift resulted in Allen requesting a trade prior to the final year of his contract in 2025, but teams knew the relationship had deteriorated beyond the point of any possible return, so they simply waited for his release to try to sign him without offering compensation.
Allen played for Vikings in 2025 and signed with the Bengals in March.
And though Allen faced his former Commanders teammates last season in Minnesota, Monday night will mark his first trip back to the city where he played the first eight seasons of his career.
Allen called his departure from Washington a business decision but admitted there is a part of him that took it personal.
“I'll be lying if I say there wasn't any hard feelings, but at the end of the day that's the NFL,” Allen said Thursday afternoon after practice. “It's a great game, and it's a terrible business.
“Is it something I hold against them? No,” he added. “Is it something that in the moment really hurt? Absolutely.”
Allen signed a three-year, $51 million contract with the Vikings in March 2025, but cut him in a salary dump after just one season.
The Bengals signed to a two-year, $25 million deal in March, and a month later they traded for Dexter Lawrence and dropped him next to Allen to instantly create one of the best defensive lines in the league after also adding edge rusher Boye Mafe in free agency.
Allen already has more sacks this season (four) than he had in 17 games with Minnesota last year (3.5), putting him on pace to challenge his career high of nine, which he set in 2021, his first of back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons.
Everything in Cincinnati, from his defensive teammates to the coaches, the scheme and elite offense and consistent winning has Allen feeling rejuvenated as he stares down his 32nd birthday in two months.
“This year has been a really special year for me as far as just the players around me, the coaches around me, the position I've been put in,” Allen said. “It’s something that I'm just not taking for granted.”
The Bengals played against Allen last year in Minnesota and in 2024 with Washington.
Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor said he didn’t know Allen personally, but he was aware of his impact at Alabama in college and what he had accomplished in the league, and he was one of the team’s top targets in free agency.
"Playing against him was not fun, ever,” Taylor said. “I've held him in high regard, and I think our whole department had. So it isn't a surprise that we're getting the production we're getting out of him.
“You see all the times he was a captain in Washington, and so I knew Alabama, Washington, he's got that leadership ability,” Taylor continued. “We watched a lot of interviews on him. I always felt that way. And then you get him in the locker room and he's exactly who we hoped he would be. He's a big impact on the D-line room, the whole defense, the whole team."
With Lawrence drawing double teams – at least – on nearly every sack, Allen has been freed to defeat one-on-one matchups, and he’s thriving.
In addition to his four sacks, Allen has 26 pressures. That ranks 12th among defensive tackles.
His win percentage of 14.2, measured by Pro Football Focus, ranks seventh. And his pressure percentage of 6.8 is ninth.
“I think he’s rejuvenated because he’s kind of gone back to his roots,” defensive coordinator Al Golden said, referring to Allen’s pass-rushing roots. “I can’t tell you back in March that we thought that he would give us as much as he’s given us, but certainly he has exceeded anything that we could have wanted.”
For all of his individual accolades in Washington, Allen never experienced a winning season until his final one with the Commanders in 2024.
He suffered a torn pectoral muscle in Week 6 and missed nine games. But he fought his way through rehab and returned ahead of schedule for the final two games of the regular season and the team’s run to the NFC Championship Game.
All of the losing led up to a profane interview with the media in 2023 where he said some things he admits now he shouldn’t have.
“I try not to live with regrets because we all have things we wish we could have said better at the time,” he said. “Do I think I handled everything the best when I was there? Absolutely not.
“But one thing I can always say is I always give that city my all, gave that team my all, and when fans come out to watch us play, they knew that 93 was gonna show up and give everything he had.
“At the end of the day, the things that I did wrong, I apologize and move on.”
As special as the 2024 season was with the run to the NFC Championship Game in Jayden Daniel’s rookie season, Allen said the 2026 Bengals are the best team he’s played for.
Yes, Allen will be going back to face the team that drafted him, and he’ll be going back to his roots, having grown up in nearby Virginia.
But more than anything else, this trip is about the road ahead and not dwelling on the past.
“I'm just trying to make it as normal as possible,” Allen said. “I'm gonna be excited to see some of the guys out there that I haven't seen in a while, but at the end of the day, I'm focused on what we gotta do.”

title: How The Bengals Cooled Down a Hot Pittsburgh Defense in Week 10
full_text:
The offseason discussion on the Bengals' run game wasn't a waste of time.
Well, it was, but it was an understandable conversation! Teams that are too spread out and can't present a credible threat on the ground are getting beaten over the head by the flexibility that allows defenses. The Bengals have, from time to time, had issues with it, and it stood in the way of maximizing their output and efficiency.
There was another part of that.
The pass protection was egregiously bad. Yes, it was more exposed to difficult rush conditions, a big part of that flexibility I just mentioned, but they were bad. That is emphatically no longer the case.
Now, Burrow, Chase, and Higgins, who have always been good enough to do this, are able to attack any defense and any coverage. They're fine with light boxes, shifting/disguised coverages, and teams putting a lid over the top. Almost no other team has a QB that can live this way, but now that he has enough time to do so, the Bengals can throw options out there and allow Burrow to point out the coverage, get through his read, and find an answer.
Nowhere is safe from a QB who can truly survey and get the ball accurately to every inch of grass. Teams know this. Now that their four-man rushes aren't working, they are beginning to get desperate and make bigger and bigger mistakes. On Sunday night, the Bengals torched Pittsburgh's pressure packages, specifically targeting the structures of their pressure coverages.
So what did exactly did they attack? And how?
Fire Zones are five-man pressures where you don't want to push all your chips in and play man. Also known as "zone pressures" or "zone blitzes". Fire zone is a specific set of coverages. It's constructed as a balance between aggression and coverage. You're only sending five instead of six like a true blitz, and you're playing softer zone coverage but matching guys that enter your zone.
Between aggression and coverage, man and zone coverage, it's almost the ultimate balance of everything.
pic.twitter.com/4Kjyamb4gd
Your typical fire zone configuration is an even 3-deep, 3-under coverage like the above.
Michigan is running a traditional Fire Zone path with a Trap 2 behind it. On the bottom, the CB plays a Squat technique to support the Deep 1/2 player coming from low to high. Plays out similar to Quarters & how the Chiefs play their 'Tango' coverage. #ArtofX pic.twitter.com/fJQTI458NN
You can also play what's called a "two-trap fire zone" where the corners can help out underneath. Standard 3d3u fire zone is very exposed in the flat with the SCF (seam-curl-flat) defenders working inside out and the CBs playing a loose third. This is meant to give some support into the flat.
These are the main way zone pressure coverages are played. When teams play the Bengals, this is how they tend to do it when they send extra pressure because they don't want to give up an automatic 50 yards down the sideline to Chase.  Understandable, but it also happens to be a terrible idea. There is no safe way to send extra bodies at the Bengals passing offense.
When blitzed in the last three games, #Bengals QB Joe Burrow is: 30 of 33 for 391 yards -- 11.8 yards per attempt!! -- with 5 TDs, 1 INT and a passer rating of 143.0. Next week's opponent, Washington, has the fourth highest blitz rate in the league.
Elite processing QBs are unblitzeable because they are comfortable speeding up their operation and finding the weakness. Even more, Burrow's pre-snap command and unlimited protection-adjusting autonomy allows them to customize based on look and optimize their pickup.
The Bengals are so effective against fire-zones for a few reasons. Against the standard 3u-3d structure, DCs tend to give the CBs big cushions, as again fire zone is designed to prevent the all or nothing nature of standard man pressures. With two of the best go-ball threats in the league, that is even more pronounced against the Bengals' offense
Primary issue with running fire zones against the Bengals is that you have to give them huge cushions on the outside to stay out of go ball territory and they're very aware of it pic.twitter.com/AsDau20fTe
The Bengals absolutely love to take these freebies whenever they're given them, and they get them a lot.
2-Trap fire zones are not much better https://t.co/oVK9ePVjCl pic.twitter.com/EMIjOJwvcS
Because 2-trap fire zones are so focused deep and outside, they leave a lot of space in the middle. This happens to be the area the Bengals are most above the rest of the league as a passing attack.
Al Golden has found a pressure that works in this 3 deep 2 underneath hot coverage pic.twitter.com/fauU7Fjq4u
The idea of HOT blitzes, which are blitzes with the unique "HOT" pressure coverage is simple. They're basically fire zone with one less guy, 3 deep, 2 under instead of 3 deep, 3 under. This is because when you send a true blitz of six guys instead of a standard pressure with five, you obviously lose that one guy in coverage. The Steelers played it a little differently than normal, with the deep middle S playing more of a "lurk" technique instead of a deep post, but the structure is the same.
This coverage exists for the same reason fire zones do though. The idea is to prevent those easy 1v1 bombs into huge deep voids. The outside CBs and deep S will play it similarly to fire zone, but the seam defenders inside will park themselves on the seams and read the eyes of the QB. They almost freeze, don't overcommit anywhere, and react as best they can. It's the best they can do given the space they have to cover.
The issue is that it's extremely vulnerable in the intermediate middle. Because a lot of college QBs struggle to process here, as it's an unclear and shifting picture with all the bodies that populate the MOF, and effectively maximize this area, HOT has become very popular in the college game.
What about "HOT" pressures? https://t.co/oVK9ePVjCl pic.twitter.com/kZecfLBHV3
Joe Burrow is not a college QB. Essentially, hot coverages need the blitz to get someone to the QB and disrupt the play. If protection is good, it is not designed to hold up at all. The Bengals pass protection has been fantastic this year, especially relative to its exposure.
Post-wheel is a concept that is death to "HOT" coverages like this with the SEAM (eyes technique) defenders having so much space to account for. It's very hard to protect for long enough against 6 rushers for it to work so it's not normally exploited pic.twitter.com/sdUCXGb1Su
Because the CB can be run off taking the outside WR deep, the seam defender is sometimes asked to carry anything vertically from the slot.
The Bengals exploited this here by putting Chase at two on a post-wheel concept. This takes a minute to develop so it's not a common answer vs this coverage, but if you can protect it and give your QB the time, it's lethal. This is where Burrow becomes a force multiplier too. In addition to the protection command and pre-snap sense we discussed above, his ability to negotiate space and get up in the pocket consistently meets the OL halfway and, in this case, unlocked a filthy coverage beater with some high barriers to entry.
The Bengals are rolling out the Greatest show on Turf 2.0.
That said, Joe Burrow isn't any different than he was last year or especially in 2024. The only difference between this offense and year's past is that, as Bengals fans have been arguing on social media for years, the pass protection wasn't there. The one answer teams had in the past was to play MacDonald-ball.
They could rush four and still create havoc while shifting on the back end to make Burrow dig through his reads and find an answer without the time. He has the time now, and he's going to find it. Sending extra guys is only going to make the beatings worse.

title: Bengals' WR Ja'Marr Chase Says He and Tee Higgins Are Embracing Historic Pursuit
full_text:
The night the Cincinnati Bengals drafted Ja’Marr Chase back in 2021, the wide receiver said he was coming to break all of the team’s records.
He’s already crossed off several, and Chad Johnson’s career mark of 66 is within reach before the end of the season with Chase sitting on 60.
But Thursday afternoon, while wearing Joe Burrow’s orange No. 9 jersey after swapping news conference dates due to his quarterback being under the weather, Chase said he has his eyes on a specific NFL record.
And it’s one he would share with teammate Tee Higgins.
No team in NFL history has ever had two wide receivers top 1,500 yards in a season, but both Chase and Higgins are on pace to accomplish it.
Asked if that would be meaningful, Chase said “100 percent.”
And Chase made it clear he was already aware of the possibility before being asked about it in the news conference.
And he made sure Higgins was as well.
“I’m definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee, just letting him know how close we are,” Chase said.
“Close” might not be the right word. They’re each barely halfway there. But the season is barely halfway old.
Chase currently has 878 yards, which are fourth most in the league. That puts him on pace for 1,658.
Higgins has 824, sixth most in the league. He’s on pace for 1,556, which would blow away his career high of 1,091, set during the Super Bowl season in 2021.
“I’m just trying to put it out there and let him know how great we’ve been going,” Chase added.
The closest any teammates have come to accomplishing the double 1,500 feat was in 1995 when the Detroit Lions, with Scott Mitchell at quarterback, had Herman Moore register 1,686 yards while Brett Perriman logged 1,488.
In 2000, the St. Louis Rams saw Torry Holt get 1,635 while Isaac Bruce posted 1,471 with Kurt Warner starting 11 games and Trent Green five.
The last time a team had two receivers finish in the top six of receiving yards was 2011, when Patriots wide receiver Wes Welker was second (1,569) and tight end Rob Gronkowski was sixth (1,327).
Chase’s 231 yards in Sunday night’s 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers marked the fourth 200-yard game of his career.
The NFL record is five, shared by Lance Alworth, Calvin Johnson, Don Hutson, Charley Hennigan and Jerry Rice.
Only Johnson and Rice did it in the Super Bowl era.
“I got a couple more years in me,” Chase said. “I ain’t rushing it.”
As for how close he is to Johnson’s franchise record, Chase shut down the conversation.
“I don’t wanna know that,” he said. “I don’t wanna hear that.”
“I just don’t want to think about it. I just want to ball out.”

title: Bengals Could Boost Secondary With Rare Opportunity to Add Veteran Talent
full_text:
The Bengals have a chance to add a defensive star in a rare occurrence after the trade deadline. Multiple reports surfaced on Thursday that Justin Reid is available on the open market after being released by the New Orleans Saints.
The veteran is not subject to waivers and could be a great way to round out the Bengals' secondary with even more juice ahead of the postseason.
"Sources: The Saints are planning to grant the release requested by safety Justin Reid, as both sides agreed this would be mutually beneficial. Reid, a 2x Super Bowl champion, is just 29 years old and has 698 total tackles, 11 INTs, 52 pass deflections, 6.5 sacks, three forced fumbles," Jordan Schultz posted on X.
Reid has tailed off in recent years, but still brings veteran experience and durability at no outside cost besides a new contract for the rest of the season.
He's posted a 49.1 Pro Football Focus grade this season after 66.7 and 78.2 marks the past two seasons. The 29-year-old has played at least 15 games in every season since 2022 and could be able to tap into his old play with the Bengals' winning culture around him.
Reid has experience mixing it up with Cincinnati . He famously called former Bengals tight end Hayden Hurst Tyler Higbee by accident before the Chiefs-Bengals 2022 regular-season meeting.
"They have 88 -- Higbee.  No, it's not. Higbee was with the Rams," Reid said at his locker in 2022. "What's his name? Higgins. It is Higgins. Higbee and Higgins. They are going to have him back. He's a very talented receiver. More of a finesse type of guy. Not the best blocker. I'm going to lock him down. Straight up."
Hurst did not take kindly to that before the Bengals beat Kansas City 27-24 that season.
"He could pick anybody in this locker room, but I feel like I'm the last person you probably want to talk s*** about. I have a long memory," Hurst said.
Ja'Marr Chase also got involved, telling Reid: "Let's put some money on it big time."
Reid may not cost a ton for the rest of the season after getting out of a three-year, $31.5 million deal he signed last offseason. Showcasing in a winning environment may be incentive enough.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Joe Burrow, Dalton Risner on Opening Commanders Injury List
full_text:
The opening injury report for Commanders Week just dropped from the Bengals . Guard Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice, as fans hope to see him get a session in over the next two days. Joe Burrow was a full participant with his illness so that should quell any fear he may miss Monday's game. Dax Hill is also dealing with an illness.
Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged a limited showing after his injury on Sunday night. Outside of those names, there aren't many big ones to discuss. Cincinnati should get back Andrei Iosivas, Brian Parker and Jalen Davis this week after all three logged full Thursday sessions.
They practiced last week and have been lifted off of injured reserve.
Backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) logged a limited session as a nice sign of improvement.
A few other special-team names popped up with illnesses but what looks like a big injury list should end up thinning out across the next few days.
Cincinnati has a pretty full arsenal of talent to attack teams with despite the above injuries. Joe Burrow was really excited to feed so many different players for touchdowns against Pittsburgh.
"Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about Drew Sample and Chase Brown. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out."
Burrow's squad is executing well during practice and should be able to keep that going this week, especially getting an extra day to rest before sparking the session back up today.
"We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are."
Cincinnati is back at practice tomorrow and Saturday before traveling to the nation's capital.

title: 'Overall, He Looks Good' - Ja'Marr Chase Gives His View on Joe Burrow's Lingering Illness
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase swapped podium times with Joe Burrow this week as his quarterback fights through an illness.
There isn't much information on the illness, but from Chase's view, Burrow looks normal out on the practice field.
"I don't know if he told y'all how he's feeling or not. You know what I'm saying," Chase noted about Burrow. "But overall, he looks good. I think everybody around the team is just coming on with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good. Still feels the same."
Cincinnati has stayed pretty healthy all week, and we will find out Burrow's official practice status later today. There isn't a big indication that he has a major illness and is at risk of missing Monday night's game against Washington.
The Bengals are trying to keep their momentum rolling from a five-game winning streak into a six-game winning streak.
"Another big game coming up, like Sunday night," Chase said. "Just Monday night football, but still gotta tackle the same way, prep the same way this week, and make sure we execute when this game starts."
Chase is loving his 2026 season. He started slow, but has been humming in recent weeks.
His most recent game with Burrow made history.
Burrow joined Peyton Manning (five consecutive games in 2004 with Indianapolis) as the only quarterbacks all-time with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games. During the scoring drive, Chase became the third player in league history with at least 10 receptions and 140 receiving yards in three consecutive games, joining Pro Football Hall of Famer Andre Johnson (2008 with Houston) and CeeDee Lamb (2023 with Dallas).
They could stand alone in NFL history by posting those numbers again this week.
Chase is always gunning for that elite 200-yard receiving mark in games. He had 11 catches for 231 yards against Pittsburgh.
"Honestly, I want to say that's probably something I would love to achieve all the time, but it's a very hard task to do. So, if you're close enough for a milestone like that, I would say try to reach it," Chase said about going for 200 yards.
Cincinnati's top playmaker gets another chance to shine in primetime Monday night.
