title: Joe Burrow Not Speaking to Media as Scheduled During Commanders Week For Key Reason
full_text:
Joe Burrow is not speaking to the media on Thursday due to an illness he is battling this week. The Bengals media team noted the star quarterback is scheduled to speak on Friday now, and Ja'Marr Chase will talk today after being originally scheduled for tomorrow.
Signs of the illness popped up during the team's opening practice of Commanders week earlier this afternoon. Burrow did not go through the normal team stretch with all the other players.
He is the best-passing quarterback in the NFL right now and leads the NFL in the following categories: 27 Pass TD (5 more than any other QB), 310.6 Pass Yds/G (26.8 more), 74.7 Pass Comp% (4.6% more), 117.7 Pass Rating (2.5 more), 95.2 Pro Football Focus Offensive Grade (6.0 more), 93.8 Passer Grade (9.5 more).
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor didn't even mention the illness Thursday, so Burrow should be good to go in a few days at the latest.
Cincinnati is facing a Washington ready to keep winning after keeping their season alive last Thursday night.
"Really, some challenging games over the last five weeks," Taylor said about the Commanders. "Two losses, two wins, a tie. They've been in all of them. They could easily have been on a five-game winning streak, just like us. Talented team. I think they're well coached. Quarterback's a really good player. So really impressed with where they're at. They got a big divisional win in prime time on the road. Very similar to what we're coming off of. So I'm sure their headspace is very similar to how we feel, and it'll be a tough battle for us."
Burrow is the biggest factor in Cincinnati's offensive success, and they need him out there as healthy and above the weather as possible.
"There's a lot of things we do that generate a lot of completions," Taylor said about the short passing game this week. "He's always been above 70%, and so how you got your yardage, and so I thought it was pretty cool. I didn't realize in the moment that it was 14 minutes to one minute in the first quarter, and obviously that's because we started with the ball. But I thought the guys did a great job controlling tempo. We're not at breakneck tempo. Sometimes we're on the ball, but it's not snap it quickly. So we typically utilize the clock. So Joe gained a lot of information, but it's unique. I can't say outside of this team that that's been a big part of what I've been a part of in the past."
Cincinnati has two more practices this week before traveling to Washington, D.C.

title: Zac Taylor Highlights Dalton Risner, Dylan Fairchild's Injury Statuses Entering Commanders Practices
full_text:
The Bengals are pushing the normal practice schedule back one day this week in anticipation of a road Monday night battle against the Commanders.
Cincinnati's guards are in the injury spotlight as Zac Taylor gave the latest check in on Dalton Risner and Dylan Fairchild. Both are dealing with some issues picked up against the Steelers, including injuries to both knees for Risner.
"He'll be out today. We'll take it day-to-day this week," Taylor said about Risner, with no clear update on Fairchild. The team is also taking all of the freshly healthy players plucked off injured reserve last week "day-to-day" as well.
If Jalen Rivers has to step in again on either side, Taylor expects him to be solid again. Rivers didn't flash a noticeable drop-off on Sunday night.
"If we ever get to the point where other guys have to jump in, we expect them to play the same standard, but I don't think it's understated the chemistry that those five guys have together and the experience they have together, dating back to whenever Dalton really started playing for us a lot last year," Taylor said. "It's been really the same five guys, and and they're close on and off the field. They do a great job communicating.
"They take a lot of pride in the group. They're not really looking for individual honors or any of the game balls or anything like that. They just want to take great pride in keeping Joe clean and getting the running game going. And they've done an awesome job doing that."
Taylor hopes to see his team jump on the Commanders like they did the Steelers at home Sunday night.
They ripped up the top rival 38-18.
"I think that's dictating the style of game that's got to be played," Taylor said about the physicality. "I thought there was a lot of great tackling. First of all, a lot of great run-stopping tackling where we got guys on the ground, and so that limited their yards after some of the catches they did get and some of the yards that they tried to get on the perimeter.
"So really proud of the way I looked up at the end of the third quarter, and so they had minus something yards passing, and so thought the defense did a really good job trying to harass the pocket, great coverage downfield, nothing easy, nothing cheap, and the tackling was really good, and they pressured him all night."
Cincinnati has practice today through Saturday before the Monday night battle.

title: Analyzing What Deshaun Watson's 2027 Offseason Contract Extension Could Look Like
full_text:
Anyone who followed the Cleveland Browns closely knew that the 2026 season was going to be an interesting one.
Not just because it felt like nearly everyone had counted the Browns out, even after they put together a strong offseason, but because the quarterback situation was a big talking point. Would the team go with second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders or turn the keys of the offense back over to controversial Deshaun Watson?
Well, not only did they give Watson a chance to be the starter in the season opener, but he has done his job well enough to lock down the job for the entire year.
And now, one major question has started to arise: will the Browns' front office extend him this offseason?
The 31-year-old is in the final year of a five-year, $230 million contract . With how he is playing right now, leading the Browns to a 6-3 record while under center and keeping up the hunt for a playoff spot, it seems likely that the front office would at least consider it.
Here is what the contractual situation could look like in just a few short months:
This past offseason, t here were actually quite a few quarterbacks who hit free agency and commanded quite a bit of attention. Funny enough, a couple were even tied back to the Browns.
But weeks came and went and the Browns stood still, opting to stick with the quarterback room they already had.
Now, though, the front office might actually be able to use some of the discussions they saw behind-the-scenes to work through Watson's upcoming contract situation.
The Browns were never really in the running for Pittsburgh Steelers veteran Aaron Rodgers, but being over 40 years old and still playing at a high level, he somewhat sets a line for what Watson's value could be at. He commanded a one-year, $22.5 million deal.
Following Rodgers, 27-year-old Malik Willis, who is still relatively unproven, grabbed a whopping $22.5 million a year deal across three seasons with the Miami Dolphins.
Being almost four years younger than Watson and entering what is expected to be his prime, the contract makes sense, especially with where the quarterback market is at right now.
The final two deals that align somewhat with where the Browns should be at with Watson are Kirk Cousins, who signed a one-year, $11.3 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, and Marcus Mariota, who signed a one-year, $7 million deal with the Washington Commanders.
Both of those contracts make sense for where they were at in their careers; however, Cousins has quickly re-emerged as one of the league's most consistent quarterbacks. He's a good example of taking a low-to-mid-level financial risk on an aging quarterback, something Cleveland could end up taking into account.
When looking at the current quarterback market and comparing some of the deals that were signed last offseason, it is quite likely that Watson ends up inking a two- to three-year deal worth anywhere from $15-22 million a season.
The $15 million mark puts him just ahead of Cousins, while the $22 million high point puts him on pace for Rodgers- or Willis-type money.
That would make his total value worth anywhere from just $30 million across two seasons, all the way up to $66 million across three seasons.
If he can continue playing at the high level he has been this season, that type of contract would be worthwhile for a young team still finding its groove in a loaded AFC North. The bigger storyline, though, is whether this season has been a fluke for Watson or not.
The Browns' front office could end up deciding to lean towards a short-term contract, just to protect themselves and the amount of money they already invested in the controversial quarterback, or if wins really do matter, they could give him another nice deal to stay in Cleveland.
Watson's future in The Land rides heavily on how he finishes the 2026 season.
The Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a date with the 2026 No. 1 pick, Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders . The two sides will clash at 8:20 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Full Cleveland Browns 2027 Mock Draft: All Seven Rounds
full_text:
As the Browns sit at 6-4 in the playoff chase, draft discussions haven’t quite taken center stage in Northeast Ohio as we approach Thanksgiving.
But it’s never too early to start considering potential draft picks. With that in mind, let’s explore some names and ideas Cleveland might consider in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft.
For this mock draft, we'll use the Week 11 draft order from Tankathon.com :
No. 18 (via Los Angeles Rams)- Arch Manning, QB, Texas
The Browns will be looking to draft their franchise quarterback in the first round after not being able to take one in the last two drafts. Cleveland might have to trade up to draft its quarterback. But for this exercise, we will not make any trades.
Cleveland has the benefit of having two first-round picks and will grab Manning here from the selection the Browns received in the Myles Garrett trade.
Manning may not declare for the draft, as he still has eligibility remaining. Many people believe he should return to school for another season. However, he has already been in college for four years and has been a full-time starter for the last two seasons.
Another season of college football might not be beneficial, and joining the NFL, even if it means sitting on the bench for a while, could provide him with a better opportunity to learn from an NFL coaching staff.
The Browns will be linked to Manning during the draft, as owner Jimmy Haslam knows Arch's uncle, Peyton, from his time as a quarterback at the University of Tennessee, where Haslam is a native and booster.
It doesn’t matter what head coach Todd Monken and general manager Andrew Berry want. If Haslam has his heart set on a Manning, he usually gets what he wants since he is the one writing the checks. Owners often draft quarterbacks in the first round, and Haslam is exactly the type who doesn’t stay out of the way too often and let the football people make the big-time decisions.
No. 20- Greg Johnson, Interior OL, Minnesota
The Browns had to rebuild their offensive line last offseason, bringing in five new starters. It looks like they have two rookies, left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber, who will be in Cleveland for a while. The Browns still need to add to the offensive line, and Johnson would be a nice fit. He can play both center and guard. Most likely, the Browns would use him at center.
Currently, starting center Elgton Jenkins is on a two-year, $24 million deal with a potential out after this season for $7.7 million in dead cap, according to Spotrac.
No. 53,- Matayo Uiagalelei, EDGE, Oregon
Since Cleveland doesn't select a pass rusher in the first round, it will choose one with its second-round pick. Uiagalelei was among a handful of Oregon players who returned to school instead of entering the 2026 NFL Draft.
In 10 games this season, Uiagalelei has recorded 10 tackles for loss, 9.5 sacks and 40 combined tackles.
No. 84- Melvin Siani, OT, Texas
The Browns will still be looking for a need at tackle, and Siani appears to fit their style. Siani is listed at 6-foot-6 and weighs 302 pounds. The 22-year-old tackle may not match the weight of current Browns tackle Dawand Jones, who came in at 6-foot-8 and 374 pounds at the 2023 combine. However, Siani possesses a large frame that could help him develop into a solid professional player.
No. 119 (via Seattle Seahawks)- Nate Frazier, RB, Georgia
No. 122- Owen Chambliss, LB, Nebraska
No. 123 (via New York Giants)- Lawson Luckie, TE, Georgia
The Browns focus on Georgia players in the fourth round, as Monken was the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator from 2020 to 2022 and helped them win two national championships. Monken still has connections inside the Georgia football program, and it is one of the best schools for producing tight ends and running backs.
Frazier could step in to help carry the running game alongside Quinshon Judkins, allowing Dylan Sampson to focus more on third-down work. Additionally, Luckie could help free up tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in the passing game. Fannin and Luckie could be used in multiple two-tight-end sets, creating mismatches for opposing defenses.
Cleveland has to get more depth at linebacker, and adding Chambliss, who has 55 tackles, five tackles for loss and a half-sack in eight games this season.
No. 148 (via Houston Texans)-Zeke Berry, CB, Michigan
No. 157- Jordan Faison WR, Notre Dam e
Cleveland uses its fifth-round pick to select two players from significant programs: Berry from Michigan and Faison from Notre Dame. The Browns don't necessarily need a starter at cornerback, with Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell already in place, but they do need depth.
Adding Berry could be a valuable addition. The same goes for wide receiver, as the Browns have Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion starting.
But Cleveland is likely to part ways with Jerry Jeudy this offseason, creating opportunities to add a few receivers, both in the draft and through free agency.
No. 230- (via Texans)- Peter Clarke, TE, Temple
No. 241- Knijeah Harris, Guard, Florida
The Browns add another tight end since they have a deep need at that position. And they add Harris as a depth piece on the offensive line.
Often, seventh-round picks don't make the 53-man roster, and since Cleveland won't have many roster spots to spare with all its draft picks and possible free-agent additions, both players might be camp bodies.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Five 2027 NFL Draft Targets for the Cleveland Browns to Watch
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are in the thick of the race for a postseason berth , so unlike a few recent seasons, upcoming draft chatter hasn’t really churned up this early in the season.
Nonetheless, it’s never too early to look at potential draft targets. That’s especially true for a team with two first-round picks in its pocket that has found ways to win despite so many obvious roster holes.
Here are five 2027 NFL Draft prospects that could land firmly on the Browns’ radar over the next few weeks:
If the Browns are looking at passers in Round 1, then all signs are starting to point towards forgetting about Drew Mestemaker, who looks like QB1 for the 2027 NFL Draft.
After that, things aren’t so clear. Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr has a chance to solidify himself as the second quarterback selected, but he lacks ideal size and arm strength, much like the two passers selected by Cleveland in the 2025 Draft, so the team might want to look at a different type of passer.
That brings us to LaNorris Sellers, who’s had an up-and-down season like most of next year’s prospects. Sellers is a bigger passer with a stronger arm, but he’s had to deal with accuracy questions in the past. He faces a monumental challenge this week against top-ranked Georgia.
Word on the street before the season began was that Jimmy Haslam was totally enamoured with Manning and wanted to have him as his franchise quarterback by the time the team moved into the new Brook Park Stadium sometime in 2029.
Good news for the Browns. Manning doesn’t look like the surefire No. 1 overall pick many were talking about before Texas’ season began, and there’ve even been rumors that he could stay for another college season, either with the Longhorns or by transferring to another program.
Manning might not be having the stellar season so many observers predicted this year, but he’s displayed great leadership and resiliency, regardless. Should he make the jump to the NFL Draft, he might even become available to the Browns after Round 1, if Haslam’s heart is truly set on a Manning.
Leaving quarterbacks aside, Cleveland should take a long, hard look at offensive tackles in Round 1, even after selecting Spencer Fano in the Top-10 and Austin Barber in the third back in April .
If Fano stays permanently on the left side, Lauck could come in on the right side and help stabilize a unit that has struggled throughout the season. Plus, the Browns could certainly use Lauck’s nasty demeanor in the run game. Along with Fano, Austin Barber, and potentially Parker Brailsford down the line, the Browns could put together a solid unit that could end up playing together for years.
If Cleveland wants to wait until the second round for some O-Line talent, Johnson could make sense as a versatile piece with experience playing multiple positions.
Whether it’s taking the center spot and kicking Elgton Jenkins out, or taking a guard spot, Johnson looks like a Day 1 starter on most offensive lines, including the Browns’.
Finding a young edge rusher in one of the top rounds seems like a must for Cleveland at this point. With South Carolina’s Dylan Stewart and Texas’ Colin Simmons likely out of range for the Browns, Traore looks like the next man up.
The Irish star has prototypical size for the position and a non-stop motor that will instantly win fans over when he reaches the pro ranks.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: How Todd Monken Played a Role in This Pivotal Stage of Deshaun Watson's Career
full_text:
Many Browns fans were not in favor of seeing Deshaun Watson ever start a game for Cleveland heading into the season.
But one man didn't care what the public thought.
Head coach Todd Monken entered the season ready to choose the best quarterback. That turned out to be Watson, who has guided the Browns to a 6-4 record, including 6-3 as a starter, despite missing the Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints.
It felt like Watson's career was over after he missed all of the 2025 season with a torn Achilles. However, Monken has found something in Watson, and the 31-year-old quarterback has given a lot of credit to his new head coach for helping him prepare during this stage of his career.
"I think the biggest thing is he took time to really get to know me," Watson said on Wednesday. He took time to understand the situation instead of just writing stories and taking what the media says about me, which they really don't know. I think just being able to sit down and talk and see the larger picture. He understood, of course; I'm not broken. I had a lot of personal things going on, and I had a lot of injuries going on in my career.
"And I think anyone who had to deal with what I had to deal with will have ups and downs too; that's part of life. You learn from it. You grow from it. He believed in me, so it's always good to have a coach and a friend, a person in the building that can sit there and talk to you and make sure that you're straight mentally."
During camp and the preseason it didn’t look good for Deshaun Watson, but he credits head coach Todd Monken’s people skills for helping him get on track #Browns pic.twitter.com/CBnBR1E02o
Watson has had his fair share of injuries ever since he came to Cleveland in 2022. He underwent surgery for a displaced fracture of the glenoid of his right shoulder in November 2023. Then, in the middle of the 2024 season, he tore his Achilles and re-tore it again in the winter of 2025.
Perhaps Watson just needed time to get back into the swing of football, and with Monken's belief in him, he helped Watson get back on track.
Watson hasn't put up great stats this season, throwing for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions in nine games.
But what has he done? Win six games, all coming on game-winning drives.
The Browns and Watson may not have many more games together, as Cleveland may not re-sign him after the season. However, Monken might have helped Watson keep his career going a bit longer than expected if another team signs him.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Former Browns Preseason Star Luke Floriea Drafted by Columbus UFL Team
full_text:
Luke Floriea shined for the Cleveland Browns this past preseason. The Mentor High School and Kent State product was a feel-good story, but ultimately didn't make the final roster or even the practice squad .
Yet he did make a name for himself, and the former undrafted NFL free agent just got drafted, albeit by a different professional football league. The good news for him is that he will once again suit up and play football in his home state of Ohio.
The United Football League draft began Wednesday with former Vanderbilt star Diego Pavia going No. 1 overall to the Columbus Aviators. He will now have Floriea as a top target after the former Browns receiver was taken by the Aviators in the ninth round at pick. No. 65 overall.
Luke Floriea has been selected with our 9th round pick ✈️ pic.twitter.com/gnzwH7F9wz
The Aviators began play as a new UFL franchise in 2026 with Ted Ginn Jr. as the head coach. The team finished 3-7 and just made a big splash by taking Pavia with the No. 1 overall pick. That should certainly get some eyes on the team when the UFL season begins in March.
This is also a great opportunity for Floriea to put great play on tape and potentially parlay that into a full-time NFL opportunity. He did have a tryout with the Seattle Seahawks after getting cut by the Browns, but he did not show enough to earn a spot.
Floriea seemed to be right on the cusp of making the Browns roster before the season. The final receiver spot was ultimately won by Tylan Wallace, who had already spent time with Todd Monken in Baltimore.
The local receiver's breakout performance came in the final preseason game when he caught two touchdown passes from Dillon Gabriel. It was a dream come true for the Mentor native, just not enough to convince the front office to roster him.
Playing with Pavia as his quarterback should mean Floriea has a chance to shine in the national spotlight when the UFL season begins in a few months. The outspoken quarterback was the Heisman runner-up in 2025 and spent the summer with the Baltimore Ravens. He, too, will try to show off his abilities and aim to get back into the NFL.
That path is possible and was proven by current Browns kicker Andre Szmyt , who spent the 2024 season with the St. Louis Battlehawks.
Steve is a lifelong Cleveland sports fan who proudly wears his Guardians, Browns, and Cavs gear in his current home of Santa Barbara. He has covered Cleveland sports online for the past decade and is still waiting for the Browns to draft a QB who signs a second contract in town.

title: How the Browns Can Flip the Script and Run the Ball for a Playoff Push
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ bye week comes at the perfect time for a playoff push. They are 6-4 and are in the last wild-card position. The other AFC teams behind them have issues at quarterback, with more difficult schedules remaining.
The Browns will need to use the bye week to improve a major area of their offense.
The rushing offense ranks 24th in the NFL with 97.5 yards per game. That number plummets to just 63.6 yards per game from all running backs. Deshaun Watson is second on the team in rushing with 266 yards, which includes broken plays that result in him improvising a run.
There is not just one problem with the run game, as both the line and running backs have been ineffective between the tackles.
In their win against the Houston Texans, the Browns used more read options. When Watson handed the ball off to Quinshon Judkins in the shotgun position, he would read the defensive end. When the ultra-aggressive defensive end crashed down the line to meet the running back, Watson would pull the ball back from the handoff and run through the exposed end of the line.
This play led to the Browns first touchdown on their way to come back from 17-0. Todd Monken called that play throughout the first half, and it continually worked as Watson led the team in rushing yards and averaged 6.1 yards per rush.
However, in the second half, the Texans adjusted. When Watson would hand the ball off to Judkins, the defensive end made his way to the quarterback no matter who had the ball. The interior offensive line was not effective enough to move their own defenders, so the defensive line did not need the defensive end. Monken and the offense can use the bye week to put in a wrinkle or two in the read option to get the ground game going.
Watson can be called a design run in the shotgun position. He can appear to do a read option by the elongated handoff, and the opposite-side guard can pull to block the defensive end going after Watson. This would open up the end, similar to the defensive crashing down, leaving his side open.
This could work against the Las Vegas Raiders, as Maxx Crosby is focused on getting to the quarterback. He could think that he has a free pass to Watson, but then the pulling guard would pick him up, and Watson would have an open field.
Monken can also mix old school with new school. He can align both Judkins and Dylan Sampson in the backfield alongside Watson. The read option would go to Judkins, but if Watson takes the ball back due to reading the defensive end, then he and Sampson would run the option. This would work if the defensive end stays home and Watson could pitch the ball to Sampson after occupying the defender.
Watson opened up the field against the Texans by airing the ball out deep. He has been more of a check-down quarterback at the beginning of the season. He heads into the bye with three straight 300-yard games. Defenses will have to start respecting the pass, which could help the run game by reducing the number of run stoppers on the field. The Browns scored the game-winning touchdown on the ground as it looked like the defense was playing the pass.
The Browns should use their bye week to focus on getting more production on the ground, which they will need as the weather gets colder. Monken has shown that he will keep trying new ways to get that production, and he now has two weeks to figure it out.

title: 2 Browns Players Who Need To Be Better Coming Out of Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are heading into their bye week with a 6-4 overall record.
Over the past few weeks, the talk of the town is whether or not the Browns can win the division, along with making the playoffs.
If Cleveland wants the chance to do either, here are two guys who need to step up their play after the week off.
Jared Verse Was Really Talking To The Texans Offensive Lineman Who Just Jumped Offsides. Letting Him Hear It After The Flag. By The Way, He Hasn't Sniffed A Quarterback Yet This Year. pic.twitter.com/qkQRW8unJO
This one pretty much goes without saying.
So far this season, Jared Verse has yet to record a sack. On top of that lack of production, the 2024 defensive rookie of the year has a combined total of 20 tackles.
For reference, Verse had a total of 58 tackles and 7.5 sacks a year ago.
Obviously, when you get traded for the best player in football along with multiple high draft picks, the expectation will be higher. However, having zero sacks and really being outplayed by backups is unacceptable.
Some may blame it on the schemes or defensive formations, but at a certain point, you have to go out and perform no matter what cards you're dealt. Especially if you are going to trash-talk at any given moment.
While Tytus Howard is coming off of his best game with the Browns, he needs to perform at that level in every game from here on out.
This past offseason, the Browns went out and traded for Howard before signing him to a new three-year deal. In return, they have gotten a mid-tier starting tackle. According to PFF, Howard ranks 42nd out of all 72 tackles in the league.
While we are on the topic of statistics, Howard has done a good job in the pass-blocking game as he ranks 16th in that category.
On the other hand, Howard has been one of the reasons why the run game hasn't been working this year, as he ranks near the bottom of the league at 52nd in run blocking.
To sum it all up, the Browns need to see more from the guys they traded for this offseason.
If Verse can produce on the field half as much as he talks about it, he will be a great player for this Browns defense. As for Howard, if he can work on blocking for the run game, the Browns offense can gain another dimension and become even more consistent.
There's still work to be done, but this is the bye week after all.
After the time off, these guys will have the biggest stage in football to prove it.

title: The Cleveland Browns Need To Get This Running Back More Involved As Year Concludes
full_text:
With the No. 126 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, the Cleveland Browns selected running back Dylan Sampson.
And within just a few days, it looked like the Browns had completely revitalized their offense.
During that draft, not only did the Browns end up selecting Sampson, but they also added multiple other pieces to the offense, including his counterpart, Quinshon Judkins . Throughout their rookie season, that draft class stood out as excellent additions. Much of that established momentum carried into this year as well.
But Sampson, who had to fill a large role at the end of the 2025 season due to injury, hasn't followed in his draft class's footsteps. Instead of continuing to play a key role in game-day plans, he has practically disappeared.
Across five games, the 22-year-old has 19 carries for 79 yards and zero scores. He has also picked up just one first down this season. In the receiving game, he has been targeted 22 times for 16 receptions and 152 yards. That isn't as much of an issue as his lack of involvement in the backfield, though.
With how dynamic Sampson is in both the rushing and passing attack, he needs more carries and the same pace of targets he is currently on, especially as the Browns' offense looks to finish the season strong.
Judkins has dominated the shares out of the Browns' backfield, taking 126 carries for 423 yards and four scores. He is averaging a team-low 3.4 yards per game , less than quarterback Deshaun Watson, Sampson, Jaleel McLaughlin, Rahiem Sanders and even wideout KC Concepcion.
Not only is he unable to break past that first wall of the defense and pick up chunk yardage, but even with a high volume, his average yards per game sits below 50.
If, through nine games, those numbers haven't grown (which they unfortunately haven't), the Browns need to make changes. It isn't that Judkins deserves a major dip in opportunities, but rather just a counterpart, such as Sampson, to balance the running game out.
Just a few weeks back, head coach Todd Monken said that the rushing game is one of the team's most troublesome areas.
"It's not a negative; it's a fact," Monken told reporters when asked about the Browns' struggles in that area of the offense. "We have got to scheme better, we have got to coach it better, we have got to call it better, and we certainly can block it better."
Since he is aware of the issues, making changes such as getting Sampson more involved could be one of the easiest ways to start making adjustments. If it works, it works. If it doesn't, at least the Browns can cross that off the list and move on to the next.
Because almost like the quarterback situation, the more you kick the can down the road, the longer you prolong the questions.
But as he has shown in the receiving game, all he needs is some open space, and he can make a defense pay.
In his college days, Sampson was elite in both the rushing and passing attacks, being able to spread the field and create chunk plays out of thin air. His speed and athleticism allowed him to weave through traffic as he averaged a whopping 5.9 yards per rush and 8.6 yards per reception.
Cleveland needs to find a way to unlock that form again.
The Browns and Sampson return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, giving them a much-needed bye week to reset before the last few weeks of the season. They will take on the Las Vegas Raiders from Huntington Bank Field at 8:20 p.m. EST.

title: Deshaun Watson Finally Sheds Light Into Future in Cleveland Beyond 2026
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a nice break from playing on Sundays.
But in the meantime, that leaves plenty of opportunities for the media to poke and pry.
On Wednesday, Nov. 18, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson was asked by media on whether he would return to the Browns or not following the 2026 campaign. The 31-year-old is in the final year of his $230 million contract.
"That’s up to my agent. That’s all David Mulugheta," Watson said with a laugh. "I don't even worry about that...my future, no matter what that holds, is all in God's hands...
“...Ultimately, it’s up to the front office. It’s up to Jimmy and Dee. It’s up to AB. It’s up to Coach Monken and the city. All I can do is continue to play good football, win games, and then let them kind of figure out what they want to do for the future.”
Browns QB Deshaun Watson was asked when he thinks is the appropriate time to discuss his future in Cleveland. Watson: “That’s up to my agent. That’s all David Mulugheta.” pic.twitter.com/iKDpjNJ3T9
This offseason, he is expected to command a deal anywhere from $ 18 to $ 25 million across two to three years , based on where the quarterback market is currently at, according to Spotrac. The Browns, who have already given Watson quite a bit of money over the last few years, are likely going to mull over the decision into the offseason.
But he has played well this season, and if he leads the Browns to the playoffs, it is going to be hard to deny a return to Cleveland in 2027.
After all, it finally seems like he is coming around as well.
Across nine starts this season, he has 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions through the air, with three straight 300-yard passing games, all while flashing more capabilities in the rushing attack. He has tucked the ball 59 times this year, rushing for 266 yards and two touchdowns.
Earlier in the season, head coach Todd Monken stressed that the coaching staff was working to make Watson more comfortable with his legs this season. Well, it seems that whatever they did behind the scenes worked, as many times he has finished as the Browns' leading rusher in a game.
Watson went on to credit Monken for his ability to grow and find success this season, which also makes his exit from Cleveland less likely, at least on his end, if he has a say.
"I think the big thing is he took the time to get to know me," Watson said. "He took time to really understand the situation, instead of just writing stories and taking what the media is saying about me when they don't really know. I think, being able to sit down and talk and see the bigger picture... he understands, of course, I am not broken.
"I had a lot of personal things going on; I had a lot of injuries going on... and I think anybody that has dealt with what I have had to deal with is going to struggle and have some ups and downs, too... you learn from it. You grow from it... he believed in me."
During camp and the preseason it didn’t look good for Deshaun Watson, but he credits head coach Todd Monken’s people skills for helping him get on track #Browns pic.twitter.com/CBnBR1E02o
It will be intriguing to see the type of contract he demands, especially if he finishes the year at the pace he is currently holding. The Browns have second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders chomping at the bit, and if Watson leaves, it would become his show on a much cheaper deal.
But winning does matter, and Watson is leading the Browns to many.
The Browns and Watson return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST for a primetime game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

title: Browns Have One Major Problem to Fix During Their Much-Needed Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns can't run the football.
Let's just say it how it is.
To begin the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns entered as one of the league's most unexpected sides. Not because they made a bunch of high-level additions, but because they made a few small, team-fitting moves.
Offensively, they added a whole new chunk of youngsters through the NFL Draft, all while bringing in some veterans through free agency and trades.
But unfortunately, the changes made to the offensive line haven't quite panned out the way the front office had hoped they would.
Through the first half of the year, the Browns are 6-4, yet the offensive line has hurt them countless times. The pass protection has led to starting quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders being sacked a whopping 42 times, while the rushing game has barely been able to get out of the backfield, averaging a measly 3.8 yards per attempt.
That's not going to cut it long-term, especially if the Browns want to legitimately compete in the playoffs.
During the bye week, the Browns must focus on finding more success for the offensive line. According to Pro Football Focus, the unit ranks 19th overall out of 32 teams.
Watson and company will be okay in the passing game, but if that rushing attack can't get going, the Browns are going to be limited.
Through nine games, Judkins has rushed for 423 yards and four scores on 126 attempts, all while picking up 22 first downs along the way. He is only averaging 3.4 yards per attempt , though, and 47 yards per game.
That just isn't enough, especially when the Browns' offense is trying to expand the passing game more.
But it isn't all Judkins' fault.
Rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, who have stolen much of the offensive line's spotlight this season, have done a good job at protecting the pass, but even they both have struggled in the rushing game. Fano's ranking sits at 26th out of 72 in the league , while Barber's is 25th out of 77.
The rest of the group, Elgton Jenkins (29th/35), Zion Johnson (26th/77) and Tytus Howard (52nd/72), all need to make better strides in their ability to free up lanes for both Judkins and counterpart Dylan Sampson.
While Judkins' numbers are down , Sampson's usage is practically nothing.
He was injured in the early parts of the season, but has still not been in the equation much when healthy. Averaging more yards than Judkins, though, he has 19 carries for 79 yards and zero scores. Jaleel McLaughlin, who got a lot of work when both backs were injured, also has been pretty effective in limited opportunities . He has 11 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown.
The offensive line may not be all to blame for the rushing attack's struggles this season, but the protection and ability to free up lanes start with them.
From there, the coaching staff needs to find better usage of Judkins, Sampson and McLaughlin, giving each a chance to establish themselves in a running back room that is averaging well below 100 yards per game.
After all, somehow, Watson ends up carrying the total rushing yards in a game at times.
The Browns are a really well-rounded side, but it is obvious that the running game is lackluster. If they can make ample improvements during the bye week and come back out on the other side stronger, they will be better positioned to not just make a push for the playoffs, but for the top spot in the AFC North as well.

title: Mike Pettine Is Cowboys' Savior & Will Lead Team To NFC East Crown, Skip Bayless Predicts
full_text:
We are days away from finding out just how much of an impact Mike Pettine will make on the Dallas Cowboys' defense . The veteran NFL coach is set to take over play-calling duties on Sunday afternoon against the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium , after the team decided to pull the plug on the Christian Parker experiment .
The Cowboys are insisting that Parker is not a lame-duck defensive coordinator because he is still leading team meetings and helping with the game plan, but this is Pettine's show now.
When discussing Dallas' recent change, a predictable debate broke out between notorious Cowboys hater Stephen A. Smith and Skip Bayless on ESPN's First Take , with Skip claiming Pettine will save the day in Dallas with his influence.
Bayless did not only say that he believes Pettine will be a game-changer for the Cowboys, but that he could help lead them to the NFC East crown.
"[The Dallas Cowboys] are about to take off and win this bad division." @RealSkipBayless believes moving Mike Pettine to playcaller is the answer for Dallas 🙌 pic.twitter.com/GW4Vxt9nVT
"You are about to have to eat a heaping helping of chicken fried crow, courtesy of Jerry Jones. Jerry Jones just finally made a painfully obvious move that is going to jump-start this Cowboys season," Bayless said. "We are about to take off and win this bad division, this 'NFC Least.' Jerry tried to sell us Christian Parker as a savior and a savant of our defense, and it was clear from the start, from game one at the Giants, that Christian Parker was in over his 34-year-old head. He was overmatched. He was, frankly, overrated.
"Mike Pettine, Jerry went out and got him to oversee all the way back on October 12 because Jerry knew it wasn't working. We had just lost at home to winless Tampa Bay on Thursday Night Football, and an undrafted rookie quarterback. And Jerry finally said, 'That's enough.' And he's elevated Mike Pettine, a real defensive coordinator, to take this team over."
While the first part of Bayless' comments were a little over the top, which is his shtick, he did make some realistic points and speak common sense in the second-half of his rant, pointing out how the Cowboys can actually put themselves in position to win the division.
"We have two very winnable home games this Sunday, then right around the corner on Thanksgiving. We will get in rhythm with Mike Patton's defense in those two games," Bayless added.
"Then we get 11 days off for a Monday night game at Seattle. Then we get two weeks off for a game out here in L.A. against the Rams that I think we will win or at least steal. And we finish with the Giants at home and at the Commanders, and we will win those two games. And at 9-8, we will win the NFC East."
If the Cowboys can't put two wins together at home against the 1-8 Titans and the 2-7 Eagles, they don't deserve to be taken serious for the rest of the year. So over the next week, the Cowboys' season will be on the line.
We'll have to see if the Pettine effect helps the defense and if the team can string together some wins to make Bayless' prediction even more realistic.

title: 3 Bold Predictions For Dallas Cowboys In Week 11 vs Tennessee Titans
full_text:
It's been a long week for the Dallas Cowboys who decided to shake up their coaching staff following their latest loss. After surrendering 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers, Dallas took play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker and will have senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine take over .
Parker will stay on as the defensive coordinator, but at this point, it's in title only. He spoke on the situation and said his focus is solely on beating the Tennessee Titans in Week 11.
With so much conversation happening surrounding Parker, it's easy to forget a game is just around the corner. For the Cowboys, it's a chance to get back on track as they take on the 1-8 Titans, and a win would be even more likely if these three bold predictions come true.
Javonte Williams has had a roller coaster season in 2026, but is still on pace for more than 1,000 yards as he has 692 through the first 10 games. He also has nine rushing touchdowns, but hasn't had multiple scores since the Week 4 win over the Houston Texans when he ran for three.
Tennessee comes into this one ranked 22nd against the rush, giving up 1,116 yards. They're 25th in rushing touchdowns, with opposing teams scoring 11 on the ground in nine games. That's a good sign for Williams, and in this bold prediction, he runs two touchdowns to help give the Dallas offense a spark.
Troy Aikman said Christian Parker was a scapegoat for Brian Schottenheimer, and he's probably right. That said, the move to Pettine could bring on some much-needed change for a team that's struggled all season. He's also facing one of the worst offenses in the NFL, which will help Pettine look good in Week 11. That's why this bold prediction has the defense recording three turnovers, finally giving their defense a hand.
The Titans are bad against the run, but they're even worse against the pass. They're dead last in pass defense this season and that's a recipe for success for Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. Even in their loss last week, this trio was impressive with Pickens recording 145 yards and three touchdowns on 11 receptins. Lamb also had a strong outing with seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown.

title: Jerry Jones Shares Thoughts on Christian Parker's Demotion, Praises Cowboys DC
full_text:
For the first time since the Dallas Cowboys took play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker this week, Jerry Jones has shared his thoughts on the decision.
The Cowboys made it official on Wednesday afternoon , with the team deciding to hand play-calling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Parker will stay on as the defensive coordinator, although really in name only.
Jones did his usual spot on 105.3 The Fan on Friday and made it clear he supports the decision to move off of Parker and go to Pettine.
“We’ve got a chance to play better doing it this way," Jones said, per Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News .
Not a shock, but Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is making it clear on @1053thefan he supports the decision to take play-calling duties away from Christian Parker. He has said multiple times he likes where they are today and where they’re going.
Parker addressed the media for the first time since he was demoted in his usual Thursday presser and one of the more surprising things to come out of it was the fact that Parker admitted he hasn't spoken to Jones about the decision.
Jones said he didn't see an issue with that.
"I don't have an issue and I don't think anybody else should if they know what I know," Jones said, according to Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News .
Not sure what Jones meant by that last part, but given the fact that he is the general manager and almost certainly had a hand in making this decision, as he does with all decisions, he should've had a conversation with Parker by now after such a massive midseason coaching change. Not a good look for Jerry.
The most impressive thing about Parker since he was demoted is how well he has handled the situation in what is a nightmare scenario for any coach.
Jones confirmed Parker is indeed taking everything in stride and rightly noted that how Parker has handled things will reflect positively on him moving forward.
"He can put that on a resumé of how he handled the initial parts of this decision. He can put that right up there at the top of his list. He’s handling it very well," Jones said, per Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein .
The only way to make good out of a situation like this is to handle it exactly how Parker has. It would have been understandable for him to try and dodge the media on Thursday, but he instead decided to face the music and did so with total class.
Parker's presser was refreshingly honest, as he didn't beat around the bush about how he felt. He made it clear he was disappointed and even admitted he thought about leaving but decided he was not going to take that approach, even though nobody would've blamed for him for doing so.
The Cowboys should take notes on how Parker has handled all of this because the team has done about as poor a job as possible on its end.

title: Cowboys Preseason Fan Favorite Returns To Dallas After 2027 UFL Draft Selection
full_text:
Leading up to the 2026-27 NFL season, there were few players on the Dallas Cowboys roster who were as beloved as Shiyazh Pete. The undrafted free agent offensive lineman was not just a fan favorite in Dallas, but around the league.
Pete went viral for an epic post-game speech during the preseason , after his historic appearance.
Not only did Pete become the first member of the Navajo Nation to sign with an NFL team, but he also became the first Navajo player to take the field for a game when the Cowboys faced the Arizona Cardinals in the preseason .
After that game, he received a standing ovation from thousands of Navajo Nation fans in attendance.
this game, this star, this team will make us brothers 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/rEcvDTzSkd
The 6-foot-9 Pete was a roster casualty of the Cowboys before the final cuts ahead of the regular season, but now he is returning to Dallas to resume his pro football career.
This week, the 2027 NFL Draft was held, and Pete was selected by the Dallas Renegades in Round 8 (No. 59 overall).
The UFL is a perfect opportunity for Pete to get another crack at a professional football career, with his rare combination of size and raw talent setting him up for success if he can continue to develop.
Potential was why he was signed by the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Kentucky, so we'll see if the Renegades coaching staff can get the best out out of him. The Renegades are led by hed coach Kevin Sumlin.
Pete wasn't the only former Cowboy to get an opportunity in the UFL this season, with former sixth-round pick Eric Scott Jr. also joining the Dallas Renegades roster. The cornerback, who also spent time with the Kansas City Chiefs and Detroit Lions, was selected in Round 4 (No. 28 overall).
It will be exciting to see how Pete and Scott perform in the UFL, and it's great that they will be in Dallas so the Cowboys can keep an eye on their progress. Everyone knows Dallas loves to find talent in the spring leagues (Brandon Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, James Houston), so who knows if a return to the Cowboys could be in the cards if the players put on a show during the 2027 UFL campaign.

title: Colin Cowherd Sees Quinnen Williams' Presser as Major Red Flag for Cowboys
full_text:
Quinnen Williams turned heads this week when he refused to answer questions during a press conference. Williams, who has been a supporter of defensive coordinator Christian Parker , was asked about the Dallas Cowboys' decision to strip Parker of his play-calling duties .
Williams said he would keep his thoughts on that to himself. He gave the same answer repeatedly when asked about the team's 4-6 record and his thoughts on Mike Pettine.
It was an odd presser for Williams, who is usually willing to talk about anything. According to Colin Cowherd, that in itself is a major indictment of head coach Brian Schottenheimer. As Cowherd says, the Cowboys have reached a weird phase where there's nothing good to say, which is alarming considering the talent they have.
"So the Dallas Cowboys are a very big brand, but they're also unique in the NFL this year. Every really bad team can be explained by either A, you just don't have enough good players, the Tennessee Titans, or B, you're not good at quarterback, the New York Jets, who are very good on the roster, they're not good at quarterback," Cowherd said.
"The Cowboys have a guy that's going to get Hall of Fame votes at quarterback and should, Dak Prescott, very good. And they have excellent personnel. Don't listen to anybody. Offensive personnel should be top five offense in the league. CeeDee Lamb, (George) Pickens, Javonte Williams, Dak, top seven offensive line. (Jake) Ferguson, I don't want to hear about it. So here's how bad it is. The Cowboys have reached a new phase. The if you don't have anything good to say, say nothing."
"Think about that. Seven years with the Jets: quotable. Dallas: "I'm done talking!" Jerry - it's time." @colincowherd reacts to Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams' comments to the media pic.twitter.com/3cOvli21Vo
As if that's not concerning enough, Cowherd brings up another point. Williams spent seven years with the New York Jets, a team known for dysfunction, yet he always had something to say. Now after just over a full year with the Cowboys, he's done talking. Again, Cowherd says that's squarely on the shoulders of Schottenheimer.
"Think about this. Quinnen Williams played for the New York Jets for seven years and never stopped talking. He's with the Cowboys. I got nothing to say here. Think about that. Seven years with the Jets, quotable. Dallas, I'm done talking. Jerry, it's time. I got nothing against Brian Schottenheimer. But he wasn't interviewing for not only head coaching jobs, top coordinator jobs."
Cowherd is a controversial figure due to his hot takes, which often rile up fan bases. That said, he's spot on with this opinion.
Schottenheimer came to Dallas with the lofty goal of " building the greatest culture in professional sports ." The problem is that he never learned to walk as a head coach before trying to run that marathon.
He also has been terrible when it comes to holding players accountable and is using Parker as a scapegoat for his own shortcomings as a head coach. That said, it's impossible to argue against Cowherd's take that this isn't the right job for Schottenheimer, and Jerry Jones would be wise to pivot sooner rather than later.

title: Cowboys Legend Troy Aikman Says Christian Parker Being 'Scapegoated' in Dallas
full_text:
Troy Aikman knows the Dallas Cowboys needed to do something to salvage their season, but he's not sure they made the right move with Christian Parker .
While speaking with The Dallas Morning News , Aikman said the Cowboys, especially head coach Brian Schottenheimer, were feeling desperate. He just doesn't seem to understand the idea behind keeping Parker as the defensive coordinator if Mike Pettine will be the one handling the play-calling duties.
"The Cowboys are desperate. I think [Brian] Schottenheimer's desperate as well with all of the criticism that has come, but I don't know about keeping the title of defensive coordinator if in fact he's not calling the plays," Aikman said.
"I don't know what exactly that that resolves. But there's no doubt that that something needed to happen."
Aikman also said he believes that the issues go well beyond Parker. As he states, the problems have been going on for quite a while, and the Cowboys haven't made such a drastic in-season move. For that reason, the Hall of Fame quarterback believes Parker has become a scapegoat for failures that aren't completely on him.
"I don't know Christian Parker that well. We visited with him before the Eagles game, and I was impressed with with our conversation. Seems like a good person, and I just hate the way the whole thing's unfolded," Aikman said.
"But the other thing to point out is is this isn't unique to to this year. I mean, this this has been going on for a while and there hasn't been an in season change like this. I hate it for him, and I hate that he's kind of being scapegoated to some extent for the for the failures that go well beyond him, or before him arriving in Dallas."
This is a question that's been asked about the Cowboys for 30 years now, and the answer remains the same. If the problems have persisted since Jimmy Johnson left, and Jerry Jones has been the primary decision-maker since then, he's clearly the problem. Jones has created a culture that prioritizes headlines over winning, and that's why the same problems come up every season regardless of the players or coaches who represent the franchise.
But pointing the finger at Jones won't do any good since he's never going to change. That being the case, we can ask who is responsible for their struggles in 2026.
First, let's be fair to Jones. While he takes a lot of heat for his antics, he did build a strong roster. The offense can be elite and the defense has the pieces to be average, which is all they need. Unfortunately, they have a head coach who is being out-coached every week. He's also been quick to pass the blame, which is what he's doing now with Parker.
Don't get it wrong, Parker has had his share of problems, but he's a first-year defensive coordinator. That was bound to happen.
What's inexcusable is the lack of discipline this team has shown, as well as their inability to stay focused in key situations, both on offense and defense. That's a problem that goes back to Schottenheimer, not Parker. But as Aikman said, "somebody's got to get pinned with it," and that somebody is Parker. At least for now.

title: Dak Prescott Deserves Better as Cowboys Star Gets Unfortunate NFL Label
full_text:
Quarterbacks get all the praise when their team wins and all the blame when they lose, but we all know it takes much more than one player to find success in the NFL. Perhaps no fan base understands this more than the Dallas Cowboys.
From Tony Romo to Dak Prescott, Dallas fans are used to watching their quarterback take the blame for failures all around them. That's been especially true for Prescott over the past two seasons as the Cowboys have had one of the worst defenses in the league .
That's why The Athletic's Mike Sando recently named Prescott the "most betrayed" quarterback through 10 weeks of the season. Sando uses a system that ranks each quarterback's EPA per start and compares it to the EPA of the team's defense and special teams. Looking at those numbers, Sando says Prescott has received the least help for the second year in a row.
"The Dallas Cowboys' Dak Prescott ranks as the most betrayed QB through Week 10 for a second consecutive season. His own production ranks eighth among the 37 qualifying quarterbacks, but his team's defense/special teams production in his starts ranks 36th (only Philadelphia's Tanner McKee has gotten worse support, on average, in his starts)," Sando wrote.
Fans know Prescott has been asked to carry a heavy burden this season, but seeing the numbers puts it into perspective. Making matters worse is knowing that this has been a theme in Dallas for several years, with no real change in sight.
Jerry Jones attempted to fix the problem this offseason by retooling the defense under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. After 10 weeks, they pulled the plug on Parker as he had his play-calling duties stripped.
While Parker will remain employed in Dallas, senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will be the one calling the plays. The Cowboys hope this change will help the offense find success, but it masks the real issue.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is somehow escaping the blame he deserves by making Parker a scapegoat. As the man who oversees the team, Schottenheimer has now been in charge for two of the worst defensive seasons in franchise history. Not only that, but he makes Prescott's life harder with his predictable play-calling on offense, which forces Dak to fight for every inch of offense .
That shouldn't be the case with players such as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal, but it proves that Prescott is betrayed by more than just the talent around him. His coaching staff lets him down just as much, if not more.

title: Stephen Jones Refuses to Elaborate on Cowboys' Christian Parker Decision
full_text:
Earlier this week, the Dallas Cowboys made the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties. For the remainder of the season, senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will handle that job , although Parker will remain on staff as the defensive coordinator.
It's an odd dynamic, and one that Parker said was tough to swallow at first. He admitted that he debated on leaving the team , but realized that wasn't the right answer. Instead, he will stick things out and is focused on helping the Cowboys defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 11.
As for the Cowboys, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he believes Parker's future is still bright with the team. He believes this could be a learning experience that helps the young coordinator find his footing. He also said there were some honest conversations had between him and Parker, which was more than Stephen Jones was willing to say.
While speaking with the San Antonio Sports Star, Jones admitted that the move was made due to their defensive struggles. Beyond that, he refused to get into any of the details , instead saying that the focus is on their opponent this weekend.
"We just felt like we were struggling and we needed to change it up. Obviously Christian is going to retain his role as DC and coach Pettine is going to call the plays and that's really where we stand on it," Jones said.
"Guys, we're not going to get into the detail or timing. We made a decision. We're ready to move forward. Our focus right now is to go beat the Titans."
Jones, who usually says far too much, is taking the right approach here. There's not much that needs to be said other than the fact that they were looking for a spark on defense. The Cowboys enter Week 11 ranked 30th in points surrendered and dead last in defensive yardage.
Considering they were just as inept on defense in 2025, the problem clearly goes far beyond Parker. That said, they're still in the NFC East race and decided their best chance of turning things around would be to get someone such as Pettine, who has far more experience, calling the plays. If that doesn't work (and there's a very real chance it won't), Jones and the rest of the front office need to have a serious conversation about the head coach.

title: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb Questions NFL After Big Fine From 49ers Hit
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered another tough loss in Week 10, falling to the San Francisco 49ers in a 46-40 finish.
Despite the disappointing result, the game wasn't without its fair share of big plays, thanks in large part to Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens.
Pickens' second touchdown of the day featured a violent block from CeeDee Lamb, who laid out 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, sending him airborne.
But as a result, Lamb told reporters Thursday that the NFL fined him $30,000 for the hit.
Lamb made it clear that potential fines have previously prevented him from trying to deliver hard blocks in the open field.
“I can block and I'm real good at doing things like that, but I get fined,” he said. “So that's where I kind of retract from doing all that. And to answer your question, I got fined $30,000 in case anybody was worrying.”
Lamb says the fine was indeed due to what the league viewed as a helmet-to-helmet play.
“Yes, but I didn’t hit with my helmet. That’s a conversation for another day.”
He questioned the NFL's decision, saying it's hypocritical to fine a receiver for delivering a violent block but not applying the same ruling to defensive backs.
“You know what? I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can't deliver to punch," Lamb said.
As Pickens reaches the goal line, Lamb lowers his shoulder into Lenoir but clearly doesn't lead with his helmet, though it looks like their helmets make contact. Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown got fined for something similar after a forced fumble against the Arizona Cardinals, where he led with the shoulder but still made unintentional helmet-to-helmet contact.
The block wasn't really necessary, as Pickens was already a few steps away from the end zone, but Lamb got hit with the fine nonetheless.
Here's a look at the play Lamb is referring to.
GEORGE PICKENS SCORES ANOTHER SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hITd6CtBqp
Despite the fine, Cowboys fans surely loved seeing their star receiver lay the boom in a rivalry game against San Francisco.
There's often a stereotype that star-studded NFL players, especially receivers, would rather avoid delivering physical blocks in order to protect themselves but Lamb shut down that notion.
But maybe the fine is for the best. Dallas doesn't need Lamb putting himself in harm's way. If the Cowboys want any chance at winning the NFC East and making the playoffs, Lamb has to be on the field and not on the injury list due to unnecessary blocks.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over Raiders in Week 11
full_text:
The Denver Broncos return from the bye and, in the second half of the season, face what is considered the easier part of their schedule, with just two plus-.500 teams remaining.
Of course, what's easier on paper doesn't always translate to the field. And while the Las Vegas Raiders are 4-6, with all their wins coming against teams with a losing record, that doesn't mean the Broncos can take Sunday's game for granted.
New Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak — the son of former Denver Broncos backup quarterback and Super Bowl-winning head coach Gary Kubiak — has shown he can do some good things. And while the Raiders may be without tight end Brock Bowers , they still have some talented players on the roster.
The Broncos cannot afford to look past the Raiders, particularly with the AFC West crown still at stake. Let's look at the three keys to the Broncos beating the Raiders in Week 11.
While the Broncos are doing a better job on offense in more recent games, they have yet to be consistently good for four quarters. If there ever were a week for the Broncos to show they can string together four quality quarters of offense, this is it.
The Raiders have given up 3,851 yards of total offense to opponents this season. While their defense has some quality pass rushers — namely Maxx Crosby, who leads his team with 35 pressures and five sacks — the Raiders have struggled in other areas.
In particular, the Raiders have been bad against the run. They've given up 1,511 rushing yards to opponents thus far at 4.9 yards per carry. The only opponent to get fewer than 100 yards rushing against Las Vegas was Miami in Week 1.
There's no excuse for the Broncos not getting it done in the run game this week. If Jonah Coleman doesn't have his best game of the season and J.K. Dobbins doesn't show consistency, then something is wrong here.
Head coach Sean Payton is aware of the issues with the running game and has hinted at what must be done to fix it. We'll see what Payton has in mind on Sunday, but between run blocking and the performance of the backs themselves, it's time for the Broncos to get it together there.
If Denver can do that, it will help mitigate the Raiders' pass rush and take some pressure off Bo Nix. That should allow Nix to settle down and press his advantage in the passing game, where the Raiders have some issues in the secondary.
We've heard the talk from Payton about the need to fix the running game issues. Now it's time to deliver with a quality run game.
Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, had a solid debut against the Seattle Seahawks this past week. He completed 62.2% of his passes, with seven of his 37 attempts considered bad throws. He had no turnovers, and two of his receivers dropped passes.
Where the Seahawks were able to get to Mendoza was through the pass rush. They pressured Mendoza on 42.9% of his dropbacks, blitzed him nine times, and got seven QB hits and five sacks.
If Bowers doesn't play, that means the Raiders are without their top playmaker. They can still get production out of fellow tight end Michael Mayer and wide receiver Tre Tucker, but they aren't the caliber of player Bowers is.
Additionally, the Raiders haven't been good at running the football. Ashton Jeanty has struggled, averaging just 3.1 yards per carry this season. Rookie Mike Washington has had more success with 3.8 yards per carry, but he's not a game-changer.
The Broncos, of course, can't take anything for granted when it comes to the Raiders' skill positions. But the Seahawks showed that the best way to neutralize Mendoza is to pressure him.
We'll see whether Vance Joseph decides to dial up more pressure and not be content to drop too many players into coverage. And while the Broncos might not force many turnovers against Mendoza, if they get pass rushers to him as often as the Seahawks did, it should limit the rookie's impact.
The one area where the Raiders have excelled is on special teams, so this is where the Broncos need to be at their best. The Raiders have a couple of third-phase players who have done their part to keep them in games.
Dylan Laube has 822 yards on 26 kickoff returns, including a 95-yarder for a touchdown against the New York Jets. The Broncos' kickoff return team will need to keep a close eye on him, as he can be dangerous.
Punter AJ Cole currently leads the NFL in punting, with 52.1 yards per punt. His net average is 44.6. He has pinned opponents inside the 20-yard line on 41.2% of his punts.
The Raiders aren't as threatening in the punt return game, though Malik Benson does have a 23-yard return to his credit. The Broncos will have to be as disciplined in punt coverage as they are in kickoff coverage.
The good news is that the Broncos' special teams is one of the better units in the NFL and has mostly done well with coverage. But this week, the Broncos' coverage units will likely get their biggest test yet.
As for the Broncos' own punt return game, Marvin Mims Jr. hasn't been as explosive in that department this season. Given how well Cole has played, Mims might not get as many opportunities.
But this is a game where special teams could be a big factor, as it's the one area in which the Raiders rank among the top teams in the NFL.
One should not assume that the Broncos' easier schedule ahead means that a win against the Raiders is all but in the bag. That's particularly true when it's an AFC West rival that would love nothing more than to surprise everyone with a win.
The Broncos have to approach the Raiders as though they're facing a top team. If the Broncos manage to build an early lead, they need to keep playing well and keep the Raiders from getting back into the game.
There are still those who have doubts as to whether the Broncos are capable of a deep playoff run. A decisive win over the Raiders would be another step toward showing that the Broncos belong in the Super Bowl conversation.

title: Two Key Matchups That Give Broncos a Decisive Edge vs. Raiders
full_text:
Coming off a bye, the Denver Broncos have to be licking their chops with the Las Vegas Raiders next up on the schedule.
The Broncos will face a Raiders team with serious, exploitable issues on both sides of the ball. The door is wide open for Denver to have a big game.
Of course, the Broncos have to go out there and exploit those issues without shooting themselves in the foot. If the Broncos can win these two key matchups, they'll be in a prime spot to walk out with their eighth win of the season, which would give them the AFC West-leading tiebreaker and vault them back to the No. 2 playoff seed.
The Raiders have been one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL, and when narrowing it down to position groups, they're terrible against tight ends. Opponents haven't really attacked them with running backs in the passing game, mainly because they don't have to, due to the Raiders' tight end issues.
Opponents remain highly efficient when using their running backs in the passing game against the Raiders.
Dean has played well, but Walker has been a liability in coverage for the Raiders' defense. Engram and Coleman are the two prime weapons the Broncos can use to exploit Walker.
The Broncos can mix it up between Coleman and Engram on Walker, but whoever Walker ends up covering should be a quick and easy read for Bo Nix to keep the Broncos ahead of the sticks.
Over the years, Joseph has done well against rookie quarterbacks, and Mendoza will be starting his second game . It will be interesting to see what Joseph pulls out to deal with Mendoza, not only in the coverage looks but also in the pressure looks up front.
It won't be surprising to see Joseph unveil some new tricks and looks to heap more onto Mendoza's plate and add to the difficulty of playing the Broncos' defense at Mile High.
The Raiders' offensive line is terrible, so Joseph should be able to create looks to exploit the unit's awareness and chemistry issues. Combine that with some new and creative coverage looks, and Mendoza will have a tough go of it.
He's a rookie quarterback getting his second start and it's on Joseph to expose him.

title: Brock Bowers' Injury Situation Just Took an Unwelcome Turn for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are getting healthier as the practice week progresses.
Coming off their bye, the Broncos are close to full strength, not counting the handful of players on injured reserve, some of whom they'll be getting back in the next few weeks.
Things are looking good on the health front for the Broncos, and they're still buzzing over the Riley Moss extension , but things are also improving for the Las Vegas Raiders. Let's take a look at how Thursday's practice report shook out for both teams.
Everyone but Jones was a full participant on Thursday, including Abrams-Draine, who was limited on Wednesday. Jones remains limited, but given that he's had nearly three weeks to bounce back from his hamstring injury, there's a good chance he'll play on Sunday, even if he ends up listed as questionable on the final injury report.
But that's me putting an optimistic spin on things. The Broncos have been without Hufanga for the past four games, so just getting him back will be great for the defense, but having him and Jones patrolling the back end will be just what the doctor ordered.
Lohner continues to practice in full after the Broncos started his clock to return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on Wednesday. It's unclear when the Broncos plan to make a decision on Lohner, but it could come before Sunday's game.
If Lohner gets activated, though, the Broncos will need to make room on the 53-man roster, and they already have four tight ends. With each practice Lohner has, there are a handful of guys at the bottom of the roster who get a little more uncomfortable.
Allen and Sutton returned to full participation, too, though they're limited designation on Wednesday was for rest only, as the Broncos ease them back into the swing of things after the bye. If Jones can progress on Friday, all the health stars will be aligned for Denver.
The Raiders have been trying out kickers this week with Gay's injury, but the real story on Thursday was Bowers's return to practice. The star tight end suffered a " significant " injury on Sunday against Seattle, and did not return in the second half.
Bowers didn't participate on Wednesday, but he was back out there on Thursday, albeit in limited form. Sources close to the Raiders indicate he's very focused on trying to play this game against the Broncos, so despite the early signs this week being unfavorable, it's too soon to count him out.

title: Gut Reaction: 3 Big Takeaways From Riley Moss' $67M Broncos Extension
full_text:
At one point, I didn't think it was likely that the Denver Broncos would extend cornerback Riley Moss. The 2023 third-round pick would have drawn interest — and a significant payday — if he had made it to the open market.
But the Broncos got a deal done on Thursday, keeping Moss in the fold for the next few seasons as he agreed to terms on a four-year, $67 million extension that runs through 2030.
It may take some time before we know more about the finer points, such as fully guaranteed money, injury-only guarantees, contract structure, and whether or not option bonuses or void years were utilized.
But let's consider a few things about what this contract extension means.
First, while the Broncos didn't get the deal done during the bye week, they actually got it done earlier in the season than the multiple extensions they finalized during last year's bye.
Last year, the Broncos' bye was in Week 12, while this season's was Week 10. Thus, general manager George Paton got a deal done with Moss a week earlier than the three extensions he inked last year.
It's another example of Paton's willingness to get deals done with players during the regular season, and he was right on schedule when it came to this extension for Moss.
Time will tell whether Paton gets any other players extended in the coming weeks, but if there are others the Broncos see as a priority to keep, they could still strike in the next few weeks.
It's important to note that the fourth-year cornerback could have made more money if he had hit the open market in 2027 free agency. Instead, Moss took a deal that, while still a considerable sum at $16.75 million per year, was less than he might have found elsewhere.
It shows that Moss wants to be with the Broncos. He likes the organization, the coaching staff, and his teammates. While he certainly wanted to be well-compensated, he showed that it wasn't just about the money.
Moss's deal pays him less in terms of average per-year salary than the Los Angeles Rams gave Jaylen Watson during the 2026 offseason. The flipside, though, is that Watson signed for three years while Moss signed for four.
Again, we should know more about Moss's contract details in the days to come, but it will be interesting to see how much he got in full and total guarantees. Watson got $26.5 million fully guaranteed and an additional $7.5 million in injury-only guarantees.
A four-year deal would allow the Broncos to put more fully guaranteed money into the deal. Thus, it wouldn't be a surprise if Moss got more guaranteed money than Watson and stood to earn more over the long term.
Finally, the Broncos showed that they want to keep their homegrown players in the fold if they have proven themselves worthy of an extension. That means we can't rule out an extension for Ja'Quan MacMillian at some point.
Other teams might not have tried to keep a player like Moss around if they expected his free-agent market to be so strong. But the Broncos saw things differently and kept a player whom many people (myself included) expected to move on after 2026.
I'm happy to eat crow on this one. It's good to see the Broncos get a deal done with Moss and secure an important part of the defense for a few more seasons.
