title: Broncos' Riley Moss Extension Raises New Questions About Ja'Quan McMillian
full_text:
Just when Denver Broncos fans had written off the possibility of GM George Paton getting any in-season extensions done, the Riley Moss news hit the wire on Thursday morning.
It wasn't technically done over the bye week — as Paton has done with four different players over the past two years — but the Broncos extended Moss to a four-year, $67 million deal that'll keep him in the fold through 2030.
Moss gets $16.75 million per year as one of the NFL's best No. 2 cornerbacks, which is a pretty nice bargain, given the projections this past offseason that he could command $20-plus million on the open market.
It's great news for Moss and the Broncos' defense. But what does it mean for nickel cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian?
Many Broncos fans fear that since the Broncos obviously prioritized Moss first, perhaps McMillian doesn't fit into the team's post-2026 plans. That trepidation was only intensified by The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson , who reported on Thursday afternoon that there "haven't been serious discussions" yet between McMillian and the Broncos.
Tempering Tomasson's report, though, was 9NEWS ' Mike Klis, who said in an appearance on 104.3 The FAN's Dover and Cecil show on Thursday that the Moss deal "doesn't affect Ja'Quan."
"Ja'Quan's going to get his deal, too. I think they're going to work on securing him also," Klis said on The FAN.
So, if you're pining for a McMillian extension , let not your heart be troubled. The NFL trade deadline, coming a few days into the Broncos' bye, likely pushed some of Paton's plans back.
The drama of the failed Daiyan Henley trade and its subsequent fallout only further delayed any extension actions Paton could take. McMillian will get his — of this, I have no doubt.
McMillian is one of the NFL's best nickel cornerbacks. And he's the Broncos' best ballhawk, which is important for a defense that has struggled, at times, to take the ball away over the past few years.
The Broncos' have improved their takeaway numbers this season, even though McMillian only has one interception. But it was a doozy, picking off Sam Darnold in overtime to help seal a big win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6.
In the four years McMillian has been the Broncos' nickel, his fingerprints have been on seven interceptions, five forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 10 sacks. He's also broken up 31 passes, and this doesn't count playoffs.
McMillian has the clutch gene. It was his amazing overtime interception in the divisional round of the playoffs that helped the Broncos clinch a 33-30 win over the Buffalo Bills to advance to the AFC championship game.
JA'QUAN MCMILLIAN INTERCEPTION BUFvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/S3yuoRu30c
The only knock on McMillian is his 5-foot-10, 183-pound size, though he plays much bigger. He's an extremely physical player, as evidenced by his sack totals and tackle numbers (221 over his four-year run as a starter).
However, the NFL has transitioned to bigger nickels over the past two years as offenses have prioritized two- and three-tight-end personnel sets. We're seeing more 'big nickel' types, meaning guys like, say, a Devon Key, who may otherwise be a safety, but is just a little bit bigger and well-equipped to handle the physical assignment of running with tight ends in coverage and shedding their blocks to make tackles in the run game.
For the most part, though, McMillian has gotten around this obstacle against opponents, like the Los Angeles Rams, who've deployed heavy tight-end sets. And while it's a factor that defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has to take into consideration as a schemer and play-caller, it's the last thing on Denver's mind when it comes to McMillian.
Undrafted out of Eastern Carolina in 2022, McMillian appeared in one game as a rookie, before beating out experienced nickel K'Waun Williams for the starting job in 2023. McMillian has never looked back.
As a restricted free agent this past offseason, the Broncos tendered McMillian at the second-round level, which guaranteed him $5.8 million in 2026. He's been worth every penny.
McMillian's time will come. And it wouldn't surprise me if an extension gets done before the 2026 season ends.
Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron have played a lot this season, thanks to a three-game absence of Patrick Surtain II and a couple of Moss injuries. While the young tandem turned in some admirable play, especially in Week 6's win over the Seahawks, it wasn't enough to persuade the Broncos to kick the Moss can down the road.
The same will hold true for McMillian. Abrams-Draine, a 2024 fifth-round pick, has another year left on his rookie deal, while Barron is in just his second year as a 2025 first-rounder. Abrams-Draine is clearly a boundary corner, while Barron has proven that he's not reliable outside the numbers, and belongs inside.
When it comes to their top three cornerbacks — Surtain, Moss, and McMillian — there's a comfort and a confidence there for the Broncos. The Broncos want to keep that trio intact, and will find a way to get McMillian re-signed; it's just a matter of when.

title: Broncos Lock Down CB Riley Moss with Massive Contract Extension
full_text:
It was Garett Bolles in 2024 . Then Luke Wattenberg in 2025. Now it's Riley Moss' turn to cash out with the Denver Broncos coming out of a bye week.
And cash out he did, agreeing to a four-year, $67 million contract extension on Thursday, ahead of the team's Week 11 home matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. The deal was reported by multiple media outlets and confirmed by 9NEWS insider Mike Klis.
Moss is now the NFL's 23rd-highest-paid cornerback at $16.75 million per year — a substantial leap from the $1.36 million he's earning in 2026 as part of his initial rookie deal.
A former third-round draft pick, Moss has appeared in eight games this season (missing one due to a rib injury), notching 17 solo tackles, eight pass breakups, and one interception across 434 defensive snaps.
Moss ranks as the league's 28th-best CB among 105 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus , which also assigned him the 21st-highest coverage mark (71.6).
“The one thing about him is his grit and his competes, and those guys [are] out there on an island a lot of times, so there’s going to be times where it’s not always what you want and yet, and he’s onto the next play. I think that’s a great skill set he has," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Moss in September.
Especially after the Daiyan Henley ordeal , this was an especially pragmatic move by Broncos general manager George Paton, who continues his longstanding habit of locking down players during the regular season.
Denver secured Moss on an extremely team-friendly pact, certainly less than he would've gotten by testing the unrestricted free-agent waters this coming offseason. It ensures both starting CBs — Moss and Patrick Surtain II — are manning the defensive backfield for the long term.
Some fans will express disappointment that Moss was signed over several other extension candidates, including CB Ja'Quan McMillian, wide receiver/returner Marvin Mims, and safety Brandon Jones. McMillian now seems destined to shop his wares on the open market.
But young, capable boundary cornerbacks don't exactly grow on trees, and Moss has shown more good than bad during his starting tenure in the Mile High City, which makes his new contract palatable — if not preferable.

title: Bo Nix Gets Candid About the Harsh Reality Facing Fernando Mendoza
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are about to face Fernando Mendoza for the first time, though it won't be the last.
Drafted No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this year, Mendoza is poised to make just his second career start against the Broncos on Sunday . The former Indiana Hoosiers National Champion and Heisman Winner had to face the Seattle Seahawks in his first-ever start last week, and while the rookie hung in there, the Raiders lost the game 21-13.
That's something Mendoza has in common with Bo Nix: both players' first-ever NFL starts came against Mike Macdonald's Seahawks defense. Much like Mendoza, Nix got his licks in against the Seahawks, rushing for a touchdown, but ultimately lost the game in Seattle , 26-20. Nix did get to balance the scales by defeating the Seahawks in Denver a few weeks back.
At least Mendoza got to start his first NFL game at home, though. The rookie didn't find the end zone as a passer against Seattle, but he did rush for a touchdown, just like Nix.
With Kirk Cousins traded to the Minnesota Vikings last week, the Mendoza era has officially begun in Vegas, and the Raiders aren't looking back. The Broncos can expect to see Mendoza twice per year for the foreseeable future.
Nix will make his 44th regular-season start on Sunday against the Raiders. Suffice it to say, Nix knows exactly what his Silver and Black counterpart is going through as a rookie starter, but he said it will get easier for Mendoza.
"It's night and day," Nix said on Wednesday. "It's hard for a rookie quarterback. I don't care if you're sitting behind a guy like Kirk [Cousins] who you can learn from, but you still have to go out there and ultimately play and ultimately do it. And so it's not easy. And to his credit, he played a really good defense last week. He's going to play a really good one this week."
Nix had to face Macdonald's Seahawks and Mike Tomlin's Pittsburgh Steelers to open up his NFL career two years ago. And nobody knows better than Nix: there's no way to make it an easier on a rookie quarterback. The only way out is through, so to speak, meaning a quarterback can only learn and develop by going through the refiner's fire.
"Unfortunately, the world's not going to give him any time to go through the obstacles that it takes as a rookie quarterback. But for him, he'll continue to develop," Nix said of Mendoza. "He's a smart kid, and he's played in big moments in college. I think that does translate, and he's going to work hard and continue to get better."
Mendoza seems to have a grit about him, but it's too early to say for sure how much his experience playing on the biggest college football stages will truly serve him as an NFL quarterback. Let's first see how the rookie fares against a Broncos defense that's ranked near the top of the league in sacks, and has a legitimate chance to three-peat as NFL sack champions.
"I would say, in my opinion, it gets easier," Nix said. "It's not always going to stay difficult, like he probably feels it is now."
Nix vs. Justin Herbert has been a great quarterback rivalry. Nix vs. Patrick Mahomes has been even better, as the Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs vie for the AFC West crown.
On Sunday, Broncos and Raiders fans will be treated to the first iteration of Nix vs. Mendoza. Although the Raiders are 4-6, I'd caution against overlooking them; remember the brutality of their last trip to Mile High?
The Broncos narrowly escaped with a 10-7 win and it came at the cost of losing running back J.K. Dobbins for the season. Now, that was a different coaching staff with a different quarterback, but Klint Kubiak and Mendoza will be coming in hot, looking to upset the Broncos.
It doesn't appear as if Mendoza will have Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers , though. But that will only mean that Denver will have to lock in on Michael Mayer, Bowers's backup who is currently the fifth-highest-paid tight end in the NFL.
If Denver takes care of business, though, its AFC West record will climb to 3-1 this season, wresting  back the tiebreaker over the Chiefs for the divisional lead. The stakes are big for Denver, even with the Raiders being a sub-.500 team right now.
Expect Nix and company to handle their business against Mendoza and the Raiders. But it won't be easy.

title: Broncos' Injury Report Delivers Triple Dose of Good News
full_text:
The Denver Broncos just had their first practice since enjoying a well-earned bye .
The 7-2 Broncos are preparing to host the 4-6 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Don't let the Raiders' schedule fool you; the Broncos are expecting a divisional rock-fight.
"The one thing that I've learned, noticed, and have witnessed myself is it doesn't matter what a team's record is when you're talking about divisional games because they're going to show up and play hard no matter what," Courtland Sutton said on Wednesday. "And the Raiders have always been that team. No matter what their record is, they always show up and play the Broncos really hard."
Be ready for anything. The Raiders are no longer led by Kirk Cousins, after he was traded to the Minnesota Vikings; it's rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza under center now. The Broncos will get their first-ever look at the No. 1 overall pick in the draft and former Heisman Trophy winner.
The bye week afforded some of Denver's injured players the opportunity to rest and recover. In the first practice report of Week 11, there are several encouraging developments and a couple of concerns we'll be monitoring over the next few days.
The big news is Lohner's return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List. The Broncos started his clock today, buying themselves a 21-day window to decide whether to activate him.
If they don't activate Lohner, he'll be unavailable the rest of the season. If he is activated — and we should assume he will be — it'll be interesting to see how the Broncos juggle the roster math. At whose expense will Lohner's return be? Rookie tight end Dallen Bentley? Or it could be a player at another position.
Hufanga is back after missing the past four games with an ankle. He was close to going in Week 9 in Carolina, but the Broncos were cautious with their All-Pro safety.
Meanwhile, all three players who suffered concussions in Carolina returned to practice in full, meaning they've cleared the protocol. Moss and Waddle are starters, so their return will be huge, while Prentice is a key role player who also contributes a lot on special teams.
Don't worry about Allen or Sutton. The Broncos just gave them a vet day of sorts to ease them back into action coming off the bye.
Abrams-Draine and Jones are a little more concerning, being limited, but it's too early to get worried. They've had two weeks to heal up, so we'll monitor Thursday and Friday's practice report, but it would be a surprise if they weren't cleared to play on Sunday.
We're keeping a close eye on tight end Brock Bowers, who suffered a "significant" ankle injury on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks. He didn't practice on Wednesday, and I wouldn't expect to see that change on Thursday.
If Bowers is a no-go on Friday, he'll likely be ruled out of action. But if he's limited, there's a chance he could play.
People I've talked to close to Raiders HQ aren't sure whether Bowers will play this week, but being the type of competitor he is, it's believed he'll do everything within his power to make it happen.
So, don't sleep on the possibility of Bowers playing in this one. And that's more than a little concerning, given the Broncos' struggles in covering tight ends this season.

title: 5 Broncos Who Have Exceeded Expectations at the Midway Point
full_text:
Even the most optimistic fans would have to admit that the Denver Broncos have exceeded expectations thus far.
Emerging from the bye at 7-2, in a vacuum, isn't all that surprising, especially given that the Broncos won 14 games last season. But with their brutal schedule through the first half of the season, not many many people expected Denver to weather that storm as successfully as it has.
If the Broncos have exceeded expectations as a team, it's because several players have also surprised at the individual level. We've highlighted the Broncos' biggest disappointments , so as promised, it's now time to flip the coin and focus on the five players who've outkicked their coverage coming out of the bye.
I think most Broncos fans believed Coleman was going to be good, but in the four games in which he's actually touched the ball, he's been great. And in each of those games, the rookie fourth-rounder has made his presence felt, contributing to each one of them as a victory.
Since returning from injured reserve in Week 7, Coleman went from the training table to the starting lineup. You don't see that often with a rookie, especially on a Sean Payton team, but since his return, Coleman has outearned J.K. Dobbins in snap and touch share, and it's not even close.
Coleman has carried the ball 47 times for 191 yards (4.1 avg) and three touchdowns, with 13 receptions for 128 yards. His burst and vision have been sorely needed in the Broncos' backfield.
Jonah Coleman gets the @Broncos back in the end zone! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E9pCf15J6A
For a fourth-rounder to be the Broncos' RB1 at the midway point of the season, with $16 million invested in Dobbins and a second-rounder invested in RJ Harvey, it's safe to say that Coleman has exceeded expectations early on. Coleman is a big reason why the Broncos didn't trade for a running back ahead of last week's deadline.
Coleman is really the Broncos' only offensive player I can say has exceeded expectations. It's going to be fun watching the rookie cook down the stretch.
According to John Franklin-Myers , the Broncos didn't even approach him about an extension before he hit free agency and signed with the Tennessee Titans. The Broncos watched his 14.5 sacks walk out the door willingly because they were so confident in Roach.
Roach secured the bag last year during the bye, signing a two-year, $7 million extension . And based on how he's played this season, he's just scratching the surface of his earning potential. The Broncos actually got him at a bargain.
Roach currently ranks third on the team with 25 pressures and has notched four sacks. He's been a force against the run and the pass, and he's showcased a growing penchant for making the clutch-time play.
BRONCOS WIN pic.twitter.com/A4SWB4IO4L
JFM's career-high in sacks came last year with the Broncos, with 7.5. Roach is on pace to surpass it. Heck, Roach could maybe even get to double-digit sacks, as the schedule is opening up for the Broncos post-bye.
Robinson was a 2025 fourth-round pick who spent most of his rookie year as a healthy scratch. But he learned a lot as a rookie, kept developing, and when Jonathon Cooper was placed on the commissioner's exempt list for six weeks to start the season, Robinson capitalized on the opportunity for actual playing time.
Zach Allen leads the pass rush 😤 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awIGMbyXcq
As a rotational rusher, Robinson is currently tied with Roach for the third-most on the team (25), and he has two sacks. He's been tough for opponents to stop, and a consistent force on the edge.
If things don't go swimmingly for Cooper in his ongoing criminal case, Robinson's Year-2 emergence gives the Broncos plenty of confidence if they have to make a tough decision. No doubt about it, Robinson has been one of the biggest pleasant surprises of the 2026 season.
As the fifth corner on the depth chart, it can be tough to get a snap in edge-wise, but injuries to Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss vaulted Abrams-Draine onto the field this season. Affectionately known as 'K.A.D.' by the fans, when the chance came to play again on defense, he was more than equal to his opportunity.
K.A.D. notched a crucial interception in the clutch in the Broncos' Week 6 overtime win over the Seatle Seahawks, and he currently ranks third on the team with five pass break-ups. He's also been significantly more reliable as a tackler, with 16 solo tackles thus far.
Kris Abrams-Draine might've made the play of the day for Denver. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cccQFhEuyP
K.A.D. missed Week 9 with an ankle, but he should be good to go coming out of the bye. I'm excited to see what opportunities may come his way down the stretch for Denver's sticky man in coverage.
It's unsexy, but Crawshaw deserves to be on this list. The 2025 sixth-round pick had an up and down rookie season, but he came on strong down the stretch.
Fast forward to the present moment, and Crawshaw ranks second in the NFL in net punting average (44.2). His coffin-corner punts have helped the Broncos flip field position and pin opponents deep.
As time marches on, the Broncos are looking all the smarter for investing a draft pick in Crawshaw. He could become an All-Pro punter, as soon as this season.

title: Broncos Move Closer to Getting Intriguing Pass-Catching TE Back
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are starting the clock on an intriguing, young — albeit star-crossed — pass-catcher.
9NEWS insider Mike Klis reported Wednesday that Denver has activated tight end Caleb Lohner from injured reserve, opening his 21-day practice window after being sidelined since June with a lower-body injury.
Klis guesses Lohner will likely need to exhaust most of the practice period before a final decision is made on his potential 2026 debut. After 21 days, the team must either place him on the 53-man roster or leave him on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.
A 2025 seventh-round pick , Lohner spent the majority of his rookie campaign on Denver's practice squad, save for a promotion ahead of January's Divisional Round win over the Bills (he was inactive for the game).
Lohner enjoyed an impressive offseason program this past spring, positioning himself as a hidden offensive gem due to his 6-foot-7-inch stature and college basketball background — this, however, was before undergoing a "routine" cleanup procedure on and "setback" with what general manager George Paton later revealed to be his foot.
“He’s looked good. He was having a really good offseason and obviously had a setback with the foot. We expect him, I’m not sure the timetable, mid-season maybe. Don’t hold me to that," Paton told reporters on Aug. 30. "He has all the traits: the size, he can run, he has great ball skills being a basketball player. This would have been a really important preseason and training camp for him. He just needs reps. We’re still excited about him. He’s here every day working, but we won’t see him until late October or so.”
An aforementioned basketball convert, Lohner had a brief but incredibly productive football stint for the Utah Utes, recording 54 receiving yards across four receptions — all of which went for touchdowns. He also scored a two-point conversion.
Upon drafting him, Broncos head coach Sean Payton compared Lohner to his former Pro Bowl tight end with the New Orleans Saints, Jimmy Graham. Payton also singled out the latter in May among the early standouts of the offseason program.
I’ll tell you who stood out, Caleb. He looks entirely different in this camp," Payton said. "Now he was here in this camp a year ago as a draft pick, but he stood out. ... You just start with total reps in the bank in football, and there was just a lot less. You’re drafting traits at that point in the draft. We’ve done that before, and sometimes you’re drafting traits [and] you see a receiving tight end. The one thing I know watching him is he’ll be plenty and very physical."
While it could take Lohner some time to meaningfully see the field — if he does at all — the Broncos' league-worst TE corps offer a fairly easy path to opportunity, with only Evan Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins comprising the depth chart.
In a best-case scenario, Lohner will provide quarterback Bo Nix with another big-bodied weapon in the red zone and between the hashes. In a worst-case, he remains buried under the veteran players, his extended absence too much to overcome as far as 2026 is concerned.

title: Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs Is 'Gaining Strength' Each Week
full_text:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is not showing any signs of slowing down anytime soon.
According to head coach Dan Campbell and running backs coach Tashard Choice, the film showcases a player that Gibbs is only getting stronger as the 2026 NFL season progresses.
“I feel like he's gaining strength," said Campbell. "I feel like he's gaining strength as we go here through the season and we go through these games. We come out of New England game and as everybody does, you break down these games as a staff and you go through the players, the scheme, what did we do well, what did we not? Who are the players playing at a top level? Who are the guys that we can help here a little bit, need a little bit of help in some areas.
"And (Tashard) Choice made that comment, and he's 100 percent right, that it just feels like he's gaining strength. He came in, I mentioned this before, he came in phenomenal shape in training camp, prepared to take the load. And as this season's gone on, he's getting stronger. And so yeah, I think the best way to say it, I love where he's at right now.”
Quarterback Jared Goff mentioned the former first-round pick has not elevated himself to be talked about in the same sentence as some of the all-time great NFL running backs.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 2026 Midseason Offensive Grades
“You look at the numbers he's doing, it's like you hear his name mentioned with LaDainian Tomlinson it seems like every week. Obviously, we know about that guy, and yeah, he's unbelievable," said Goff. "He really is. He's a special player. He's a special guy, special teammate. The work he puts in I think gets unnoticed sometimes. He's a worker and has elevated his game from last year to this year in a lot of ways that you guys have obviously seen and it's paid off. It's been great for him and he's playing really well.”
The veteran signal-caller also pointed out that many do see just how competitive the former Alabama Crimson Tide running back is during each practice.
"He's very competitive. Anytime there's a competitive situation in practice, he wants the ball, he wants to make someone look silly, he wants to make somebody miss and he wants to make the play," said Goff. "And when he doesn't, he gets upset and that's kind of what you like to see when he makes a mistake or misses a block.
"He's truly upset about it and that's a sign of a good player and a guy who's striving for greatness.”

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup With Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking at the second game of a crucial three-game stretch midway through the NFL season.
After dispatching of the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the Lions are returning home to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 at Ford Field. Detroit has a chance to remain in first-place in the NFC North heading into a Thanksgiving clash with the Chicago Bears next week.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding the Lions’ matchup with the Buccaneers.
Barring any changes or last-second set-backs, Sunday is expected to mark the season debut for safety Kerby Joseph . The Illinois product hasn’t appeared in a game in over a calendar year with what is being reported as a degenerative knee issue, but has looked good in practice and will get an opportunity to return to action on Sunday.
It will be interesting to see exactly how the Lions utilize Joseph, as they’ve spent the last three weeks ramping him up to his return. If he can contribute in a fairly significant way in his first game back, it will be a huge boost to the confidence of the defense.
The Lions will be facing a Buccaneers team littered with former Lions, with linebacker Alex Anzalone headlining the group. Anzalone departed Detroit after five years this past offseason, and was a huge part of the team’s resurgence throughout his time in Motown.
Joining Anzalone on the Buccaneers’ defense are players like Al-Quadin Muhammad, Ifeatu Melifonwu, A’Shawn Robinson and Miles Killebrew. All had different tenures in Detroit, but it will be an opportunity for all to make a statement against their former team.
Lions quarterback Jared Goff had been playing at an MVP-caliber level with zero interceptions through the first six games of the year. However, those fortunes have changed over the past three weeks.
Goff has thrown a total of four picks in that stretch, including two last week against the Patriots. One of those picks was an especially devastating mistake, as he was picked off in the end-zone late in the first half. The Buccaneers rank first in the league with 16 interceptions, and as a result Goff will have to be careful against the opportunistic defense.
The Buccaneers have two players that have four interceptions each, those being Anzalone and cornerback Zyon McCollum. Interestingly enough, Robinson has two interceptions from the defensive line as well.
The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s game in a dubious situation, in part due to an injury that kept Baker Mayfield out of three games. Tampa Bay currently ranks first in rushing offense led by Bucky Irving’s 825 yards, but ranks last in passing offense.
As a result, the Lions will likely enter Sunday’s game in need of a plan for stifling the run game and forcing Tampa Bay to throw. They have talent on the perimeter, with Irving serving as a receiving threat in addition to Emeka Egbuka, Tez Johnson and Chris Godwin, but Mayfield’s injuries have prevented them from getting going consistently.
The Lions will be without defensive end Aidan Hutchinson for the remainder of the season, which is a devastating blow to a defense that is already without another one of its leaders in linebacker Jack Campbell.
Hutchinson's injury will likely create opportunities for rookie Derrick Moore, who is on a hot streak with four sacks in his last two games. Additionally, it appears that this is paving the way for Ahmed Hassanein to make his debut.
Detroit has gotten plenty of pass-rush production from its other options, including Alim McNeill and DJ Wonnum. Hutchinson will by no means be easy to replace, but the team has options available to help them produce and pressure opposing passers.
The Lions will wear their black alternate uniforms for the second time this season, and the seventh time in total since they re-entered the rotation prior to the 2024 season. Detroit is 5-1 all-time wearing these uniforms, with the lone loss coming to Buffalo late in the 2024 campaign.
Detroit wore these in their most recent matchup with the Buccaneers, that being on Monday Night Football in Week 7 of last year. That was the ‘Legion of Whom?’ game, where Detroit’s secondary stifled Tampa Bay despite being without multiple starters.
Now, as Detroit looks to extend its winning streak to six games this year, they’ll be hoping to get more magic from their ‘Motor City Muscle’ uniforms.
All indications point to defensive end Ahmed Hassanein making his NFL debut on Sunday. It has been a bit of a tumultuous road to get there for the Boise State product, but it appears as though he’ll get his chance after being inactive for the team’s first nine games.
Hassanein was set to make the team as a rookie last year, but suffered an injury late in the preseason and was waived with an injury designation. At the conclusion of his injury settlement, he returned to Detroit on the practice squad but did not appear in a game.
After signing a futures contract to return, Hassanein made the team out of camp but has yet to appear in a game. Now, the motivated defender will get his chance to make an impact for the first time in his career against the Buccaneers.
The Lions remain focused on the task at hand with a big game looming on a short week and handle business. They batter Tampa Bay’s top-tier run defense, as the offensive line shines with the play of interior linemen Tate Ratledge and Christian Mahogany setting the tone.
Jared Goff doesn’t fall victim to Tampa’s opportunistic secondary, as he delivers a pair of touchdown strikes in the first half. The Buccaneers threaten with late momentum, but the Lions never lose control and win comfortably.
With that Bears game on the horizon and coming off an international trip, the Lions could fall victim to a trap game. This Buccaneers team is better than their record indicates, and can challenge Detroit’s secondary with their array of weapons.
In a worst-case scenario, former Lion Alex Anzalone picks off Jared Goff and returns it for an early score. Al-Quadin Muhammad gets a sack, and Ifeatu Melifonwu makes a big play as well. On defense, the absence of Aidan Hutchinson is felt immensely as the Lions can't corral the quarterback.
Detroit is dominated by its former players, and their hopes of earning the No. 1 seed take a big hit ahead of the crucial matchup with Chicago.
If the Lions are going to win this game, they’re going to have to do it with Jared Goff making big plays through the air. Tampa Bay’s run defense is right up there with the best in the league, and defensive-minded head coach Todd Bowles will have a good plan for Jahmyr Gibbs. My bold prediction is Gibbs is held under 100 all-purpose yards, which forces Goff to have to make big plays with his arm to help the offense be successful.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Makes Clear Decision Regarding Future Celebrations
full_text:
Detroit Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took to social media to react to his season-ending ACL injury.
Unfortunately for the former first-round pick, the injury suffered was self-induced, jumping in celebration early in the game against the New England Patriots.
Hutchinson expressed he has celebrated in that fashion many times, but now that he is facing months of grueling rehabilitation for another significant injury, he has made the decision to stop celebrating by leaping in the air.
Here is what Hutchinson shared on social media:
"I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me.
But even something like this won’t hold me back.
I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him.
Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes.
Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger. 2. That’s the last time I go airborne
Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys."
Kelvin Sheppard, Detroit's second-year defensive coordinator, is now tasked again with figuring out how to navigate the remainder of the season after losing a star defender.
Just recently, lineabcker Jack Campbell was placed on the injured reserve after suffering a neck injury at Ford Field.
"Kind of the elephant in the room is, we lost another one of our captains on Sunday due to a very unfortunate incident," said Sheppard. "So, I'll just put it out there right now, the same thing I told the unit when we met yesterday, that there's no replacing Aidan Hutchinson. And that's not just in this building, that's in this league. I think he's the best defensive end and edge player in this league. He's the best I've ever played with. He's the best I've ever coached. He's the best I've ever seen with my two eyes. That's just my small, humble opinion.
"That's what I've always thought of Hutch and he knows that. The person that he is, the player that is, he's everything that you want in a man," Sheppard continued. "The way he goes about his day, the way he goes about life, it's a lot more than just football that we'll miss with losing his presence, but now there's weight. And what we can't do is think one person is going to carry that weight or think who's going to be the guy. It's going to take all 11 to pick up a little piece of that weight and then I believe we all can be able to carry it."

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions could be facing a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team devoid of two of its top players: QB Baker Mayfield (foot injury) and S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle).
Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers.
Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three).
Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six).
Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players.
A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties.
Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties.
Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday.
As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026.
Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue.
Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers.
Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense.
At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Midseason Grades: Defense
full_text:
Early in the season, many were concerned about the longevity of the Detroit Lions ' defense.
Through four games, the defense had been one of the league's worst. They ranked near the bottom of the league in many major categories, and had been exposed in the team's two losses.
However, things have changed for the better in part thanks to improved play in the secondary, as well as a pass-rush that ranks third in the league in sacks. There are a pair of major injuries that they will need to overcome moving forward, but the group has changed the outside tune with its performance as of late.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance through the Lion
The defensive line has been a pleasant surprise throughout the first nine games of the year. Aidan Hutchinson was every bit the dominant force he was expected to be, but unfortunately suffered a season-ending knee injury last week that the unit will have to overcome.
Fortunately, the Lions appear to be better suited to handle his absence than they were when he suffered a season-ending injury two seasons ago. Alim McNeill is playing at a potential All-Pro level, as he leads the team with 6.5 sacks rushing from the interior.
McNeill, an explosive and athletic force, has the rare ability to blend both run defense and pass-rush within his snaps, and as a result has become an every down player for the defense. DJ Wonnum has also been a nice complementary piece to Hutchinson, as he's notched six sacks playing on the opposite side.
It's also been noteworthy to see the performance of rookie Skyler Gill-Howard, who was initially viewed as an afterthought when the Lions drafted him in the sixth-round. However, he has proven to have the necessary chops as a pass-rusher and has owned his opportunities.
2025 first-round pick Tyleik Williams has taken on a bigger role this year, as he has essentially replaced DJ Reader and Roy Lopez as the team's nose tackle.
With Hutchinson out, the Lions will likely be giving Ahmed Hassanein an opportunity this week which will be intriguing. Hassanein showed plenty of flashes in the preseason, and could give the defense a huge spark if that performance carries into the regular season.
Detroit also brought back Tyrus Wheat via a waiver claim, who appeared in 15 games for the team a season ago.
The linebacking corps has been on a bit of an adventure through the first nine games. There's plenty of talent in the room, even with Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder out for the remainder of the year. Still, there have been some struggles particularly in pass coverage.
When healthy, Campbell started the year struggling but had been playing well as of late when he suffered the scary neck injury. Rolder, meanwhile, was just coming into his own after starting the year as a healthy scratch when he went down.
Devin White, who the team signed during training camp, is also sidelined currently with a forearm injury. That injury, however, is not expected to sideline him for the remainder of the season.
Derrick Barnes has anchored the group, and is having one of his best seasons as a pro. He has had some struggles in coverage, but has contributed as a pass-rusher and handled his assignments well in the run game.
With Campbell out, the Lions have relied more on Malcolm Rodriguez. The veteran has been reliable as a spot starter in the past and has lived up to that billing this year. Trevor Nowaske has served as the third linebacker, with Joe Bachie, Amen Ogbongbemiga and newly acquired K.J. Britt also contributing snaps.
After four games, the secondary did not earn high marks. However, they seem to have found a bit of a groove that could be attributed to the return of Brian Branch. The Alabama product came back after the bye, and has been a stabilizing force for a group that dealt with a number of injuries early in the year.
D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin began the year as the starting corners, but Roger McCreary soon earned more snaps after outplaying Ya-Sin. McCreary has been one of the team's best free agent adds, and notched his first pick of the season last week against New England.
With Reed out the last two weeks, Ya-Sin has re-entered the starting lineup. Detroit relied on a rotation of cornerbacks that also featured Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw when all were healthy, but the snap counts from last week could suggest that the rotation is thinning out.
At safety, the Lions had to overcome being without Branch and Kerby Joseph at the beginning of the year. Chuck Clark has been solid, and the team leaned on rookie Keith Abney II after losing both Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper to injured reserve early in the year.
With Branch and Joseph both back , it will be interesting to see where Abney and newly acquired safety Andre Cisco fit within the defensive scheme. Regardless, the safety room is healthy for the first time all year, and it could give the defense a big boost moving forward.

title: NFL Players Using Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson as Cautionary Tale
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo does not want to end up like Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.
After witnessing a star player tear his ACL celebrating a sack, Skattebo has finally accepted that doing backflips after scoring touchdowns might not be the best idea.
He has long resisted ditching his touchdown celebration, even after he suffered a significant injury of his own as a rookie.
It took Hutchinson's injury to force him to see the error of his ways.
According to Giants On SI , the talented running back shared with the New York Post recently, “I’m saying, 'Yeah no more backflips.' Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.”
On the latest episode of "The St. Brown Bros." podcast, Amon-Ra St. Brown shared that he, along with Hutchinson and Jahmyr Gibbs, were talking about celebrations and that he also wanted to do that same celebration in front of the German crowd.
“We had practice Saturday, like a mini-practice," St. Brown explained. "And we were talking about celebrations after we broke it down , walking to get back on the bus. And it was me, Aiden and Jahmyr Gibbs. I'm like, bro, I got to do the fist bump celly. And I did it like two or three times, showing them how to do it. Hutch was there and then, I didn't know Hutch was going to do it."
St. Brown realized quickly that he should not ever again do that type of celebration.
"I was actually going to do it after I scored, and he ended up doing it and got hurt. I'm like, 'F**k bro.' Like, there's no way that we just talked about that and he did it and just got hurt. At the time, I didn't know how bad his injury was. But to find out after that he tore his ACL doing that, I was like, 'There's no way I can ever do that again.' I feel bad for Hutch, because I know how much work he puts in. ... I think it was a freak accident.”

title: Lions Draw Official With Past Controversial Call For Buccaneers Game
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions ' Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has been revealed.
When the Lions return to Ford Field on Sunday, their game against Tampa Bay will be officiated by Adrian Hill and his crew. Hill has been a lead referee since the 2019 season, and has  officiated nine Lions games in his career with Detroit holding a 3-6 record in those games.
Hill did not ref a Lions game last year, with his most recent assignment for Detroit coming in the 2024 season when he presided over their shootout loss to the Buffalo Bills at Ford Field.
It has been a bit of an up-and-down year for Hill. He drew the assignment for the first game of the NFL season in Seattle between the Seahawks and Patriots,  but also served a one-game suspension for an incident during his Week 5 assignment.
In that game, which was between the Minnesota Vikings and Miami Dolphins, Hill was knocked to the ground inadvertandly by Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson, who was blocked into the ref by Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon.
After the collision, Hill appeared to get up angrily and had choice words for Wilson. The NFL reviewed the incident and elected to suspend him one game for unprofessional conduct.
Hill also has some history with the Lions . He officiated Detroit's 37-35 loss to the Minnesota Vikings that would be the final game of the Matt Stafford era and end the 2020 season.
In that game, the Lions appeared to have a stop when Tracy Walker had a sack of Kirk Cousins on a fourth-down early in the fourth quarter, but Walker was called for a controversial roughing the passer penalty. The penalty extended the drive and led to a Vikings touchdown.
Sunday's game between the Lions and Buccaneers won't be the first time Hill has presided over a game between these two teams. He was the head ref when these squads met at Ford Field in 2019, with the Tom Brady-led Buccaneers winning 38-17.
Hill's crew ranks fifth in the league in flags per game with 16, and his total of nine penalties dismissed is the least amongst any crew that has officiated more than two games. He is coming off reffing the Monday Night Football game between the Ravens and Chargers, which featured a season-low in flags for his crew with 10.
The most common flags thrown by his crew are false start and offensive holding, as there have been 30 and 23 total flags in those categories by his crew.

title: 4 Key Detroit Lions Facing Most Pressure With Aidan Hutchinson Out
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a big absence to account for on the defensive line for the remainder of the 2026 season.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL, meaning he will miss the rest of the year. He won't be easy to replace, and becomes the latest Lion to suffer a significant injury. As a result, the Lions' defense has several players who will need to step up moving forward.
Here are the four players facing the most pressure after Hutchinson was lost for the season.
The rookie defensive end has taken a big step forward as of late. It was a quiet start to the year, as he went the first four games of the season playing less than 20 snaps. However, an injury to DJ Wonnum gave him an opportunity in Week 9, and then Hutchinson's injury did the same in Week 10.
In each of those games, Moore recorded two sacks. This indicates the potential he has as a player, but now the expectations will be ratcheted up for him. The recent hot streak has been an intriguing development, but with Hutchinson out Moore has to be a consistent producer opposite of Wonnum.
Through nine games, McNeill is playing at an All-Pro level. The interior lineman has 6.5 sacks, which is a phenomenal number for a player who plays his position. Having McNeill producing at that level from the interior line has been a huge asset for the Lions, as he's exploited some of the extra attention being paid to Hutchinson by winning his 1-on-1 matchups.
However, with Hutchinson out it could be McNeill that sees the extra attention moving forward. While it's been a great bounce-back season for him, opposing teams are more aware of the impact he has on the game by this point in the season.
McNeill will likely see more double teams at the point of attack in pass-rush situations moving forward, and will need to continue playing at a high level even if that doesn't result in more sacks.
A first-round pick of the Lions last year, Williams has yet to make himself a household name as a pass-rusher. Williams has been solid against the run, but hasn't been a difference maker in passing downs. Without Hutchinson, that could change.
Williams was billed as being a player who is growing in that area, but he hasn't been asked to play much as a pass-rusher with the emergence of rookie Skyler Gill-Howard.
If the Lions want to get bigger on the defensive line without Hutchinson, though, it could involve using McNeill as a 5-tech or potentially a big end and keeping Williams on the field with Gill-Howard.
Wonnum is the veteran of the room, and his role just got magnified with Hutchinson out. Never considered to be a rush-first defensive end, he has been quite productive for Detroit to the tune of six sacks through his first eight games.
Now, Wonnum is two off a career-high and will have plenty of chances to get there. He's been the edge-setting force for the defense opposite of Hutchinson, and has done a fine job of handling that up to this point.
However, with Hutchinson no longer in the mix, teams may be less inclined to run at him as they try to expose the other side of the defense. Wonnum will need to be consistent moving forward to help stabilize a defense that is without one of its biggest leaders.

title: Dan Campbell Turns Heads With Recent Comments About DE Ahmed Hassanein
full_text:
The Detroit Lions feel they have enough depth to navigate the injury to star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.
On Wednesday afternoon, head coach Dan Campbell expressed that he wanted to get second-year defensive end Ahmed Hassanein going a "little bit" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
For the first nine games of the 2026 NFL regular season, the former sixth-round draft pick has been inactive, causing many to wonder why he was not seeing much playing time, especially since he had a solid training camp in the summer.
The former NFL tight end expressed earlier this week he feels the roster is better equipped to handle the loss of Hutchinson than back in 2024, when the former first-round pick was lost for the season, after a severe leg injury suffered against the Dallas Cowboys.
“Yeah, we are much better equipped than we were then," said Campbell. "That's the reason why we have the depth that we have in that room. We knew that was important. I mean, these are the things that you learn over a six-year period, is how important depth is. And so, we feel really good about that room. Now I mentioned this before, (Alim McNeill) Mac is playing at a high level. He's got to continue to do that and then some. (DJ) Wonnum, it was good to get him back. He's got to continue to play at a high level and we need even a little bit more. Derrick Moore, hey, he looks good, he's improving. We need more."
Detroit has also been stout along the interior of the defensive line, led by McNeill, Gill-Howard and Tyleik Williams.
"Gill-Howard, we need more. Tyleik (Williams), we need more. We can keep going here a little bit, but the good news is those guys are improving, they're getting better and they're playing as one unit. And so, got a ton of faith in those guys," said Campbell. "And so yeah, we'll be able to handle this. And our backend's playing pretty good right now.
"Our backers are doing a good job. And really, we're using the totality of that roster, that defensive roster. (Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard) Shepp's doing a good job, those coaches, and really all of them have a role and a hand in this. And that's probably, you say, 'What's the strength of our defense right now?' They're playing as one unit.”

title: Jahmyr Gibbs Earns NFC Offensive Player of Week After Patriots Win

After securing 153 rushing yards on 22 carries, two touchdowns and seven receptions for 99 yards, (252 all-purpose yards) the former first-round draft pick was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff commented postgame about Gibbs' monster performance in a
“I think we got to pinch ourselves sometimes and not take it for granted how special he is. He’s just so explosive with the ball in his hands. We threw that check down to him; it goes 50 yards. title: Packers Create Roster Spot, And That Means Two Things
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers on Thursday announced they released running back Pierre Strong.
That leaves the Packers with a 52-man roster. You know what that means.
All signs point to Micah Parsons making his debut against the Rams on Wednesday. Before he can take aim at Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford, he’ll need to be added to the 53-man roster. The release of Strong made that possible.
“First of all, I just want to praise him for his work and our training staff for all the things they’ve been doing to get back to be ready to perform for our football team,” position coach DeMarcus Covington said this week. “And it’s been fun working with him. Obviously, worked with him last year and as he’s been getting ready to play, whenever that is, him being in the classroom, he’s always been in the classroom with us the whole time.
“And he’s done a really good job with that leadership portion, helping us out throughout the week, film study with the guys and then also just giving his evaluation within the meeting room. And then also you guys see him on the sideline, he’s been doing a really good job stepping up as far as his leadership role during the time that he’s not on the field. He’s been doing a good job in the classroom with our guys, too. Excited to eventually get him out there so he can help our defense, help our team win some football games.”
The release of Pierre Strong leaves the Packers with four running backs on their roster: Josh Jacobs, Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd.
The Packers had five running backs on their roster. In the loss to the Vikings, Jacobs was out with a broken finger and Strong was a healthy scratch. By snaps, Brooks led the way with 26 in his return from injured reserve, followed by 14 apiece from Johnson and Lloyd. By touches, Johnson had 10 (all rushes), Lloyd had seven (four rushes, three catches) and Brooks had three (two rushes, one catch).
Jacobs had surgery to repair his broken right ring finger. It was a clean break, meaning a quick return to the lineup. Could that be against the Rams? After a mini-bye, the Packers will return to the practice field on Saturday.
Whether Jacobs returns this week or next week, the release of Strong clearly means the team does not believe Jacobs will be out much longer.
Once everyone is healthy, it’ll be interesting to see which direction the Packers turn in the backfield. Jacobs is the proven workhorse who they’ve waited for through thick and thin this year. Johnson has been the most impactful runner. Brooks has a critical role as a trusted pass protector. Lloyd is the former third-round pick.
Johnson would seem to have a role going forward based on how he played against Minnesota.
“There were some flashes, obviously,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “There were some good runs in there. But the one thing about Kaleb is you can feel him attack the line of scrimmage. He was coming off the ball really well. He was running hard. So that was really encouraging, to see him go out there and do that. I’m very excited about him as we move forward, for sure.”
The Packers have a total of 11 players on injured lists. Of those, only Micah Parsons has been designated for return.
Four are out for the season: right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles), defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (Achilles) and receiver Jayden Reed (neck).
The others, in terms of their return to game action:
Defensive tackle Warren Brinson’s groin injury required surgery. Asked about him last week, coach Matt LaFleur said: “it usually takes a little bit longer time to recover than five weeks.” After a significant injury, he’d obviously need some ramp-up to get him on the field.
Defensive tackle Jonathan Ford was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 17 with a calf injury. He is eligible to be designated to return.
Center/guard Jacob Monk replaced Sean Rhyan in the Detroit game on Oct. 25 but suffered a quad injury. He was placed on injured reserve the next day and has to spend at least one more week on IR before he can return to practice.
Tight end Josh Whyle was placed on injured reserve last week with a concussion so will be out at least three more games.
Edge Collin Oliver was placed on injured reserve at the end of training camp, presumably due to the calf injury he sustained in the second preseason game at Denver. When Parsons spoke to reporters a couple weeks ago, he mentioned Oliver had a “setback” in his recovery.
Tight end Luke Musgrave is on PUP with the neck injury sustained during the offseason. Obviously, the longer Musgrave is out, the more unlikely it is that he will return this season.
Of note, teams can bring back eight players from injured reserve during the regular season. Savion Williams and Oliver (who were designated to return at the end of camp) along with Chris Brooks and Skyy Moore mean the Packers have used four. Parsons, because he opened training camp on PUP, does not count against the eight.

title: Good News, Bad News, Projections From Packers’ Long List of 2027 Free Agents
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The NFL Draft is the lifeblood of the Green Bay Packers. While general manager Brian Gutekunst has been more aggressive in free agency and trades and less reluctant to find veterans for in-season help, the draft remains the team’s primary source of talent.
After this season, the 2023 NFL Draft class is scheduled to reach free agency. First-round pick Lukas Van Ness was given the fifth-year option, so he’ll be back for 2027, and second-round receiver Jayden Reed and third-round tight end Tucker Kraft earned contract extensions. However, of the team’s other 10 draft picks, seven are no longer on the team and only one is a starter.
A dud of a draft class is the bad news. The good news is there shouldn’t be much stress on Gutekunst or the salary cap in terms of determining who to keep and who to let go.
With that as a backdrop, here are the Packers’ 16 unrestricted free agents, listed in order of playing time on offense and defense, according to OverTheCap.com, plus a prediction on whether they will stay or go.
Nixon, who will turn 30 in June, picked a fine time to play the best football of his career in terms of his work on defense. Nixon allowed seven touchdowns and was penalized 12 times last season. This season, he has allowed one touchdown and been penalized three times. While he’s on pace to allow a career-high 66 completions, according to Pro Football Focus, most of them have been short catches.
The Packers typically don’t re-sign 30-year-olds, and that probably will remain true even though he’s as tough as a $2 steak, but he’s set himself up for a nice payday.
Projection: Will not return because of age and the team’s salary cap.
After the Week 3 debacle against Atlanta, the Packers grabbed the 34-year-old Tomlinson off Dallas’ practice squad. He’s played almost every snap in seven starts, bouncing from four starts at left guard to two at right guard and now one back at left guard.
PFF has charged him with only one sack. He hasn’t been great, obviously, but he’s been a phenomenal bargain compared to Aaron Banks .
Projection: Will not return.
Of the upcoming free agents who were drafted in 2023, Brooks is the only starter. The former sixth-round pick is having a fantastic season. After recording just a half-sack and one tackle for loss in 16 games (seven starts) last season, Brooks has three sacks and six tackles for losses in 10 games (all starts) this year. He leads the unit with 14 pressures.
“I thought he played probably his best game since I’ve been here in my mind and he lit it up vs. New England, too,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said this week. “From a play-style standpoint, always on point. Schematic and technical executions, most of the time is on point.
“He’s a guy that plays a lot of different spots. To the eye just watching the game, plays defensive tackle. Yes, he does. But we align him in a lot of different spots by front structure, by who we have out there, and I feel good about him doing everything.”
Nixon, Tomlinson and Brooks are the only free agents playing more than half the snaps. Brooks routinely plays the most snaps of the defensive tackles.
Projection: Will not return because he’s playing his way out of Green Bay’s price range.
The former undrafted free agent has only 1.5 sacks but he’s second on the team with eight quarterback hits (official stats) and 26 pressures (PFF). Of 72 edge rushers with at least 150 pass-rushing opportunities, Cox is tied for 23rd in PFF’s pass-rush win rate, which is just behind Will Anderson and just ahead of Trey Hendrickson and Danielle Hunter.
Cox has played 40.5 percent of the snaps; the return of Micah Parsons will cut into it but perhaps not by much.
The Packers signed Smith at the end of training camp. It seemed like a brilliant signing considering he caught 50 passes for the Falcons in 2023, 88 passes for the Dolphins in 2024 and 38 passes for the Steelers in 2025. In nine games for the Packers, though, he has only six receptions, including just one in the team’s last six games.
Projection: Will not return.
The addition of Brandon Cisse in this year’s draft cost Valentine his starting job. A seventh-round pick in 2023, he came off the bench against the Vikings and had one of his better games. He’s always been able to cover; he’s allowed just 88 yards on 17 targets this season, according to PFF. What was noteworthy, given his career-long ineptitude as a tackler, was his physicality against the run and a couple receiver screens.
“I would say this: When we got here, everyone had a clean slate, want-to and physicality was not his issue when we got here,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. “It was technique. I think he’s worked really hard on that with DB [Daniel Bullocks] and Bobby [Babich] of cleaning up some technique. If you have the wrong technique, it can look to the naked eye as one thing but it’s really not that. He is not soft, he is not afraid at all. He just had to clean up his technique. I thought he came in and played extremely well.”
Projection: Could return if the price is right, because the Packers will need a starter opposite Cisse in 2027.
A seventh-round pick in 2022 who never played in a game during his first go-around with the team, Ford returned late last season and earned a roster spot this season. He’s played in five games (one start) but missed the last five games due to injury. A big run-stopping force, he had the first half-sack of his career in Week 1.
Strong, a fourth-round pick by the Patriots in 2022, spent last year on Green Bay’s practice squad. This season, he’s played in five games, carried 25 times for 59 yards (2.4 average) and caught 10 passes for 61 yards (6.1 average). He might be the odd man out on the roster once Josh Jacobs returns.
Moore returned from injured reserve following an ankle injury, only to suffer another ankle injury on his third kickoff return against Minnesota. He leads the team with a 27.2-yard average on kickoff returns and a 14.8-yard average on punt returns but has been a nonfactor with his 93 snaps on offense.
He’s got a chance to be ready to face the Rams.
Projection: Will return if he can get on the field and stay on the field.
Niemann is perhaps the team’s best player on special teams. He ranks first on the team in snaps (208) and second in tackles (nine), and he played well while playing most of the game at linebacker against New England.
Whyle, who caught 28 passes for the Titans in 2024, was part of the Packers replacing Tucker Kraft last season. After catching five passes in eight games in 2025, he has zero catches in eight games in 2026 and is on injured reserve following a concussion.
Projection: Will not return.
Once again, Welch fell short of a spot on Green Bay’s roster at the end of training camp. Once again, Welch is a key player on special teams. He is sixth on the team in snaps and has six tackles.
With quarterbacks dropping like flies around the league, Taylor has only had to play mop-up duty for the Packers. The 37-year-old who was signed to replace Malik Willis is with the team because of his experience, knowhow and ability to help Jordan Love behind the scenes.
Projection: Will not return.
The Packers signed Becton to the practice squad following the Week 3 debacle. A first-round bust as a left tackle, he resurrected his career as a right guard for the Eagles in 2024 and Chargers in 2025. He’s played 11 snaps on offense in two games. That includes three as an extra tight end against Minnesota, and those didn’t go well with one sack and one additional pressure allowed.
Projection: Will return as an inexpensive bridge player following the potential departures of Aaron Banks, Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler.
A second-round pick in 2023, Musgrave should be in the prime of his career. Instead, his career has fallen off a cliff following a promising rookie season. He has not been on the practice field since June due to a neck injury.
Projection: Will not return.

title: Grand Theft Contract: Six Worst Packers Free-Agent Signings of GTA Era
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Today’s the day some gamers have been waiting for for years. It’s the release date for Grand Theft Auto VI .
That got us thinking about the six worst free-agent signings in Green Bay Packers history, or at least since the original GTA debuted in 1997. Here are our picks, in order from bad to worst.
Jeff Saturday was a five-time Pro Bowler and two-time All-Pro while with the Colts. After 13 excellent seasons alongside Peyton Manning, he joined the Packers in 2012 on a two-year, $7.75 million contract. Saturday was signed to replace standout Scott Wells but was benched late in his debut season and retired after the season.
At least there was no signing bonus involved, so the Packers were able to wash their hands of the situation.
The Packers under first-year general manager Brian Gutekunst took a big swing at a chronic problem by signing five-time Pro Bowl tight end Jimmy Graham to a three-year, $30 million contract in 2018. To create space for Graham’s top-of-the-market contract, which included $11 million guaranteed, the Packers released fan-favorite but past-his-prime Jordy Nelson.
Graham wasn’t terrible. Far from it. He just wasn’t the player who caught 10 touchdown passes in 2017 or had four seasons of more than 900 yards. He caught 55 passes for 636 yards and two touchdowns in 2018 and 38 passes for 447 yards and three touchdowns in 2019. The Packers released him in March 2020.
In 2016, tight end Jared Cook was one of the key players for an injury-plagued team that reached the NFC Championship Game. The Packers were unable to re-sign Cook, so pivoted to Martellus Bennett. His three-year, $21 million contract included a $6.3 million signing bonus.
He played just seven games for the Packers before an ugly divorce in which he accused the Packers’ conservative medical staff of making him play through a shoulder injury.
Bennett signed with the Packers due in part to the presence of Aaron Rodgers. Did Rodgers’ broken collarbone affect Bennett’s shoulder?
“You can’t deny the facts of your timeline and how everything went down,” then-coach Mike McCarthy said. “Really, to tie all that together, you’re asking me to get inside somebody else’s feelings, conversation, more on a personal level. I think this all started coming out of the bye week. Everything leading up to that, I can’t really comment on it. And then we went down this injury path and then here we are today.”
Not all contracts are created equally.
In free agency in 2024, Gutekunst signed running back Josh Jacobs to a four-year, $48 million contract that included a $12.5 million signing bonus and got a centerpiece of the offense. In 2025, Gutekunst signed Hobbs to a four-year, $48 million contract that included a $16 million signing bonus. The $12 million averaged ranked 21st among cornerbacks.
“We just really thought he’s a really versatile all-around corner, can do everything,” Gutekunst said at the time. “We really like his ability to play on the outside, which he hasn’t done a ton of, but the ability to move him inside and match different receivers, and his play style I think is one of the things that really stood out to all of us. Really, really excited to see what he’s going to do for us this year.”
Instead of a centerpiece of the defense, the Packers dumped him overboard after one season with an equal mix of injuries and ineffective play. Hobbs played 32 percent of the defensive snaps. PFF charged him with a 125.3 passer rating when targeted. He gave up two touchdowns and broke up two passes.
It’s a mystery why the signing didn’t work out . In four years with the Raiders, he missed 17 games due to injuries, started 38 games and intercepted three passes. The Packers projected Hobbs as an every-down player, though there was little evidence of him being that type of player.
The Packers ate $4 million of dead cap for this season and will ingest another $8 million next season.
After sitting out the 1999 season due to a knee injury, Johnson was named the NFL’s Comeback Player of the Year in 2000 with his 12 sacks. After adding another nine sacks in 2021, the Packers in 2002 under then-general manager Mike Sherman signed Johnson away from the Saints with a six-year contract worth $33 million that included a $6.5 million signing bonus.
Johnson had two sacks in five games in 2002 and zero sacks in six games in 2023. The Packers got rid of him after that season, and he never played in another NFL game.
“We watched him on tape and he looked great and did a lot of good things,” Sherman said. “It’s unfortunate that he’s had the injuries that he’s had. I think everybody learns lessons from everything they do in this business or any business.”
Gutekunst had impeccable forays into free agency in 2019 and 2024 but whiffed on Banks and Hobbs in 2025.
Banks signed a four-year, $77 million contract. The $19.25 million average ranks ninth among guards. The signing came as an incredible overreaction to the Packers getting overwhelmed physically in the 2024 playoff loss at the Eagles.
Banks had been a solid but not spectacular starter for the 49ers; the Packers gave great-player money to a player who had never been great.
Coaches like to say a player’s greatest ability is his availability. After playing only five offensive snaps as a rookie second-round pick by the 49ers in 2021, Banks played 88.3 percent of the snaps in 2022, 78.5 percent in 2023 and 71.8 percent in 2024. With Green Bay, he has been dogged by a mountain of lower-body injuries.
After starting against Carolina and New England, Banks was on the bench against Minnesota. The Packers opted to start Laken Tomlinson, who was signed off Dallas’ practice squad, at left guard and Travis Glover, who had missed the past two games with a knee injury, at right guard. Ten games into the season, Banks has played 70 percent of the snaps in only one game. He might be the No. 4 guard behind Tomlinson, Kevin Zeitler and Glover against the Rams after the bye.
“I think the biggest thing is just the consistency aspect, getting him out there – his health, obviously, is huge,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said this week “And I think just getting him out there playing with consistency, it’s going to be the biggest thing.”
The Packers’ offensive line is a mess. Signing Banks and moving on from Elgton Jenkins is a big reason why.
Banks is owed a $9.5 million roster bonus at the start of the league-year in March. There is almost a 0 percent chance that will be paid and the worst contract in NFL history will be off the roster (if not off the financial ledger, with a residual dead-cap charge of about $26.3 million).
Typically, I'm a glass-half-empty kind of person. Today, let me bring some sunshine to a cloudy day. Yeah, the Packers got trounced on Sunday, but I've got six reasons why they can (and will) rebound. ⬇️ https://t.co/YPVQLYyTHn
