title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams.
For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best.
So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions.
No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues.
According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)."
Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks.
The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game.
With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut.
No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab.
According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.."
The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver.
J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that.
The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week.
Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson.
The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for.

The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks.
To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect.
So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below.
Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started.
Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role.

title: Jaguars Stock Report Entering Week 11: These Rookies Keep Pushing the Envelope
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have a lot of players playing good football. That goes without saying.
But after the Jaguars' impressive Week 10 win over the Tennessee Titans, the Jaguars have a few players with their stocks pointing firmly upward ... and then a few players who are going the other way.
So, which Jaguars have their stocks pointing upward after the Jaguars improved to 7-2? We break it down below.
The Titans mignt not have Jeffery Simmons any longer, but they still have some talented defensive lineman who have the ability to test the Jaguars' interior offensive line. Despite this, Pregnon had arguably the best game of his career. Pregnon did not allow any pressures in the passing game, did a good job of displacing blockers at the line of scrimmage, and looked as consistent as he has at any other point in his rookie year to this point. This was a good week for the rookie guard, and he looks like he is getting better and better.
Jarrian Jones was amongst the most-targeted players in football over the first half of the season, which felt more like teams opting to not attack Travis Hunter in coverage. Since the bye week ended, the Jaguars have played Jones in the slot more than he was during the first-half of the season (in part due to Montaric Brown being healthy). As a result, he has been one of the team's most-improved players since the bye week, and he had a terrific outing against the Titans that saw him record a well-timed third-down pass breakup. Jones has had a great last three weeks, but he was especially good against the Titans.
Josh Cameron had a few quiet weeks in recent games, though he was still an important part of the Jaguars' offense and special teams. He got his opportunities ramped up in a big way in Week 10, though, catching all three passes for 67 yards and a touchdown ... while also serving as the critcal block against the Titans' defense during Bhayshul Tuten's fourth-quarter touchdown. Cameron has gotten better and better since he was drafted, and this game was a pure reflection of what he can do when given chances.
This did not feel like a very strong week for second-year safety Rayuan Lane. It already looked like he was entering his final week as a key piece of the defense considering that Jessie Bates III is set to debut for the Jaguars (and play quite a bit) against the Giants this week. But Lane had one of his weaker games during his extended run of snaps against the Titans, missing a key tackle in space on Tony Pollard and missing a few other chances to limit Titans gains. Lane has been a good player for the Jaguars more often than not during his second season, but this game was a good example of why the Jaguars had to go out and get Bates.
The Jaguars are playing with an injured Bhayshul Tuten, who practiced once over the last two weeks as he deals with an ankle/foot injury. Despite Tuten clearly entering Week 10 at less than 100%, the Jaguars only had Chris Rodriguez Jr. play a small share of snaps and get just four carries ... compared to Tuten's 26. Even though Tuten is not playing with the same burst that he was able to earlier in the season, the Jaguars are still giving him a heavy workload, despite Rodriguez being readily available. This is clearly Tuten's backfield, and that isn't going to change anytime soon.
This one, of course, has nothing to do with anything Regis did. The last time Regis was on the field against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9, he did some good things. But the Jaguars had Regis as a healthy scratch in Week 10 against the Tennessee Titans after the Jaguars added veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Then there is Jordan Davis , who is set to debut for the Jaguars' defensive line this week against the Giants. If the addition of Godchaux pushed Regis back to being a healthy scratch, then the addition of Davis will likely make it hard for him to see the field again during his rookie season.

title: Predicting the Jaguars' Second-Half Slate: How Jacksonville Can Roll to the Playoffs
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have a massive opportunity over the next two months, but it will take quite a lot of winning.
Winning is what the Jaguars have done almost exclusively since head coach Liam Coen was hired, with the Jaguars going 20-6 in the process. But for the Jaguars to reach higher goals than simply another AFC South title, they will have to keep their winning ways going.
So, how do we see the second-half of the season playing out for the Jaguars? We break it down below, starting with their Week 11 battle with the New York Giants.
I think the Giants are a better team than I ever expected them to look like this year, but I still think they are spunky overachievers with a quarterback who has a bit too much doofus to his game. The Giants will test the Jaguars more than most teams have since the Jaguars' bye week ended, but the Giants' own resume of wins is not exactly encouraging. The Giants will test them more than other teams have in recent weeks, but the Jaguars will win their third road game in a row, and the Jaguars will improve to 8-2 in the process.
The Titans gave it their best effort on Sunday, and it still resulted in allowing the Jaguars to score 40 points in a 17-point win. The Titans were scrappy, but they are just nowhere near the Jaguars in terms of talent or coaching ability. These teams are playing different sports right now, and the Jaguars should make quick work of them at home. The Jaguars have been destroying teams at home since Coen was hired, and nothing about the Titans' efforts on Sunday indicated that they can change this trend.
This is, by far, the toughest game left on the Jaguars' schedule. This would have been the case even if the Bears didn't trade for the best defensive tackle in the game today, but the addition of Jeffery Simmons could prove to be a difference-maker. The Jaguars have struggled at stopping elite defensive tackles this season, and I think this continues in Chicago in a few weeks. I see this as a potential Super Bowl preview that the Jaguars lose closely in the fourth quarter. Do not come at me with pitchforks and torches, because I would likely flip this result.
I think we have a chance to see some truly disgusting quarterback play from Aaron Rodgers against the Jaguars' scheme. He takes forever at the line of scrimmage to try to get the ball out of his hand as quick as possible, and that is exactly what Anthony Campanile wants quarterbacks to do against his defense. The Steelers can run the ball, but I do not think their defense can keep up with Trevor Lawrence considering what they are likely to get out of Rodgers.
I picked the Jaguars to split their season series with the Texans before the 2026 season began, and I am sticking with that. The Jaguars are the better team by quite a bit this year, even if they are not a great matchup for the Jaguars. Their defense is no longer fearsome, though, and I would expect another big day out of Trevor Lawrence and the passing game in their Week 6 rematch. The Jaguars should’ve won last time, and will get it done this time.
The Cowboys just soft launched a firing of their own defensive coordinator halfway through the season, to give you an idea of where their defense is at. I expect fireworks in this game as Trevor Lawrence and Dak Prescott get into a classic quarterback duel, but the difference in the defenses gives Jacksonville the edge.
The Washington Commanders have a mostly-toothless defense that is ran like an off-brand version of the Vikings' defense, so I do not expect the Jaguars' offense to struggle in this one. Jayden Daniels has had some OK flashes this season, but he does not even look as dynamic as he did two years ago. The Jaguars are a few tiers above of the Commanders, and I expect them to play like it at the end of the season.
The Colts will still be starting Daniel Jones in this game, for some reason, which means I have no choice but to call this a Jaguars win. The Jaguars will still likely be playing for seeding in the AFC by Week 18 as well depending on how things play out, so there is no real reason to think they would sit anyone. With that said, I would pick Quinn Ewers against the Colts if they did sit the starters. Really.

title: Robert Hainsey's Absence Could Open a Door for Jaguars' Jonah Monheim Beyond 2026
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to turn to second-year center Jonah Monheim to start at the offensive line's anchor spot in Week 11, giving the former seventh-rounder a potential long-term open door.
The Jaguars will be missing starting center Robert Hainsey in a critical Week 11 bout against the New York Giants, head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Hainsey would be week-to-week with a knee sprain.
Jaguars starting center Robert Hainsey is considered week-to-week with a knee sprain, per sources. Very well could miss time but not season-ending. pic.twitter.com/8d6cqd5uxT
Now that Hainsey is set to miss at least one key game for the Jaguars during their playoff run, Jacksonville will get another extended look at Monheim. Good this look give them confidence in him as a potential starter in 2027?
Monheim, one of the Jaguars' last picks in the 2025 NFL Draft, has been able to carve out a role as a reliable depth piece for the offensive line since he was drafted. He started two games for the Jaguars in the place of an injured Hainsey last season, while also filling in for Hainsey during the second-half of the Jaguars' Week 5 Monday Night Football win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
Now, Monheim will have to do it again, and this time it will be on the road against an NFC divisional leader that has a defensive scheme that is meant to put pressure on the offensive line's communications and protection calls.
"We have a lot of confidence in Jonah," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said earlier this week.
"Jonah was playing really well during training camp, I don't know if you remember, and then we had the injury to Ezra [OL Ezra Cleveland], I believe, and we ended up playing Jonah at more guard. It kind of maybe put a curtain over how well he was playing at the time. We have a lot of confidence in him moving forward.”
Monheim was one of the few rookie centers to get playing time a year ago, giving the Jaguars an early look at a player who very well could develop into more than just solid depth. Monheim has impressed time and time again with the Jaguars, and there does not seem to be much concern over his ability to do so again this week.
"Jonah's only a second-year player, but he's very mature, takes things seriously, but doesn’t overcook it either, tries not to overdo it. Obviously played at a high level at USC and that's good football, so he's been in big games, he's been in big moments, he’s played big games," Coen said.
"And then I think just his preparation throughout the week, learning from Hainsey and that group and the communication. He gets a lot of reps during the week as well, whether it's stealing those reps in blitz protection walkthroughs, in run walkthroughs. In practice as well, he gets a lot of reps.
There are a few other Jaguars players whose futures look in doubt due to potential cap savings if they are released, and a strong stretch by Monheim could put Hainsey in a similar boat. According to OverTheCap, the Jaguars would save a little over $7 million in March if they release Hainsey with a post-June 1st designation. They would still have dead money for a few years due to void years on his deal, but it would make sense for the Jaguars to back out of Hainsey's deal a year early if Monheim plays well down the stretch.
Monheim's limited flashes over the last two seasons have looked at least on par with Hainsey, who was an important addition last March due to his connection with Coen after their time together in Tampa Bay. Hainsey has played solid football for the Jaguars, is a two-time captain, and is a big reason they are 7-2 with one of the NFL's best offenses.
But the NFL is still about drafting and developing. Teams around the NFL each year are seeing younger, cheaper players take prominent roles from more experienced veterans in the same situation. If Monheim plays well in Hainsey's place this week and potentially beyond, then the Jaguars will need to at least ask the tough question.

title: 3 Unsung Jaguars Who've Already Made Their Case to Stay in 2027
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will have a lot of tough decisions to make after the 2026 season, decisions that got even tougher after the Jaguars' flurry of moves at the trade deadline a week ago.
But beyond those headline decisions, the Jaguars have smaller decisions to weigh just like they must each offseason. The decisions on which role players and underrated contributors to keep as the Jaguars continue to build and reinvent themselves each season.
So, which of those underrated players have played key roles in getting the Jaguars to 7-2 and deserve consideration to be brought back next offseason? We break it down below.
The Jaguars will be hoping the additions of Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates make an impact right off the bat in terms of boosting the defensive line and secondary. The one position group that wasn't touched by Jaguars general manager James Gladstone at the trade deadline was linebacker, where the Jaguars made a big bet this offseason on Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs to replace Devin Lloyd.
That bet has paid off, with Miller posing some of the best run-defense numbers of any linebacker in football. He is appreciated inside Jacksonville, but he is likely the best Jaguars player who gets no credit from outside analysts for the Jaguars' defensive success. It is hard to imagine the Jaguars would be as physical as they are without Miller in the middle, and the Jaguars should work to ensure that he sticks in the picture this offseason. He has plenty of value to the Jaguars' defense and is unlikely yto cost what Lloyd did last March.
The Jaguars' special teams unit had a few off games at the start of the season, but they have turned it around in a big way since then. They have been strong on kickoff and punt coverage more often than not, while the return teams have made some big plays in critical moments to give the Jaguars more bites at the apple. Jaguars backup linebacker Jahlani Tavai has been an underrated part of those efforts.
Jacksonville added Tavai during training camp when they were hit by a rask of injuries at the linebacker spot, and he has been consistent for them in his role since. He is a true core-four special teamer, and the Jaguars could bring him back next year the same way they brought back Quintin Morris and Matt Dickerson on small deals this past offseason. Tavai has been a helpful addition for the Jaguars special teams and deserves to stick around.
The Jaguars' running back room has played a big role in their success this season, with Bhayshul Tuten taking the massive second-year leap that has turned him into one of the NFL's most consistent producers at the position. Add in Chris Rodriguez's value as a short-yardage runner and then LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah in specific roles, and the Jaguars would be wise to keep this room together next season as well.
The only member of the unit who is currently not under contract for 2027 is Abdullah, who has steppped in as the Jaguars' No. 3 running back this season after a stellar training camp. Abdullah has gotten chunk yards when utilized on offense, but his special teams value has been even clearer -- they do not beat the Eagles in Week 5 without his big return. Add in his leadership value to a young Jaguars' running back room and the Jaguars should do what it takes to bring Abdullah back as a key depth piece next season.

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Cardinals Showdown in Week 11
full_text:
Before entering a short week in a marquee showdown against Buffalo on Thanksgiving, the Chiefs have to get through one more contest first. They will look to remain undefeated at Arrowhead Stadium with the Arizona Cardinals coming to town for Kansas City's final home game in a month.
These two teams are in completely different positions, as the Cardinals are already playing for draft position after turning to rookie quarterback Carson Beck. The Chiefs are battling for the top overall seed in the AFC and trying to overtake the Broncos in the AFC West . Kansas City unsurprisingly enters this showdown as a massive favorite over the three-win Cardinals. However, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what its computer model forecasts prior to kickoff.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 88.0%, Cardinals 11.9%.
With a win probability of nearly 90%, this figure marks the largest advantage the Chiefs have held in the matchup predictor all season, even more than when they played the Dolphins or Jets.
The Cardinals are in the midst of a putrid offensive stretch in which they've mustered a mere nine points over the last two weeks. They sent Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore at the trade deadline and lost Gardner Minshew II to a torn ACL, forcing them to rely on their third-round rookie to orchestrate the offense.
While the Chiefs recently endured a mini-slump that featured losses to the Seahawks and Broncos, they have bounced back by scoring 35 points in consecutive wins. Patrick Mahomes has finally shaken off the early rust coming off his torn ACL and LCL, and this squad is now playing some of its best football all year. Due to the lopsided nature of this particular game, the medical staff is in no rush to get Kenneth Walker III (groin) back on the field. Rookie tailback Emmett Johnson should continue to handle a large offensive workload, which he has undoubtedly earned with 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns last week.
The Chiefs will face every team from the NFC West this season and have already played Seattle. They still have the Rams and 49ers after this weekend, which will serve as the final interconference matchups on the schedule.
All three of Arizona's victories have actually come on the road, so perhaps it will give KC a run for its money. However, the computer model indicates that this one will get out of hand fairly quickly Sunday afternoon.

title: Chiefs Fans May Want to Pump the Brakes on Hype for Omarr Norman-Lott’s Return
full_text:
The Chiefs didn't make a defensive line swap at the annual NFL trade deadline , but you already know the logic is outlined for their de facto trade being the pickup of tackle Omarr Norman-Lott.
Considering that the 2025 second-round pick has yet to make his season debut, it's only natural to take anything he contributes down the stretch as a bonus. With Norman-Lott rejoining the active 53-man roster from the physically unable to perform list , he's finally closer to getting back in the lineup.
With that said, any hype surrounding Norman-Lott's return may be misplaced. Judging by defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's comments this week, getting the former Tennessee standout up to speed will be more of a slow-burning process than a rapid reintroduction.
"Yeah, I mean, good to always get those big guys back," Spagnuolo said. "We'll see where he is. He's kind of working through the injury. I think the training staff has done a great job with him. Now, it's getting him acclimated back. The hard thing when you come off this in the middle of the season [is] you don't have the luxury of training camp. We'll have to see where we're at."
What's a realistic workload for Norman-Lott in his first stint of game action this year? Looking at his past and Kansas City's present could provide a potential answer.
Casting his Week 7 showing against the Las Vegas Raiders aside due to his ACL tear, Norman-Lott got mixed involvement on defense as a rookie.
Outside of not appearing in Week 1 or Week 5, he managed to combine for 66 defensive snaps in four contests — good for 28.1% of those available. Given that he's endured a grueling rehab path that lasted longer than most expected , it's foolish to assume he'll sniff that percentage soon.
There's also the matter of how the Chiefs are divvying up their defensive tackle snaps right now. Leading the way is All-Pro Chris Jones with 438 reps; he's logged a 76% share in back-to-back weeks. Behind him, veteran nose tackle Khyiris Tonga was at 55% in Weeks 7 and 8 but has slipped to 44% and 22%, respectively, in his last two showings.
That's coincided with the likes of Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris getting a bit more work. The two have combined for 41 snaps in the last two games, largely due to the continued absence of first-round pick Peter Woods . With that said, Woods was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, a positive indicator for his Week 11 status.
Additionally, the versatility of defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah must be accounted for. The Kansas State product, according to Pro Football Focus , has actually lined up in the A-gap or B-gap on 105 snaps this year. He has 182 on the outside and 15 directly over the opposing offensive tackle. Sophomore man Ashton Gillotte, too, has experience moving inside.
Whether that's because of a perceived lack of depth at tackle or merely out of creativity by Spagnuolo is unclear. This writer leans the latter.
If one of Harris or Eason is released, that'd pave the way for a handful of Norman-Lott snaps. Said player could always return to Kansas City on the practice squad after clearing waivers — Eason was an August waiver pickup , and Harris is no stranger to being elevated to the 53. That still doesn't mean Norman-Lott would be in line for double-digit snaps, nor should he necessarily be at this juncture.
Don't get it twisted: Kansas City could benefit from another intriguing interior rusher. The club is right down the middle (16th) in pressures (128) and pressure rate (36.5%) as a defense, via TruMedia , and opts to send max pressure at the fourth-highest rate in the sport (2.8%). In college, Norman-Lott showcased the ability to win quickly and profile as a three-technique at the professional level.
After a whirlwind of a rookie training camp that saw him look closer to a nose guard and a serious knee injury, however, placing any legitimate level of expectation on him isn't wise. Fortunately for Norman-Lott, he's entering a low-pressure environment on a team that seems perfectly fine allowing him to reacclimate at his own pace.
That's best for everyone involved.

title: Chiefs Injury Report: Latest Updates on Kenneth Walker, Trey Smith
full_text:
Coming off a 35-13 victory over the Falcons , the Chiefs are hoping to heal up quickly heading into their Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals. Several Kansas City starters have been banged up over the past few weeks and the team is hoping to get healthy before Sunday.
While the franchise added former Colts wideout Josh Downs before the trade deadline, his first game in the red and gold was overshadowed by the absence of Kenneth Walker. The superstar running back was a late addition to the injury report last Friday after pulling his groin, forcing him to miss the win against Atlanta. In addition to Walker, multiple starters on the offensive line remain sidelined. Here are the latest updates head coach Andy Reid provided during Wednesday's press conference .
Wednesday marked the Chiefs' first practice session of the week, and Walker was not on the field with the rest of the squad. Reid indicated that the medical staff would take a cautious approach as the Super Bowl LX MVP works his way back.
"He had a sore groin. It's getting better," Reid said. "With those, we just don't want to do something stupid. It's still bugging him a little bit. He's feeling a lot better than he was." Yesterday, ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported a similar sentiment , suggesting Kansas City could rest Walker for the Cardinals showdown to prepare for the short week ahead when the Chiefs face the Bills on Thanksgiving Day. The emergence of fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson , who tallied 171 yards from scrimmage and two receiving touchdowns last week, allows the team to prioritize Walker's long-term health.
Unless Walker appears on the injury report as a limited practice participant on Thursday or Friday, it can be safely assumed that Johnson will earn his second consecutive start in the backfield.
In addition to the ongoing situation with second-year tackle Josh Simmons , the Chiefs are facing additional uncertainty on the offensive line. By the second half of last week's victory, KC had to turn to a pair of backups on the right side.
Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not practice today either as they nurse their respective injuries. Both of their statuses for Week 11 remain up in the air.
Reid told the media that Moore was "making progress" with the ankle he injured in Week 9 against the Jets, while Smith has yet to clear concussion protocol. He didn't offer a firm timeline for either lineman's return. Mike Caliendo filled in at right guard for Smith after previously starting two games at left guard during Kingsley Suamataia's mysterious benching . Joshua Ezeudu has been filling in at right tackle for Moore. Should neither starter be ready to return, those two would be the next men up along the offensive line.
Kansas City doesn't have much reason to rush Walker or either of its offensive linemen back into action this week. The Cardinals enter Sunday's contest with a 3-7 record and are merely playing for draft position after scoring nine points over the past two games.

title: Grand Theft Contract: Which Chiefs Salary Cap Hits Are Holding KC Back in 2026?
full_text:
For those who may not be familiar with the cultural behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto VI , let's put it into context. The game, set to release on Thursday, is rumored to have cost more than $1 billion to develop . It has reportedly made more than $1.5 billion before being officially released .
For comparison, the NFL's salary cap in 2026 is set at just over $301 million per team.
So, with a new GTA just around the corner, let's take this tenuous link as an opportunity to review the Chiefs' 2026 salary cap and decide which players are underperforming on their substantial deals and which ones might be justifying their large cap hit.
While a $7 million cap hit isn't an outrageous number in a vaccuum, it is enough to make Harrison Butker the league's most expensive kicker in 2026. His $7.3 million cap hit narrowly outpaces Seattle's Jayson Myers ($7.2 million), but Butker and Myers have a $1.5 million lead on third place and beyond.
Of course, if you're reading Chiefs On SI , you don't need me to over-explain Butker's disastrous 2026 season so far. The team signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad and just worked out veteran kicker Matt Prater this week .
Still, the Chiefs are publicly holding out hope that Butker can stabilize this year. Could he return to something resembling his previous form by playoff time? It's possible! Will he have provided the kind of confidence and consistency that $7 million typically buys? Definitely not.
If there's any player who I expect an argument about, it's star defensive tackle Chris Jones. Through half the season, has he been worth nearly $45 million? No, that's an enormous number and makes him the priciest defender in the NFL this year.
The second-highest interior defensive lineman cap hit in the league belongs to Alim McNeill at $29 million, while the highest cap number for an edge rusher is T.J. Watt's $42 million . According to Spotrac , Jones has the third-highest cap hit in the entire NFL this season, behind only Matthew Stafford and Justin Herbert.
Has Jones been the best defender in football this season? No. So you'd assume his cap hit is borderline criminal, right? It's still not that simple for me.
If the 32-year-old Jones was having a better season and showing fewer signs of slowing down, I think the Chiefs would have restructured his contract by now. On his current deal , this '26 cap hit is his highest number, taking up nearly 15% of the Chiefs' cap. But any effort to restructure Jones' deal would move money into future seasons, making it harder to part with Jones in years to come. If the Chiefs wanted to cut Jones before the 2027 season, they'd free up $18.6 million in cap space but hold $19.5 in dead cap. If KC keeps Jones at his $38 million hit in '27, they could clear up $35 million in 2028 with "only" $9.75 in dead money.
Despite only having three sacks this season (with two coming against the New York Jets two weeks ago), I'm not sure that Jones' future has been decided. If he can regain his game-wrecking gear down the stretch while commanding attention from opposing offenses, he's still an extremely valuable player. Plus, I still just can't fault the Chiefs for being willing to overpay a franchise cornerstone in order to keep the defense's most important player under contract through the back end of his career while they continue to chase Super Bowls.
Is it a great contract for the Chiefs? No. Do I still understand why and how Kansas City agreed to a deal that would pay a 32-year-old $45 million this season? I do.
Jaylon Moore's time with the Chiefs has never really gone according to plan. He was expected to be the team's starting left tackle until they drafted Josh Simmons shortly after signing Moore in free agency, leaving Moore to move into a swing-tackle role behind Simmons and Jawaan Taylor in 2025. After starting six games in '25, Moore appeared to be in some level of competition with undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson for the right tackle position in training camp this summer. Moore looked to win the job before Simmons suffered a back injury, leaving Benson to take over on the left side.
This year, Moore has not performed particularly well on the right side while carrying the team's third-highest cap hit.
Free agent tackles are expensive because it's a tough position to confidently fill out and great players rarely hit the open market, but there's no real argument that Moore has met his contract numbers across his two-year, $30 million deal. I never cared which side of the line Moore played on, as long as he was a positive force. Unfortunately, it's hard to say that he's been much more than passable.
Kristian Fulton's two-year, $20 million contract looked like a borderline disaster last season, when Fulton never seemed to get fully into the mix at corner until he got more opportunity (and played well) at the very end of the year.
The Chiefs could have cut Fulton this offseason to free up $5 million with an $8 million cap hit, but through '26, Fulton has made an argument to justify his salary, even as the team's third corner.
Second-year third-round pick Nohl Williams has been the team's most consistent cornerback, playing 94% of the Chiefs' defensive snaps, while No. 6 overall pick Mansoor Delane (54%) has been excellent when he hasn't been sidelined due to a recurring shoulder injury. Meanwhile, Fulton (47%) has been very good in his part-time role. Is $13 million an expensive No. 3 corner? Sure, but with Delane's injury and so much youth in the room, Fulton's cap hit is large, not egregious.

title: Chiefs Reportedly Adding Tackle Depth: What Does It Mean for Battered O-Line?
full_text:
It's been a trying season for the Kansas City Chiefs' offensive line, as a combination of fluctuating performance and lackluster durability has created some obstacles despite a 7-2 start for the team.
Week 10's win over the Atlanta Falcons may have summed that up to perfection, as Kansas City dominated the opponent but also showed plenty of cracks in the foundation along the way. Ahead of Sunday's contest against the Arizona Cardinals, general manager Brett Veach is doing something to potentially improve the situation.
Per a Wednesday morning report from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN , the Chiefs are signing former Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Fred Johnson to the practice squad.
The #Chiefs are signing former #Eagles OT Fred Johnson to their practice squad and he’ll likely be elevated to the 53-man roster. pic.twitter.com/zV3ITTxp48
Johnson, who entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2019, has spent time with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Jacksonville Jaguars as well. He's appeared in 86 regular-season games to date, making 22 starts and logging just under 1,900 offensive snaps in total.
Rapoport adds that Johnson is "likely" to be activated to the 53-man roster at some point, whether it be via standard elevation (he's allotted three during the regular season) for game day or a straight-up signing down the road.
Johnson brings a defined set of skills to the table, yet it's ironic that one of his core traits is versatility. According to Pro Football Focus , the 29-year-old has played most of his snaps at either right tackle (893) or left tackle (833), with a decent chunk still residing at the right guard spot (158).
He split time between tackle alignments during his fill-in duties with Philly in 2024 and 2025. His most extensive experience came during that window — he combined for 626 pass blocking opportunities and surrendered 57 total pressures.
The eighth-year man boasts intriguing physical tools, too. Per MockDraftable , Johnson is in the 94th percentile in height (6-foot-7), the 91st percentile in wingspan (84.5 inches) and the 88th percentile in hand size (10 5/8 inches). It's easy to see why the Chiefs were interested in him, especially given the state of affairs with the offensive line.
Neither tackle position is in a good place. On the left side, Kahlil Benson turned in one of his worst games as a professional down in Atlanta and looks like less of a true answer with each passing week. Projected starter Josh Simmons remains on the injured reserve list and, via head coach Andy Reid, wasn't expected to return to practice this week.
On the opposite side, veteran Jaylon Moore is dealing with a lingering ankle injury and hasn't fared particularly well when available. The jury is still out on backups Joshua Ezeudu and Diego Pounds , both trade acquisitions from August. The former is coming off a solid outing that saw him get credited with a pair of pressures ceded but appear much more competent in the lineup.
There are multiple paths the Johnson add can take. At the extreme end, he could be signed to an active roster contract and finish out the season in place of someone like Pounds if the club felt its depth needed to be improved. Thinking more conservatively, it's also possible that Kansas City simply desires someone with the ability to pinch hit at multiple spots.
Being able to count on another battle-tested chess piece is nice this time of year. That's without even factoring in right guard Trey Smith also getting banged up in Week 10. A player like Johnson entering the fold makes plenty of sense.
It's as low-risk as it gets for a franchise that's battered and bruised along the offensive line.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Which Receivers Should Get the Largest Workload in the Second Half of the Season?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 7-2 after their comfortable victory over the Atlanta Falcons , and with an impressive Chiefs debut for wide receiver Josh Downs , the Chiefs' passing game looks to be the healthiest it's been in quite some time.
Where does that leave the wide receiver rotation just after the midway point of the year? That's where we'll begin in today's Chiefs On SI mailbag.
What is the ideal, gotta-have-it, three-receiver set for this team with the players currently available on the roster today? (And if Worthy isn't on your list, do you think the coaching staff will reach the same conclusion?) - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
Downs and Rashee Rice are the obvious No. 1 and 2, regardless of which order you'd rank them in. The third spot is the tricky one.
In his third season, Xavier Worthy leads Chiefs wide receivers in snaps taken by a healthy margin, having taken 478 snaps to Rice's second-place 273. Worthy has been on the field more than Travis Kelce and Kingsley Suamataia this year; he's fifth in snaps on the Chiefs' offense. That doesn't look like a player who's about to see his role decrease significantly.
However, we've seen the same issues in recent weeks. Despite his experience and health, he hasn't been making a significant impact in the box score or on film. With a few sideline-related miscues gaining traction amongst some Chiefs fans on social media, I understand why Worthy's stock appears to be in decline.
Worthy's 33 catches on 50 targets for 278 yards adds up to more than double rookie Cyrus Allen's early-season production (seven catches on 14 targets for 109), but Worthy has quadrupled Allen's offensive snaps (108).
I've seen enough flashes from Allen and enough miscues from Worthy to at least be willing to hear out an argument on behalf of the rookie being a more useful weapon in this "gotta-have-it" scenario. For now, I do think Worthy retains that spot for the KC coaching staff. Still, Worthy's role seems destined to decrease with the addition of Downs and the return of the now-healthy Rice; if Worthy doesn't start making plays again soon, Allen will continue to close that gap.
Cyrus Allen is two months older than Xavier Worthy. They're both 23.
What playoff team in the AFC would be toughest to beat at home? My money is on the Broncos strictly based on the pass rush. When Mahomes loses in the playoffs, he isn't able to overcome his offensive line. They could overwhelm us. - @jaymaul4.bsky.social
Bo Nix aside, I think this logic for Denver absolutely holds water. The single area on the team that I am the most short- and long-term worried about is the offensive line, so we logically have to pick a team that has the ability to challenge that unit.
The question the Chiefs will need to see answered over the next month or so: Do the Bills and Bengals have enough defensive firepower to push through KC's questionable line? Maybe this is out of blind loyalty to Mahomes, maybe it's because he's been so good behind such an iffy group already this season , but I think that any team planning to beat the Chiefs in January will need to have a solid day rushing the passer and an offense that's better and more consistent than what Denver offers... which is also where the perpetually under-the-radar Jaguars come into play for their part of the conversation.
With how our offense looks, both with the elite running game from either K9 or E10 and our passing game looking WAY better now that Josh Downs is already making an impact for us, do you think we can come out of the gauntlet of games to end the season 5-2 or better? - @zandersahlia.bsky.social
For record-keeping, here's the gauntlet in question: at Buffalo, at Cincinnati, vs. New England, vs. San Francisco. Then, the Chiefs go to LA to face the Chargers and host the Raiders. You have to expect that Kansas City wins the final two AFC West showdowns of the year, leaving that brutal five-game stretch where you're asking about going 3-2.
The Rams are significantly depleated from their preseason hype, and the Patriots are expected to be without quarterback Drake Maye. The Bills, Bengals and 49ers are all legitimate Super Bowl contenders.
Going even 2-3 down that stretch would be plenty for a playoff spot, sending KC to a hypothetical 11-5 season if they do handle those final two divisional games after the gauntlet. Even if the Chiefs are underdogs at Buffalo, at Cincy and home to the Niners, I'd be a bit surprised if they lost all three of those games.
Now, if they beat the Bills and Bengals, we're back to talking about their chances at the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
Can this team win the Super Bowl with this offensive line? - @MarkKnopke
Yes! I'm quite concerned about the state of the O-line, but (yes, even after two Super Bowl losses enabled by completely overwhelmed offensive line play) if you give me Mahomes, a fully stocked array of weapons both through the air and on the ground, and a defense that might be hitting its stride, that team can absolutely win a few one-off games while trying to hide the line's deficiencies.
Would it be more likely with better performances across the trenches? Absolutely. But the AFC doesn't have a singularly dominant team, and the Chiefs are just as plausible of a Super Bowl representative as anyone else in the conference.

title: Making Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes’ Case as the 2026 NFL MVP
full_text:
Considering how well he's performed in 2026, it's almost easy to forget that Patrick Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL and LCL . Just nine months removed from suffering a potentially career-altering injury, Mahomes made his comeback in the season-opening win over the Broncos and has appeared in every game since.
While it took the future Hall of Fame quarterback some time to rediscover his rhythm, he has returned to his usual form in his 10th season in the NFL. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns without an interception in the Chiefs' dominant win against the Falcons last week, putting him ahead of Peyton Manning for the most combined touchdown passes in a player's first 10 seasons. Nobody could have expected Mahomes to re-establish himself this quickly, but that's exactly what's happened. After his stellar Week 10 showing, Mahomes now holds the fifth-best odds to be named NFL's Most Valuable Player, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Could he capture his third MVP award by season's end?
Since the Chiefs inked running back Kenneth Walker to a three-year deal in the offseason, Andy Reid's offense has become more balanced and less reliant on the aerial attack. Even so, Mahomes ranks inside the league's top 10 in passing yards, passing touchdowns, and is second among all quarterbacks in touchdown-to-interception ratio (19-to-4).
The last three weeks alone, Mahomes has averaged over 300 yards through the air per contest, tossing 10 touchdowns without an interception on 70.1% passing. Those are numbers that could earn him serious MVP consideration if they persist.
Currently listed above Mahomes on the MVP ladder are Joe Burrow (+100), Josh Allen (+350), Brock Purdy (+400), and Trevor Lawrence (+550). But aside from Purdy and the injury-riddled 49ers, the other three quarterbacks don't come close to sharing Mahomes' predicament at wide receiver. Tyquan Thornton suffered a likely season-ending ankle injury in Kansas City's win over the Raiders in Week 4, while Rashee Rice missed time with a hamstring ailment. Those developments have compounded an already unpredictable receiving corps entering the campaign, yet Mahomes' production hasn't wavered one bit.
Not to take anything away from Burrow's historic first half of the season, but Mahomes doesn't have the luxury of throwing to the best receiver tandem in football in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins every week. The Chiefs also have a more dependable defense that allows the offense to play with a lead, whereas Cincinnati's defensive struggles often force Burrow to throw 40+ times just to keep the Bengals competitive. There's far more to consider in the MVP discussion than yards and touchdowns.
Although Mahomes still has some ground to make up in the passing-yardage department, his efficiency has been difficult for the other MVP hopefuls to match. He has been able to limit turnovers in addition to showcasing his new-and-improved deep ball, something that has contributed to Kansas City's offensive resurgence.
With former Colts slot wideout Josh Downs now in the mix , Mahomes can finally maximize the weapons at his disposal. That was made evident in the Falcons game when five different pass-catchers recorded 40 or more receiving yards and Mahomes was distributing the rock to everyone. MVP voters put a lot of stock into a team's record when evaluating prospective award contenders. Burrow, Allen, Lawrence, and Mahomes are all battling to secure AFC's top playoff seed, which could go a long way in determining the eventual winner. A 13 or 14-win finish for the Chiefs may be enough to push Mahomes over the top if the other candidates lose ground in the playoff race.
It understandably took time for Mahomes to trust his surgically repaired knee and gradually learn what his body could withstand on the field. His comfort levels have steadily improved throughout the year, and he's now playing even better than he did in the past few seasons. There is no better time for Mahomes to start hitting his stride than now.
Burrow will remain the consensus favorite for the award until further notice, but if he experiences a second-half slump and Mahomes keeps playing at this level, don't be surprised if the three-time Super Bowl champ receives first-place MVP votes at the end of the year.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Emmett Johnson, Cyrus Allen Take the Cake
full_text:
As the home stretch of the 2026-27 campaign arrives, the Kansas City Chiefs have one more game against a struggling team before a gauntlet of a schedule in Weeks 12-16. If there's one thing recent outings have shown, though, it's that the club's young players have plenty to offer.
With the war of attrition setting in and injuries piling up, the organization's depth will undoubtedly continue to be tested. Is it a good or bad thing that Kansas City could be asking the future of the team to rise to the occasion in the present?
Following Week 10's win over the Atlanta Falcons , let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, who is running low on time to be activated to the roster from the physically unable to perform list , isn't included here.
Left tackle Josh Simmons remains off the list after going to injured reserve . The same applies to running back Brashard Smith .
No young Chiefs player — and very few members of the team in general — was more productive than fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson in Week 10. The halfback made his starting debut due to a groin injury to Kenneth Walker III and ran with it, both literally and figuratively. Johnson was fantastic on the ground and kept dicing up the defense as a pass catcher, cementing him as a force to be reckoned with .
Elsewhere, defensive end Ashton Gillotte is coming on strong after a slow start to the season . The 2025 third-round pick has a sack in back-to-back games and is no stranger to playing plus run defense.
The cornerback duo of Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane was far from perfect, as Williams lost to Drake London a couple of times and Delane seemed to get banged up, but the former logged an interception to cap off Sunday's blowout win.
One of the stories of Sunday was wide receiver Cyrus Allen, the second of Kansas City's two fifth-round selections back in April. The Cincinnati product scored the first touchdown of his professional career against a quality cornerback in A.J. Terrell, making it look easy with a masterclass of a route:
Cyrus Allen with a nasty double move to cash in the long TD🥵🥵 Sully gonna have to leave the app pic.twitter.com/M8GfmtekqM
Rounding out the top tier of Chiefs youngsters is defensive end R Mason Thomas. Thomas was quiet down at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, going without a pressure for the first time in his KC tenure. We'll chalk this up to a one-off.
Even after the trade acquisition of now-former Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, sophomore pass catcher Jalen Royals logged 19 snaps in Week 10. For the first time since Week 1 of the regular season, however, he went without a single target on offense. Left tackle Kahlil Benson also had a rough outing , surrendering a new career-high figure in pressures and continuing to look like he's crumbling as the foundation of the line.
Defensive tackle Peter Woods stays in his usual spot after missing Sunday's showdown with a lingering neck injury. Keep an eye on the injury report to see if he'll play this weekend against the Arizona Cardinals.
Speaking to the media this week, head coach Andy Reid made it a point to allude to how wideout Andrew Armstrong is a lesser-known player both in Chiefs circles and nationally. He made a name for himself in Week 10, though, when he hauled in a beautiful 43-yard bomb from quarterback Patrick Mahomes for the Dallas native's first touchdown.
THAT'S 5 TOUCHDOWNS FOR 15 ⏰ pic.twitter.com/d6NkVGDKyI
It'll be interesting to find out whether the potential return of Norman-Lott will impact Bryson Eason's status on the roster. He's squarely in the rotation along the interior of the defensive line, playing 20 snaps in Week 8 and rising from five in Week 9 to 11 in Week 10, but he doesn't stand out a ton when on the field. Sometimes, that isn't a bad thing for the waiver pickup .
With tight end Travis Kelce hurting his calf/ankle on the club's opening possession and Jared Wiley sustaining an ankle fracture, 2025 undrafted free agent Jake Briningstool wound up getting more of a workload than most anticipated. He played a career-high 17 offensive reps, hauling in one of his two targets for 20 yards in the process.
Last is fourth-round cornerback Jadon Canady, whose stint as a rookie for the Chiefs has been tumultuous to this point. His snap count swelled to 26 on defense and 18 on special teams in Atlanta, seeing him record three tackles but also look more vulnerable in coverage.
Nothing to see here regarding 2025 fifth-round linebacker Jeffrey Bassa, who continues to be a trusted special teams ace for coordinator Dave Toub. Now several weeks into his return from injury , fellow 'backer Cooper McDonald saw the field just once on defense in Week 10 but set a season high with 25 special teams snaps.
Former Iowa standout, safety Xavier Nwankpa, recorded two tackles on a combined 31 reps (five on defense, 26 on special teams). He's settled into a consistent role in his debut campaign.
For the first time in his career, tackle Diego Pounds got into the lineup and split time between offense and teams. Given how banged-up the offensive line was and the game script of a lopsided contest, this was a nice reward from the Chiefs for the UDFA's work since coming over via trade .
Seventh-round pick Garrett Nussmeier continues to be Kansas City's emergency third quarterback on game days. Rookie running back Jaydn Ott sat this one out with a hamstring injury, whereas cornerback Melvin Smith was a Week 10 inactive after playing special teams in Weeks 8 and 9.

title: Chiefs Stock Watch: Reality Check Time After Week 10's Blowout Win
full_text:
For the second game in a row, the Kansas City Chiefs squared off against an inferior opponent and actually managed to make the quality of each team obvious on the playing field.
Week 10's showdown with the Atlanta Falcons seemed destined to be a Kansas City victory from the beginning. Within the final result of a 35-13 blowout triumph on the road, there were plenty of positives but also a few negatives to take away with a new week arriving.
Let's dive into the good and bad from the Chiefs' Week 10 win against Atlanta and single out three players whose stock is trending up, as well as three who could use a better showing in Week 11 and down the stretch of the year.
These players stood out for positive reasons on Sunday, potentially changing the trajectory of their seasons in the process.
Given how fantastic starter Kenneth Walker III has been when on the field, there wasn't much need for premium reps for rookie running back Emmett Johnson in Weeks 1-9. He still found ways to impact the game, but Sunday was his coming-out party with Walker sitting due to a groin injury. The Nebraska product logged a whopping 28 touches down in Atlanta, averaging 6.1 yards per opportunity and scoring two touchdowns in the process.
Johnson's ability as a receiver out of the backfield is second to very few at the position right now. He's logged at least a catch in two of his last three outings, going for 11 receptions on 12 targets for 198 yards and three scores in that span. The fifth-round pick has clearly adapted to life as a professional at a rapid pace and made the most of his first NFL start.
There's a case to be made that Johnson is a starting-caliber player for multiple teams. That includes the Chiefs. Even though Walker is the superior option and will resume the role once he returns, having such a dangerous backup has to make Kansas City feel good with tough, cold-weather football on the horizon.
Yards per Route Run Leaders 1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.09) 2. Mike Evans (3.65) 3. Emmett Johnson (3.13) 🔥👀⁉️🤯 RB Leaders by Yards From Scrimmage per Touch 1. Emmett Johnson (7.63) 🔥 2. Jaylen Warren (6.66) 3. Christian McCaffrey (6.13) RB Leaders by Missed Tackles Forced… https://t.co/9XcDTPzidE
Coming into Week 10, first-year wideout Cyrus Allen was an interesting case. Were the Chiefs truly planning to give him more snaps and opportunities, or would the trade acquisition of Josh Downs put a cap on the fifth-rounder's ceiling within the offense in 2026-27? Considering Allen had averaged 22 snaps and a pair of targets in the three games leading up to Atlanta, there were reasons for the answer to go in either direction.
Fortunately for the former Cincinnati man, the club found a perfectly happy medium for at least one week of play.
Allen had the best showing of his young career to date on Sunday, turning four targets into two receptions for 44 yards. His snap count of 23 was good for 35.4% of those available, which is more than enough time to make a play or two. That's precisely what Allen did, as he was held on a non-call for a potential touchdown earlier in the contest but rebounded with a masterpiece of a route against A.J. Terrell later on for his first-ever score:
Filthy route from Cyrus Allen 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/YNh2IdJZjU
It's not just that Allen found the end zone. It's how he found it. The rookie was lined up on the boundary of the formation with tight coverage and won with technicality and some burst. That's more of what the Chiefs need in the receiver room; that highlight will be remembered in Allen discussions for weeks and months to come.
Before the season, many thought the Chiefs' defensive line would live and die with what All-Pro tackle Chris Jones could provide. While there's still some truth to that, defensive end George Karlaftis has emerged as a worthy running mate for the veteran pass rusher in more ways than one.
He's also established himself as one of the more valuable assets on the team after plenty of folks questioned the four-year contract extension he was previously signed to before the expiration of his rookie deal.
Karlaftis was tremendous once again in this one, recording a second-down sack on Atlanta's second drive, batting down a pass early in the third frame and also combining for a quarterback takedown with Jones later on. The former first-round pick is the only player this century to log both a tackle for loss and a pass defended in seven straight regular-season games.
Add in that all five-and-a-half of Karlaftis' sacks have come since Week 6, and you get the full picture of a 25-year-old who's having a breakout in season No. 5.
These three players didn't meet the bar in Week 10 and need to recover moving forward.
Back in the spring and summer, nobody expected undrafted rookie free agent tackle Kahlil Benson to still be in the Chiefs' starting lineup. That's especially true when considering it was the right tackle job he wound up competing for . Once Josh Simmons' health became an issue again, however, the Indiana product was thrust into the lineup and actually didn't look too bad early in the season.
With Simmons still on injured reserve and the Chiefs' offensive line becoming increasingly banged up, though, Benson is struggling to string together effective performances.
Pro Football Focus tracking metrics aren't everything, but the 24-year-old surrendered a then-career-high four pressures in Week 7's loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He followed it up with an improved one-pressure outing versus the Denver Broncos, but those figures are five and eight, respectively, since then.
Rolling into Week 11, Benson is tied for seventh in most pressures ceded (30) by a tackle. He's got a significant lead in quarterback hits, allowing 16 to second-place Kolton Miller's 12. For all the talk about how much Kansas City needed a wide receiver at the deadline, the return of Simmons would have a massive swing for the floor and ceiling of the offense as well.
If there's one thing you can't accuse the Chiefs of, it's not trying to make 2024 first-round pick Xavier Worthy a legitimate weapon. Before Sunday's game, the lowest single-game target total he'd logged this year was two, and he only did it once. In all other contests, his average was 6.4. Despite him repeatedly showing that he isn't worth the on-field investment, it doesn't seem to be going anywhere.
Worthy saw three passes thrown his way in Week 10, although none connected for a completion. On the afternoon, he drifted too much on a second-and-15 drop, ran a bad route and lost the ball on a fourth-quarter first-and-10 and also let an onside kick get recovered on special teams. His 57 snaps were the third-most for him this season; being on the field for 87.7% of opportunities isn't a signal that the club is moving away from him.
Perhaps it should, though. In all, Worthy has turned 50 targets into 33 receptions, 278 yards and a single touchdown this year. According to SumerSports , he leads the Chiefs' wide receiver room with a 17.92% target share but is fourth in yards per route run with 0.93.
Only 40 receivers have run at least 250 routes in 2026-27. Worthy is one of them, yet he's 38th in YPRR. He needs either a change of role right now or a change of scenery in the offseason to find whatever best form he's got left.
It's been a strange season for one Kingsley Suamataia, as the left guard has put excellent reps on tape but also completely whiffed on other occasions and looked totally out of place. There's the matter of availability, too, with head coach Andy Reid benching him on two separate occasions ahead of road contests but not revealing why that was the case.
The third-year man bounced back in Week 9 with a splendid overall game, but that didn't translate to this one.

title: Why George Karlaftis Has Been the Unsung Hero for the Chiefs’ Defense
full_text:
Despite a strong 7-2 start for the Chiefs, many Kansas City fans were underwhelmed with how the defensive line performed early in the season. The lack of production along the front four became a major talking point during a lengthy sack drought that lasted 15 quarters.
Since that prolonged dry spell, though, the pass rush has come alive for Steve Spagnuolo's unit. The Chiefs have recorded eight sacks over the past two games while surrendering just 12.5 points per contest during that span. While critics have been calling for "CEO of Sack Nation" Chris Jones to elevate his play, George Karlaftis has flown under the radar. In the final year of his rookie contract , the fifth-year defensive end is quietly putting together the best statistical season of his NFL career.
Across the last five weeks, Karlaftis has totaled 11 QB hits, eight tackles for loss, and 5.5 sacks. More impressively, the Athens native has been better than anyone else in the NFL at batting balls down at the line of scrimmage.
🚨 NFL HISTORY! George Karlaftis becomes the FIRST player since at least 1999 to record both a tackle for loss and a pass defended in SEVEN consecutive regular-season games! pic.twitter.com/zkpnKrlcju
When evaluating edge rushers, it's easy to dismiss their contributions when their sack total is low. However, Karlaftis would remain among the most disruptive defensive ends even if he hadn't started racking up more sacks.
Right now, Karlaftis is tied with a few other players for eighth in the league with 10 pass deflections. That's a remarkable number for any position other than defensive back. Only one other defensive end in the NFL (Jaylahn Tuimoloau) has managed five or more pass breakups — and Karlaftis is doing it on a weekly basis. Even when he isn't getting into the backfield to pressure the quarterback, Karlaftis is obstructing passing lanes, making life difficult for opposing signal-callers. It has become a valuable and underrated weapon for a Chiefs defense that still ranks in the NFL's bottom half in sacks.
With the 32-year-old Jones having a relatively quiet year by his standards, Karlaftis has needed to assume more responsibility within the defensive scheme. After receiving a massive contract extension last offseason, any questions about whether he was worth the investment have seemingly been put to rest.
Karlaftis caught a lot of flak from the fanbase after being sackless heading into the team's bye week. He certainly heard the noise and has responded emphatically in recent weeks. There have been few pass rushers more productive than Karlaftis since the beginning of October. Now that the defensive line has broken out of its slump, Chiefs fans can finally appreciate what Karlaftis has done this season. He'll continue to play a key role anchoring KC's defensive front throughout the remainder of the campaign.

title: Chargers Add Former Top-100 Pick, Raising Doubt on Charlie Kolar's Sunday Status
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers, for the majority of the NFL season, have been a terrible offense , being the main cause of the team's 1-8 start to the year. One of the very few weapons that have been effective this season has been the team's biggest free-agent signee, Charlie Kolar.
Kolar, a former Baltimore Raven, came to the Chargers as a blocking-first tight end who has upside as a pass-catcher. Since his arrival in Los Angeles, Kolar has been very good when on the field...but him staying on the field for large stretches of the year has not come to fruition.
On September 20, 2026 (Week 2 of the NFL season), Kolar suffered a broken left forearm, missing two games. Upon his return, he continued his strong play as a blocker, with his pass-catching abilities continuing to shine. Now in Week 10, after the Chargers beat his former team , Kolar is in concussion protocol and is expected to miss another game due to injury.
It should be noted that even with the games missed due to injury and the season only halfway through its endpoint, Kolar has already set career highs in receptions (15) and yards (145).
With this injury occurring, it seems that the Bolts are prepared to replace Kolar until he is back from injury, signing a former top-100 draft pick.
Josiah Deguara, a former third-round pick of the 2020 NFL Draft, finds his way onto the Chargers' practice squad as a versatile tight end/full back hybrid. He was drafted out of Cincinnati as a prospect that was viewed by NFL.com scout Lance Zierlein as a "Hard-nosed move tight end who will garner consideration as an NFL H-back. He's a gritty blocker who plays with good positioning and works hard at sustaining blocks to help his run game. As a pass catcher, Deguara is sure-handed with good feel for soft spots against zone..."
Deguara has career totals of 53 catches for 471 yards and 3 touchdowns. In 2026, he has only logged 21 special teams snaps with the Philadelphia Eagles.
2025 was the last time Deguara had "real" playing time, having 170 special teams snaps with the Arizona Cardinals, while also chipping 84 offensive snaps that had Deguara recording three catches for 21 yards and a touchdown.
Now that he is on the Chargers, he is expected to be the immediate addition to the active roster if Kolar were to miss Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets. It should also be expected that the recently healthy David Njoku and the up-and-down second-year pass catcher, Oronde Gadsden II, to be the main snap getters at the tight end spot.
Nate Gosney is lifelong Chargers fan and football nerd who has been writing NFL content since 2022. As a former OL/TE in a run-only offense, he loves some old-school, tough football. title: Hints of Mike McDaniel’s Chargers Fate Keep Emerging
full_text:
At this point, it’s fair to speculate whether anyone will survive this season for the Los Angeles Chargers , as far up as head coach Jim Harbaugh himself.
But Mike McDaniel’s fate seems written, no matter what.
Before the season, it was also fair to wonder if McDaniel would only last one season in Los Angeles due to demand from around NFL. He was, after all, considered a top offensive mind in the league and was expected to work wonders with quarterback Justin Herbert.
Wonders, though, has taken on a new meaning in this context.
Now, it sure feels like we’re headed toward McDaniel leaving the Chargers for all the wrong reasons.
Yes, this is still a conversation after the Chargers’ first win of the season. A 1-8 record is still a 1-8 record.
The Athletic’s Noah Furtado put it best this week: “McDaniel remains squarely on the hot seat and seems unlikely to survive beyond 2026. Herbert has clearly not meshed well with his fifth coordinator in seven seasons.”
It’s not like McDaniel’s offense was dominant while escaping a nosediving Baltimore team, 23-20. Justin Herbert only completed 12 of his 18 attempts for 129 yards. His only touchdown came as a rusher.
It does more harm than good to mention that Omarion Hampton had a big day with 22 carries for 105 yards and a score on a 4.8 average. McDaniel was, after all, largely ignoring the recent first-round pick in favor of guys like Keaton Mitchell instead.
Yes, McDaniel has suffered from injury woes to the roster. He’s likely suffered a front office that doesn't do a good enough job assembling talent.
He’s also said some brilliant things recently, like his battle to get Herbert to stop being so hard on himself for the overall team’s failures.
“The frustrations of the scoreboard, which is an entire team thing, I could feel him press — at the early, early portion of the season — as the game progressed,” McDaniel said of Herbert, per Furtado.
But McDaniel is a part of that, too. His arriving and asking Herbert to change his footwork in certain stances sounded great on paper. So did installing his own anticipation-throwing offense that requires speed with a roster that just doesn’t have much of that to go around.
Ripping up a scheme and making Herbert start over yet again with a new coordinator would simply be continuing old problems for the Chargers. But if things don’t get dramatically better around him over the next month or so, it feels like all involved won’t really have a choice.
That would, of course, bring the running tally to his sixth coordinator in eight seasons.
