title: Jim Harbaugh Confirms Rookie has Earned Starting Job
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have finally won a game . The Chargers walked into Baltimore on Monday Night Football and took down their former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter and his Ravens squad to earn their first victory of the 2026 season.
The Chargers have been searching for an identity on offense all season. One of the biggest factors in the struggle to find an identity has been a consistent wave of injuries on the offensive side of the ball. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been in and out of the lineup all season as well as the rest of the wide receiver room.
One of the biggest problems has come from the inconsistency in both play and availability along the offensive line. Dating back to training camp, the Chargers are now on their sixth option at left guard and have had four different tackles take snaps at left tackle and three at right tackle this season.
Entering training camp, the Chargers were expected to have veterans Kayode Awosika and Trevor Penning competing for the starting left guard spot alongside rookie Jake Slaughter as he attempted to make the conversion to NFL guard from college center. Veteran Trey Pipkins entered the conversation later in camp as did second-year lineman Branson Taylor.
Four out of the five of these players mentioned have taken snaps at left guard this season, Slaughter did so in an emergency when the Chargers were down to their last reserve lineman and had to plug in backup center Jacob Spomer in week four against the Seattle Seahawks. Taylor had taken a few snaps at right guard before getting injured again and sent back to injured reserve.
Penning, Taylor and Pipkins have all spent time on IR and Awosika missed weeks three through nine and finally is off the injury report for Week 11. Following Trevor Penning's injury in week four against the Seahawks, sixth-round rookie Logan Taylor entered the lineup and has been the starting left guard ever since.
Taylor was a versatile offensive lineman in college with starts at every position but center during his time at Boston College. His versatility and leadership led many to be surprised he was available in the sixth round of the 2026 draft where the Chargers selected him with pick number 202.
This past week against the Ravens, Taylor posted his highest-graded game to date since entering the starting lineup while giving up zero pressures. With original starting left guard Kayode Awosika now fully healthy and off the injury report, there were questions if he would get a chance to re-enter the starting lineup.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked if Logan Taylor has earned the right to continue at left guard despite Awosika being healthy and Harbaugh's response was simple, "I see it that way." It appears the consistent revolving door and uncertainty at left guard has finally been solved. At this point of the season, if Logan Taylor can build on his performance and continue to grow and establish himself as an NFL offensive lineman, it could potentially solve a major concern heading into the offseason for Los Angeles.
Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs. He graduated from UC Riverside with a degree in Political Science and The University of Redlands with an MBA.

title: Chargers Week 11 Injury Updates: McConkey is Back, Handful of Starters Questionable
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers finally showed signs of life on Monday Night Football and took down the Baltimore Ravens on the road for their first win of the season. All three phases played well and the offense built a lead in the first half and never surrendered the lead after quarterback Justin Herbert scrambled for a touchdown score on the opening drive.
The Chargers have returned home and with a short week will host the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium this upcoming Sunday. The Jets are 2-8 and it is unknown if starting quarterback Geno Smith will be able to play after taking a massive hit against the Buffalo Bills last week and was knocked out of the game.
This matchup will have draft order implications after the Chargers have now fallen out of the number one spot. Smith himself did say he plans to play against the Chargers this week.
Geno Smith is here in the stretch line at the start of practice. He said he plans to play Sunday at the Chargers. #Jets
The Chargers on the other hand did not leave Baltimore unscathed. The Chargers' first injury report of the week did appear smaller than the several weeks prior but some notable starters are listed on the injury report.
Linebacker Daiyan Henley was listed out of practice with what Jim Harbaugh called knee soreness. Joining Henley as a did not participate is starting tight end Charlie Kolar who has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after self reporting symptoms upon returning home. On a short week, it may be a longshot for Kolar to play against the Jets.
wednesday's injury report for week 11 vs NYJ pic.twitter.com/PLfegFap4H
Cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Isas Waxter were both DNP's to start the week with ankle injuries. Fellow cornerback Donte Jackson was limited to start the week with a groin injury. The injuries clustered together in the cornerback room will further test the Chargers depth at the position
Offensive lineman Trey Pipkins is also practicing after having his practice window opened on Novemeber 12th, he is still on injured reserve. Guard Kayode Awosika is off the injury report and currently has no injury designation.
Ladd McConkey is the biggest update on the injury report. The third-year wide receiver has been having terrible luck on the injury front and has only played two full games this season and has seemingly been on the injury report every week with something new. McConkey has missed the last two weeks after suffering back spasms during pregame warmups against the Houston Texans. He did not practice at all last week in the lead up to the Ravens game.
McConkey's return to practice in a limited fashion is good news but also a cautionary tale. Including him in the gameplan carries a risk given his inability to stay on the field. McConkey is a major boost to the offense when healthy but this season, unfortunately, he has dealt with significant injuries consistently.

title: Latest Updates on Police Response at Home of  Madison Beer, Chargers' Justin Herbert
full_text:
Wednesday night, reports of police activity outside the home of Madison Beer, the fiancée of Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, were confirmed.
The LAPD told Michelle Fisher of ABC 7 that the Hollywood Division received a report of a break-in and dispatch “upgraded the call to a burglary after speaking with the caller.”
According to Fisher, “officers on scene determined no crime had occurred.”
Video from ABC7 appeared to show Herbert and Beer outside the scene, though that remains unconfirmed:
#BREAKING : LAPD races to the Hollywood Hills home of singer-songwriter Madison Beer after reports of a break-in. Beer is the fiancée of Chargers QB Justin Herbert. The scare comes after multiple mansions are targeted by burglars overnight. A live update - Tonight at 11 from ABC7 pic.twitter.com/9G6NZKJhL3
As hinted, though, a string of high-profile burglary attempts at mansions in the area recently included tennis star Sloane Stephens. Earlier in the week during those incidents , three suspects believed to be related to the break-ins were detained by police after a vehicle chase.
Beer and Herbert, who went public as a couple in July of 2025 and announced their engagement last summer, were presumably in town during this event.
Beer had last been seen on the red carpet at the ELLE's 2026 Women in Hollywood last Monday around the time Herbert was suiting up for “Monday Night Football” against the Baltimore Ravens before returning home this week for practice ahead of the Chargers’ Week 11 home game against the New York Jets.
Herbert’s Chargers, of course, are 1-8 after picking up their first win of the season in Baltimore. He went 12-of-18 for 129 yards with a rushing score.
Unfortunately, a string of high-profile break-ins involving the homes of star quarterbacks and professional athletes as a whole aren’t uncommon in recent years. In July of 2025, a pawn shop owner pleaded guilty of buying and selling items stolen by a national burglary crew that broke into homes belonging to the likes of Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs, Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers and others.
As The Athletic's T.M. Brown wrote in January, globalization, media and the very public schedule of professional athletes merge to create these scenarios as of late and play a role in the robberies of names like Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders.
In the case of Beer and Herbert, while nothing has been confirmed yet, the concern in the area over the last week speaks for itself.
This story will be updated with more information if/when it becomes available.

title: Chargers' Charlie Kolar Fires Back at Ravens After Revenge Game Win
full_text:
Charlie Kolar made sure the Baltimore Ravens heard what he had to say after the Los Angeles Chargers walked away with a 23-20 victory on Monday Night Football.
Following the Chargers' victory on Monday Night Football , Kolar delivered a short but memorable message about his former organization. When speaking to a fan postgame he said, “I told yall they should have paid me.”
It was a confident response from a player who had just helped his new team defeat the organization that originally gave him his opportunity in the NFL. Monday night’s matchup gave him the opportunity to face the team he previously represented, and the result certainly made the experience sweeter.
Kolar spent the first four seasons of his professional career in Baltimore after the Ravens selected him in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Iowa State. During that time, he developed into a dependable tight end who contributed through his blocking ability and occasional opportunities as a receiver. However, his future took a different direction during the offseason. After becoming a free agent, Kolar signed a three-year contract worth $24.3 million with the Chargers. That decision brought his Baltimore chapter to an end and gave him an opportunity to establish himself somewhere new.
The Chargers entered the matchup desperately searching for a victory after enduring a difficult start to their season. Los Angeles had dropped its first eight games, making the trip to Baltimore an important opportunity to finally change the direction of its campaign.
The team delivered when it mattered, earning a 23-20 victory and ending an 11-game losing streak that extended from the previous season.
Kolar played a role in the closing moments, catching an important 11-yard pass from quarterback Justin Herbert on the Chargers' final possession. That completion helped Los Angeles maintain possession and run valuable time off the clock. Although his individual receiving numbers against Baltimore were modest, finishing with two catches for 16 yards, the overall result was significant. His message was direct, confident, and impossible to miss. Whether the Ravens agreed with his assessment or not, Kolar made his feelings clear.
Although Kolar did not need to make a lengthy statement, his words quickly became one of the biggest talking points surrounding the matchup. For a player returning to face his former team, there could hardly have been a more satisfying way to leave than with a victory and a final word.

title: Justin Herbert Locker Room Footage After Win Raises Some Eyebrows
full_text:
In the aftermath of the Los Angeles Chargers picking up their first win of the season, some strange messaging appeared to go public from the team.
That win sent some odd messaging without the help of reporters, though.
The Chargers did, after all, punt on the trade deadline, except for that failed trade where they attempted to move a young core piece to a divisional foe. And the Chargers, at least for now, punted on the No. 1 spot in the draft order .
To top off the odd week full of complex feelings and stuff was some post-win locker room footage that briefly captured Justin Herbert in a strange light.
As a disclaimer, Herbert is well-known for disliking the camera, so maybe none of this should be a surprise.
Alas, here we go: Locker room footage from the win over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night briefly caught Herbert looking quite a bit more stoic than the rest of his teammates and coaches:
Justin Herbert is sick of Jim Harbaugh 😳 He did NOT look enthused for the postgame high-five. Is that just how Herbert is or is there something deeper? pic.twitter.com/KimFxX3ln4
Big deal? Probably not. That’s Herbert being Herbert. He was playing through an injury and as an uber competitive person, probably isn’t all that charged (sorry) up about being 1-8 on the season. Things have gone way off the rails compared to expectations and there are big questions about the future.
Times like these, it might be wise to see the words of Mike McDaniel on the topic of his star quarterback.
“The game of playing quarterback is so much a mental state of being, where you have to derive your self-confidence by what you do, not necessarily the results,” McDaniel said, according to The Athletic’s Noah Furtado, “because you can’t determine if you have appropriate protection or if someone’s going to win on the route or if they’re going to catch it even when they’re open.”
Still, it’s hard to blame fans who see this footage and wonder. That's what they do. And the outside perception sometimes matching what they can actually see is strange.
In all, a strange season. But the Chargers have stuck true to their word about no changes until next offseason, when actions will speak louder than words or any seconds’ worth of clips behind the scenes.

title: Chargers Rookie Report Card After 9 Games Yields Concerns For Joe Hortiz's Future
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have finally gotten their first win of the 2026 NFL season, putting their record at 1-8 at what is deemed to be about the halfway point of the season. With 17 games on the year, it is a great time to look at how the Chargers' 2026 NFL Draft class is shaping up halfway through the year.
Akheem Mesidor was a somewhat controversial selection by the Bolts, as he was 25 years old at the time of drafting. This is older than his teammate, Tuli Tuipulotu, a player looking to get a massive contract extension at the end of the year, as his rookie contract is up after the year.
That said, Mesidor being older allowed him to instantly adapt to the NFL level, playing well enough early on, and he is now starting to really find his stride halfway through the year. He has 2.5 sacks and 22 pressures this year and is expected to be the future at the position...hopefully alongside the aforementioned Tuipulotu.
Jake Slaughter was viewed as a Center-only prospect coming out of Florida, but was drafted as a guard by the Chargers. This was a controversial decision by the team, but the hope was that the individuals who get paid a lot of money to make these types of decisions would end up being correct.
Slaughter began the year as a competitor to start at LG, then was forced to move into his home position of Center after starter Tyler Biadasz went down with an injury. Back at the position he has the most experience with, Slaughter has started all nine games for the Chargers. While there have been some flashes, Slaughter has struggled, giving up 14 pressures and two sacks, while ranking 26th among 35 qualified centers in overall PFF grade.
Brenen Thompson was the draft selection that had Mike McDaniel seemingly most excited for, as Thompson is a small wide receiver with game-breaking speed. Like all things McDaniel this season, he has been a major disappointment.
Thompson has been hurt with a plethora of different injuries and, when on the field, did not make much of an impact. He has one catch for 13 yards on the season, doing so on 22 offensive snaps.
Travis Burke, the hulking 6'9 mauling offensive lineman, was drafted to be the Chargers' competitor for Trey Pipkins III for the swing offensive tackle position. Once Pipkins III was designated to play guard and eventually hurt, Burke found himself as the swing tackle. Soon after, he was starting as both Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater have missed time with injury.
Burke has played 208 snaps at right tackle and 140 at left tackle, showing true versatility, giving up one sack and 22 pressures. He ranks 48th among 72 qualified offensive tackles in overall PFF grade, with a grade of 63.5. Going from a Day 3 developmental offensive lineman to a starter and playing admirably, especially as a run blocker, Burke has a case for the best draft selection in the entire Chargers 2026 draft class.
Genesis Smith was viewed as a draft steal, as the Arizona safety possessed high-end instincts and range at the safety position. While tackling was an issue in college, Smith has seemed to improve on it since seeing himself on the field with the Bolts.
Smith has been called upon often with Derwin James Jr. and Elijah Molden missing time thus far this season. His youth has shown with coverage lapses popping up often on film. However, his ball-hawking ability and improvement as a tackler have been a very nice addition to this defense. Smith should continue to improve and eventually work his way to becoming a real starting-caliber safety in the NFL. Not too bad for a fourth-round pick.
Nick Barrett was someone who was not very coveted during the NFL Draft process, but somebody that Chargers fans seem to like the more that they watched his college film. Barrett was not expected to have much of a role early on, as the team's interior defensive line room was quite deep, but with injuries occurring, Barrett has seen himself on the field for 140 snaps.
On those snaps, Barrett has recorded half a sack, a tackle for loss and 12 tackles. He grades out as a 50.0 overall PFF defensive grade,106th among 133 qualified interior defensive linemen. Not too bad for a fifth-round rookie.
Logan Taylor was viewed as one of the team's best draft selections prior to the season, as getting a prospect that was viewed as a fourth-round pick by most in the sixth is a massive steal. With the Chargers' offensive line injury luck, he was expected by most to eventually find himself on the field.
Exactly such happened, playing 11 snaps at left tackle and 320 at left guard. After struggling early in his time on the field, Taylor has improved mightily, seemingly beating out the now-healthy and returning Kayode Awosika, the initial starter at the position. Taylor has given up two sacks (one of which was at offensive tackle, a position that most scouts wanted Taylor to avoid at the NFL level) and ten pressures. He ranks with a 54.5 overall PFF grade in the 2026 season, which is 57th among 77 qualified offensive guards.
Alex Harkey was the last offensive lineman drafted by the Chargers during the 2026 Draft cycle, being known as the selection that was supposed to "shut the fans up." While Harkey has not single-handedly "shut the fans up," he has been surprisingly playable early in the NFL season.
This is now a diss towards Harkey;  it is more so that he was viewed as a developmental lineman who should play guard at the NFL level. He was also a sixth-round pick who was seemingly on the outside looking in when cut-down day occurred. He obviously made the team and has now played 160 snaps due to all of the injuries suffered across the Chargers' OL.
On those snaps he has given up 8 pressures and one sacks.

title: Chargers’ Victory Lap at 1-8 Feels Hollow, Concerning for Future
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers picked up their first win of the season and the narratives have flowed, coursing through media in pretty predictable fashion.
Joe Hortiz, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers have been overly concerned with messaging in the media this year, to the point one report even attempted to suggest that the failed Daiyan Henley trade was some sort of master plan to get draft picks for his departure , then re-sign him in free agency.
Next up is a note from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , who suggested during a television appearance that the Chargers moving to 1-8 should be viewed as proof of what they’re building.
“And they did get validation with a win,” Rapoport said. “Perhaps they will get some more. But I really do wonder if just the good feeling in the locker room right there to show the players that what they are building is worth it was worth giving up on those late-round draft picks.”
There are problems with the idea, to say the least.
The Chargers aren’t mathematically eliminated from the playoffs, but they aren’t making the postseason, either.
That out of the way, there are some serious concerns with this idea that the Chargers suddenly have proof of the building concept.
There are other examples, but onlookers get the idea. It’s great for the players in the locker room to get a win and avoid the stigma of 0-17.
But what could be Rapoport echoing what the Chargers front office wants to put out through the grapevine here as a big sign of things to come is just misguided.
The cold reality is that what the Chargers put on tape through 10 weeks might not be good enough to win another single game, and the entire coaching staff and even Hortiz in the front office could be on the hot seat as soon as the season ends.
Tough spot, though. The Chargers could also be “right” and win a few more times, knock themselves out of the top-10 draft order and keep everything the same before doing it all again in 2027.
It should be mildly entertaining to watch and see which way it goes for the Chargers at least, right?

title: Mike McDaniel's Mistake: Why Omarion Hampton Should Be Chargers' Every-Down Back
full_text:
This should be obvious by now, but Omarion Hampton has shown enough to make a strong argument that he deserves to be the primary running back moving forward.
His performance against the Baltimore Ravens was another reminder of what he can bring to the offense when he is given the opportunity to take control of the backfield .
He looked comfortable handling the workload and demonstrated why his presence can make a difference
The biggest reason Hampton should become the main workhorse is that he has consistently shown the ability to make the most of extended playing time. A running back needs opportunities to find his rhythm, understand how the defense is attacking, and establish himself throughout a game. Giving
Hampton only a handful of touches does not necessarily allow him to display everything he can do. When he is involved throughout the contest, he has a much better chance to become a major part of the offensive game plan.
He is not simply a player who should be brought onto the field for a few specific situations. He has the ability to be involved on early downs, passing situations, and important moments when the offense needs someone to step up.
One of the most important things about developing a starting running back is allowing him to build consistency. It is difficult for any player to establish a rhythm when his opportunities constantly change. Hampton needs the opportunity to get comfortable and become the dependable centerpiece of the rushing attack. The more responsibility he receives, the more chances he has to demonstrate that he can handle different defensive looks and situations. There is also something valuable about having a running back who can bring physicality to an offense. Hampton has the kind of running style that can make defenders work for every tackle.
Another important factor is what happens when Hampton is allowed to play the majority of the game. His performances suggest that increased involvement benefits his overall effectiveness. Rather than constantly dividing the workload, the coaching staff should consider letting him establish himself as the primary option while using the other backs in supporting roles. That does not mean the other running backs should disappear from the offense. Having additional options is important, especially during a long season.
However, there should be a clear leader in the backfield and Hampton has earned a legitimate opportunity to fill that position. It’s not very common for a team to use three backs equally and have their production at its peak.

title: Rams' Playoff Hopes Take Major Hit With Puka Nacua Out for Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. After suffering a PCL and MCL injury in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Nacua underwent surgery on Thursday and is set to be out several months.
The NFL was unaware that Rams WR Puka Nacua had undergone knee surgery Tuesday when it suspended him for three games Wednesday, per source. pic.twitter.com/bwVg4X3A9q
There was initially some hope that Nacua could return when the Rams played the Dallas Cowboys in Week 15 on December 20, as that was when he was first eligible to return from injured reserve. However, with Nacua opting for surgery, he will miss the remainder of the season.
Nacua missing the remainder of the year is a big loss for the Rams offense. The Rams were hoping to get healthy over the next few weeks as they make a late push for the postseason. While the Rams are set to get Davante Adams back over the next few weeks, they will still be thin at the wide receiver position.
The Rams relied heavily on Nacua this season when he was healthy. He’s the only Rams wide receiver with over 500 yards despite missing three games. Nacua has three games this season with over 15 targets and three games with over 10 receptions.
On Thursday, Nacua was suspended by the NFL for three weeks for an off-field incident during the offseason. According to Adam Schefter, the NFL was unaware that Nacua had undergone surgery when they handed out his suspension.
With Nacua out for the season, it will be interesting if the Rams continue to take the approach of waiting for players to get healthy or if they make a move at wide receiver. Signing a player like Brandon Aiyuk when he becomes available would make sense as he could fit into that role. However, the Rams have trusted their depth all year and with Adams coming back soon, they may see that as enough.
The Rams adjusted the offense last week to utilize the running backs in the passing game. Head coach Sean McVay implemented Pony Personnel to get both running backs on the field at the same time. Matthew Stafford went 12-for-16 for 202 yards and a touchdown with an EPA per dropback of 0.89.
Throughout the season, the Rams simply haven’t been able to escape the injury bug. After trading for Myles Garrett in the offseason, he missed the first eight games of the year. They signed cornerback Jaylen Watson in free agency and he’s set to miss the rest of the season with a shoulder injury.
The Rams have shown an ability to overcome adversity throughout the season, but losing Nacua for the remainder of the year may be their biggest challenge yet. They’ve managed to remain in the playoff hunt at 6-4, but replacing his production won't be easy as they get set to take on one of the toughest schedules in the NFL over the next seven weeks.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Injured Reserve Decisions, NFL's Strong Message to Puka Nacua, and More
full_text:
A large theme for the Los Angeles Rams this season has been injuries. They’ve been one of the most-injured teams in the league, and it seems like as soon as one player gets healthy, they lose two more. However, they've remained in the playoff hunt .
Over the next few weeks, the Rams will hope to get healthy and that some of their luck changes. However, that will also come with some potentially critical roster decisions.
Entering the season, each team is given eight return designations from injured reserve. This means that a team can put a player on injured reserve, and after four weeks the team can opt to designate that player for return while activating their 21-day practice window. A team has 21 days to add them to the active roster. If a team makes the playoffs, they are given two more designations.
Throughout the season, the Rams have had to use a few of their designations. Prior to Week 1, the Rams used return designations on offensive linemen Justin Dedich and Keagen Trost to avoid losing them for the season.
The Rams activated Trost in Week 6 ahead of their game against the Arizona Cardinals. Before Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, the Rams designated Ronnie Rivers, Terrance Ferguson, and Myles Garrett to return.
With just those returns, the Rams have used up five of their eight return designations. There has been some confusion with Ferguson because he hasn’t been moved out of the practice window. However, even if Ferguson’s practice window expires and the Rams don’t bring him back, that’s still a used return designation.
That leaves the Rams with some difficult decisions to make. They are projected to designate Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua to return. If that’s the case, the Rams wouldn’t have any return designations left.
Where this becomes complicated is in the case of Coleman Shelton, who is out 4-6 weeks. Because the Rams can’t designate another player to return, the Rams either have to work with one less roster spot or be ok with losing Shelton until the playoffs.
It also goes back to the decision for the Rams to bring back Rivers. The Rams brought back Rivers despite him being their RB3 and a special teams contributor. That’s a role that the Rams should have been able to replace via an available free agent.
Given the amount of injuries the Rams have had, every return designation and roster decision matters. While Rivers has been a valuable depth player, the Rams used a limited resource on a replaceable role. Now, with Shelton potentially needing to go on injured reserve, that decision could have significant consequences with the Rams out of return designations.
On Thursday afternoon, the NFL announced a three-week suspension to wide receiver Puka Nacua for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. Nacua’s suspension coincidentally will take place while he’s on injured reserve, and he won’t miss any time that he would have missed otherwise.
The timing of Nacua’s suspension is certainly odd. It can certainly be argued that the NFL missed the mark or didn’t read the room correctly. However, none of that makes it some sort of conspiracy that the NFL is favoring the Rams.
There is some precedent here as it has happened four times since 2018. In 2018, 2024, and 2025, David Perry, Sam Williams, and Daniel Ekuale all got handed suspensions while on IR or after suffering a season-ending injury. Mike Woods in 2023 was suspended while also on the non-football injury list.
It’s rare, and maybe the NFL needs to change it, but it’s not an exception because the Rams made some shady deal in a dark alley with the league.
With that said, the NFL has come down hard on Nacua. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the league communicated that, “Any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League.”
Sticking with Nacua, a big topic of conversation this offseason will be whether or not the Rams decide to pay him. Nacua is in the final year of his rookie deal, and as a fifth-round pick, he doesn’t have a fifth-year option.
It will be interesting to see if the Rams pay Nacua this offseason. As one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, it would seem crazy not to. For all of his off-field issues last offseason, he has seemingly turned a corner this year. There may be some concern, but after the suspension and conversations in the building, there is likely some understanding that something needed to change.
However, outside of the off-field situation, Nacua is set to miss at least six games with injuries this year. It would be the second time since 2024 that Nacua has missed six or more games. The Rams also played one of their best offensive games of the season in Week 2 without Nacua and did so again last week against the Arizona Cardinals.
“He's 25 years old and a brilliant player, but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity,” said ESPN’s Dan Graziano. “All of that is to say: I could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers.”
The Rams have done well to pay their players, and they certainly understand how important he is. If the Rams give him an extension, it’s hard to see it not being team-friendly to some extent. With that said, the franchise tag likely isn’t out of the question either.
Last week, the Rams rolled out Pony Personnel on offense for the first time in the Sean McVay era. The Rams ran 17 plays out of 21 or 20 personnel as Matthew Stafford went 12-for-16 for 202 yards and a touchdown with an EPA per dropback of 0.89. The Rams had a 56 percent success rate out of 20 personnel.
It seems unlikely that Pony Personnel becomes the main identity for the offense, but that doesn’t mean that the Rams won’t build on it going forward.
“The Rams' two-RB sets aren't going away any time soon,” said ESPN’s Dan Graziano. “Coach Sean McVay is going to lean into the areas where his personnel is the strongest, and right now Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are delivering in the run game.”
In Week 9, the Rams were in 11 personnel at a 42.5 percent rate. That was down to 4.5 percent on Sunday against the Cardinals. Instead of three wide receivers with one tight end on the field, the Rams subbed the tight end for another running back. It seems very possible that going forward, many of the Rams’ three-wide-receiver sets will come out of 20 personnel.
This is really contingent on the Rams staying mostly healthy on the offensive line. The loss of Coleman Shelton will hurt, but the Rams may be able to get by with Limmer. A loss at tackle and the Rams could start to see things begin to snowball. However, if they can get by, the Rams’ defense is playing at a level right now where 11-6 is possible. If that happens, it should be enough to make the playoffs.
The Rams were able to scheme around the loss of Nacua on Sunday against the Cardinals. However, they still need a third wide receiver and Brandon Aiyuk makes the most sense. The Rams may need to wait to sign him until after the game against the Green Bay Packers, but they need wide receiver depth going into the final stretch.
It’s hard to see the Rams ever making the change, but there’s an argument to be had that Shaun Dolac should be starting at linebacker. Nate Landman hasn’t played up to the contract that the Rams gave him last season. Dolac has limited snaps, but whenever he has played, he’s played well. It may be worth giving him an opportunity, especially if he can create turnovers like Landman, as he showed last week.
There’s obviously no injury report this week with the Rams on their bye week. Still, this seems like a good time to look at some of the Rams’ current injuries and see when they might be back in the lineup.

title: Rams Catch Major Break With Timing of Puka Nacua Suspension
full_text:
Throughout much of the summer, there was some speculation that Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua could get suspended for some of his off-field issues from the offseason. On Tuesday, the NFL officially announced that Nacua will be suspended for the next three games. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, he will be eligible for reinstatement on December 14.
The timing of the suspension is somewhat lucky for the Rams. Nacua will serve his suspension while on injured reserve. If everything works out, Nacua won’t miss any games with his suspension that he also wouldn’t have missed while he was hurt.
This isn't the first time that the NFL has suspended a player while they are on injured reserve. Last season Pittsburgh's Daniel Ekuale was suspended five games despite being out for the season. In 2024, Sam Williams of the Dallas Cowboys was suspended three games while being out for the year. It's certainly rare, but not unprescented.
Nacua was placed on injured reserve last week and was eligible to return for the December 20th game in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys. His minimum injured reserve absence will extend beyond his suspension. Nacua will also still be allowed at the facility for medical treatment for his knee injury that he suffered in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders.
Puka Nacua will still be allowed at the Rams team facility to rehab his knee and toe injuries during his suspension https://t.co/CKE56BjxHM
On New Year’s Eve, Nacua allegedly bit a woman on the shoulder. While Nacua hasn’t denied that he bit the woman, he has characterized the physical contact as “horseplay.” Following the incident, Nacua checked himself into a holistic rehab facility for a short stint and didn’t miss any of the Rams’ offseason program.
Nacua hasn’t been criminally charged, but the NFL doesn’t require criminal charges to suspend a player, but it doesn’t take a charge for the NFL to decide whether a player is worthy of being suspended. Late in the summer, Nacua’s civil trial was pushed to 2028.
Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Schefter reported that the NFL had been reviewing Nacua’s case. With the suspension now official, it's clear the NFL felt it had enough evidence to discipline Nacua without waiting for the civil trial. It’s also worth wondering if the NFL is close to a decision on Alaric Jackson following his off-field issues this summer. Jackson was arrested for felony domestic battery, although the charges were eventually dropped and the case was assigned to a pre-filing diversion program.
Nothing changes from the Rams' perspective. They were already planning on being without Nacua for the next three games.  Had the NFL announced the suspension earlier in the season, the Rams could have been forced to play without Nacua for three additional games. Instead, the suspension overlaps with his injury recovery.
The Rams will hope to get Davante Adams back in the lineup for the Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers. Until Nacua is back, the Rams will continue relying on Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, and Tutu Atwell.

title: Rams 2026 Rookie Report Card: Grading Every Draft Pick at the Bye Week
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have reached their bye week at 6-4 , making this a good time to evaluate their 2026 rookie class. While the Rams have gotten some contributions from their younger players, they have once again taken a patient approach.
That makes evaluating this rookie class somewhat difficult. First-round quarterback Ty Simpson has yet to be active on gameday, while second-round tight end Max Klare has seen limited opportunities. However, the Rams have gotten some surprising contributions from an undrafted free agent. With 10 games in the books, let's hand out midseason grades for the Rams' 2026 rookie class.
Through the first 10 weeks of the season, quarterback Ty Simpson has yet to be active on gameday. That shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise considering how the Rams tend to bring their rookies along slowly and Stetson Bennett's experience gives him an advantage. Still, with the Rams leading 34-6 in the fourth quarter on Sunday, it would have been nice for their rookie quarterback to get some snaps.
There’s been a lot of discussion about how the Rams should have drafted a wide receiver with the 13th overall pick, especially given the injuries at the position. However, if Simpson works out, that remains the best pick in that spot. It’s hard to grade Simpson because he hasn’t played, but he seems to be following the development path that the Rams have set for him. Grade: B
Much like Simpson, it’s hard to fairly evaluate Klare. This is the spot where a discussion of whether the Rams should have taken a wide receiver instead makes the most sense. Klare is the TE5 on the roster and hasn’t gotten a lot of playing time.
Even still, the Rams are going to have some openings at tight end going into next season. Tyler Higbee could retire and both Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are set to be free agents. When Klare played in the second half against the Los Angeles Chargers, his blocking in 13 personnel changed the game. The Rams may have a good player here, but the lack of opportunity has made this pick easier to criticize. Grade: C-
The issue with many of the Rams’ rookies is that they just haven’t played. Still, the Rams did bring Trost off of injured reserve when they were without Alaric Jackson for a game. That could signal that they are at least comfortable with him as a depth piece. With Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton out for the next few weeks, it will be interesting to see if the Rams give Trost an opportunity at guard or opt for a more experienced player while continuing to develop him at tackle. Grade: B-
It wasn’t until last week against the Arizona Cardinals that the Rams finally got a good look at CJ Daniels . Daniels played 60 percent of the snaps and had one catch for 22 yards. Matthew Stafford also targeted Daniels in the red zone. As Daniels plays more, he should get more comfortable in the offense. There was a lot to like with Daniels in training camp and the preseason. We’ll see how much the Rams use him with Puka Nacua out until mid-December. Grade: C
The Rams hit the jackpot with Wesley Bailey as an undrafted free agent. Any contribution from an undrafted free agent is positive. The fact that Bailey made the roster was impressive given how competitive it was. Bailey has two sacks and two forced fumbles this season. Last week against the Cardinals, he had an interception. With depth players like Josaiah Stewart and Desjuan Johnson, Bailey has earned a large role in the pass rush rotation. Grade: A+

title: Rams Midseason Awards: MVP, Breakout Players, and Biggest Surprises
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have reached their bye week at 6-4 following four consecutive wins. With the team getting a much-needed break, it's a good time to recognize some of its top performers. Let's hand out our Rams midseason awards, including MVP, Offensive and Defensive Player of the Year, and more.
This isn’t to say that Blake Corum wasn’t good last year. He still had a respectable 746 yards and six touchdowns. With that said, Corum has gone from being a solid complementary running back  to a player who could arguably start for other teams in the NFL . Corum leads the NFL in EPA per rush and rushing success rate. He also ranks ninth in pass-blocking via PFF.
The only real contender for Offensive Player of the Year is wide receiver Puka Nacua. Nacua ranks third in yards per route run and leads the NFL in targets per route run. While he’s been injured throughout the season, he has been the most impactful player on offense and continues to show why he’s one of the best wide receivers in the NFL.
Similar to Nacua, McDuffie has also been injured throughout the season. However, when he’s played, McDuffie has been an elite cornerback. McDuffie’s 0.51 yards per coverage snap ranks eighth while his 4.08 yards per target ranks sixth. Pro Football Focus has him as the second-highest graded cornerback in the NFL. McDuffie has been great in coverage, but his physicality in the run game has also been notable.
Cornerback target rate vs catch rate over expected: JPJ as advertised for the Cowboys pic.twitter.com/TQzc4HtS0y
The Rams haven’t gotten a lot of production out of their rookie class. Ty Simpson and Max Klare are both in red-shirt seasons while Keagen Trost and CJ Daniels have been depth pieces. However, the Rams have gotten great production out of their undrafted rookie edge rusher Wesley Bailey. Bailey turned heads during the preseason and has played a large role in the pass rush rotation. He has two sacks, had an interception last week, and also has two forced fumbles. There’s a lot to like with Bailey and it’s possible the Rams found a gem.
For the Biggest Surprise award, it’s going to be a shared award between two players. With Jaylen Watson out for the season and McDuffie dealing with injuries, the Rams have had to rely heavily on their cornerback depth. There were some concerns about Emmanuel Forbes coming into the year, but he’s played very well in a smaller role and when he’s been called on. The same can be said about Josh Wallace. Not many expected a lot out of Forbes and Wallace heading into the season, but they’ve both been important players in the secondary.
There’s certainly an argument for Alaric Jackson or Steve Avila for this award. The Rams lost to the Cardinals in a game in which Jackson missed. Avila has played at a high level this season and has certainly earned a potential contract extension. However, Coleman Shelton has been the most important player on the offensive line. His 99.1 pass-blocking efficiency via PFF ranks second among centers. He also ranks eighth among all offensive linemen in pressure rate allowed.
I’m not sure Jimmy Lake has gotten enough credit for everything that he’s done this year as the passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach. The Rams had an average pass defense last year and their cornerbacks struggled at times. This season, the Rams rank third in EPA per pass. While they upgraded at cornerback, the depth players like Forbes and Wallace have stepped up nicely. That’s also been with an inconsistent pass rush. Lake deserves a lot of credit for that improvement.
In most seasons, this would likely be Matthew Stafford. However, Stafford hasn’t played as well this season. While Williams may not rank inside the top 10 in the NFL in rushing and has taken on a smaller role in the offense than in past years, he’s been asked to do a lot more . The Rams have relied heavily on him in the passing game while also benefiting from his efficiency as a runner. Williams has remained a consistent presence that the Rams can rely on every week.

title: Exclusive: Rams RB Kyren Williams on Surprise Offensive Install, Blake Corum and Playoff Push
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have faced their share of adversity this season, but one constant has been running back Kyren Williams. As the Rams enter their bye week at 6-4 following four consecutive wins, Williams has remained an important piece in the offense.
Williams has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL, and with the Rams managing several injuries, he’s been one of the few constants. He has 616 rushing yards this season and has six rushing touchdowns.
With the help of Invisalign, we talked to Williams this week to discuss the Rams’ sudden shift to 20 personnel, how he and Blake Corum push each other to be better, and the outlook for the second half of the season.
Invisalign gives athletes and patients a choice . It’s confidence with convenience: no wires, no brackets, and clear aligners that are removable and made to keep up with your life.
“Caring for my smile has been everything. I think my smile has been something that I've always wanted to fix, and I didn't get the chance to until I was able to get into the NFL, and I got around some of my teammates who have used Invisalign treatment, and you get to see the confidence in which they walk around and smile, always smiling,” Williams said.
“It allowed me to really care about my oral health. Just being able to, you know, have that smile that I've always wanted has been, for me, a no-brainer and an easy decision to go with Invisalign.”
Williams has remained consistent throughout his career behind his preparation, including how he approaches sleep, recovery, and the routine he’s shifted and refined over four NFL seasons to stay consistent.
One of the bigger stories coming out of Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals was the Rams using pony personnel . Previously, the Rams had never used it under Sean McVay, but they used it 17 times in Week 10. The Rams did something similar last year when they had to adjust the offense to 13 personnel.
When the Rams introduced 13 personnel last year, it wasn’t something they had practiced in training camp or the offseason. The Rams introduced and installed it the week of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. That’s exactly how it played out last week against the Cardinals as well.
“We never practiced it before, but the way that Coach McVay, how his offense is, the way he sets things up, he can make anything out of anything, and he'll make it make sense,” Williams said.  “He installed 21 personnel on Monday of game week, and we didn't get to it till Wednesday, but we knew what we needed to do because of how well, systematically his playbooks are, and how his offense is, and how it all just makes sense if you just know what you're doing, right?
“Being able to, you know, have a coach like Coach McVay who's able to put you in situations and put the team in situations to go win a football game, it's been so cool, because like you said, you've seen him with 13, now you're seeing him with 21, and who knows what's coming next, but it's so cool because he's able to, you know, be creative and get in his bag with how he calls his plays.”
The Rams have opened a can of worms and should be able to continue to build on that. While pony personnel may not become their offensive identity, it may be a way for them to get their best players on the field. McVay has done well adjusting the offense and getting deep in his bag of tricks when the Rams need it. Sunday was the latest example.
Over the last two seasons, the Rams have had one of the better running back duos in the NFL. Williams and Corum are the only running back duo in the NFL this season with both players rushing for more than 500 yards.
“Yeah, I think we compete and push each other on a high level. We're  not competing against each other, but we're competing because we love the game of football, and we know that we're both capable of making big plays, we're both capable of going out there and just being exactly what we need to be for the team and the organization,” Williams said.
The running-back-by-committee approach is different from early in Williams’ career when he was “the guy.” However, it’s something that Williams has embraced, and the Rams’ running back has benefited from it.
Williams and Corum may have similar builds, but the way they run is different. While Williams is more of a downhill runner who keeps the offense on track, Corum is very good at making guys miss and bouncing plays outside.
“It's so smart, because it keeps your defense on edge,” said Williams. “You don't know what's happening, and you get to see a different person each and every single drive. I think it's allowed us to keep our offense efficient, allowed us to keep us ahead of the chains so that Coach McVay can go into his playbook and call the plays that he wants to do.”
As the Rams head into the bye week, they’ve had to face a lot of adversity through injuries and tough losses. However, they sit at 6-4 and are in the thick of the playoff hunt . It may not be exactly where they expected to be, but it’s allowed the Rams to stay connected and build character.
“The first half was just a test of our adversity, a test of our strength and our character and our culture. We had to really get connected in a way that doesn't allow us to be broken through hard situations and tough times,” Williams said. “We still just gotta stay connected and that is gonna allow us to be with the team that we've always wanted to be throughout this back half of this season, because of the things that we went through early on in the season.”
When the Rams drafted Kyren Williams in the fifth round back in 2022, a photo of him and Steven Jackson together at the Edward Jones Dome in St. Louis surfaced. Williams has since gone from fifth-round pick to an NFL starting running back with the help of small, consistent shifts.
The rookie and the legend. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/zYQYDvk2Qq
Last week, we talked to Jackson about that full-circle moment and what he took away from it and asked Williams the same.
“From that exact day, that's what inspired me to be the person I am today. That's what inspired me to work so hard to be an NFL running back. You gotta put your mind to it,” said Williams. “I was in the 5th grade, I went home, and I told my mom, like, man, I'm gonna be an NFL football player. I don't wanna be anything else.”
After meeting Jackson, Williams embraced the discipline and mindset to achieve his goal. When Jackson left the Rams in 2013, the Rams struggled to find consistency at the running back position. Over the past three seasons, Williams has eclipsed the 1,000-yard mark. He is the only Rams running back since Jackson to rush for 1,000 yards in three consecutive seasons.
Williams and Jackson may be different styles of runners due to their builds. However, some of the same passion and “heart on his sleeve” mentality that Jackson played with is also evident in Williams’ game.
“Our builds aren't the same, we're not the same, obviously, but I think the mentality and the passion that we do play with is definitely where I got that from,” Williams said. “He was so downhill, and the way that he was able to run through tackles and then continue to keep going.”

title: Rams 2027 Mock Draft: A Way-Too-Early Look at Potential Draft Targets
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are in the thick of the playoff hunt and likely won’t be thinking about the NFL Draft anytime soon. However, with the Rams on their bye week, it’s a good time to take a step back and look at what their potential roster needs are and how they could approach this offseason. Let’s get into a way-too-early 2027 Rams mock draft.
It’s possible that the Rams could be looking for a new starting tackle this offseason. While they have Alaric Jackson, he’s set to count for $24.4 million against the cap. That’s not a bad number, but Jackson has had his legal troubles and missed a game this year with a suspension for an incident in which he punched a Buffalo Bills player after the game. The Rams can save $19 million by cutting Jackson. They did draft Keagen Trost, but he may be more of a swing tackle and option on the right side. Paige is an experienced tackle with size and could develop into a starter.
Got my first look at #USC LT Elijah Paige this afternoon Big kid (6'7 319) with good movement and a natural ability to drop his weight. Pretty good recovery ability in early exposures. More skilled in pass pro than in run game. But he has makings of a starting NFL OT #FightOn pic.twitter.com/KnaCCwosf2
Some may want the Rams to address the wide receiver position earlier. They could also sign a wide receiver in free agency. At some point, the Rams need some more wide receiver depth and they’ve done well to find players at the position in the middle rounds. The Rams will likely need to replace Davante Adams and Puka Nacua is also a free agent. Wingo is arguably a first-round athlete but has aspects of his game to clean up. He could go back to school. Still, if he’s available, Wingo would be a great fit for the Rams offense.
Ryan Wingo was an absolute hero on Texas' final drive. Had 42 of #Texas ' final 58 yards Contested catch on third down Soft spot in zone on 2nd and long Forcing a missed tackle + YAC to get inside the red zone pic.twitter.com/BF1frE3PYx
It seems like we enter draft season every year with the Rams needing a linebacker and they don’t take one. The Rams have some depth with Shaun Dolac and Omar Speights has played well. However, they need a player they can develop into a key contributor in the middle of the defense. Woodson is a former safety turned linebacker, and that shows with his speed and range in coverage. He’s also a good tackler in space.
Saturday night was the 2nd week this season where I thought Alabama LB Caleb Woodson (#7) looked like one of the best LBs in the country. Excellent closing speed combined with upper level athleticism, and great size for an NFL LB (6’3” 240). pic.twitter.com/Ig6gw9LmlX
The Rams like versatile players on defense, and Bailey is a player who could compete with Jaylen McCollough to play in the box. He’s very experienced and a physical player. Additionally, the Rams need to prioritize special teams with some of their later selections. Bailey could potentially start on special teams before developing into a contributor on defense.
Illinois S Matthew Bailey (#7) brings so much versatility to the table. Bigger body (6’1 5/8”, 222 LBs) who excels against tight ends… outstanding in the box. Really strong and physical. pic.twitter.com/usw5GebWFd

title: Rams Game-by-Game Predictions: Will Los Angeles Survive a Brutal Final Stretch?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are at the midway point of their season as they sit at 6-4 heading into their bye week. As the Rams head into the second half of the season, they face the toughest schedule in the NFL. If the Rams are going to make the playoffs for a fourth consecutive season , they’ll have their work cut out for them. Let’s jump into our game-by-game predictions for the remainder of the season.
The Rams are set to play the Green Bay Packers out of the bye week on Thanksgiving Eve. Jordan Love has played at an MVP level this season, but the Packers remain extremely volatile. They have the ability to blow the doors off a team like they did to the New England Patriots two weeks ago. However, their offensive line remains an issue and the defense is inconsistent. The Packers' secondary that ranks inside the top five could make things difficul t if the Rams don’t have Davante Adams back . Prediction: Win, 24-19 (7-4)
It seems likely that the Rams split the two games out of the bye week. If they lose one, losing to the Chiefs would be the preference. The Rams will play the Chiefs close, but will come up just short in the fourth quarter. Prediction: Loss, 20-17 (7-5)
Coming out of their mini-bye, the Rams will have a rematch against the San Francisco 49ers . If the Rams can avoid getting swept by the 49ers, it would go a long way toward their playoff hopes. The extra time to prepare and get healthy should benefit the Rams. These two teams have split their season series in three of the last four years. This game will be in San Francisco, but I’ll take the Rams to win. Prediction: Win, 23-20 (8-5)
This is around the time when the Rams should be getting Puka Nacua back in the lineup healthy. The Cowboys’ defense hasn’t been very good this season. While the Cowboys could provide a challenge, the Rams should be able to come away with a win. Prediction: Win, 30-24 (9-5)
It seems odd that the Rams are playing the Seahawks in Week 16 for the first time. This will be a rematch of the NFC Championship Game from last year. While the Seahawks haven’t been as good offensively this year, their defense is still elite. This game being in Seattle is the difference. Prediction: Loss, 23-17 (9-6)
While it may not be a true mini-bye, the Rams will get some important rest heading into the final two weeks. Over the past few seasons, the Rams have owned the series with the Buccaneers. That seems unlikely to change this year. Prediction: Win, 30-20 (10-6)
Given how tight the NFC playoff race is, it’s possible that this game is for one of the final playoff spots in the NFC. This game is at SoFi Stadium and the Rams will remember how their season ended last year in Seattle. The Rams get a dominant performance from their defense to sneak into the playoffs. Prediction: Win, 27-23 (11-6)
At the end of the day, 11-6 should be enough to get the Rams into the playoffs. If they beat the Packers out of the bye week, they’ll hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over Green Bay and will have two opportunities to earn it against Seattle. The Rams may have the most difficult schedule in the NFL going forward, but at 6-4 and on a four-game win streak, they are in a good spot to make a playoff push in December.

title: Rams May Have No Choice But to Turn to Justin Dedich After Latest Injuries
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have struggled with the injury bug all season and now will be managing injuries to the offensive line. On Monday night, the team announced that center Coleman Shelton would be out 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury and backup Dylan McMahon would be placed on injured reserve.
While the Rams have been managing injuries throughout the year, they have remained relatively healthy on the offensive line. With that said, the Rams already used a return designation on Justin Dedich to start the season.
Prior to the season, the Rams placed two key depth players on the offensive line on injured reserve. Justin Dedich injured his hand in a fireworks accident and Keagen Trost hurt his hamstring in the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
When the Rams were without Alaric Jackson in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, the team took Trost off of injured reserve and added him to the active roster. However, despite some of their injuries, they have avoided doing the same with Dedich. With the added injuries to the interior of the offensive line, there has been some speculation that the Rams may look to bring Dedich to the active roster.
However, as the Rams enter the bye week, they are currently running out of potential injured reserve return designations. Teams are only allowed eight during the regular season and the Rams have already used half of those.
The Rams have used return designations on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson, and Ronnie Rivers. They are projected to use return designations on Davante Adams, Puka Nacua, and Kobie Turner as well.
That would put the Rams at seven return designations used.
With that said, the Rams already previously used a return designation on Justin Dedich to start the season. Dedich was placed on injured reserve during roster cutdowns. Had Dedich been placed on regular injured reserve, he would have been done for the season without having the option to bring him back.
By using a return designation on Dedich, the Rams had the option to bring him back during the season once he got healthy. However, they also used one of their return designations. That would mean that the Rams are already out of IR return designations as they head into the back half of the season.
At this point, one potential reason Dedich hasn't returned to the roster is the lack of available roster spots. With Shelton hurt and McMahon on injured reserve, the Rams could use some interior depth even if they stick with Bill Murray. It makes sense at this point to bring Dedich up to the active roster.
That’s also likely a reason why the Rams haven’t placed Shelton on injured reserve. He is set to be out 4-6 weeks, but if they were to place him on injured reserve, he would be done for the season.
The Rams already activated Terrance Ferguson's 21-day practice window. If he were to not be brought back after those 21 days, that would still count as a lost designation. As it stands, the Rams would need to decide if they prefer another return designation or if it’s worth bringing back Adams, Turner, and Nacua.
It’s also why designating Ronnie Rivers off of injured reserve was so significant.The Rams used a return slot on their third-string running back who primarily plays special teams. That’s a role they likely could have replaced with Jordan Waters or another available running back on another team’s practice squad.
With the Rams now dealing with injuries to both Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon, bringing back Dedich should be a priority. The Rams used a return designation on Dedich before the season specifically to keep that option available. Now that the offensive line depth is being tested, it makes little sense to continue leaving him on injured reserve if he's healthy enough to contribute.
The Rams have been forced to make difficult roster decisions throughout the season because of injuries. However, those decisions are now beginning to catch up with them. With seven games remaining and several key players still working their way back from injuries, the Rams have left themselves with little flexibility.

title: Rams Playoff Picture: What Will It Take to Make the Postseason?
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams enter their bye week at 6-4, they are right in the thick of the NFC playoff picture. While the Rams are on the outside looking in, they are in a three-way tie with the Seattle Seahawks and Green Bay Packers for the seventh seed in the NFC. That's who the Rams will be competing with in the playoff hunt.
There is still a lot of football to be played and a lot will change over the next seven games. However, the NFC remains extremely competitive. With the Minnesota Vikings trading for Kirk Cousins, a falloff doesn’t appear to be on the horizon. It’s possible that all four teams in the NFC North make the playoffs. Both teams from the NFC Championship Game last year could be left out.
According to ESPN’s model , the Rams have a 46 percent chance to make the playoffs. The Athletic’s model has the Rams at a 47 percent chance. That’s nearly a coin flip, and with matchups against the Packers and Seattle Seahawks over the next seven weeks, the Rams have an opportunity to control their own destiny.
It's not going to be easy for the Rams to make the playoffs . There's a chance that both the Seahawks and Packers go 10-7. With that said, because of the Rams' division record, the Rams likely wouldn't hold the tiebreaker. If the Rams want to safely make the playoffs, they almost need to go 11-6, which would mean a 5-2 record over the next seven games.
The Seahawks still have games against the 49ers, Panthers, and Rams on the road. They may not lose all three of those games, but those are potential losses. Home games against the Cowboys, Giants, and Rams could be challenging as well, but are winnable.
For the Rams to make the playoffs, the Packers losing as many games as possible is the best path. Jordan Love is playing at an MVP level, but they remain inconsistent on defense and have injuries on the offensive line. The Packers come out of their bye week to play the Rams on the road before facing the Bills and traveling to Chicago. They finish the season at home against the Texans and Lions. However, the Texans and Lions games are winnable and they also play the Saints and Dolphins.
However, the Rams' schedule isn't easy by any means. Going 5-2 won't be a walk in the park. It essentially means that the Rams can split their next two games, preferably beating the Packers, split their two games against the Seahawks, and win the rest of their games. The game against the Packers out of the bye week is almost a must-win and then the Rams likely have to win two out of three games between the 49ers and Seahawks. It's very possible that the Week 18 matchup between the Rams and Seahawks is for a playoff spot. They can't afford a bad game against the Cowboys or Buccaneers.
When all is said and done, it's possible we could be looking at a playoff picture like the one below. If the Rams sneak in as the seventh seed, it's going to make for a difficult path through the playoffs. The Rams may need to travel to Chicago or San Francisco in the first round, but that's the path they've built. It will take three straight road games to win, but with the current Rams' defense, it may be possible.
If there is any positive takeaway, it's that while the Rams haven't found any consistency, neither have the Seahawks or Packers. The Seahawks have a quality win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but the Packers' best wins have come against a Chicago Bears team that started Case Keenum and a very flawed New England Patriots team. It isn't much different from the Rams, who have close losses against two of the good teams they faced, while their best win came against a very flawed Philadelphia Eagles team.
As it stands, the Rams currently rank sixth in team DVOA via FTN Fantasy and the Seahawks are fifth. The Packers rank 14th. There is a clear and significant gap between the Rams and Seahawks on one side and the Packers on the other. The advanced metrics also place the Rams on the outside looking in or right with some of the best teams in the NFL.
The Rams have done a good job getting themselves back into the playoff conversation after starting 2-4. Entering the bye week, the Rams have given themselves a chance. The advanced metrics suggest this is a team capable of making noise in January. Whether or not they get that opportunity will come down to how they perform over the final seven games.
