title: Eagles vs. Steelers Week 11: Who Wins & Why in Upcoming Battle Of Pennsylvania
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Eight games remain, but in the watered-down NFC East, the Eagles are clinging to the hope that a winning run over that stretch could land them atop the division for a third straight year.
It’s a slim chance, but a chance nonetheless. To make it happen, it has to start with a win on Sunday against the 6-3 Steelers , who visit the 2-7 Eagles.
That said, here are some matchups to be mindful as the Eagles look to beat the Steelers, along with a final score prediction.
Pros don’t like losing on purpose in a violent sport where a career can end at any time, but Philly would complain about a top-five draft pick if they lose out. That doesn’t mean the players will necessarily mail it in.
As left guard Landon Dickerson so aptly put it: “You don't make it to this highest level being a quitter when things get tough. That's not a professional athlete mindset. So, no matter what the circumstance is, we're gonna come in here every day and work and try and get better.”
With the NFC East as bad as it is, you never know what might happen if the Eagles find a way to keep the competitive fires burning and start winning.
“As we see that there's still hope, there are still things that are happening in our division that still provide hope that you can get this thing turned around,” said head coach Nick Sirianni.
The Eagles rookie has struggled the past two games, particularly in pass protection. That’s not a good sign with T.J. Watt coming to town. Watt is tied for seventh in the league with 7.5 sacks and has 122.5 in his Hall of Fame career. He lines up primarily as the left-side outside linebacker, but he also moves to the right side in subpackages.
Losing Jordan Davis in a trade opened a hole in the middle of the Eagles’ defense, specifically at nose tackle. It would help if the Eagles knew who their nose tackle would be. Davis was really their only one. Whoever it is—Ty Robinson and Byron Young will likely be the main players here—will have their hands full against Frazier, one of the best centers in the game.
Frazier is ranked first among 35 qualified centers in Pro Football Focus 's overall grade (79.5), third in run blocking, and fourth in pass blocking. He hasn’t allowed a sack, with just seven pressures and three penalties on 532 offensive snaps.
The Steelers’ QB is going to be in the Hall of Fame one day, but he is 4-3 against the Eagles in the regular season. All those games came with the Packers. It will be up to the Eagles' defense to put pressure on Rodgers. The defense is coming off a six-sack performance against the Giants, though linebacker Zack Baun, who had two of those, may not play due to a back injury.
Britain Covey should return from a knee injury that cost him the previous two games. His 12.6 yards per return are second-best in the NFL, while the Steelers' punt return coverage is ranked No. 8 in punt return yardage.
On kickoffs, the Steelers are ranked 30th in covering kicks but have a very good returner in Iowa rookie Kaden Wetjen.

title: Joe Milton’s Quiet Confidence Shines As Opportunity Knocks With the Eagles
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - A month ago, Joe Milton was on the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. On Wednesday, he stood in front of reporters at the Jefferson Health Training Complex.
The QB1 of the moment in South Philly was discussing his thoughts about the legendary Aaron Rodgers as the 2-7 Eagles try to steady the ship against a 6-3 Pittsburgh team that hasn’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
When asked by Eagles On SI how closely he has followed Rodgers, Milton smiled and admitted he was watching film of the current Steelers starting QB the night before, realizing he is about to headline against one of the best to ever do it.
“Damn, I’m 26 going against A-Rod,” Milton said. “That’s A-Rod we’re talking about.”
A few minutes earlier, another NFL legend, Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, was describing Rodgers as one of the best QBs in history.
“Obviously I've seen a lot of him over the years,” Fangio said of Rodgers. “I mean, I don't think anybody can make a top five list of quarterbacks all time without him on it. Just a very pretty passer, great release, super knowledgeable, great anticipation. Just a guy I have a total lot of respect for.”
It’s a big moment and “a blessing” to square off with Rodgers, according to Milton, before the grounded part of the equation mixed in for the young QB.
That mix for Milton—wide-eyed enough to feel the moment, steady enough not to get lost in it—is the story of the signal caller’s sudden opportunity with the Eagles.
Milton has the next eight games to make a case and show whether he belongs.
When asked what’s different from Milton’s first thrown-together start before the bye against the New York Giants, the Florida native didn’t talk about his arm talent or scheme fit. He settled on confidence and how it's burgeoning.
“My confidence in knowing this offense and what these coaches and my teammates around me are instilling in me,” Milton said. “And just my reason to asking questions. I’m great at asking questions… I don’t think I can ask no lesser questions than I already do.”
Milton used the extra time the bye week provides to echo what the coaches wanted fixed—protections, blitz pickups, the verbiage.
“It was very helpful… being able to pick up the blitzes whenever they show up, and just really just understanding the verbiage that we’re pronouncing and saying here,” he said.
Milton’s opportunity with the Eagles arrived sans a training camp with the organization after having spent the first month of the season in a different city.
On Wednesday, he sounded like someone who stopped treating the playbook as a foreign language.
“I know what I need to know far as this offense… It’s not rocket science. Football is football no matter where you go,” said Milton. “Coverage is not gonna change… A play gonna be a play. And if it’s a run game, just hand it off to a running back.”
Milton doesn’t care for “Bazooka Joe,” a nickname developed as a nod to his prodigious arm strength. “I don’t like it,” he said flatly before offering up an alternative. “Rocket. Mr. Rocket.”
Why? “’Cause bazooka’s only travel so far.”
The smile came out again when he was asked about throwing to DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for the first time at practice. Both starting receivers are expected to return on Sunday after missing multiple games.
The most revealing comments came when Milton was asked about the opportunity in front of him and the conversations he’s been having with those close to him.
Adversity has taught him to stay exactly where his feet are.
“I’ve been through a lot of adversity in my life, to where if you would’ve put me in this situation six years ago, I probably would’ve been too happy for the moment,” Milton admitted. “… But being able to go through so much adversity… I’m able to just be exactly where my feet are, and just take a deep breath.”
Milton pointed to his college career, which started at Michigan and finished at Tennessee. He got hurt with the Vols and watched his roommate, Hendon Hooker, ball out and win SEC Player of the Year.
Milton mulled transferring again and decided there was no point—just learn the offense and get better.
It’s the same approach he’s using now: ask the same question twice if he has to, take the notes, let the coaches repeat the teaching point until they stick.
Pittsburgh’s defense will come with its own problems. T.J. Watt and company can get home with the best in the league.
“They are allowed to do whatever. All I know what I have to do is just move the ball. Get the ball out and just move the ball,” said Milton.
His relationship with Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has evolved quickly, something Milton attributed to Mannion’s own experience of playing the position at a high level in college at Oregon State and for many years as an NFL backup.
Eight games to prove your worth is not the longest runway, but it’s significant enough for a quarterback to make a dent in the NFL’s psyche.
Milton believes he belongs in the moment he’s been given.

title: Eagles' DeVonta Smith Gets Honest About Injury, His Return and Losses Piling Up
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – There were some changes inside the Eagles’ locker room when they returned from their bye on Wednesday.
Practice squad defensive tackle was in Jordan Davis's old locker, and along the row of offensive linemen starters, Drew Kendall had moved into Cam Jurgens’ locker and Markel Bell took up residence in Lane Johnson’s locker.
Oh, and DeVonta Smith was back at his usual locker. The receiver was holding court for reporters, too. Usually a Friday talker, Smith was available two days earlier than he usually takes questions.
He is on track to return to the field on Sunday, when the Eagles host the Pittsburgh Steelers, after missing three straight games leading up to the bye. He has been out for five of the Eagles’ nine games this season with an injured hamstring.
He took aim at reports that he could miss the rest of the season after returning from a two-game absence to play against the Carolina Panthers, then being shut down for the next three games after that.
“I was 100 percent (against Carolina),” he said. “I know someone asked Nick about shutting me down during the season. I didn't rest my (butt) this whole summer. I didn't continue to get up at 4:30 in the morning every day to not play. My focus had been getting to where I was supposed to be. I felt 100 percent for that game. I feel 100 percent now. Some things happen out of my control because I know I do everything I can do for my body to make sure I’m in tip-top shape.”
Smith was a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice but that didn’t stop Joe Milton from enjoying his return. Same with Dontayvion Wicks, who was limited but should be available on Sunday.
“Those two guys coming back, obviously helps out the team, and for me to throw to those guys today was amazing,” said the third-year quarterback who will make his second straight start. “I mean, shoot, I couldn't stop smiling for real if you ask me. It was great because those guys, they, they boost the offense more, but they also give the guys that are younger in the room some more juice.”
Smith didn’t get too much into what happened against Carolina to sideline him again. He said he was on a snap count.
“We were right at the number, it just happened to happen,” he said.
It was likely reaggravated in a game that saw him targeted 14 times by Taner McKee. Smith made seven catches for 75 yards, including a 19-yard touchdown.
That he is ready to return is all that matters now, along with his ability to stay healthy and play the final eight games. He was asked if it’s been one of the most frustrating seasons from an injury standpoint and the losses that continue to pile up.
It’s something he certainly isn’t used to having spent his career mostly healthy and without absorbing many defeats. It’s a career that has seen him become just the fifth player to ever win a national title, a Heisman Trophy, and a Super Bowl, joining Tony Dorsett, Marcus Allen, Charles Woodson, and Reggie Bush.
“The injury, it is what it is,” he said in response to the frustration question. “Nothing I can do about it. I kind of got away from frustrating myself with that. I'm doing everything I can. But from a team aspect, I mean, it is frustrating.
“At the end of the day, you know, it's not over, especially in this division. I feel like there's still a chance in our division right now. But you can only take it one week at a time, so focusing on this week. Getting the win would be the biggest thing right now; just get back on track.”

title: Eagles Add Jaydon Blue to 53-Man Roster: How the Signing Impacts the RB Room in Week 11
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles had to do something .
Coming out of their Week 10 bye , Saquon Barkley was the only active running back on Philadelphia's 53-man roster, and Barkley is banged up, as he's been playing through hamstring and back injuries in recent weeks. So, the Eagles made a move by signing back Jaydon Blue to the active roster ahead of their Week 11 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Blue previously appeared in Philadelphia's two most recent games against the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, but he didn't receive any carries in either game. That will likely change this week.
With Blue as the only active back on the roster behind Barkley, he's almost guaranteed to get his first carries of the season, as the Birds have been cautious about Barkley's workload given the injury issues that he's dealing with. The last couple of weeks it was Elijah Mitchell in the role of the other back behind Barkley, but the team clearly wants to go in a different direction with Blue this week. Meanwhile, Mitchell is back down on the practice squad.
In five games for the Dallas Cowboys last season, Blue tallied 38 carries for 129 yards and one touchdown while averaging 3.4 yards per carry. It makes sense that the Eagles would want to see if they could potentially get some similar production out of the Texas product.
Barkley may be a bit healthier than he was before the bye thanks to an extra week of rest, so it remains to be seen how many carries he'll receive against Pittsburgh. It's possible that he'll be able to handle an increased workload, but the team will still certainly want to mix things up by sending Blue in for some plays at least.
The Eagles also opened the practice window for running back Will Shipley, who has been sidelined for the past month due to a partial tear of his plantar fascia in his foot. That means that Shipley is trending towards a return to on-field action, but it's unlikely that he'll be ready by the weekend. So, Blue should have an opportunity to show his stuff.
Blue is currently on a one-year contract, which means that he'll be a free agent over the offseason. Perhaps he'll be able to use his upcoming on-field opportunity to showcase his skills in order to help himself out at the negotiating table in a few months.
If he performs well in his role, it could encourage the Eagles to consider bringing him back next season as a depth piece. He could also be auditioning for other teams, but the Eagles will have first dibs, as Blue will be an exclusive rights free agent, meaning that the Eagles will be able to dictate whether they want to bring him back, or not. How he plays in the coming week(s) could have a major impact on his football future.

title: Eagles Sticking With Sean Mannion Looks Even Bolder After Cowboys' Christian Parker Decision
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—The struggling Dallas Cowboys stripped Christian Parker of defensive play-calling duties after 10 games. The Eagles, staring at arguably an even worse offensive situation, are sticking with Sean Mannion despite a 2-7 start and seven consecutive losses.
Both are first-time coordinators and play-callers. Dallas’s defense is last in the NFL in yards allowed (393.8 per game) and rushing yards allowed (154.1), and 30th in points allowed (28.2).
After surrendering a franchise home-record 584 yards and three long touchdowns in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer handed the headset to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine while keeping the 34-year-old Parker, the former Eagles secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator, as the DC.
Parker will still run meetings and lead walkthroughs. He just no longer will call the games. Schottenheimer framed it as a win-now decision with Pettine’s experience, not a full demotion, and reiterated that Parker has a bright future.
Parker's former boss in Philadelphia, Vic Fangio, agreed with that sentiment after watching the young coach aid in the development of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean en route to a Super Bowl LIX championship with the Eagles.
“Patience is not in overabundance in today’s society, especially in the sports world, but Christian will recover from that,” Fangio insisted. “It happened to [Broncos Head Coach] Sean Payton many years ago in New York and I think he’s recovered nicely. Joe Brady, who’s the head coach at Buffalo, he got fired during the season, didn’t even get kept on. I think he’s recovered nicely, as has [Cardinals Head Coach] Mike LaFleur in Arizona. The Jets fired him during the season a couple years ago. He’s recovered nicely. Christian will do the same thing. He’ll be fine.”
The Eagles are in their own mess on the offensive side of the ball, of course. They are  last in total yards and near the bottom in scoring under Mannion .
Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, the offensive line and skill-position groups have been thinned by attrition, and the offense has struggled to generate consistent drives or an identity.
After a bye-week evaluation, however, Nick Sirianni confirmed Mannion remains the play-caller.
“Yeah,” Sirianni said when asked if Mannion is still calling the plays. “I think we had a really good bye-week process, got to evaluate a lot of things within that. You go through that — I think I put into pretty good detail how we go through things and the things that present themselves as you go through it.
“I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of the things that we want to do to move forward and to get better. Obviously, we haven’t been good enough on offense, but I like our plan of attack and our process that we went through last week.”
Pressed on what he sees beyond work ethic, Sirianni pointed to Mannion’s process: “I think he’s really smart. I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything. I think one thing I always value about him is [that] anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the detail that he has.”
Sirianni admitted “it hasn’t gone well enough for any of us this year offensively.”
“That’s coaches, that’s players,” the Eagles coach said. “We all have things that we need to do better, but I do love that approach that he has with that. As we looked at some of our schemes that he’s brought in, some of those have been really, really good. It has to be better as a whole without getting too much into the specifics of what those are. We just need to build on that.”
The contrast here is stark.
Dallas treated 10 games of historically poor defensive performance as enough to strip a first-time play-caller of the job’s most visible duty. The Eagles are showing that patience Fangio noted is in short supply and giving Mannion more runway after an even longer stretch of bottom-of-the-league offensive production.
The dichotomy between two organizations reveals different risk tolerances – patience vs. pragmatism.
The Cowboys are prioritizing experienced in-game management while the division race still theoretically exists. Philadelphia is betting on the process, the detail, and the schemes, even as the demonstrated performance to date remains among the worst in the league.

title: Joe Milton’s New Nickname Comes With the Same Eagles Challenge
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – "Bazooka Joe" might be a good name for bubble gum, but not for Eagles quarterback Joe Milton. Some might be trying to force that nickname on him, given an arm that can throw the ball out of a stadium. Don’t bother, though. He doesn’t like it.
“Bazookas only travel so far,” he said as to why he doesn't like it.
He prefers another nickname–"Mr. Rocket".
Whatever nickname he goes by won’t get him very far in his quest to finish the job as the Eagles’ starting quarterback. What matters is finding a way to win a game and snap a losing streak that has reached seven games. To break it, Milton will have to deal with a Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde defense that is third against the run but 30th against the pass. Pittsburgh is a dangerous pass-rush team with J.J. Watt and has 27 sacks, which is tied for the fifth-most in the league.
Milton had an extra week to prepare and iron out the verbiage and pass protection calls. Perhaps that will help him get sacked fewer than the seven times he was sacked by the New York Giants in his first career start two weeks ago.
He said he returned from the bye week with more confidence, thanks to some help from his teammates, passing game coordinator Parks Frazier and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion.
“I'm great at asking questions, and I ask Parks [Frazier] and Sean a lot of questions,” he said. “I don't think I can ask no lesser questions than I already do. I think I do a great job at that, so yeah, just my confidence for sure.
“Just what do I need to do on this play? What is the quarterback's job specifically on this play? That goes for every play. Like, what do you exactly want me to do on this play? And if there's anything different, just tell me now. I ask questions every day. It can be the same question. I just wanna make sure I heard correctly and I took down the right note.”
On the other side of the ball will be his quarterback counterpart, Steelers veteran Aaron Rodgers. It’s a matchup that has Milton excited, even though they won’t be going head-to-head.
“To be honest with you, to be real honest with you, I [thought about it] last night,” he said. “I was watching film last night in my living room, and I was like, ‘Damn, I'm 26 going against A-Rod.’
“Like, that's A-Rod we're talking about. It feels different. It's also a blessing just because, I mean, he’s been in the league for however long he’s been in the league. And obviously this is, what, year three for me, and being able to play against him and starting against him is re- It's a blessing for sure.”
Milton should be helped by the likely return of DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks. Smith and Wicks have each missed the previous three games due to injury. Both were listed as limited practice participants on Wednesday, which is a step in the right direction after being listed as ‘did not practice’ for the last three weeks.
Running back Saquon Barkley, who has dealt with several injuries so far this season, was a full participant.

title: 3 First-Round EDGE Prospects Eagles Must Already Have on Their 2027 NFL Draft Board
full_text:
It's never too early to start looking ahead. The Eagles sport a disappointing 2-7 record entering Week 11, making their playoff chances incredibly slim. General manager Howie Roseman's greatest opportunity to retool the roster in hopes of competing next year comes through the 2027 NFL Draft .
Nailing a first-round pick can do wonders for an organization. In Philly's case, building in the trenches is a top priority. The Eagles have averaged the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (88.6) and logged the fourth-fewest sacks (16) in the NFL this season. What used to be a strength is now a weakness.
Let's stick to defense. Here are three first-round EDGE prospects that the Eagles must already have on their 2027 NFL Draft board.
Texas' Colin Simmons has been a game-wrecker ever since arriving as a top-25 recruit in the 2024 high school class. He won the Shaun Alexander Award as the National Freshman of the Year (48 tackles and nine sacks) before earning first-team All-SEC honors in 2025 (43 tackles and 12 sacks).
Simmons' performance this season has been even more impressive. The Texas native leads the SEC with 16 tackles for loss and 10.5 sacks across eight games. He has lived in the backfield by utilizing his sensational burst to get around the edge and quick twists to discombobulate offensive linemen.
Colin. Simmons.🔥 pic.twitter.com/CmlI0RndCH
Frustrating quarterbacks isn't Simmon's only strength. He's forced eight fumbles in college and shown the speed needed to reliably drop into coverage. Snagging Simmons with a top-five pick would create a nasty foursome alongside Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, and Jalyx Hunt in Philly.
Dylan Stewart is Simmons' main competition to be the first edge rusher off the board. The South Carolina standout's traits are undeniable. Stewart uses an explosive first step to get past offensive linemen on pass-rush snaps and maintains a steady frame (6'5", 250 lbs) to close lanes in run defense.
Stewart has tallied 73 tackles, 27.5 tackles for loss, and 13.0 sacks in 31 college contests. The 21-year-old attacks quarterbacks with ferocity, ranking 18th among 869 qualified edge defenders in PFF 's pass-rush grade (90.4) this season. Stewart has also posted nine forced fumbles in his career.
Welcome back, Dylan Stewart😤 (Via: SEC Network) pic.twitter.com/U5z2P2nXql
Character concerns are holding Stewart back from being a no-doubt top-five selection. Multiple on-field infractions, ejections, and suspensions have put him in the headlines for the wrong reasons. The Eagles have made it work with challenging prospects before, though, with the most recent being Jalen Carter.
Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore is a name to keep an eye on if the Eagles grab an edge rusher with the first-round pick they acquired from the Jaguars. Traore's ceiling was considered a quality rotational pass-rusher in the NFL entering the 2026 campaign. That has since risen to an every-down disruptor .
Traore's versatility sticks out. He's recorded 33 tackles, eight tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles, and an interception in 10 games. Traore possesses the skills of an elite pass rusher and the athleticism to slide over to defensive tackle or read a quarterback's eyes in coverage.
Watch these guys work 🔥 #GoIrish ☘️ | @24era24 | @sneed_jaylen 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/6CXVg5YGTW
Traore's non-stop motor and drive to win would fit in well along a Philly defensive line hungry to return to its former dominance. He's never shy to jump on a loose ball or track down a ball-carrier at the second level. Roseman has yet to draft a player from Notre Dame since taking over as GM in 2010.

title: Joe Milton Headlines Eagles Takeaways From Sirianni's Post-Bye Presser
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Joe Milton will get another start as the Eagles’ quarterback when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit Lincoln Financial Field in a Week 11 matchup in a battle of two Pennsylvania teams .
The Eagles returned from their bye week on Wednesday, and Nick Sirianni kicked things off with his first press conference since a Zoom call on Nov. 9, a day after losing 19-11 to the New York Giants. It was their seventh straight defeat and is now the longest losing streak in the NFL after the Los Angeles ended its 11-game slide with a win on Monday night.
Asked if he will start, Sirianni said that Milton will make his second straight start.
“Yeah, he'll be in there,” said the coach. “He works extremely hard with everything; I really love his approach, like his personality.”
Milton completed 53 percent of his passes and didn’t commit a turnover or throw a touchdown, and he was sacked seven times against New York.
Sirianni said that all his coaches are returning after the bye week, including embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion .
“I think he's really smart,” the coach said about his OC. “I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything. He, you know, I think one thing I always value about him is that he thinks through things.
"Anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this,’ or, ‘I want to do that.’ But I think he just has a really good, monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, and what the downfalls are and what is the upside I think that just speaks to the detail of what he has.”
While there were no subtractions from the coaching staff, the Eagles added T.J. Paganetti as a consultant. Paganetti is on his third stint with the team. His first game was as an analyst for Chip Kelly in 2013. Later, he was Jeff Stoutland’s assistant on the offensive line in 2024 and a run-game specialist.
He left when Kellen Moore became the Saints’ head coach, but Moore fired him after a year-and-half as his run-game coordinator.
“He has been huge to the success of our football team in the past,” said Sirianni. “Really bright coach.”
The coach said he has done things like this in the past and reference Marcus Brady in 2022 and Jim Bob Cooter in 2021.
“It's just another pair of eyes that can look at it from a different lens,” he said.
Asked about defending Aaron Rodgers, Sirianni said that people have come up to him thinking he is the Steelers’ quarterback. There is a three-year age difference between the two (Sirianni is 45, and Rodgers is 42).
“People tell me I look like him and we look alike,” he said. “Someone asked me at a restaurant one time and said, ‘That, man, that's Aaron Rogers.’ But I got a lot of respect for him. He's so fun to watch throw the football, and how it comes off his hands and how he is able to get himself outta trouble, how he's able to direct the offense up there.”

title: 3 Reasons Why Eagles Have a Realistic Shot at Upsetting the Steelers in Week 11
full_text:
The Eagles will attempt to snap a seven-game losing streak when they host the Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 11. The two Pennsylvania squads haven't met head-to-head in the regular season since 2024, when Philadelphia triumphed 27-13 en route to winning Super Bowl LIX.
Pittsburgh boasts a 6-3 record and enters as a 4.5-point road favorite on FanDuel Sportsbook . Of course, that projection matters little once the players step on the field on Sunday afternoon .
Here are three reasons why the Eagles have a realistic shot at upsetting the visiting Steelers.
Running the football and protecting quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been the foundation of the Steelers' success this year. It's how they control the clock and avoid turnovers. Pittsburgh's offensive line has successfully carried out that strategy at home, but has faltered away from Acrisure Stadium.
Rodgers has been sacked just six times across four home victories. The veteran gunslinger has been sacked 20 times across five away games (2-3 record). Pittsburgh is also the only team in the NFL that has yet to score a rushing touchdown on the road. That's a big enough sample size to cause concern.
Boye Mafe gets the third sack of the game for the Bengals 🗣️ PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pHk4cKIkEs
It's worth noting that Pittsburgh left guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 that is expected to sideline him beyond Week 11. This is a matchup that Philly's Moro Ojomo, Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard can exploit. A few timely sacks could be the difference in a low-scoring duel.
Injuries have played a crucial role in Philadelphia's struggles in the passing game this season. Pro Bowl wide receiver DeVonta Smith has only appeared in four of the Eagles' nine games as he deals with a hamstring injury. Dontayvion Wicks has missed the last three weeks with an ankle injury.
Both players are trending in the right direction ahead of Week 11, though. Their returns would provide a huge boost for quarterback Joe Milton. Smith is a crisp route-runner and has the body control to haul in contested catches. Wicks provides versatility and excels at tracking deep balls through the air.
My understanding is that the #Eagles expect DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks to return after the bye or shortly thereafter and are now in a position where they want to provide younger players more opportunities… https://t.co/epaEgIwSbj
The Steelers have surrendered at least 89 yards to an opposing receiver in each of their three losses. That includes when Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase tallied 231 yards on 11 receptions in Week 10. Relying on Milton's rocket of an arm to feed Smith and Wicks the ball could be the recipe for an upset victory.
The Steelers have lost 11 straight games in Philadelphia. It's a streak that dates all the way back to 1965. The past three clashes at Lincoln Financial Field haven't been close, either. The Eagles smoked the Steelers 27-13 in 2024, crushed them 35-13 in 2022, and destroyed them 34-6 in 2016.
It's clear that Philly's passionate fan base makes its presence felt whenever the Steelers come to town. Don't expect that to change on Sunday, despite the team's losing record. The Eagles have drawn in 349,395 fans through five home games (per ESPN ). That's the 10th-highest total in the NFL.
There's one more trend to point out. Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy is well known in Philly from his time leading the Packers and Cowboys. He sports a lackluster 4-5 head-coaching record at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles will take any edge they can get in hopes of ending their skid.

title: Sean Mannion Is Officially in the Hot Seat as Eagles Return to Action in Week 11
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ bye week is over. The self-scout is done. The excuses have a shelf life, and that shelf life expires for Sean Mannion on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Mannion’s first season as Eagles offensive coordinator has been a disaster. The numbers are ugly. The process has looked messy. The results have been even worse.
Head coach Nick Sirianni—and by extension, GM Howie Roseman and owner Jeffrey Lurie—has stuck by the unconventional hire through a seven-game losing streak and a 2-7 record overall. That said, any patience that was granted in September and October due to the attrition now has to be earned in the final eight games if Mannion wants any hope of a sequel.
Getting back starting receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks , and potentially running back Will Shipley, does not require a 180-degree transformation. It does require proof that Mannion can elevate players through adversity instead of simply managing their absences.
Smith and Wicks have been the clearest examples of Mannion's rocky start. When both receivers have been healthy, the offense has at least looked like it has a pulse. When they have not, the drop-off has been steep, and the supporting cast has not been maximized.
That is the difference between a coordinator who is scheme-centric and one who gets the most out of what is available on a given Sunday.
Smith remains elite when healthy and is the most reliable separator on the roster; Wicks has shown he can win with his route running. Reintegrating both should make the passing game less one-dimensional, even with the inexperienced Joe Milton at the controls.
If the same late-to-the-line, overloaded-at-the-snap issues that have plagued the unit persist even with those two back, you can rest assured the problem is not solely personnel.
Shipley’s potential return also adds another layer. He is not Saquon Barkley, but he is a legitimate complementary back who can handle a share of the load and contribute to the passing game.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The Eagles have been thin at running back for large stretches of this season. Adding a functional piece behind Barkley should help. It also gives Mannion another chance to show he can build a more balanced attack rather than leaning on whatever is least injured against Pittsburgh.
The bye week gave the staff time to self-scout without the immediate pressure of a game plan. The Eagles also added old friend T.J. Paganetti , a run-game specialist, as a consultant on Monday. Those levers have to prove to be useful.
Any film sessions and schematic adjustments only matter if they show up in how the offense performs against the Steelers, an AFC playoff contender that hasn’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
The Eagles don’t need Mannion to suddenly become the next Sean McVay. They do need him to demonstrate that his system can still function when key pieces are available, that the communication issues can be cleaned up, and that available players can be put in positions to succeed rather than simply asked to survive.
It’s esoteric and somewhat intangible, but that’s the bar for continued patience. Not a complete overhaul. Not a sudden jump into the top half of the league in scoring. Just clear evidence that the coordinator can raise the level of the players he has when they are actually on the field.
If that evidence does not appear soon, the conversation around the rest of the season will shift from “give Mannion time” to speculation about the next OC.
The bye was the intermission after a disastrous first act. Sunday is Mannion's first opportunity to prove that lessons were learned during the adversity.

title: Seven Former Steelers Players Selected in 2027 UFL Draft
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Multiple former Pittsburgh Steelers were selected in the recent 2027 UFL Draft, giving them their next chance to make it in professional football.
While their opportunities with the Steelers didn't pan out, seven players who recently spent time in Pittsburgh are set to make their way to the spring league, which kicks off their upcoming season in March of 2027.
A few of these names will be very familiar to the Steelers and their fanbase, but the rest are names that spent brief moments here during preseason or training camp.
Beanie Bishop was the definition of a flash in the pan with the Steelers. Originally undrafted out of West Virginia University, Bishop signed with the franchise as a free agent ahead of the 2024 training camp and preseason.
Despite little fanfare upon his arrival, Bishop earned a spot on the active roster and exceeded expectations. He appeared in 17 games as a rookie, making 45 total tackles and 0.5 sacks.
What was most impressive, however, was his playmaking ability as a first-year player. Bishop defended seven passes and recorded four interceptions, two of which came off of current Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
After that breakout rookie year, Bishop's NFL career quieted. He failed to make the Steelers' roster the following season, and he bounced around the league looking for a home.
Now, he gets his next chance with the St. Louis Battlehawks, who made him the 29th overall pick in the recent draft.
Another round down 💪 #UFLDraft pic.twitter.com/qmHqVVlHTS
At this most recent training camp, a pair of defensive backs stood out. Those players were Devan Boykin and Jack Henderson, and it seems the UFL agreed, as both were taken in the recent draft.
Boykin was a member of the Indiana Hoosiers' 2025 NCAA National Championship team before signing with the Steelers as an undrafted free agent. He appeared in all three games of the preseason, playing mostly as a nickel corner.
Henderson is a long and rangy safety who displayed an impressive level of athleticism during this past preseason. He spent two preseasons with the Steelers after finishing his collegiate career at the University of Florida. He couldn't quite displace rookie seventh-rounder Robert Spears-Jennings, however, and that cost him a spot in the organization.
For all of the seven players drafted by UFL organizations, it's a golden opportunity. It provides the chance to show that they are the type of players many NFL franchises wish they could be, and it might land one or several of them another chance in the top professional league in the world.

title: Aaron Rodgers' Roster Comments Should Send Message to Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a few issues on their team, but wide receiver sits right at the top.
DK Metcalf has underperformed and the team is hoping that the r eturn of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson will be enough to help this group reach the level it needs to. If not, they'll keep looking at their internal options, with Max Hurleman being the name that keeps coming up.
Hurleman was mentioned by both head coach Mike McCarthy, quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Metcalf himself as an option to help the receiver core. The second-year player out of Notre Dame is on their practice squad and just returned from the practice squad IR.
And once again, Rodgers is making a pitch for him.
"I'd love to see Max [Hurleman] get some opportunities on special teams," Rodgers said during his weekly press conference. "Again, that's above my pay grade, though."
Hurleman is an explosive athlete who was the Fighting Irish's punt returner during his final college season. While also a reliable pass-catcher and someone who has experience playing running back and cornerback as well, he could be a contributor for Pittsburgh in multiple ways.
But Rodgers pointing out special teams is interesting. The Steelers have one of the worst kick and punt return units in the National Football League, and rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen has been a pretty big disappointment in his first season.
Hurleman may be the answer they're looking for, or at least another direction the team can look to help improve the group.
On a weekly basis, McCarthy seems to discuss the poor performance of the special teams unit, and special teams coordinator Danny Crossman doesn't have much of an answer for Wetjen other than continuing to get more comfortable.
The second-year UDFA has shone in two preseasons and training camps, and may be worthy of a shot on the 53-man roster. Even McCarthy admitted that.
If it also helps the Steelers get into better field position before the offense takes the field, why not test out the move? It almost makes too much sense for Pittsburgh to give it a shot.
Wetjen may be the future of the return position, but he's not making the plays a fourth-round returner needs to make. Right now, he's one of the big problems this team needs to solve before the postseason.
And their answer may have just came back from injury and is waiting on the p-squad.

title: Steelers Offense Must Lean on Two Names Against Eagles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' rushing attack disappeared in Week 10. The Cincinnati Bengals decimated the Steelers in their AFC North showdown, defeating them by a final score of 38-18.
The Steelers were outplayed in every facet of the game, but the most disappointing part was Pittsburgh's inability to move the ball on the ground. The Steelers finished Week 10 with 102 rushing yards, but that doesn't tell the full story.
It was a forgettable performance all-around, but in order to find any success on offense, they must reignite the running game. Thankfully, their Week 11 opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles, presents a favorable opportunity for the Steelers to get back on track.
Needing a win, the Steelers have to rely on their top duo of Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren, no matter what.
The lack of a run game in Week 10 can be attributed to the fact that the Steelers were down early. After the Bengals jumped out to a 24-3 lead at halftime, the offense had little choice but to abandon the run game in a comeback effort.
Still, whenever the Steelers went back to the rushing game, it proved unproductive. Lew Nichols led the team with 43 rushing yards, but that was all gained in garbage time. The top two running backs, Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren, combined for 41 total rushing yards on just 12 carries and 34 receiving yards on seven receptions.
But I would argue the Steelers abandoned the run game too early against the Bengals. Even facing a three-touchdown deficit, the Steelers' only productive piece of their offense during the season is their run game. Their best players all season long have been Jaylen Warren and the offensive line. So, when the team went down, it made no sense to me that their comeback efforts were so reliant on passing the ball.
Sure, the running game wasn't bearing any fruit, but it produced just 43 fewer yards than the passing game did.
Thankfully for the Steelers, the Eagles are a far inferior team compared to the red-hot Bengals. It's been a season of disarray in Philadelphia, with starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season, plus the trading away of multiple starters on both sides of the ball.
That's led to a 2-7 record and one of the NFL's worst defenses. The Eagles are allowing an average of 353.4 total yards per game and 126.1 rushing yards. Both figures rank 25th in the NFL. They are also allowing 24.6 points per game, ranking 19th in the league so far.
The Eagles' defense is especially vulnerable against the Steelers' rushing attack after they moved defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a pair of draft picks ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline.
Down one of their most impactful defensive players, Dowdle and Warren must be the focal point of Pittsburgh's offense in Week 11. The pair combined for just 12 carries in Week 10, and that number has to be doubled against the Eagles.
The Steelers have to get their top duo more involved on offense. No matter what happens or how the game plays out, the Steelers absolutely cannot abandon the running game again.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Antonio Brown Shares Advice for Steelers' DK Metcalf
full_text:
Antonio Brown offered some advice to Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf as he continues to run into issues with drops.
During an appearance on "The Matchup" podcast with former Steelers teammate Emmanuel Sanders and Chris Harris Jr., Brown stated that Metcalf needs to start going back to the ball while improving his concentration.
"I see DK Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to the ball. Take your nose to the ball," Brown said . "I feel like guys gotta be more confident taking their nose to the ball. You gotta take your nose to the ball first, and your eyes gotta catch it. It's eyes, nose hands.
"Most of these guys, they just use hands, no eyes. You gotta have the concentration. You gotta be focused to be a good pass catcher."
"I see D.K. Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to ball. Take your nose to the ball." @AB84 on WR drops in @NFL With @ChrisHarrisJr & @ESanders_10 on 'The Matchup' https://t.co/wK4t72rMEb pic.twitter.com/48O6vrYwlr
The Steelers can't afford for their No. 1 wide receiver, who also has three seasons left on a four-year deal worth $132 million, to keep dropping passes.
The reality of the situation, though, is that Metcalf's hands have always been inconsistent. He posted a combined 20 drops during his first two seasons in the NFL (2019 & 2020) with the Seattle Seahawks, per Pro Football Focus , before settling in and having 18 over his final four campaigns with the team.
Metcalf then finished with six drops in his first season with Pittsburgh in 2025 after arriving in a trade from Seattle.
Now, however, he has six drops through nine games, which is the second-most among wide receivers, behind only Matthew Golden of the Green Bay Packers with 11 ( per PFF ). That means Metcalf is on pace for 11 drops in 2026, which would tie his career-high from 2020.
If he were producing at a star level, Pittsburgh could at least put up with a drop here and there. That's not the case, though, nor is it close to it.
Despite being tied for the 18th-most targets in the league with 71, which is also the most for any Steeler this season, Metcalf has just 432 yards and has an incredibly poor catch rate of 49.29 percent to go with it.
To Brown's point, Metcalf has some work to do in terms of refining his technique and building on his concentration.
There are times when he lets the ball travel too deep instead of extending his arms, which leads to drops such as the one he had down the field in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns.
On the flip side, there are also instances where Metcalf doesn't track the ball into his hands and starts turning upfield before he has it secured.
At this point, Metcalf might just need a reset. Whether that's having his role simplified or playing less snaps once Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are officially back from the reserve/injured list, he can't continue to go about his business like usual until he fixes his woes.
Metcalf isn't unsalvageable, nor is his 2026 campaign, but there's a lot of work to do over the final eight games of the regular season.

title: Steelers Waive WR After Wilson, Pittman Return to Practice
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are parting ways with a veteran wide receiver.
Ahead of their Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Steelers announced that they have waived Brandon Smith from the 53-man roster.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) both having their 21-day practice windows opened this week while on the reserve/injured list, a bit of a roster crunch is coming at receiver for Pittsburgh. As a result, Smith is now on his way out.
The 27-year-old signed to the 53-man roster just before the Steelers took on the Cleveland Browns in Week 8 after the team exhausted all three of his elevations from the practice squad this season.
Smith's first time on the game day roster, which came by way of a practice squad elevation, was back in Week 5 vs. the Indianapolis Colts after Pittman Jr. landed on IR.
He was then elevated again in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after Wilson was placed on IR, and his third elevation was in Paris vs. the New Orleans Saints during Week 7.
Smith, who was a standout during training camp, has played in a total of five games for Pittsburgh this season. Over that span, he recorded four catches for 39 catches over 154 offensive snaps.
Smith will likely return to the practice squad when and if he clears waivers, though he can no longer be elevated and thus would have to re-sign to the 53-man roster somewhere down the line in order to play for Pittsburgh again during the regular season.
After placing Mason McCormick (ankle) on IR earlier this week in addition to waiving Smith, the Steelers now have two open 53-man roster spots.
As a result, Wilson and/or Pittman Jr. could theoretically be back on the roster in time to play against the Eagles. The same goes for Gennings Dunker (knee), whose own 21-day practice window was opened this week as well.
It's a safe bet that at least one of Wilson or Pittman Jr. will suit up vs. Philadelphia and take Smith's spot. Dunker would appear to have a good shot of making his return this weekend too and serve as the top backup guard behind starters Spencer Anderson and Brock Hoffman, though Pittsburgh could also elevate Doug Nester and/or Steven Jones from the practice squad and have them fill a depth role.
Because the Steelers will ultimately need to free up three spots in order to accommodate the returns of Wilson, Pittman Jr. and Dunker, another 53-man roster move will be required.

title: Steelers’ Nick Herbig Becoming Growing Concern Before Eagles Game
full_text:
There's some concern for the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers EDGE rusher Nick Herbig for the team's Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
On the Steelers ' second injury report of the week following practice on November 19, Herbig was listed as a non-participant with a hip/ribs injury.
The 24-year-old has now missed each of Pittsburgh's first two practice sessions this week, and with game designations set to come out on November 20, Herbig's status bears watching as the team gets ready to head over to Philadelphia.
Though he finished out the remainder of the contest and thus was not ruled out, Herbig did go down with an apparent injury during the first half of the Steelers ' 38-18 blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10.
Herbig got banged up as he was attempting to tackle Bengals running back Samaje Perine from behind while Patrick Queen hit him high.
From there, Herbig headed to Pittsburgh's sideline and was checked out by the team's trainers before reentering the game shortly after.
He logged 40 total snaps vs. Cincinnati, with 33 coming on defense and seven on special teams (per Pro Football Focus ) while posting a single tackle and a pressure.
Herbig, despite a fruitless outing against the Bengals, had really started to kick things into gear as a pass rusher ahead of the Steelers' Week 9 bye.
He logged five pressures ( per PFF ) and a sack in the team's Week 8 victory over the Cleveland Browns after having finished with five pressures and a pair of sacks in a Week 6 comeback win on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
If Herbig isn't active against the Eagles, T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Jack Sawyer would all be in line to play more snaps for Pittsburgh.
None of the Steelers' EDGE rushers have missed any games up to this point in the season, making it tough to pinpoint what the workload would look like in the event that Herbig doesn't suit up this week.
Herbig has logged an average of 34 defensive snaps per game this season, with 29 of those coming along the defensive line according to PFF's data.
Watt and Highsmith would likely see a larger increase in their snap count over Sawyer, but the latter has been on the field for 32 percent of Pittsburgh's defensive reps this season (up from 25 percent in 2025, per Pro Football Reference ) and thus should also earn a few more opportunities if Herbig isn't out there against the Eagles.

title: Steelers’ Spencer Anderson Playing for More Than Redemption
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers received some bad news coupled with a bit of good news following their Week 10 loss.
The Steelers lost starting left guard Mason McCormick to an ankle injury. The third-year lineman had a cast placed on his ankle and was carted off the field, forcing him out of the game and out of the lineup for an extended period.
The good news, however, is that the Steelers don't expect to lose McCormick for the entire season. According to a recent update from Ian Rapoport , McCormick will not require surgery on his injured ankle and could return for the postseason. That means backup lineman Spencer Anderson will fill in until McCormick is able to go again.
It's a huge opportunity for Anderson. The former seventh-round pick has played a series of roles during his time in Pittsburgh, but now he has a chance to keep the offensive line afloat down the stretch and earn a second contract with the Steelers.
This will be the second time this season and the third season in a row that the Steelers turn to Anderson in a starting role. He began the 2026 campaign as the team's right guard. He dealt with a bone chip in his leg and still managed to earn first-team reps ahead of the regular season schedule.
After two weeks, however, the Steelers made a switch. They swapped out Anderson and right tackle Dylan Cook for veteran Brock Hoffman and rookie Max Iheanachor. The switch worked, igniting the team's run game and giving them their best five-man unit.
Despite the demotion, Anderson remained a key piece of the offensive line. As the swing tackle and extra offensive linemen in heavy sets, he's continued to help fuel the run game. That's helped the Steelers produce an average of 116.1 rushing yards per game, the 15th-most in the NFL.
Now, he gets the chance to move back to the position where he played nearly 200 snaps during the 2025 season, according to PFF , and it's clear that head coach Mike McCarthy fully trusts him at any position along the offensive line.
"Spencer’s, you know, he’s just a 360 football player," he said at his weekly press conference . "I mean, just to coming in here to see to see him play the different positions.  You know, last year, obviously compete. You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guards. Played all the different, you know, combinations of the tight ends on the ball and off the ball for us too, caught a few routes last week in practice. So I mean, he’s a he’s a gifted football player, this will be his opportunity."
The Steelers clearly value Anderson. Two different coaching staffs have expressed the same sentiment regarding him, and it's not a coincidence that he is the player they turn to in a pinch.
While that is true, it's also true that the last time he was given a starting opportunity, he needed to be replaced.
Now, that can be forgotten, and Anderson can earn a new contract by limiting the damage from McCormick's absence. The best way for him to do that is to help keep this run game going.
That starts with Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Running back Jaylen Warren was rendered useless in Week 10, and the loss of McCormick and game circumstances forced the Steelers away from their bread and butter on offense.
Against the Eagles and seeking a rebounding victory, the Steelers have to establish the run. If Anderson leads that charge, bringing a nasty demeanor and winning at the point of attack, the ground game can lead the way.
It can't end there. While the Steelers hope McCormick returns before the end of the season, Anderson might have to play the rest of the year at left guard. The Steelers need a steady anchor to fill in for McCormick. It's an unenviable and difficult task, but I believe Anderson has the skill and determination to do it.
If he does that, or plays well enough, it sends a clear message to the Steelers: Anderson is a crucial part of this roster for the second half of the regular season and in the years to come.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Incentives Check-In: Aaron Rodgers or Bust
full_text:
Unlike a majority of NFL teams, the Pittsburgh Steelers often don't include incentives in their contracts.
Quarterbacks are seemingly the exception to that rule for the Steelers, however, as the only two members of the roster chasing incentives throughout the remainder of the 2026 campaign are Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph (according to Spotrac ).
With that, let's dive into what those incentives look like for both signal callers.
After a 38-18 loss at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10 that still wasn't as close as the final score makes it appear, it's hard to be optimistic about the prospects of Pittsburgh's season moving forward.
Regardless, though, the Steelers are still sitting at 6-3 and would be the No. 6 seed in the AFC as the conference's second Wild Card team if the campaign were to end today.
Considering it is a game-and-a-half up on the New England Patriots, who are the first team out of the playoff field at the moment and are due to lose quarterback Drake Maye for an extended period of time because of an ankle injury, Pittsburgh has to feel pretty good about its chances of making the postseason for a fourth-straight year.
In terms of Rodgers' incentives on his one-year deal that carries a base salary of $22.5 million, he'd earn $625,000 for each playoff win the Steelers pick up as long as he also plays 75 percent of the team's offensive snaps this season. The 42-year-old is a lock to hit that number barring an injury, as he's been on the field for 96.8 percent of the reps thus far.
That means the 42-year-old can earn up to $2.5 million in incentives, though reaching that amount would require winning Super Bowl LXI.
While taking home the Lombardi Trophy feels far-fetched at best for Pittsburgh, it's not out of the realm of possibility that Rodgers could help lead the team to a victory in the Wild Card round, snap the franchise's seven-game postseason losing streak and make an extra $625,000 in the process before retiring.
Rudolph's two-year, $7.5 million deal that he signed to return to the Steelers in March 2025 included $500,000 in incentives for both the 2025 and 2026 campaigns, which comes out to a potential total of $1 million.
In order to reach those incentives, however, Rudolph would've had to play 50 percent of Pittsburgh's offensive snaps while the team also makes the playoffs.
He missed the mark by a wide margin last season, logging only 11 percent of the Steelers' reps, and he's well on his way to meeting that same fate in 2026, considering he's played 3.2 percent of the snaps up to this point.
Rudolph is set to become a free agent next offseason, but with Rodgers set to hang up his spikes, it's possible that Pittsburgh could look to bring the former back and have him compete for the starting job in 2027 with the likes of Will Howard and Drew Allar.

title: Former Steelers Player Wants DK Metcalf Benched
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have not gotten enough out of wide receiver DK Metcalf. The team's "star" wide receiver has struggled for most of the season, and since Pittsburgh lost Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. to injuries, he has not stepped up in ways the team needs him to.
Against the Cincinnati Bengals, Metcalf has zero receptions for zero yards before the fourth quarter. That mark seems to be a trend for Metcalf, who has collected a good chunk of his stats in the final few minutes of games, while doing very little before the fourth quarter.
Fans aren't happy with Metcalf. And with his $150 million contract that the Steelers doubled down on in the offseason by restructuring it, it's becoming a question of whether or not Metcalf's play or his paycheck is what's keeping him on the field.
Former offensive lineman Trai Essex says that shouldn't matter. And he wants to see Metcalf moved down the depth chart.
"Find out a way to motivate DK to get the hell better," Essex said on his podcast 'The Snap Count.' “There’s no excuses at this point. We can’t coddle him and be like, ‘We’re not doing enough for you. We’re not running enough slants for you. We’re not running enough hitches for you.’ At some point, if you’re making $30-plus million, you need to figure it out or sit down until you do. … I think the most clear thing you can do and send a message to the team in that you are holding each and every position accountable is to bench DK and bring somebody else in."
That motivation may help. Metcalf has not played well, but the Steelers' solution has continued to be force feeding him the ball through screen passes and fades. Neither of which have worked.
Instead, maybe they should try a different approach.
Pittsburgh now has weapons at the wideout position. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson returned to practice and could play as early as Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Rookie Germie Bernard and veteran Brandon Smith are still around, and Ben Skowronek is available if needed.
So, if the Steelers wanted to look at others to step up when Metcalf cannot, they can finally do so without having to put players with little experience on the field.
Will they? Probably not. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy have continued to praise Metcalf and stand behind him. Rodgers seems determined to force him the football more than any other weapon on the field.
So, don't expect them to listen to Essex. But maybe they should.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: GTA VI Release Date: Where Steelers Were When GTA V Dropped
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and the entire world of football will have to battle for attention with Grand Theft Auto 6 this weekend.
GTA 6, which is made by Rockstar Games and will release on November 19, is among the most anticipated video games in recent memory, if not all-time. According to Sensor Tower , it has already sold just under 16 million copies and generated over $1.5 billion in revenue.
A major reason why there's so much hype surrounding GTA 6 is the fact that it's been 13 years since its predecessor, GTA 5, was put out in the fall of 2013.
Considering just how much of a phenomenon GTA 6 is, we thought it was worth looking back on the release of GTA 5 and where the Steelers stood at that moment in history.
While some might think the 2026 Steelers have it bad as GTA 6 comes out after losing 38-18 to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, this year's team doesn't hold a candle to the 2013 squad in that regard.
When GTA 5 was released on September 17 of that year, Pittsburgh was in the midst of its worst start to a season during the 21st century.
After collapsing down the stretch of the 2012 campaign, opening 6-3 before finishing 8-8 and missing the postseason for just the second time since 2007, the Steelers lost each of their first four games in 2013 and began the year at 0-4.
The Steelers did bounce back from there, going 8-4 to close out the season and finish 8-8, but it wasn't enough to make it into the playoff field in the AFC.
Antonio Brown was named an All-Pro for the first time in his career, earning second-team honors while finishing with 1,499 yards and eight touchdowns.
2013 was also the last time Troy Polamalu was named a Pro Bowler before later retiring following the 2014 campaign.
Furthermore, Cam Heyward is the only player left on Pittsburgh's current roster from the 2013 team. He started 13 of 16 games that year and recorded 59 tackles with 5.0 sacks.
Outside of Heyward, the only other member of the 2026 Steelers who was playing in the NFL during the 2013 campaign was Aaron Rodgers .
Rodgers was in the middle of his ninth season with the Green Bay Packers at the time and his eighth with Mike McCarthy as his head coach.
The future Hall of Famer only played in nine games, however, after breaking his left collarbone that November. Over that span, he threw for 2,536 yards, 17 touchdowns and six interceptions.
Only a few current Steelers were even playing collegiately when GTA V came out, as Chris Boswell was in his final season at Rice in 2013 while Jalen Ramsey (Florida State) and T.J. Watt (Wisconsin) were true freshmen while Robert Tonyan was a redshirt freshman quarterback at Indiana State.

title: Why Seahawks OC Brian Fleury is Fighting for His Job
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is in his first season with the team , and it hasn't gone exactly as planned.
After spending seven seasons on the coaching staff for the San Francisco 49ers, Fleury was given a promotion to become the Seahawks' offensive coordinator , but the numbers have shown that he hasn't quite been ready for the job. Here are the reasons why the Seahawks could keep Fleury and fire him as well.
The Seahawks have had four offensive coordinators in the last four years, and it could become five if they choose to fire Fleury. He isn't likely going to be a head coach in 2027, so the only reason he wouldn't be back with the Seahawks is if they fired him.
As a team, the Seahawks are averaging 333.2 yards per game, which ranks 15th in the league, right in the middle of the pack. They're also scoring 22.3 points per game, which ranks 17th in the league. The numbers aren't at the standard of a Super Bowl contender, but they also aren't completely awful either.
One could also make the argument that the Seahawks' offensive troubles have not been linked to the play calling, but rather to the personnel. The team has not been fully healthy in the backfield until the past few weeks, and the quarterback situation has been a work in progress with Drew Lock and Sam Darnold splitting time under center.
If the Seahawks fail to reach their goals this season, they are going to have to make some kind of change or pivot in the offseason. While Fleury may deserve a second chance to correct some of his mistakes, the Seahawks might not have the time to give him that opportunity.
They may look for a different voice in the league that could elicit the results they got when Klint Kubiak was the offensive coordinator in 2025.
If they feel there is someone better suited for the role other than Fleury, the team might take those actions this offseason, as opposed to waiting another year or two for things to get better. Time is of the essence in Seattle's Super Bowl window, and they can't waste it.

title: 3 Most Disappointing Seahawks Players Entering the Bye Week
full_text:
At 6-4 , the Seattle Seahawks are still in good shape to make a run at the playoffs, but it's still not an ideal record for them. The defending champs have already lost more games this year than they did in 2025 when they went 14-3 and secured the No. 1 seed in the NFC.
Of course, expecting the same record might have been foolish. As Super Bowl winners , the Seahawks entered 2026 with a target on their backs. They also have a more difficult schedule as the reigning NFC West champions.
Still, they have the talent to win every week, making their current record somewhat disappointing. On that note, here's a look at three individuals who have contributed to the up-and-down season and are considered the biggest disappointments entering the bye week.
Looking for a spark at the 2025 deadline, the Seahawks made a trade with the New Orleans Saints to bring over receiver and return man Rashid Shaheed. He had just 188 yards on 15 receptions in nine games with Seattle, but scored two touchdowns on special teams.
He flashed enough to give the Seahawks hope that he could be a key piece of the puzzle going forward, leading to a three-year, $51 million extension . Through 10 games, he has 17 receptions for 171 yards with no touchdowns. Making matters worse, he hasn't been explosive on returns, averaging 10.3 yards per punt return and 27.0 on kickoffs, both down from 2025. Seattle bet big in Shaheed, and so far, that gamble hasn't paid off.
Seattle made the bold move to let Kenneth Walker leave in free agency, and they replaced him with rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price. Injuries have slowed him down as Price has missed four games. He has yet to break out this season, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and has just 208 yards. He did score his first career touchdown in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders, which hopefully will give him a boost in the second half, but as of now, he hasn't delivered as expected.
As we enter the bye week, there's no player who has been more of a disappointment for Seattle than quarterback Sam Darnold. After a strong 2025 campaign, Darnold has struggled with accuracy and ball protection. His completion percentage dropped from 67.7 to 60.2 and he has 10 touchdowns against nine interceptions.
Darnold has missed three games due to injury, and is just 3-4 as the starter. Seattle is 3-0 with Drew Lock playing in place of him, which has led to questions about Darnold's job security. He proved in 2025 that he can play at an incredibly high level, and needs to show he can bounce back once the bye week ends.

title: 3 Seahawks Fighting for Next Contract
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are at the bye week , looking ahead to their final seven games of the season.
The team has over 20 players expected to hit free agency at the end of the season , some of whom Seattle will want to keep to continue their winning trends. Here's a look at three players who are likely on the team's radar to try and return for next season.
Quenton Nelson is the new kid on the block after being acquired in a trade ahead of the deadline with the Indianapolis Colts. It remains to be seen if Nelson would agree to a long-term extension with the Seahawks, but Seattle would certainly entertain the idea if it was possible. Nelson is 30 years old and still has a lot of high-level football ahead of him as one of the top interior linemen in the league.
The Seahawks would consider signing him to a new deal if the price was right, but the value of his new deal will likely be determined by how he performs coming off this injury in the final seven games of the year.
Myers has been the Seahawks' kicker for every game since 2019, but his contract is up at the end of the year. So far this season, Myers has only missed three field goals, one of which came against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10.
Myers can be one of the top kickers in the league when he's performing at his best, so the team will likely want to renegotiate a new deal with him, depending on how he performs in the last half of the season. Myers could sign a deal that keeps him in Seattle for the remainder of his career, so there should be interest on both sides to get something done.
Sundell is in a different boat than the others as an exclusive rights free agent. This means Seattle will be the only team that can negotiate with him, and they will likely keep him, considering he has played every snap this season as the team's starting center.
Sundell could earn up to $5 million on his next contract, so it is in his best interest to put his best football in front of him so that he can be rewarded with a handsome payday in the offseason.

title: Positions the Seahawks Can Upgrade in the 2027 or 2028 NFL Draft
full_text:
There are plenty of games left for the Seattle Seahawks (6-4), who are just on the outside of the NFC playoffs. The Seahawks have been dealing along the roster since the season started , but it’s been developing as the season progressed. Seattle is still competing for a playoff spot, but the front office is creating scenarios for building their roster.
​The 2027 NFL Draft will give the Seahawks several opportunities to build their roster. The biggest focus will be on the front office to address the biggest weaknesses on the roster or problems that will be coming after next season. This 2027 Draft possesses a lot of talented players that the Seahawks will address with their biggest position needs. The 2028 NFL Draft also has a lot of potential.
​The Seahawks didn’t acquire an edge rusher in the 2026 NFL Draft or the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline. After this season, Derick Hall is the only rusher returning to the team for the 2027 season. This might be an indication that the Seahawks might wait until the draft to make a move for a franchise edge rusher.
While the pass rush pressure is high, the Dark Side Defense doesn’t possess high sack numbers . If there is a position for general manager John Schneifer to select in the first round of the 2027 Draft, it would be for an edge rusher.
​The Seahawks possess the league’s best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba , but they are limited outside of him. Cooper Kupp is running out of steam, Rashid Shahed is an explosive gadget receiver, and second-year receiver Tory Horton hasn’t stepped up. Quarterback Sam Darnold or Drew Lock needs another young receiver to be open when they are escaping the pocket. The wide receiver position would be an area that the Seahawks could address within the first three rounds.
​This season raised a lot of key concerns about the interior defensive line moving forward. Veteran defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili have gone through injuries . There is still a lot of information and concern over Williams’ stinger injury.
Their other veteran in Jarran Reed, might have been on the trade block, but has one year left on his deal. Finally, Rylie Mills has been good, but not great in his first full season. A day-two pick in the 2027 or 2028 Draft might have to be accessed on a reliable, young defensive tackle opposite Byron Murphy II.
​Here is the wildcard position. The Seahawks might trust Darnold or Lock moving forward after this season with a new contract. If the Seahawks take this route, then a day three pick should be accessed.
If, however, Seattle’s front office is ready for a new franchise quarterback in 2027 or beyond, then a day one or early day two pick would have to be made for a young quarterback in the 2027 draft. If the Seahawks bring back Darnold next season without an extension, then they should be at the front of the quarterback-needy teams for the 2028 NFL Draft.

title: Six Players the Seahawks Should Note from College Football Week 11
full_text:
Throughout the College Football Season, we’ll be monitoring top performers who might be available to the Seattle Seahawks in the 2027 draft . We’ll focus on players that play positions that are likely, or at least possibly, going to be one the team considers going after. This should give us a chance to spotlight players that the team targets well ahead of time.
The quarterback play this week was especially poor, so I’m skipping that crew in favor of someone who is not going to be in this class. Raiola will be one of the top prospects next season, and this last game showed why, as he helped get Oregon back into the playoff conversation with 341 yards and 4 touchdowns. He’s going places.
An intriguing Michigan Wolverine running back last year, Haynes transferred to Georgia Tech and has been pretty quiet this season so far. But I still think his style could fit the Seattle offense. This last week, the Yellow Jackets upset the Clemson Tigers on Haynes’s back, with 116 yards and a touchdown on the ground and a 13-yard catch as well.
Emphasis on almost. Sometimes there’s nothing you can do when your defense allows 42 points to the Buffaloes. Overmyer is exempt from any blame, after reeling in 9 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. You won’t find many tight end games this season better than that. With any luck, he can be had late in day three as well.
Princely’s younger brother is not going to be the black sheep brother. He may end up about as ballyhooed of a prospect when all is said and done. LSU came up a little short against Texas, but Princewill punched in 7 tackles and a sack, batting down a pass and getting 5 pressures. There’s a lot of talent in there, but it’ll take a little work to get it all out.
We’ve discussed Biles in this space quite a bit this year. In a linebacker class that I would consider quite strong, Biles just continues to crank out big performances. 11 tackles, including two for a loss and a sack, and 4 QB pressures as Texas managed to scrap out a last second win. Of course, he wasn’t the best Longhorn defender on the field…
Any time a safety registers three interceptions in one game, he’s definitely doing something right. That it came in a game where Texas needed every last bit of it in order to get out with the victory. Throw in 11 tackles and another pass breakup, and you’ve got your pretty clear-cut player of the week. McDonald should be a great day two safety.
