title: Seahawks' Nick Emmanwori: The NFL’s Most Versatile Defensive Player
full_text:
When Nick Emmanwori was drafted by the Seattle Seahawks , he was considered to be a safety. Most major NFL websites list him as a safety. He played a lot of safety in college.
And yet, according to Pro Football Focus, he’s played a single snap as a deep safety this season, and zero snaps as a box safety. So, where is he being deployed, if not at his draft position?
That’s not to say that Nick doesn’t play in the box a lot. But when he does, he does so as a full-blown linebacker. Depending on the circumstances of the game, you can count on Emmanwori getting linebacker snaps anywhere from 10-25 times per game. He’s currently sitting on 134 this season, mostly as an outside backer on either side.
This is more-or-less in line with how Nick was used in 2025, where he stacked up 285 box linebacker snaps in the regular season. He’s spreading his wings a little bit, but this will always be a huge part of his game thanks to his size. At 6’3 and 220 pounds, he’s as big as some modern NFL linebackers , and much faster. But this year, he’s spread his wings beyond.
As a rookie, Emmanwori emerged as an asset most readily as a slot corner. That has continued on into 2026, naturally. The slot is still where he does most of his damage. He’s currently got 175 snaps there, and he’s also sprinkled in 10 as an outside corner. Matching up on slot receivers and wrecking outside runs with his skills is the foundation of his game .
Rookie year Emmanwori was primarily a slot corner, recording 378 snaps there, as well as 8 on the outside. It’s the perfect place for him in this defense, allowing him to mostly stay close to the line of scrimmage and be a bigtime force multiplier for the run defense. But this season has been about moving him around a bit, away from the secondary and towards…
This has been the big transformation in Emmanwori’s usage this season . After testing the waters as a rookie with 88 snaps off the edge on the defensive line, Nick has been unleashed here. 123 snaps and counting. His ability to play off the edge has been very important for this defense, due to the team going relatively light at the position this year.
Assuming he stays healthy, it’s very likely that Emmanwori will end up with at least 200 snaps in each deployment. I can’t find another player in the league right now who is even close to that. Mike Macdonald has unlocked the perfect way to get the most out of this very unique player, and he should continue to in seasons to come as Nick’s game improves even further.

title: Seattle Seahawks' Midseason 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Season is halfway done , and some teams are seeing some big roster issues. These issues are hampering their contention for a Super Bowl title and even a playoff spot. The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) have some roster concerns that might be keeping them from contending for a playoff spot.
Some, if not all, 32 front offices have already started evaluating some of the talent for the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft. The Seahawks might be in a good position to draft key talent based on where they are in the draft. It can help pick up the slack left from a less effective 2026 NFL Draft class .
The following 2027 NFL Mock Draft is based on a draft machine, but with the Seahawks’ picks being made. Most of the picks are made based on the biggest current position needs, expiring contracts, players that will likely retire at the end of the season, and other team outlooks like depth.
Round 1, No. 17: Edge Rusher Yhonzae Pierre (Alabama) Round 2, No. 50: Wide Receiver Jackson Harris (LSU) Round 3, No. 101: Safety Bray Hubbard (Alabama) Round 3, No. 134: Defensive Tackle DJ Hicks (Texas A&M) Round 4, No. 153: Cornerback Bo Mascoe (Texas) Round 5, No. 172: Quarterback Drake Lindsey (Minnesota) Round 5, No. 177: Guard Malachi Brand (Arkansas) Round 6, No. 213: Running Back Cam Cook (West Virginia) Round 7, No. 235: Offensive Tackle McKale Boley (Virginia)
The Seahawks didn’t address the need for an edge rusher in the previous 2026 Draft or the NFL Trade Deadline. At this point, Dante Fowler Jr. and Uchenna Nwosu are in the final year of their deals, and DeMarcus Lawrence will retire at the end of the season. This leaves essentially only Derick Hall as a key edge rusher moving forward. Having Pierre opposite Hall would create a solid young tandem on the Dark Side Defense.
​The Seahawks need more help at receiver outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Rashid Shaheed is a gadget receiver, then Harris can be a younger and more explosive Cooper Kupp. There are other needs than safety, but the depth at safety is limited this season.
Even if Bud Clark is fully healthy, he would play other positions outside of safety. Hubbard would be a strong backup to Julian Love and can play linebacker and special teams. The depth at the interior defensive line is limited and there isn’t a guarantee that Jarren Reed and Brandon Pili will be back.
​Cornerback isn’t as big a need as many analysts previously thought during the last draft process. The Seahawks could upgrade this position’s depth, along with quarterback. Lindsey isn’t expected to be a contender for a starting quarterback, but he could be a reliable player and backup with development.
Decisions have to be made with the depth at running back after this season. Cook’s addition should help with the need. Finally, this season has been brutal for the offensive line in terms of injuries. The Seahawks will have to reload the depth at the tackles and interior offensive line.

title: Week 11 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks on the Move as Defense Shines
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks enter their bye in Week 11 on a two-game winning streak. Backup quarterback Drew Lock has filled in for injured starter Sam Darnold over the past two weeks, and helped them defeat the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders .
Now with a record of 6-4, the Seahawks are in the mix for a Wild Card spot, but they have a lot of ground to cover if they hope to catch the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers. While it's true that they would prefer to be in better shape, they're still one of the teams to watch in the NFC thanks to their elite defense.
That defense finds itself being praised in many of this week's NFL power rankings, which we see in the following roundup.
Ranking: 8 | Last week: 12
This is the biggest leap the Seahawks made in any power ranking this week as Connor Orr is buying their defense. As he says, they're on a historic pace and can carry this team far.
"Alert: The Seahawks have allowed the fewest yards per game out of any team since 1999, and are still really, really good on defense," Orr wrote.
ESPN decided to highlight every team's non-quarterback MVP and that had to be easy for the Seahawks as Brady Henderson chose Jaxon Smith-Njigba. As Henderson writes, he would have been the choice even without the non-quarterback rule.
"Smith-Njigba would be Seattle's undisputed MVP even if quarterbacks weren't excluded, and the historic numbers he's producing should at least get him consideration for the leaguewide award. His 1,207 receiving yards are more than the rest of the team has combined (1,122)," Henderson wrote.
"According to the Elias Sports Bureau, that's the highest percentage of a team's receiving yards (52%) through 10 games since 1966. It puts the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year on pace to break Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964. Smith-Njigba's 10 touchdown catches and 79 receptions also lead the NFL. He has been unstoppable despite Seattle's instability at quarterback, with Sam Darnold missing the better part of four games."
Ranking: 10 | Last week: 11
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff of The Athletic moved Seattle up one spot this week. They highlighted every team's breakout player and for the Seahawks, that happened to be Drew Lock. The backup quarterback has filled in well enough that the duo at The Athletic is asking if he is the superior option to Sam Darnold.
"The Seahawks’ backup quarterback started his third game Sunday in place of the injured Sam Darnold. Seattle has won all three of those games. Among quarterbacks with more than 50 attempts this season, Lock is third in the league in EPA per dropback (0.32). He has seven passing touchdowns and no interceptions, and that last number has some Seahawks fans wondering if he’s a better option than the turnover-prone Darnold."
Ranking: 11 | Last week: 9
Nick Shook said the ground game is starting to improve, but thinks the Seahawks still need to be much better after the bye. Their win over the Raiders didn't impress him as he dropped Seattle two spots despite the victory.
"Seattle’s offense is slowly starting to improve -- especially the running game -- but a win over the Raiders isn’t a great barometer for where it is in this process. Credit is due to Drew Lock, who has handled the quarterback job as well as one can expect from a backup, and the defense remains stifling, especially against lesser competition," Shook wrote. "The 'Hawks better come out of the Week 11 bye ready, though, because a massive test awaits on the other side in the form of the rival 49ers."
Ranking: 10 | Last week: 12
Bleacher Report has Seattle moving up to No. 10 overall, from the 12th spot. Kristopher Knox says their defense is still championship worthy, but he knows their ground game needs to be better.
"Seattle's defense is still championship-caliber, and its ground game is starting to come together with Zach Charbonnet and Jadrian Price both healthy. If the Seahawks can reach the playoffs and get reliable quarterback play in the postseason, they're fully capable of making another run," Knox wrote.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 14
Pete Prisco is another one who is asking about the starting quarterback position in Seattle. He's not ready to say Lock needs to replace Darnold, but he did give the backup credit for how well he has played when called upon.
"Quarterback Drew Lock is 3-0 as the starter in place of Sam Darnold. Should he stay there? Not yet. But he is playing well," Prisco wrote.

title: Seahawks Report Card: Seattle's Bye Week Grades
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are at the bye week , which gives them a chance to sit back and evaluate their progress over the course of the season.
At 6-4, the Seahawks are doing something right , but they have already lost more games this year than all of last season and have not quite met the high expectations they had in 2025.
Some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff got their red pens out and graded the team through the first 10 games of the season.
Expectations were high for the Seattle Seahawks this season. While there was some expected turbulence, the Seahawks haven’t done the best job of getting out of their own way. They’ve made some progress in addressing their weaknesses as they back into playoff contention form.
The Seahawks started with a statement this season by knocking off the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl LX rematch despite losing Sam Darnold on the opening drive. Since then, it’s been a mixed bag. Their defense has been solid, but they’ve been asked to carry the load as the offense has been inconsistent, and without Jaxon Smith-Njigba, it might have been non-existent. Perhaps the return of Zach Charbonnet will turn things around, but for now, the Seahawks are falling short of expectations.
I can understand why my colleagues have given the Seahawks a "C+" for their efforts so far this season. As the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seahawks came into this season with expectations to either get back there or at least get close. They haven't looked like that so much this season.
However, they still have the league's No. 1 defense, which has been battle-tested, limiting the Kansas City Chiefs to a mere three points and zero plays in the red zone. That game gives the Seahawks some hope that they are who they strive to be.
The offense needs a lot of work, but Sam Darnold has been battling through injuries all year long and Quenton Nelson should provide a boost once he's fully healthy.
This team has only lost one game by more than three points this season, which is why I can't give them any less than a "B."

title: Seahawks GTA Rewind: Seattle's Record for Every Game Release
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks , the rest of the league and its fans are awaiting the long-overdue release of Grand Theft Auto VI.
It's been 13 years since the franchise released a game, so we figured that we would take a trip down memory lane to see how the Seahawks performed every year a game came out.
The Seahawks were still an AFC West team when Grand Theft Auto was first released in 1997. Hall of Famer Warren Moon was 41 years old and started 14 games for the team. It was the last of his nine Pro Bowl appearances. The team went 8-8 but missed the playoffs.
When the second iteration of the game was released, the Seahawks started 8-2 but lost 5 of their last 6 games, limping into the playoffs. They still won the division, but lost to Dan Marino and the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round. This was the last win of Marino's career.
The Seahawks had an identical record, but how they got there was a little different. Instead of starting 8-2, the 2001 Seahawks were 3-4 before winning six of their last nine games. Unfortunately for the Seahawks, it was not enough for them to move on to the playoffs in their final season in the AFC. The Baltimore Ravens and New York Jets advanced as wild cards with 10-6 records that year.
In Seattle's first season in the NFC, another installment of GTA was released. The Seahawks took a step back in their first NFC campaign, going 7-9 and missing the playoffs once again.
The Seahawks made it back to the playoffs for the second year in a row after snapping their drought in 2003. They won the NFC West in 2004, but fell to the St. Louis Rams 24-20 in the first round of the playoffs.
The Seahawks were in the midst of their rebuild by the time GTA IV came out. The following year, they hired Pete Carroll and went on the most successful run in franchise history.
The last time GTA released a game, the Seahawks went on to win the Super Bowl. The Legion of Boom was taking over and the Seahawks were establishing themselves as one of the top teams in the league.
Seahawks Record: 6-4 (so far)
The Seahawks finished as Super Bowl champs the last time Grand Theft Auto was released. That is a positive sign of what could happen this year, at least for Seahawks fans. The players themselves can take this weekend off , download the game, and relax as they get ready for the final seven weeks of the season.

title: 49ers Coach Reveals What Makes Vikings Defense So Dangerous
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 11, it will feature one of the best offenses in the NFL against one of the best defenses in the NFL. 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak opened up on the challenges that the Vikings defense presents, making them one of the best in the NFL.
Kubiak noted that everything starts with the experience and comfort level the players have in the defense.
“They're going to throw a lot at you,” stated Kubiak on Thursday. “To me, the thing that jumps out the most is: this is a unit that's been playing together for, I think, 3 or 4 years now, and so the comfort level and the familiarity that this group of players has is kind of unmatched in this league.”
Jalen Redmond and Levi Drake Rodriguez have been on the team since 2024. Dallas Turner was a 2024 draft pick, and Andrew Van Ginkel was signed that same offseason, along with Blake Cashman. Byron Murphy has been with the team since 2023, while Josh Metellus and Harrison Smith were in Minnesota before Brian Flores.
Kubiak noted that the experience the core has could not be replicated easily.
“I mean, these guys— they're playing in this scheme where they're throwing different blitzes at you, different coverages, but the way they're tied together and the way that they can all play so fast and decisively— that's what makes this an elite defense to me,” stated Kubiak. “I think if you tried to go and install this defense in a new place, it would take a while to get a group of guys to play the way they play.”
Due to that ability, Kubiak noted that this makes it easier for Flores to call up different pass rushes and blitzes that other teams cannot.
“They know how to kind of back each other up. It's just a unit that is so tied together that it's so impressive,” added Kubiak. “Then you add the challenges of the scheme on top of it. It's probably the most unique scheme you're going to go against in the league in terms of the amount of blitzes they're going to run. The different ways they're going to try to affect the quarterback. Ut's a huge challenge, and they're going to do that to stop the run. They're going to do that to affect you in the drop-back passing game to get to the quarterback. So we got to work cut out for us.”
The 49ers offense ranks first in both EPA/play and success rate. The Vikings defense is also first in EPA/play and success rate.

title: Kyle Juszczyk Reveals His Proudest Moment in a 49ers Jersey
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Juszczyk have worked in tandem for over a decade.
In fact, he's technically the longest-serving player for the 49ers in the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era. He's been there since the initial rebuild after joining in free agency and has since played a role in both of the franchise's trips to the Super Bowl.
2026 marks his tenth year representing the City by the Bay, and Juszczyk was asked by NBC Sports Bay Area for his career highlight with the franchise so far, he stated: "It's a big question because I'm proud of so many moments here. It's really hard to pinpoint one because I've been part of so much.
"My favourite game as a 49er has to be the 2023 NFC Championship Game, when we beat Detroit here to reach the Super Bowl.
"Being down 17 points at halftime and making that comeback was special. It was a special season, too. George and Deebo were doing the Netflix series Receiver, so every once in a while, my wife and I go back and watch that episode.
"It feels like there's no chance we're going to win that game, and then it turns into this magical comeback. I felt like I played a big part in it, too. I had some really big plays that I'm proud of.
"Going back and watching that game is such an emotional rollercoaster, and it's incredibly fulfilling."
The game in question featured what could only be described as one of the most memorable comebacks in recent NFL history. However, one intriguing detail is that Juszczyk admits he still watches the documentary focused on his own teammates, revisiting those memories of that remarkable occasion.
In the same interview, he shared words that would undoubtedly resonate with the Faithful, reflecting exactly what they would want to hear from a player.
"Just a sense of pride [of representing the 49ers]. You walk in every day and see those faces and plaques up on the wall," he said.
"When you first join the program, you envision yourself one day maybe being up there. For it to finally be real and to have my face and George's face right there is pretty cool."
Of course, Kittle joined just a month later in the 2017 NFL Draft. Having two players who have been around since then is invaluable, as both have helped set the tone for the culture Shanahan and Lynch wanted to instil when they arrived.

title: 49ers GM John Lynch Predicts Nick Bosa's Return to Form In Coming Weeks
full_text:
A lot of eyes are on San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa as he hasn't produced at his previous peak levels so far this season.
In his defense, he's had very limited playing time over the past two seasons due to injuries. However, there is a growing argument that his best days may be behind him because of those injuries . He's had three ACL tears.
Despite this growing concern, general manager John Lynch ( like head coach Kyle Shanahan ) is defending Bosa's subpar performances this season.
"When you're a tremendous player, like Nick is, you create a standard," Lynch said on his usual weekly interview with Bay Area radio station KNBR . "And there's somewhat of a—I don't want to call it a burden because that has a negative context—but there is a responsibility that you feel as a player. Nick impacts every game that he plays, and he does at such a high level.
"I think when he doesn't [live] up to his standard, he's going to call himself things like 'weak link.' ... Nick did have five pressures the other day, which is a high number, but he expects more out of himself.
"He didn't have training camp," Lynch added. "We're in a new defensive scheme, which asks some different things of him. And so, I think that's what Nick's alluding to. There's some adjustment, but he's stacked some good weeks of practice.
"And I just have so much confidence in him that I have the same standard that he has for himself. Nick's standard for himself is probably higher than anybody, but we have such a high standard.
"I know that we have a motivated Nick Bosa. He's an incredibly diligent worker, and I think he'll be impacting games starting this week in a big way."
Bosa has yet to pick up a sack in four games so far. It's a significant drop-off, and the 49ers are paying him a huge amount of money to make as many sacks as possible.
It makes sense to defend him because the reasons Lynch made are completely valid, but Bosa will need to improve drastically with each passing week or the front office might have to make some incredibly tough decisions.
His future has been uncertain, largely due to speculation and financial considerations, but Bosa knows better than anyone that he needs to deliver on the field. His decline since 2021 and 2022 has been significant.

title: 49ers Have Clear Blueprint to Beat Vikings' Defense
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 7-2 and have the best defense in the NFL. However, there is a key to beating them. The way to beat the Vikings is to lean on the run and continue to push the ground game.
The Vikings have played five above-average rushing attacks, according to rbsdm.com . They are 4-0 when facing below-average rushing groups and 3-2 when facing teams who have had success running the ball.
They beat the Chicago Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in a storm, and Caleb Williams got hurt. Despite that, the Bears threw the ball more than they ran it in a game that ended 9-3.
They beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before Tampa Bay realized that their ground attack was the way to win games. Baker Mayfield had 34 pass attempts in the game and also got hurt. Bucky Irving had 15 rushing attempts.
They beat the Indianapolis Colts, but Indianapolis showed a blueprint for success. They hung tight in a 16-10 win despite four sacks and one intercepion by Daniel Jones. That is because Jonathan Taylor had 18 rushes for 95 yards, and Seth McGowan added 11 rushes for 46 yards.
Since then, the Vikings have gone 1-2, beating the Green Bay Packers, who have one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL. Jordan Love was sacked eight times as the Vikings' defense knew exactly what was coming.
The Lions beat them with 39 rushing attempts to 25 passing attempts. That is despite trailing 7-6 most of the game and trailing 15-12 late. The Lions' seven-play, fourth-quarter, game-winning scoring drive to take the lead featured five rushes for 57 yards and two pass attempts for 12 yards.
Buffalo controlled the game in their win, but they had 44 rushing attempts to 31 pass attempts for Josh Allen attempts. You could argue the Bills leaned on their MVP candidate too much in the win. Allen was sacked four times and threw an interception.
The 49ers have Christan McCaffrey. This is what you drafted Kaelon Black for. The 49ers' rushing attack is just as strong as Detroit's and Buffalo's. Throwing the ball will lead to trouble. Running the ball can be a slog at times, but it will keep the team in the game and allow them to wear down the Vikings late. Look for San Francisco to get very run heavy in Week 11.

title: Five Major Questions the 49ers Must Answer Against the Vikings
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 11 it will be one of the more anticipated matchups of the season. What are some of the biggest questions that are likely to be answered this week?
With Keenan Allen in the mix, Deebo Samuel healthy, and Jordan Watkins taking strides, the need for the depth receivers to play is dwindling. Robinson went from 37 snaps in return to the field to 21 snaps with Allen added to the team.
Cowing played 26 snaps in Week 7, then 18 snaps with Robinson back. He was down to 12 snaps with Allen added. Do either of them need more snaps, or do we see them start to get phased out?
The 49ers drafted Black to take on the tough carries between the tackles and to grind out yards. The way to beat the Vikings is to avoid third down and obvious passing by all means. So, Black being able to grind out a few yards at a time is beneficial in this scenario. Do they lean on Black for a career-high in attempts?
The last time that Brock Purdy had an MVP case, it was derailed by Mike MacDonald and the Baltimore Ravens in a prime-time scenario. It was later in the 2023 season, but the game and the stakes have a similar feel, with Purdy going up against the top defense at the time. This game will go a long way in his candidacy.
It has only been two weeks into the safety rotation , but it is starting to get clear that Mustapha is one of the three safeties that cannot leave the field anymore. He has played 82% and 77% of the 49ers' defensive snaps in the past two weeks. Is it time to get back to 100% for the third-year safety?
Bosa tore his ACL last season. He came back for two games this year and injured his calf. Now, he is back from that injury for two games. It is fair to highlight how long it has been since Bosa has had a sack, but the slump can be explained. However, production has to come soon.

title: How Brock Purdy Can Separate Himself  in MVP Race Against Vikings
full_text:
Up until Week 7, Brock Purdy looked like the MVP favorite. He was being praised like never before for how sweet he was playing, and rightfully so. The 49ers are thriving because of him.
However, losing to the Falcons and the Week 8 Bye have cooled down his MVP push. It's also been tougher with Joe Burrow lighting it up recently. He's undeniably the MVP favorite entering Week 11.
Still, there's plenty of time left for Purdy to regain momentum as the MVP favorite. In fact, he can separate himself as the MVP favorite on Sunday in Mexico City against the Vikings.
By far, the Vikings boast the best defense in the NFL. They've allowest the least passing touchdowns (six) of all defenses and are No. 2 in passing yards allowed (161.4).
No quarterback has had success against them. Not even Josh Allen. Plus, Purdy has struggled against the Vikings' defense the last two times he's faced them.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has Purdy's number. The Vikings are going into Mexico City with a lot of momentum, especially after acquiring Kirk Cousins.
This is the perfect time for Purdy to lead the 49ers to victory over them. The fact that the game will be in primetime on Sunday Night Football emphasizes it further.
Purdy doesn't need to play great. He just needs to play well. His stat line can be 20 of 29 for 236 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one turnover.
So long as he makes an off-script play, creates an explosive play, or a clutch first down conversion or score, he will be credited as the driving force for the 49ers beating the Vikings.
And if Purdy somehow does light up the Vikings, he will have created significant distance as the MVP favorite between himself and Burrow and whoever else is in the running.
A win alone will not suffice. It will help strengthen Purdy's MVP case, but it won't separate him. He needs to play well and be a clear-cut reason for the 49ers' win.
If Christian McCaffrey steals the show on the ground, it will be tough for him to take the MVP lead. It's possible that's how it plays out, since the Vikings can be exploited on the ground.
In any case, this is a big-time opportunitiy for Purdy on Sunday night in Mexico City.

title: Nick Bosa Blames 49ers' New Defensive Scheme for his Current Struggles
full_text:
Nick Bosa isn't playing good foorball this season. Even he would agree with that .
Through four games, he has zero sacks, and just two quarteback hits. This has been the worst stretch of his career and the first time he has gone four games without recording a sack. Keep in mind, the 49ers are paying him $34 million per season primarily to sack the quarterback. They gave him that extension a few months after he recorded 18.5 sacks in the 2022 season. Since then, he 21.5 sacks in four years.
"If I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats," Bosa said Wednesday in Colorado Springs. "But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now. So that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats."
But why isn't Bosa playing good football right now? Why does he get pushed past the quarterback almost every time he rushes?
Could it be that he's not the same player following his third ACL surgery? He has to wear a brace on his right knee now, and he doesn't seem as dynamic as he used to be.
Bosa doesn't seem concerned about his knee. Instead, he thinks the issue is schematic.
"I think there's a learning curve and ... a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am."
This is s strange response from Bosa.
First, just because he was injured during training camp and for five weeks early in the season, that doesn't mean he couldn't have gone to meetings and walkthroughs and learned the complexities of Raheem Morris' scheme.
Second, it's true that Morris' scheme is different than Robert Saleh's scheme, but how complex are the differences for Bosa? It's not like Morris is making him line up in a two-point stance and play outside linebacker and drop into coverage.
Bosa is still playing defensive end. He's still lining up with his hand in the dirt. Morris isn't asking him to slant and stunt and twist that often. He's doing what he always has been asked to do -- set the edge in the run game, contain the quarterback in the pocket (don't rush past him), beat the offensive tackle and record the sack.
Bosa isn't doing any of those things well right now. Instead, he's desperately trying to time the snap just so he can generate some pressure. That's why he jumped offside three times on Sunday in Dallas. There is no scheme that can mask his current issues.
And that's because his issues are tied to his knee. He simply isn't the same player he was before he tore it again, and he probably never will be.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Gushes Over Vikings DC Brian Flores
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers will face their toughest test on offense this season when they take on the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
The Vikings' defense is the best in the NFL, thanks to the brilliant scheme led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores . Shanahan has struggled against Flores since he joined the Vikings.
The chess match with Flores will demand Shanahan and the 49ers to be at their best. It's a matchup that is stressful to plan for, but it also invokes a ton of admiration from Shanahan for Flores. He can't help but gush over Flores' brilliance.
"He's more unique than all the other 31 guys," Shanahan said. "He's the one guy who commits to this and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He's been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He's as good as it gets at that stuff. Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it's usually a matter of time.
"They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure's really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it's 70-straight plays of that.”
Saying that a defensive coordinator is "more unique" than the rest is as good a compliment as you can get. Flores should be blushing over the heap of praise Shanahan bestowed upon him.
It makes sense why Shanahan feels that way. He's battled Flores' defense over the year. It's always tough to crack and get the upper hand.
Not even in 2023, when the 49ers went to the Super Bowl, were they successful against the Vikings' defense. Odds are, it's going to be more of the same in Mexico City.
The 49ers are doing everything in their power to make sure it's different this time. Unlike in 2023, this matchup has significant playoff seeding implications.
If there were ever a game for the 49ers and Shanahan to finally get the best of Flores and the Vikings' defense, it's this one. In any case, you can expect a tough and gritty matchup.
"You're going to try to be consistent and efficient in everything, but I promise you that's not going to happen for all the plays. Brian creates too much stuff.

title: Vikings Defense Has a Weakness the 49ers Can Exploit
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will need to be at their very best when they take on the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City, especially on offense.
Minnesota's defense is easily the best in the league.  Moving the ball and putting up points against them will be difficult. It will be night and day compared to playing the Dallas Cowboys.
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy have always struggled against the Vikings' defense thanks to defensive coordinator Brian Flores . However, as vaunted as the Vikings' defense is, they have a weakness the 49ers can exploit.
It's their run defense. Minnesota's run defense ranks No. 17 in yards per game allowed at 111.9. They've also allowed the 13th-most runs of 10 yards or more.
This is where the 49ers will find success. In fact, it's the only way they will beat the Vikings. It's if they can successfully exploit this weakness.
For starters, it will wear down the Vikings' defense, especially with the game being played at high altitude in Mexico City. Of course, the 49ers can tire on offense as well, which is why rookie Kaelon Black will need a lot of carries.
Tiring games also tend to favor the offense. Just look at the 49ers' defense last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Shanahan said that their defense was gassed, especially the defensive line.
Another reason running the ball will help the 49ers is because of third down. This will help them stay in manageable third-down situations. That is crucial to defeating the flurry of blitzes from the Vikings.
It will place Purdy in an advantageous position to drop back for a quick pass to either Keenan Allen or Christian McCaffrey. There won't be enough time for the blitz to get to him since the yardage for a conversion will be short.
Shanahan must avoid dialing up a ton of passes for Purdy to get blasted on early downs. That will set them back well behind the chains and make converting first downs extremely difficult, if not impossible, against Minnesota's defense.
The run-blocking will need to be elite for the 49ers. Left guard Connor Colby will be their biggest worry, especially since he struggled against the Cowboys last week.
Everyone else should be fine to execute at a high level. Everything hinges on the 49ers running the ball against the Vikings.
If the 49ers can't find success on the ground , they won't win the game.

title: 49ers Have Clear Mike Evans Decision After Injury Update
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans missed practice once again with his Achilles injury. Evans has not practiced since Week 5 and has not played since Week 6. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that the team is hopeful to get him back at practice on Thursday. However, whether he practices or not, the plan for Week 11 should be clear. There is no reason to play Mike Evans.
First off, Evans is 33 years old. He missed two games in 2024 and nine games in 2025. He is starting to be on a downward trend due to injuries and age in the NFL. Still, the team signed him with one idea in mind, and that is to win a Super Bowl.
If the 49ers can get three or four healthy games from Evans from January into February, the team will have gotten their money's worth. In the first six games, they saw just how good he can be when he is on the field.
They are sitting at 8-1, and they have a three-game lead in the NFC West. They also have wins over the two teams that matter in their division. A loss to the two-loss Vikings would hurt their chances at a home game in the NFC Championship. However, if you asked most 49ers whether they would rather be at home for that game or have Mike Evans fully healthy, most would take Evans.
So, the team should be cautious and only play him when he is 100% ready to go. Even if he is close, there is no reason to push it, and he should take the extra week.
It is not like the 49ers are certain to lose without him, either. They are currently lis ted as short favori tes. The team just got Deebo Samuel back healthy. They just traded for Keenan Allen. More than that, second-year wideout Jordan Watkins is starting to ascend in recent weeks.
When adding in Demarcus Robinson as a depth option, the team is not thin at receiver right now. Adding Allen and seeing Watkins emerge has allowed the team to take things slow with Evans and not see it impact them on the field.
So, there is no reason to push it. We will see if he practices later this week. His game status should be determined Friday.

title: Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Gets Put on the Spot About Bruce Arians
full_text:
Bruce Arians handed the keys to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coaching position over to Todd Bowles after he retired in 2022, and the two have maintained their close friendship ever since.
Arians had a short stint in a front office role with the Bucs since his retirement, but in a recent interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, he relayed that he is itching to get back into coaching in 2027.
Arians expressed that he doesn't want to join a team in any capacity other than as the head coach, so it will be interesting to see if he garners any interest once the coaching carousel begins.
When speaking with the media following practice, Bowles gave his thoughts on whether his predecessor could still coach despite being 74 years old.
"I talk to Bruce [Arians], but we don't talk about coaching," Bowles exclaimed . "Tom Moore made Bruce look like a college student. So, you can still coach at that age, and Tom's probably a younger heart more than anybody. And so, it doesn't surprise me. Bruce can do whatever he wants to do."
It was a funny little quip from Bowles comparing the former Bucs' offensive assistant Tom Moore to Arians.
Moore coached in some capacity until the age of 88 years old, which means that Arians has some 14 years to catch him.
With all that said, it's hard to imagine that Bowles isn't right in stating that Arians can do whatever he puts his mind to.
Arians had retired before unretiring and joining the Bucs in 2019 to try and win his first Super Bowl.
If he does in fact return to coaching, he likely will only accept an offer where he can foresee himself having ultimate control while also having high thoughts on how the roster is stacked up to potentially go out and contend for his second Lombardi Trophy.
But will Arians return to coach the Bucs if Bowles is relieved of his duties at the end of the season? It's highly doubtful.
Arians handed the keys to Bowles after winning a Super Bowl, so taking over following him could likely create a rift between the two, especially if there were to be behind-the-scenes talks.
On top of that, this Bucs' roster probably doesn't move Arians enough to come back and coach.

title: Buccaneers Announce Likely Starting Quarterback vs. Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a must-win game on Sunday (they all are, from here on out) when they play the Detroit Lions in Week 11.
The Bucs would like to have their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield, available for that contest. His status was in doubt this week, though, as he's been dealing with a foot injury in conjunction with his dislocated thumb that he suffered in Week 3.
There were initial reports that Mayfield would be a "long shot" to play against the Lions, but that all changed when he practiced on Thursday and then spoke to the media afterward.
The Bucs held their final practice of the week on Friday, and Mayfield once again practiced — so head coach Todd Bowles' announcement on who would start against Detroit should come as no surprise.
Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction" to play Sunday — as a result, he should be good to go and is expected to start the game against the Lions.
Todd Bowles says Baker Mayfield is “trending in the right direction” to play Sunday: pic.twitter.com/1Rw7DdD4vo
Bowles told the media on Wednesday that he was waiting to see how Mayfield responded in practice for the rest of the week before making a decision. Mayfield has clearly been able to practice without too much limitation, and because of that, he'll get the nod under center against Detroit.
If Mayfield were unable to go, the Bucs would turn to undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. Daniels has started three games this season and is 1-2 in those games, and although he told the media Thursday that he was prepared to start if needed, Mayfield is healthy enough to get the start.
"Continue to do what I've been doing since Chicago – doing everything I can to get all the treatment and rehab possible and prepare like a professional," Mayfield said Thursday. "For me, it's continuing that. If I continue that, I imagine being able to play. Obviously, like I told you guys before, when it came to the Steelers game, didn't think I was going to be able to. If I feel like ‘J.D.’ (Jalon Daniels) gives us a better option to win, [I have] no shame in admitting that. We'll see how it goes, but [I’m] progressing well and [we'll] see how tomorrow shapes up."
Mayfield has thrown just three touchdowns to four interceptions at the head of a league-worst passing offense in yards per game. He'll work with offensive coordinator Zac Robinson and the rest of the offense to try to turn things around, but he'll have to do it while battling injury — something Mayfield is no stranger to.
The Bucs will play the Lions at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Ford Field. When they do, it seems Mayfield will get the nod.

title: Buccaneers and NFC South Could Be Reason for New NFL Rule
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won the NFC South four out of the last five seasons, but it has never come in dominant fashion.
The Bucs have won the NFC South with a double-digit record just once since 2022, and they won the South with a losing 8-9 record once in the same timespan as well. They've only ever won the NFC South by more than a game a single time, since then, too, in 2024.
The NFC South has been the worst division in football for some time now, and that isn't changing this year — the division doesn't have a team with more than four wins in it after Week 10. The division may be so bad, in fact, that the NFL could look to change the rules about how the playoffs work.
As it stands, every division winner gets a top-four seed in the playoffs and hosts at least one playoff game. That includes the NFC South, meaning that a divisional winner can — and in the NFC South's case, often has — host a playoff game against a much better team with a better record simply because they won a weaker division and the visiting Wild Card team did not.
That may be changing soon, and partially because of the NFC South's ineptitude. Per NFL insider Dan Graziano, the NFL may revive a discussion from last year about potentially changing the format where poor teams who won their division can host a playoff game and get a No. 4 seed.
Graziano: There are rumblings from league office about reviving discussion from 2025 offseason about whether teams that win their divisions with sub-.500 records should be guaranteed home playoff games and top-four seeds in their conference.
The Bucs and the NFC South have been the biggest culprits here, but it was the Detroit Lions, who have been on the other side of this dilemma, who proposed this rule change in 2025. The Lions finished last in the NFC North in 2025 despite finishing 9-8, while the 8-9 Panthers won the NFC South and were a No. 4 seed in the NFC.
As it stands right now, the Bucs are just one game out of the NFC South lead with a 3-6 record. Meanwhile, the Lions lead the NFC North — but they're in a three-way tie at 7-2, and the last-place Green Bay Packers are 6-4.
The Buccaneers likely wouldn't have made the playoffs in seasons like 2022, 2023 and 2024 had they been in a more difficult division. That advantage they have could go away soon if the NFL were to change this playoff rule.
Divisions are cyclical, however, so the NFC South could become very good in the next few years and the NFC North could potentially falter. There have been plenty of bad divisions over the past few years, but the Buccaneers and the NFC South are major reason why this conversation has been happening lately.
The Bucs and Lions play each other at 1 p.m. in Detroit on Sunday.

title: Buccaneers Know They Must Stop This Lions Star
full_text:
Alex Anzalone knows a thing or two about the Detroit Lions.
Before joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2026 off-season, Anzalone played with the Lions from 2021-25 and achieved a good amount of success there while also being a team captain for multiple seasons.
He is also not the only transplant from Detroit, as fellow Buccaneer Al-Quadin Muhammad also joined the Bucs this offseason and was with the Lions from 2024 to 2025.
Both of these players know what the Lions are capable of, especially on the offensive side of the ball as they faced the Lions' stars every day for multiple years. One major player they are going to have to keep an eye on in this upcoming game is Jahmyr Gibbs.
Gibbs has already had a fantastic season for the Lions, reaching 1,000 rushing yards through only nine games and also posting 11 rushing touchdowns, 384 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns as well. He may very well be the best running back in the entire NFL and is a surefire candidate for Offensive Player of the Year
Anzalone has a simple answer when asked to describe Gibbs and players like him.
"In the league, when you play against players like this, I call them Aliens," Anzalone said. "They're from a different planet, and you have to play them differently... Gibbs is obviously one of them, and he's proven that."
Thankfully for the Bucs, the defense has been playing very well as of late in terms of getting turnovers and has been especially good at stopping the run this season.
Right now, the Bucs have the No. 1 rushing defense in the NFL in terms of yards allowed and are also first in the NFL in rushing touchdowns allowed. However, it is important to note that teams have not tried to run against the Bucs much this season, as they are second-to-last in rushing attempts against their defense.
The biggest concern that could be Gibbs' receiving ability. Both Anzalone and Trotter have struggled in moments with coverage this year, but have been doing much better in recent weeks.
If the Buccaneers are able to slow down Gibbs and really take control of the game as they were able to do in games against the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons with good defense, they could get their biggest win of the season to date.

title: Buccaneers Get Good News and Bad News After Bye Week
full_text:
Despite the fact that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a disappointing 3-6 on the season, in addition to being one full game outside of first place in the NFC South, there are still positives to be found regarding the team's outlook for the remainder of the regular season.
Most notable among those positives is the Buccaneers' remaining strength of schedule, which is widely considered to be the easiest in the NFL after what was a difficult first half of the year. The other is that, despite their struggles, the Bucs remain undefeated in division games (2-0) on the season with four NFC South games still remaining.
Despite the potential that somehow still exists for the Buccaneers to go on a run and make the postseason, a few things will need to go right. And right now, one of the main things is the injury front.
As it stands right now, the Buccaneers have several key players dealing with injuries, which could threaten their availability for this Sunday's matchup against the Lions in Detroit.
Despite exiting last week's game vs. the Bears due to a knee injury, OLB Yaya Diaby appears to be trending in the right direction to play on Sunday.
First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.
After practice, Bowles confirmed that Diaby is "trending in the right direction", which is a big boost to a defense that has played like one of the best in the league over the past month or so. The Bucs will need all of the defensive reinforcements they can get in order to slow down the Lions' explosive offense.
Another piece of good news coming out of Tampa today is that All-Pro LT Tristan Wirfs was also at practice. Although Wirfs didn't necessarily sustain a significant injury, as far as we know, he was seen limping off the field after the team's tough loss in Chicago.
Not only was star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. not seen at practice on Wednesday, but Bowles cast some serious doubt on Winfield's availability for this game in Detroit when he spoke to the media after practice.
Todd Bowles says that Yaya Diaby is “trending in the right direction.” Antoine Winfield Jr. is “very sore right now” and Bowles didn’t seem as optimistic about his chances this Sunday
Winfield left the game vs. Chicago when he injured his ankle trying to make a tackle and he did not return. Although the Bucs' defense looked excellent as the game went on even without Winfield in the lineup, his presence is still essential for Bowles' defense to function at full capacity.
Trying to limit the impact of players like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams will be that much more challenging without Winfield on the field than it would be if he were to suit up for this game.
When the Bucs promoted QB Easton Stick to the 53-man roster and signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad, it was an obvious sign that Baker Mayfield's status was in serious doubt for this contest. Mayfield took a number of big hits last Sunday night in Chicago, and he was hobbling around most of the night with a foot injury.
Although we haven't got much specific info about the nature of the injury, those moves did not inspire much confidence in the belief that Mayfield would be healthy enough to start this weekend.
That being said, Bowles was not ready to not rule Mayfield out for this game after Wednesday's practice.
"He's made a lot of progress," Bowles said. "We want to see him do some things later on today and tomorrow and kind of make that determination on Friday, but he's a lot better than he was a week ago. I don't know if that's ready or not, I want to see it myself, and we'll see what he can do tomorrow."
Any time a starting quarterback is hurt, it can't be good news for the team. That being said, the fact that a glimmer of hope still exists for Mayfield to play this weekend is worth taking note of.
Regardless of whether Mayfield suits up on Sunday in Detroit or not, the Buccaneers will need to have as many healthy players on the field as possible in order to upset a very talented Lions team.

title: The Craziest Buccaneers Stats Through the First Half of the Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had a season of ups and downs (mostly downs). They're 3-6 and have the worst passing offense in football, but they're just a game out of the NFC South, have an elite defense and boast an impressive running game.
The Bucs are, in many ways, a statistical enigma — it's hard to tell whether they are much better than their record or right where they're supposed to be. We've collected a few stats that make the Bucs a bizarre football team throughout their first nine games of the season.
The Buccaneers have the best rushing offense in the NFL (163.9 rushing yards per game) and the very worst passing offense in the NFL (141.9 net passing yards per game). They also have more rushing yards than passing yards at this stage of the year — not great.
The Bucs have to find ways to throw the football if they want to win games. They can really lean on the run game (and have in all of their wins), but the passing game has failed them in more ways than one.
Bucs kicker Chase McLaughlin has yet to miss a kick in any capacity. He's a pristine 22-for-22 on field goal attempts and he's 18-for-18 on extra point attempts. He's also Tampa Bay's leading scorer, currently accounting for 84 points.
We don't mean to jinx him, but McLaughlin could be on his way to a historic season. Three NFL kickers in history — Gary Anderson, Jeff Wilkins and Mike Vanderjagt — have had a perfect kicking season during the regular season.
Only Vanderjagt has had a perfect season through the regular season and the playoffs. The Bucs would have to make it to the playoffs for McLaughlin to test out that record, too.
The Buccaneers are 3-6 and one of the worst teams in the NFL by record (and most of the others are also in the NFC South). Despite that record, though, the team has a positive point differential of +24 points. That's the 11th-best number in the NFL.
Every team ahead of Tampa Bay has won six or more games. The Bucs have lost every single one of their games by one score, and two of those losses were by three points.
Tampa Bay has had a blowout against the Panthers to help increase that number, and holding the Atlanta Falcons to zero points the week after helped their differential, too. But two things seem to be for certain — the Buccaneers find themselves in close games a lot, and they have a lot of trouble actually winning them.
The Bucs have been doing this for the past few years now, but they seem to play better on the road than they do at home.
The Bucs are 2-2 on the road this year, but they're just 1-4 when playing at Raymond James Stadium. Their average points scored across those splits is also fairly interesting — they average 16.8 points per game on the road and 29.5 on the road.
The team's win over the Panthers is a bit of an outlier, by either way, the Bucs seem more comfortable on the road. Thankfully, they'll be heading to Detroit to play the Lions next Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Chris Godwin is Costing the Buccaneers $85,000 Per Yard Right Now
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers passing attack has been their weakness this season.
The Bucs currently own the NFL's worst passing game in the league, having not even thrown for over 1,500 yards at the midway point of the season and not a single wide receiver eclipsing the 300-yard mark.
It hasn't been pretty, and for one wideout in particular, it's starting to look even worse thanks to how much money he is making.
Former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chris Godwin signed a contract extension with the Bucs before the start of the 2025 season for three years, worth $66 million. The $22 million per year was enough to keep him in Tampa Bay rather than seeing him walk to a team like the New England Patriots.
But now, just a year and a half into that deal, it's looking like a massive overpay.
Godwin has never looked quite right after dislocating his ankle in 2024, and his stats mirror that sentiment.
Last season, Godwin had the lowest receiving yardage total of his career with just 360 yards. He also only saw action in nine games as he dealt with rehab and injuries, and he only found the end zone twice.
Now, Godwin, who has already seen as much action as he did all of 2025, is set to have yet another down season. Godwin has only mustered 29 catches for 259 yards and no touchdowns.
That means that he is currently earning nearly $85,000 per yard in annual cash compensation. That is not a great return on your value or investment. If you account for his actual salary cap hit, that number gets higher at $130,050 per yard.
It's highly unlikely that a magic wand is waved and the Bucs' passing game improves enough for Godwin's contract to be worth it. That means the Bucs' front office should be looking at alternatives this offseason.
Godwin's team option, $20.7 million, is in 2027. However, the Bucs do have a potential out once the 2026 season concludes if they decide to cut bait with the aging wideout.
If Tampa Bay decides to cut Godwin outright before June 1, they would not only save the $22 million he is owed in salary, but they would also save approximately $13.7 million in cap space with his dead money coming way down.
There are always options on the table, however. Godwin and the Bucs could decide to meet for him to take a massive pay cut to stay with the team until his contract runs out — see Jamel Dean just last year — before he hits free agency.
They also could come together on a trade that could net them draft capital this offseason, but this scenario seems highly unlikely as they should have traded him beforehand if they were to go that route.

title: Why Wide Receiver is the Buccaneers' Biggest Need
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have plenty of areas to look at fixing this offseason when the regular season wraps up.
The Bucs are 3-6 at the moment, and if that gets worse, head coach may be an area the Bucs try to improve on after five years of Todd Bowles. The team could also serve to shore up its interior offensive line, and tight end will definitely be a point of consideration.
There's one area that may be the most crucial for Tampa Bay, though. And unfortunately for the Bucs, they've spent a lot of draft capital investing in that position very, very recently.
There are a lot of problems with Tampa Bay's offense. Bucs' offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is having some trouble scheming up the passing game, and quarterback Baker Mayfield is having some trouble executing that already-poor scheme.
Those are all parts of it. But the Bucs need wide receivers desperately because, right now, the lack of talent in that room is a big reason why the passing game has faltered the way it has.
Wideout Jalen McMillan is injured and has been since Week 2 of the NFL season. In his absence, the Bucs have rolled with three main wideouts — Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Tez Johnson. Neither of those receivers have over 300 yards at the moment, with Egbuka leading the pack at just 278.
Godwin is on a three-year, $22 million deal, and his age has shown itself over the past two seasons. Johnson has been good in spurts, but he doesn't have the skill set to be a main target in Tampa Bay, and he isn't big enough to be a viable threat between the hashes that the Bucs desperately need at the moment.
Finally, there are the two players the team drafted over the last two years. Egbuka was supposed to be a future WR1 for this team when he was drafted in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, but he hasn't looked the part at all from the back half of last season through this one. He lacks physicality at the catch point, struggles with getting separation and has been battling injury frequently this year.
The Bucs also drafted wideout Ted Hurst in the third round of this year's NFL Draft, and while it's very early, he hasn't made much of an impact this year. He's dropped two passes that could have been touchdowns, and his drop problem was bad enough against the Chicago Bears that he got benched early in the game.
The Bucs are 3-6 right now. It's unknown exactly where they are going to pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but they should definitely be looking for help at wideout. They need a receiver who can open up the middle of the field for them and be able to get separation through either their speed or their route-running acumen — the Bucs have neither on the squad right now.
Tampa Bay plays the Detroit Lions at 1 p.m. on the road Sunday.

title: The Tony Pollard Debate: Titans Have a Huge Offseason Decision to Make, For Multiple Reasons
full_text:
Once the Titans' 2026 season comes to a merciful end, all eyes will turn toward draft season. Tennessee's moves prior to the trade deadline allowed the franchise to stack up on assets in an effort to speed up the progress of their multi-year rebuild.
Although, certain moves regarding their thinner-than-ever veteran presence loom overhead. Perhaps the most important among those is what to do with RB Tony Pollard, who has had his best season as a Titan, and one of the best seasons of his career, in the final year of his contract.
Not only is Pollard on pace for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season, but his six touchdowns are already just three short of the career-high nine he set with the Dallas Cowboys, back in 2022. He faces Dallas for the first time as a Titan this coming Sunday - the matchup is extremely favorable, to boot.
Pollard is the least of the Titans' worries currently; he's been the team's most consistent player on the offensive side of the ball for weeks now. But when his contract is up, does Tennessee pay a soon-to-be 30-year old back?
Not only that, but do they outbid the other inevitable suitors that had interest in him at the deadline?
Coming into this year, long-time backup Tyjae Spears was Pollard's clear successor. But Spears is also a free agent next year, and between consistent injury issues and poor production when he's on the field (22 carries for 94 yards on the year), that route looks less viable now than ever.
Tennessee could also sign a different free agent, but that list is dominated by veterans who don't look near as polished as Pollard right now; names like Alvin Kamara and Aaron Jones headline an underwhelming pool of possibilities.
Realistically, the Titans either sign Pollard to a new deal, draft his replacement, or both. RBs Jadan Baugh and Kewan Lacy would both pose as promising developmental pieces for the Titans, if one or both fall to Tennessee at the right spot.
30 is typically the cutoff for backs' efficiency. We can't forget that Pollard has performed way above the bar of expectation this season; this sort of production can't be expected of him for long, even if he shows no signs of slowing down right now.
The debate really comes down to how soon general manager Mike Borgonzi is willing commit to a full-youth roster. When do veterans from past coaching regimes phase out in favor of a completed rebuild? We'll find out where the GM stands by next spring.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: How Titans' Abysmal Coverage Stats Create a 2027 Draft Need Tennessee Can't Afford to Ignore
full_text:
Draft season starts early for 1-8 football teams. That's an unfortunate reflection of a squad's progress, but for the Tennessee Titans, the sheer amount of draft capital they hold over the next two years makes this phase more exciting than usual.
We've already dreamed up a draft where Tennessee ends up with absurd offensive firepower; Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith finds himself at the center of those dreams, and in one instance alongside Florida RB Jadan Baugh. But are those necessarily needs?
You could argue that to some extent, but a recent stat from Fantasy Points Data charts the 30 defenders in the league who have allowed the most Expected Points Added (EPA) when targted this season.
Alontae Taylor came in fourth, with +28.0 EPA, while fellow CB Marcus Harris placed eighth, with 24.1. Tennessee has allowed 40+ points and 350+ passing yards in back-to-back games. The Titans won't get far in the long run with coverage that poor.
Tennessee could always try and scrounge up a fix in free agency, but that's what they tried to do last offseason. You could say it was a matter of poor decision-making that could be rectified, but even then, the draft promises more future-forward potential.
The Titans will benefit from two first-round and two second-round selections in 2027. That's what trading your two best defenders and longest-tenured veterans gets you, in addition to the heartache.
That turns us to the candidates, which NFL Draft On SI just conveniently grouped into an early rankings system for us to pull from.
The obvious one is Notre Dame CB Leonard Moore, whose speed and length have consistently led to him topping pre-draft charts. He's been the undisuputed best CB in this class all year, and is currently a finalist for the 2026 Nagurski Trophy given the best defender in the nation.
Kelley Jones, out of Mississippi State, could be another intriguing option a little further down draft boards if Tennessee becomes attached to Jeremiah Smith first. He's got the speed and size to blanket receivers downfield, at 6'4", 205 lbs, and poses as another promising option.
The Titans will have the picks to take their pick at a bit of emergency help in a secondary. Ultimately, this debate will be decided by general manager Mike Borgonzi, who will have to choose between more offensive weapons to strengthen an already surging unit, and defensive help in a position group that is actively losing the Titans games.

title: Could Titans Have the Best of Both Worlds by Trading Top Pick, But Still Landing Jeremiah Smith?
full_text:
With the Tennessee Titans ’ season all but over, a lot of the talk surrounding the team revolves around what they’re going to do with their plethora of draft picks that currently includes the top pick in next year’s draft.
The undisputed prize of the 2027 class is undoubtedly Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith. He’s the type of prospect who could immediately jump in and give the Titans one of the most formidable receiver tandems in the league on day one alongside WR Carnell Tate — his former college teammate. Smith is only 20 years old and is legitimately one of the true can’t-miss non-QB prospects this century.
Another possible scenario ESPN’s Adam Schefter mentioned this week is the possibility of the Titans having a bidding war between QB-desperate teams should they secure that top pick. That's also an appealing possibility... but what if the Titans somehow manage both?
It’s unlikely, but let’s look at how it could happen.
I’ll just be honest from the start, this is not gonna be a normal trade. If I’m giving up the right to have Smith inside the building for the next decade, I’m gonna be asking for a lot.
If nobody wants to reach that price, then the Titans should have absolutely no problem staying put with their current haul of five picks in the top 70, especially when that class is headlined by arguably the safest slam dunk prospect regardless of position since DE Myles Garrett.
In most cases, the conversation wouldn’t even start without three first-round picks. Ideally, the Jets would be the trade partner since they currently have three first-rounders at their disposal. Even if they miss out on Smith in that scenario, a package that could potentially give them five first-round picks come April would be the type of move that could get this team back on track sooner rather than later.
But for the Titans to land a package of Smith plus picks, they’ll likely need to trade with a QB-desperate team that hopefully sits towards the top of the draft.
The ultimate dream scenario is a team like the Dolphins or Jets ending up with the second pick and they end up falling in love with Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker to the point where they end up doing whatever it takes to make sure they get him.
That would put the Titans in a perfect scenario where they could take the best offer from the team with the second pick and still select Smith. It definitely sounds like a fever dream, but crazier things have happened.
Only time will tell how all of this will play out, but one thing is for certain, the Titans have a massive offseason ahead of them and they absolutely cannot let it go to waste. If Tennessee does end up with that first pick, the options are limitless — and it's possible a historic trade is the cherry on top.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Titans Starting Cedric Gray Should Force Robert Saleh to Bench a Long Overdue LB
full_text:
Cedric Gray, after missing the Titans' Week 1 loss as a result of a concussion, spent the entirety of this season's first half trying to work his way back into Robert Saleh's rotation. His lack of snaps was confusing after Gray's great 2025 season, but that noise is in the rearview mirror now.
Without Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton in Week 10, Gray was essentially left as Tennessee's lone reliable LB against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He left no doubt in that contest that it was time to make a change in the unit. Gray hauled in his first career INT and had a team-high nine tackles.
Fittingly (and finally), Gray seems to be trending toward a promotion. Today, DC Gus Bradley said Gray is getting the majority of first-team reps in practice. Gray proved he deserves to start at WILL, and all signs point to him getting that opportunity vs. the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday.
Who, then, starts next to Gray. Where one question is answered, another is raised for Tennessee. The answer should be obvious: Hill, in his first season, has been arguably the Titans' best defender. Now is the time for Saleh and the Titans to bench Barton... but will they?
Hill leads the Titans with 82 tackles in eight games - and that's by a comfortable margin. Second to Hill is S Kevin Winston Jr., with 56. Gray comes in an fourth, with 46, in eight games also.
Where does Barton slide into the picture? All the way down in ninth, with 34 tackles. With both Hill and Barton practicing again ( to varying degrees ) after missing last week, the question is naturally begged as to which one will join Gray more often than not.
Coach Saleh has made it clear that he and this Titans regime value veteran talent. Calvin Ridley should've been traded at the deadline, but he was kept around. John Franklin-Myers (30) and Jermaine Johnson (27) were two of his biggest offseason pickups.
Barton is 29, and definitely fits that bill with eight seasons in the league. But with underwhelming tackling metrics and nothing else about his game that specifically stands out, there should be nothing stopping Tennessee from committing to the youth in their LB room.
The vet can play complimentary minutes, and fill in where needed. But at this point, both Hill and Gray have proven to be superior playmakers in a defense that desperately needs help. If you're willing to play the young guys on offense with Cam Ward (Ayomanor, Dike, Restrepo), why not here as well?
This is more of a preventative warning than anything else, but after Barton played over Gray for unclear reasons up to now, it wouldn't be a shock to see him get the nod again. We just have to hope Saleh sits the veteran and trusts the future of his own unit.

title: Analyzing a Realistic Path for Titans to End up With the Best WR and RB in 2027 Draft
full_text:
The 2027 NFL Draft is shaping up to be the Tennessee Titans' most important in years. We said that last spring, too, but both things can be true. The rebuild got more dire this season, but due to a handful of trades, we could be looking at an outlook-changing haul.
In our own draft speculation, we've vied for Tennessee to select top WR Jeremiah Smith. That is assuming the Titans hold on to the first pick. The natural follow-up to that would be a defensive piece, but ESPN's Jordan Reid just threw out an offense-heavy mock that's hard to refuse.
Therein, Tennessee takes RB Jadan Baugh at 26th overall (via the Chicago Bears), which would equip Cam Ward with the top receiver and back in the draft. This seems outlandish, but the cards are falling into place to make this a real possibility.
The Titans currently have the first pick, and while Baugh is undeniably talented, he's not as highly-rated a prospect as Jeremiyah Love was last season. As things stand right now, Tennessee is in position to steal Smith off the board, and then take the top back right where he's projected.
Worries about the defense - which is currently Tennessee's biggest problem - would be fair to assert here. The Titans already took Carnell Tate last season; why triple down on the offensive side of the ball?
The answer is a three-parter: Tennessee has two second-round picks in 2027, there are multiple strong candidates in free agency, and investing in Cam Ward is simply that important.
The first point is the simplest. Two second-rounders offers plenty of promise to build young defensive depth after the proposed first round. LB Anthony Hill Jr. was a second-round selection, and he has a case as the best player on the Titans' defense post-deadline.
Turning to free agency, guys like S Brian Branch, EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu, and CBs Ja'Quan McMillian and Isaiah Rodgers are all likely to be available. Per Spotrac, the Titans' in-season cap ($39.1 million) is still the highest in the NFL. That's a good sign for potential offseason additions.
The last one almost doesn't have to be said. Ward is Tennessee's most important player; his development as the team's franchise QB is critical to this draft not being all about taking a signal caller and resetting the system once again.
If Ward continues to get better, drafting to maximize his potentially and build around him should be the top priority. Why stop with Tate? Add a record-setting WR and an RB with 15 touchdowns in the SEC. That's taking the next step.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 1 Chimere Dike Stat Makes the Entire Argument for Titans to Start Him at WR
full_text:
Perhaps the Tennessee Titans' greatest story heading into Week 11 is the shakeup coming in the WR room. With Carnell Tate returning at WR and Wan'Dale Robinson being sent to IR, Cam Ward's arsenal of weapons is shifting in multiple ways.
This could come as a worry for Titans fans, as Ward has played his best football in the past two games prior to this movement. But, if anything, it should bode well for Tennessee's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys.
However, we're here today to hone in on one specific player that the Titans should be pushing as a result of this movement. Second-year WR Chimere Dike deserves to be catching passes right behind Carnell Tate.
Check out this all-purpose yards statistic from Ian Hartitz, which went viral on X :
Most all-purpose yards this season: 1. Jahmyr Gibbs (1,384) 2. Chimere Dike (1,267) 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (1,236) 4. Bijan Robinson (1,207) pic.twitter.com/D48PstGaZd
Gibbs, Smith-Njigba, and Robinson are three of the league's premier playmakers. These are team-defining guys that are typically the beginning and end of lists like these. Then you have Dike.
It's true that the bulk of those yards are on returns, but it should say something about Dike (a Pro-Bowl special-teamer) that he found his way on this list as someone who is typically limited to kickoffs. The extended impact Dike has had in his short run as a WR demands more clock at the position.
Prior to Carnell Tate sitting in Week 8 with a shoulder injury, Dike had six total receptions on the season, and 53 yards. In the two games without Tate since, Dike has seven receptions, 87 yards, and scored his first touchdown of the year against the Cincinnati Bengals.
What's more, Dike seemed to play a major part in Ward's recent rise under center. The two caught fire at the same time; just because Tate is returning doesn't mean that Dike should again be relegated to the scraps of receiving opportunities for other pass-catchers.
Dike is either the second or third best WR on this team, with fellow sophomore Elic Ayomanor having a horse in the race as well. Either way, that makes him a starter, especially with Robinson out. Nothing about Dike's game has suggested that this will be a temporary move, either.
Tennessee drafting Jeremiah Smith next year would obviously change the rotation, but if things stay as they are at WR, Titans fans can look out for Dike to play a more permanent role going forward. He just got a real, extended shot, and the aforementioned statistic is the proof in the pudding that it's only up from here.
